body:
- Merges `upstream/main` into the fork, the first sync since the March squash (#40).

## Why the merge base needed repairing first

The March sync was squashed, so it recorded no ancestry. Git still believed the fork branched at 2025-05-23 and re-presented all 305 upstream commits that squash had already incorporated as incoming changes, on top of the 360 that are genuinely new.

The first commit is a `-s ours` merge of `cf4a260acd`, the upstream commit the March squash corresponded to. It changes no files; it only records what was already incorporated. Verified before relying on it: at the squash, our tree was byte-identical to upstream at that commit for every component the fork does not touch (kayenta, halyard, fiat, keel all show zero differences).

After this, the merge base is correct and future syncs diff only what is new.

## Conflict resolution

45 conflicts against 6,651 cleanly merged files. Resolved toward upstream throughout. Only three fork changes were re-applied, because they are the only ones upstream does not already cover:

- `LaunchTemplateService` — guard a blank `keyPair` on the create path; upstream guards only the modify path
- `ImageCachingAgent` — cache `imageOwnerAlias` and `ownerId`
- deck azure services — plumb `loadBalancerResourceGroup`, `backendPoolName` and `bootDiagnosticsStorageUri`

Dropped as redundant: our `OrcaService` change (upstream has it verbatim, including `pipelineNameFilter`/`pipelineLimit`) and our `securityGroups === []` fix (upstream fixed it too).

The 27 `.github/workflows` deletions are kept — restoring them would run upstream's full CI on the fork. That is the one place this does not prefer upstream.

## Deck: AngularJS is gone

Upstream removed AngularJS in July 2026. The fork was 1,032 files behind on that migration, and deck now builds with pnpm on Node >= 24 rather than yarn.

Superseded by upstream's React versions, so dropped: the Angular Azure instance details, server group details, health settings and advanced settings screens, and the Azure-specific instance writer (upstream uses core's `InstanceWriter`).

## Fork capabilities restored on top

Upstream's conversion did not carry these, and each is ported to React following upstream's own patterns:

| Restored | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `findImageFromTags`, `resizeAsg`, `tagImage` stages | 163 `findImageFromTags` and 56 `resizeServerGroup` stages across the Azure deploy pipelines, plus `upsertImageTags` in both azureloaf bake pipelines. Without a provider registration deck renders them as unknown stage types. `shrinkCluster` and `scaleDownCluster` need none — core registers them with `useBaseProvider`. |
| Server group Resize action | Upstream's Azure menu has no Resize. Rewritten against the current API (`DeckRuntimeContext`, `onDismiss`/`onTaskComplete`, `confirmNotManaged`) since core dropped `ReactInjector` and `TaskMonitor.modalInstanceEmulation`. |
| Resource-group aware load balancer selection | Upstream lists every load balancer but never sets `loadBalancerResourceGroup`, so one outside the application's group was offered and then failed at deploy time. Restores the resource group filter, the opt-in that loads all load balancers, and the backend pool field. |
| Boot diagnostics storage URI | Still plumbed and still had help text, but no input remained to set it. |

## What was audited

All 228 fork-authored files were checked against the merge result. Two deltas reverted to upstream, both intended. All 25 fields the Angular wizard could set are reachable in upstream's pages. Instance actions match exactly; server group actions gain Clone and Rollback.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` on `@spinnaker/azure`: clean
- `eslint --max-warnings=0` on the touched directories: clean
- `prettier --check`: clean
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the `@spinnaker/core` build: both succeed

Not verified: the JVM build (upstream's range includes a Java 25 upgrade) and deck's karma suite, which is the whole-of-deck runner. `AzureCloneServerGroupModal.spec.tsx` and `azureServerGroupDetails.spec.tsx` both touch areas changed here.

author: kiran-jones
body: ## Problem Every date/time **input** in education already uses the shared `DateField`, and every **display** uses the tz-aware `~/lib/display` helpers. But the server parsed the wall-clock strings in between with a zone-naive `new Date(str)`. On the UTC-on-Fly host, a session set for **2:00 PM** was stored as `14:00Z`, which the ET-anchored displays then rendered as **10:00 AM**. Net effect: every session, assignment due date, and registration window showed ~4–5h earlier than what was typed. Education never adopted the app's canonical wall-clock↔instant helper (`zonedWallTimeUtc`) that the calendar, hiring, MCP, and digest all use. ## Fix - **`lib/timezone.ts`**: add `zonedDateTimeLocalToUtc(value, tz)` — the write-side inverse of `getZonedParts`/`formatInTimeZone`, anchoring a `datetime-local`/`date` string to a zone. - **`offerings.server.ts`**: `parseDate` now anchors to `APPLICATION_TZ` (ET). This fixes add/update-session, registration open/close, interval-series start, the clone shift delta, and the weekly-series time combination (the UTC date-math anchor is kept — it's DST-safe — only the final time combine changed). - **Assignment `dueAt`** (create + update): parsed ET-anchored. - **`toDatetimeLocal`** (edit-form prefill): derives parts via `getZonedParts(ET)` instead of host-local `getHours()`, removing an SSR/client hydration flip and the re-save drift it caused. - **`certificate-templates`**: use shared `formatDateShort` instead of a hand-rolled `new Date(...).toLocaleDateString()`. Widgets were already correct (`DateField` everywhere, `~/lib/display` for output); this only changes the parse/format layer between them. ## ⚠️ Data backfill (handled manually) Existing session / registration / `dueAt` rows are stored UTC-naive and will still display shifted until their stored wall-clock parts are re-anchored through `zonedWallTimeUtc(...ET)`. Per discussion this backfill is being done manually and is **not** part of this PR. ## Tests - New `zonedDateTimeLocalToUtc` cases (ET winter/summer offsets, round-trip with `formatInTimeZone`, date-only midnight, null/malformed) in `timezone-display.test.ts`. - Typecheck clean; existing `offerings.server` + timezone tests pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? ## Finding

Cause (from the v1 traces and cached mapper rationales): the extractor names the diabetes problem every time, but BM25 candidate retrieval omits E119 when the description carries qualifiers ("under control", "stable with medication", lab findings), and the mapper, told to choose only from the candidates, returns null or settles for R7309. One extra `map_dx` call for active, note-evidenced problems the first pass left uncoded, with the head term's candidates that were not offered; a problem a billed line depends on gets a wider net. body:
Rego side of the agent-governance hardening (compliance#616 is the server/schema side; compliance docs PR #615 is the architecture brief). Method-free by design — nothing here embodies the spine join.

## Self-protection: the governance plane is a crown jewel

Two real escalation paths existed and are closed:
1. **Direct** — the legacy ID allowlist auto-approved the templates that reload OPA policy (27), redeploy OPA (28), seed/mutate the registry OPA decides from (36/37), and rotate the MCP token (40). These now classify `blocked` and override every allow path (name-fragment match survives ID drift; `data/aac/governance_plane_template_ids` extends without a policy change).
2. **Indirect (create-then-launch)** — scaffold ops let an agent create a template; any `AAC`-named registered template was then auto-approved for launch. Creation ops are now `blocked`: agents run reviewed automation, they do not author it.

## Identity + jewels + emergency box

- `input.agent` becomes load-bearing: publish `data/aac/agents` (same push path as the template registry) and only registered identities act; absent registry = documented transition state.
- Action layer gains `business_rules` / `data` jewel classes (critical, dual-control minimum + justification, no lone-emergency path), tagged `jewel_class` through classification, response, and audit entry — the decision-log analytics key on it.
- **Latent gap fixed:** `emergency_access_valid` was computed and consumed by nothing — an `ai_emergency` system worked forever. `emergency_ok` now gates every decision path.
- Workflow launches now ride the registered-name/allowlist path instead of the scaffold bucket.

## Verification

- `opa test governance/` 108/108 (+15 new red-team/jewel/emergency tests, incl. precedence: plane-denial reported over identity-denial)
- regal-lint: GO — 0 bugs/performance in scope (one pre-existing `rule-assigns-default` fixed)

## Ops after merge (with compliance#616)

Consumer bump + OPA reload; optionally publish `data/aac/agents` + `data/aac/governance_plane_template_ids`. Note: launching templates 27/28/36/37/40 via MCP flips from ALLOW to DENY — that is the point; humans use the console/API for those.

author: olehakengo-svg
body:
## 要約

autopilot 起動時、作業が **3 箇所で座礁**していた。前 2 者 (PR #272 / #273) は本日着地済み。本 PR は **3 つ目 = ローカル `main` の乖離** を、**発生源ごと**塞ぐ。

## 1. 発生源の特定と修復 (本 PR の主題)

`scripts/hooks/session-end-save.sh` は step 2 で KB 変更を **HEAD (主 checkout では `main`) へ直接コミット**し、step 3 の `git push origin main` は **local main が behind だと必ず失敗**する。失敗は stderr に出すだけだったので「**コミットは main に積まれ、push は落ちる**」が毎日繰り返され、**乖離が再生産**されていた (起動時実測 **ahead 8 / behind 112**)。

2026-09-17 の PR #264 は *backlog* を掃除したが *ジェネレータ* を残しており、**5 日で ahead 8 まで再蓄積**した。09-21 の daily review が独立に同じ機構を特定していた (本 PR で救済した `index.md` に記録あり)。

**修復**: main への push が失敗したら、その commit を **`kb-rescue/<branch>-<date>` として origin へ退避**する。**成功時の挙動は一切変えない**、`--force` なし、`origin/main` 不変。

### pin (3 本) — grep ではなく実挙動

`tests/test_session_end_save_rescue.py` は **実 git repo + bare remote に対して実スクリプトを走らせる**。「正しいメッセージを出しつつ commit を座礁させる」実装は grep pin では通ってしまう。

- NG 状態 (behind main) で rescue ブランチに **当の commit sha** が届く
- counter-pin: happy path で rescue ブランチを作らない / KB が clean なら空コミットを作らない
- counterfactual 確認済 (fallback を外すと `origin has only {main}` で落ちる)

## 2. 座礁 KB の救済 (8 commit → 実質 4 ファイル)

main 側が既に上位互換だったもの (session log 4 本 / cell_deepdive summary 2 本) は **main を採用**。実質的に失われていたのは 4 ファイルのみ:

- `raw/trade-logs/2026-09-21.md` (362 行)
- `wiki/index.md` の 09-21 System State
- `wiki/log.md`
- `wiki/strategies/tokyo-nakane-momentum.md`

救済した 09-21 review の中身 — **`tokyo_nakane_momentum` の 8 発火は 59 分以内・3 ペア・全 BUY = 独立 8 標本ではなく「JPY 売り」1 ベットの 8 重複**、勝ち 3 本の `close_reason` が全て `SL_HIT` = ラベル破綻の 3 例目。**昇格審査でクラスタ性を N から割り引く前処理が必須**という論点が保存された。

## 3. committed conflict marker の修復

`wiki/sessions/2026-08-30-session.md` に conflict marker が **2 箇所コミットされたまま 3 週間 main に載っていた** (未解決の `git stash pop`)。union 解決し **KB 全体で marker ゼロ**を確認。

## 4. セッション内インシデント (検知・撤回済み、記録として)

hermetic 化**前**のテストが pre-commit 経由で走った際、リークした `GIT_INDEX_FILE` 越しに**実リポジトリの index へ `git add -A` を適用**しており、直後の commit が **3,568 files / −1,156,926 行を削除する commit** を作っていた。`git show --stat` の規模が異常だったため **push 前に検知**し `reset --mixed` で撤回、**ファイル名を列挙して再 stage** (working tree は無傷 = index のみの汚染)。

教訓: **(1) テストが実リポジトリを触りうる形なら CI/pre-commit 経由で実際に触る** — hermetic 化は品質ではなく**安全性**の問題 / **(2) commit 後に `--stat` の規模を必ず見る**。

## 検証

- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → **3,586 passed / 15 skipped / 1 xfailed**
- `python3 scripts/check.py` → **全 10 チェック通過**
- KB 全体で conflict marker **0**
- commit scope 実測 **9 files / +644 / −23**

## 順序の規律

ローカル `main` の 0/0 復帰は**本 PR がマージされた後**に行う。2026-09-17 は先に `reset` して未コミットの `index.md` 編集を破壊し System State を 13 日巻き戻した — その順序を繰り返さない。

body:
Closes #407

## Summary

A first lap now starts from the forge's current default branch, not from the local clone's `main` (D-0100).

- `fetchLapBase` (`src/access/forge.ts`) force-fetches `origin/<base>` into a branch rondo owns, `rondo/base/origin/<base>`; `origin/<base>` moves too.
- At admission (`src/access/conductor.ts`), a first lap fetches first and hands that branch to continuo as `--base-branch`. A failed fetch refuses the lap with git's reason, before the delegation record is written or continuo is spawned. Revisions fetch nothing (their base is the previous lap's topic branch).
- The plan's `baseBranch`, the PR base, the reading and the delegation record still say `main`; only continuo gets the mirror branch name.
- Why a mirror branch: continuo's `--base-branch` accepts `refs/heads` only, and git refuses to fetch into a checked-out branch (the lap 12 clone has `main` checked out).

Known limits (in D-0100): one extra branch per remote and base; two simultaneous admissions can clash on that ref lock (one is refused); a base not on `origin` (a fork) refuses every first lap. The proper fix is continuo accepting a remote-tracking start point.

## Test plan

- `npm run verify`: 1846 passed / 8 skipped locally. **The 3 press-path cases this PR touches were skipped locally** (the sandbox cannot create a Unix socket); CI must run them.
- New real-repo tests in `forge.test.ts`: behind clone catches up to the forge head without moving the clone's `main`/HEAD; refusal on missing branch / missing remote.
- Codex review round 1: no findings.

author: jakkapon-dev
body:
The four blockers found before Final QA. The headline is Quick Restock; the other three are the remaining items from the same report.

---

## 1. [P1] Quick Restock wrote the wrong field

The admin console computed `stock + amount` and PUT it as the whole product's total. For the 75 garments that keep stock per size, that total is only the sum of `sizeStock`, kept in step by a `pre('validate')` hook — **and `findOneAndUpdate` does not run that hook.** So the number moved on screen, no bucket moved with it, order placement kept drawing on the untouched per-size figures, and the next full save recomputed the total straight back down.

Four production rows drifted this way:

| SKU | `stock` | Σ `sizeStock` |
|---|---|---|
| `LOOK-01-CARGO` | 12 | 50 |
| `LOOK-05-CARGO` | 12 | 50 |
| `LOOK-06-SHIRT` | 12 | 50 |
| `LOOK-06-VEST` | 12 | 50 |

### What changed

**`PATCH /api/products/:id/restock`** takes a signed `delta` and the `size` it lands in. It is one conditional `findOneAndUpdate` on the bucket — the same shape order placement uses:

```js
{ ...selector, sizeStock: { $elemMatch: { size, stock: { $gte: -delta } } } }
{ $inc: { 'sizeStock.$[bucket].stock': delta, stock: delta } }
```

The floor is the update's own condition, not a check the route runs first, so a restock racing an order cannot drive a bucket negative and neither write can be lost. `stock` moves by the same delta in the same operation, which is what keeps the derived total agreeing with the buckets it sums.

- **ONE_SIZE** — a garment sold without sizes has a single `ONE` bucket, so the endpoint targets it without being asked and the admin row hides the picker. Naming `ONE` explicitly still works.
- **`PUT /api/products/:id` now refuses** a total-only write on a per-size product (`SIZE_STOCK_REQUIRED`, plus the list of valid sizes) rather than silently desynchronising it. That endpoint is the exact mechanism that drifted the four rows.
- **Both derived fields are settled from the document the write produced**, not the one read a moment before it — an order slipping in between would make a guess from the stale figures wrong, and a product wrongly left marked out of stock vanishes from the shop. This also rebuilds a total that had *already* drifted, so restocking one of the four rows heals it instead of carrying the drift forward.
- **Admin UI** — the inventory row shows a size dropdown with current per-size counts; Add stays disabled until a size is picked. The response is the persisted product, so the table is correct immediately *and* after a refresh.

### Repairing the live rows

`backend/scripts/repairStockTotals.mjs`. **Nothing has been run against production.**

```bash
cd backend && node scripts/repairStockTotals.mjs
```

- Dry run by default; `--yes` to write.
- Writes a JSON backup of every affected document first, on dry runs too.
- `--only=LOOK-06-VEST` to do one row, check it in the console, then the rest.
- Idempotent — a row whose total already matches is not touched.
- Finds drift from the data rather than a hardcoded list, so a row fixed in the meantime is not "repaired" back.

**The buckets win.** They are what order placement decrements under a condition that refuses to go below zero, so they are the only figure that has ever reflected the shelf. Rewriting them down to match the total would destroy 38 real units per row.

---

## 2. [P1] Admin loads cancelled each other

`useAdminData` shared one `generation` counter between inventory, orders and members, and `refresh()` fires all three at once — so by the time the first response arrived the counter had already moved twice and that response was discarded as stale. One counter per resource; a request can now only be superseded by a later request for the same resource.

## 3. [P2] Dashboard counted one page

Every KPI, the category split and the revenue chart were summed from the ≤25 rows a table happened to be holding, out of 75 garments. New **`GET /admin/stats`** returns whole-collection aggregates (product count, stock units, low stock, category split, order count, paid revenue, monthly series, member/VIP counts). The dashboard reads those and falls back to per-page sums only if the request fails. `AnalyticsTab` is fixed by the same change, since it shares `totalRevenue` / `monthlyData`.

## 4. [P1] Abandoned payments held stock for good

An order takes its units in the same transaction that writes it, before Stripe is asked for anything — that ordering is the only way two shoppers cannot both buy the last M, and it is kept. But a declined card, a closed tab or an unscanned PromptPay QR left that order `unpaid` and `pending` with nothing anywhere that would give the goods back.

- Orders with an online payment step carry a `reservationExpiresAt` (30 min, `ORDER_RESERVATION_MINUTES`). COD gets none.
- `services/reservationSweeper.js` runs every 60s: cancels the Stripe intent **first**, so a payment that landed seconds earlier is left alone for the webhook, then cancels the order and releases stock inside a transaction whose conditional update makes double-crediting impossible.
- `payment_intent.canceled` releases immediately. A **declined card deliberately keeps the reservation** — retrying with another card on the spot is the common case, and pulling the goods mid-checkout would turn a retry into an out-of-stock.
- `create-intent` refuses an already-released order and restarts the clock on a genuine retry; dismissing the QR releases at once rather than waiting out the window.

---

## Tests

```
ℹ tests 150
ℹ pass 141
ℹ fail 0
ℹ cancelled 9
```

The 9 cancelled are the pre-existing `durable-order-notifications` suite, which needs a local MongoDB test database. Frontend production build passes.

**New coverage (16 tests), including everything asked for on restock:**

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| refuses a total-only restock on a per-size product | req. 2 |
| adds units to one size and the total together | req. 1, 3 |
| requires a size on a per-size product | req. 1 |
| adjusts the total on a product with no size buckets | back-compat |
| targets the ONE bucket without being told to | req. 4 |
| cannot drive a size below zero | req. 5 |
| cannot drive an unsized product below zero | req. 5 |
| concurrent restocks of the same size both land | req. 6 |
| brings a sold-out size back on sale | `inStock` settlement |
| rebuilds a total that drifted from its buckets | the 4 live rows |
| + 3 reservation-sweeper, 3 admin-stats | items 2–4 |

The concurrency test drives two simultaneous restocks of the same bucket through a stand-in that applies each `$inc` to one shared figure, with both requests reading before either writes — the interleaving that lost a restock before. 25 + 10 + 7 = 42, neither overwritten.

---

## Review notes

- The sweeper touches live Stripe. Safe in Test Mode, but worth watching the first real expiry in the logs (`[reservations] released stock held by expired order …`) before trusting it unattended.
- `PUT /api/products/:id` returning 400 on a per-size total write is a deliberate behaviour change. The admin console no longer sends that shape; any other caller doing so was already silently corrupting the row.

author: bugscoderlab
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #56 (home chat on Ask plumbing). The Ask pipeline's structural credit multiplier: the strategy prompt advertised "up to five searches" with **no hard cap in code**, so one question fanned out into up to 5 per-search model calls (each carrying ~10 retrieved chunks of input) plus strategy and synthesis — ~8 calls at `ASK_MAX_TOKENS = 8192` each.

## What

- **Hard search cap** (default **3**, ceiling 5): `strategy.searches` truncated after blank-term filtering; the `Strategy` field description now tells the model the server caps the list. Applies to the Ask tab and home chat alike (both run the same graph).
- **Per-search extraction budget** (default **2048**, range 256–8192): the extraction answer is intermediate material for the synthesis, not user-visible prose — 8192 there was pure worst-case insurance. The user-visible stages keep `ASK_MAX_TOKENS = 8192` untouched (#1221 protections intact).
- **Settings page**: new "Ask Pipeline" section (admin-only mutation, matching the existing settings router). Values persist in `ContentSettings`, take effect immediately (singleton updated in place), and the graph degrades to defaults on a settings read failure (the `graphs/source.py` pattern). Stored values are clamped defensively in the graph.

## Verification

- Backend: **1087 passed** (14 new: fan-out cap defaults/overrides/clamping/fallback, per-search budget from settings + clamping, domain bounds, settings API round-trip + 403/422 cases)
- ruff clean; mypy at the pre-existing 7-error baseline (`tests/test_integrations_api.py` only)
- Frontend: lint clean (0 errors), `npm run build` green, form + locale-parity tests pass

## Notes

- Worst case per question drops from ~8×8192 output tokens to 2×8192 + 3×2048, plus up to two eliminated fan-out calls (input included).
- Skipped for now: a cheaper default `answer_model` for extraction — that's a product decision about defaults, not a conservation tweak.

body:
## Context

Explicitly allowed forwarding hosts such as `host.docker.internal` passed Gateway's early HTTP validation but were rejected by the embedded MCP SDK's narrower localhost guard when the listener context was loopback.

## Changes

- Disable only the redundant localhost guard in both embedded SDK transports; Gateway retains authoritative Host/Origin validation and agent authentication.
- Add composed-boundary regressions with explicit loopback listener context for legacy initialization/tool discovery and modern SDK `server/discover`, alongside canonical numeric access.
- Verify early Host/Origin/forwarding rejection and credential-domain failures; document security ownership.

## Review Notes

author: kiro-agent[bot]
body:
E 세트 250단어 중 11차 20단어(`exhilarating ~ explicit`)를 넣었다. 챕터 11이 확정된다.

E 세트 200 → **220단어**, 전체 1,629 → **1,649단어** / 83 → 84챕터. **남은 것은 30단어(2차수)다.**

## ★ 이 구간은 뜻이 겹치는 짝이 유난히 많다 — 다섯 짝을 손봤다

`exp-` 로 시작하는 낱말이 몰려 있어서, 한 차수에 이렇게 많이 겹친 것은 처음이다.

### 레벨을 두 칸 벌려 해결한 것 (9차에서 쓴 방법)

| 짝 | 레벨 | 뜻도 갈랐다 |
|---|---|---|
| `expenditure` / `expense` | C1 / B1 | '지출, 소비량' / '비용, 돈' |
| `expert` / `expertise` | B1 / C1 | '사람'(전문가) / '지식'(전문 지식) |

### 레벨로 풀 수 없어 뜻으로만 가른 것

| 짝 | 왜 레벨로 못 푸는가 | 어떻게 갈랐나 |
|---|---|---|
| `expand` / `enlarge`(6차) | 둘 다 B2. **B2 와 두 칸 떨어진 레벨은 C2 뿐**인데 `expand` 에 C2 는 맞지 않는다 | 자동사(`커지다, 확대되다`) / 타동사(`확대하다, 확장하다`) |
| `expect` / `anticipate` | `anticipate` 가 B2 `"기대하다, 예상하다"` — 원본대로 두면 **글자까지 같아진다** | 둘째 뜻을 `'당연히 여기다'` 로 (첫 뜻 '기대하다' 는 `anticipate` 가 이 낱말을 유의어로 쓰므로 유지) |
| `explicit` / `evident`(9차)·`apparent` | 원본의 `'분명한'` 을 앞에 쓰면 셋이 뒤섞인다 | 기존 GLOSS 의 `'명시적인'` 을 앞으로 |

**여기서 배운 것:** 레벨 간격은 `B1·B2·C1·C2` 넷뿐이라 **B2 짝은 C2 로만 벌릴 수 있다.** B2 에 있는 기본 낱말끼리 겹치면 레벨로는 풀 수 없고 뜻으로 갈라야 한다. 헤더에 적어 두었다.

## 추방 낱말이 한 무리가 되었다

`exile`(C2)·`expel`(B2) 이 들어오면서 기존 `banish`(C1)·`deport`(C1)·`eject`(B2) 와 다섯이 모였다. `banish` 와 `deport` 는 **11차 전부터 이웃 레벨**이었으므로 새로 만든 문제는 아니다.

뜻을 갈라 글자까지 겹치지 않게 했다.

```
expel   = 추방하다, 퇴학시키다
exile   = 추방하다, 망명시키다
banish  = 추방하다, 내쫓다            (기존)
deport  = 강제 추방하다, 국외로 내보내다  (기존)
eject   = 몰아내다, 쫓아내다           (기존)
```

## 사전 정리

이미 사전에 있던 낱말 **9개**, GLOSS·PRON 양쪽 **18항목**을 지웠다. 영향받는 기존 표제어가 **16개**라 베이스라인을 먼저 떠 두고 대조했다. **이번에는 내가 앞 차수에 넣은 항목이 하나도 없었다**(7~10차에는 매번 있었다).

| 파일 | 지운 항목 |
|---|---|
| `gloss.js` | exile, expect, expel, expenditure, explain |
| `words.js` | expansion, explicit |
| `words-c.js` | expand, expert |
| `pron.js` | 위 9개 전부 |

## 기존 문제를 지키려고 원본과 달리 정한 것

- **expel** — 기존 뜻 `"추방하다, 퇴학시키다"`. 표제어 `banish`·`deport`·`eject` **셋**이 유의어로 쓴다. 원본의 '내쫓다, 방출하다' 를 쓰면 `banish` 자신의 뜻(`"추방하다, 내쫓다"`)과 겹치는 낱말이 늘어난다.
- **expenditure** — 기존 뜻 `"지출, 소비량"`. 표제어 `consumption` 이 유의어로 쓴다.
- **expect** — 첫 뜻 `'기대하다'` 유지. 표제어 `anticipate` 가 유의어로 쓴다.
- **explicit** — 첫 뜻 `'명시적인'` 유지. 표제어 `ambiguous`·`equivocal`(7차)의 반의어다.
- **exile** — **동사로 정리** (원본은 `'국외 추방, 망명자, 추방하다'` 로 명사 둘 + 동사). `banish`·`deport`(둘 다 동사)가 유의어로 쓴다.

## 원본의 품사 혼재를 정리한 것

- `exile` `'국외 추방, 망명자, 추방하다'` → **동사**로
- `experiment` `'실험, 실험하다'` → **명사**로

## 유의어 렌더를 눈으로 확인해 걸러낸 3개

| 표제어 | 버린 유의어 | 실제로 뜨던 뜻 | 대체 |
|---|---|---|---|
| exhort | urge | "충동; 재촉하다" (명사 갈래가 앞) — 5차 `encourage` 와 같은 이유 | urge strongly |
| expense | charge | 표제어인데 품사가 **동사** "청구하다, 충전하다" | payment |
| expert | authority | 표제어 "권한, 당국" | master |

## 발음은 기존 표기에서 찾아 맞췄다

- `exist`·`existence` — `coexist`(`"코이그지스트"`)·`come into existence`(`"컴 인투 이그지스턴스"`)에 맞췄다
- `expense` — `at the expense of`(`"앳 디 익스펜스 오브"`)에 맞췄다. 이 구는 `pos` 가 phr 이라 명사 표제어 `expense` 와 오답 후보로 겹치지 않는다
- `experiment` — `experimental`(`"익스페러멘털"`), `anticipation` — `anticipate` 에 맞췄다

## 분포

```
품사   adj 59  adv 3  n 73  phr 2  v 83
레벨   B1 36  B2 99  C1 72  C2 13
```

이번 차수는 `syn` 을 비운 단어가 **하나도 없다**. PRON 에 `growth`·`swell` 을 채웠다.

## 검사

8종 전부 통과.

```
words-e-audit        검사 6종 + 출제 시뮬레이션 (220/220, 아닌것 202/202, 문장빈칸 218/218)
words-d-audit        OK
pron-audit           발음 커버리지 100% 유지
pron-render-check    --all 전수 OK
d-impact             짝 맞추기 지문 2c5b7afb8552 유지  ← 기존 문제 무변
match-order-check    OK
match-swallow-check  OK
match-label-audit    OK
```

캐시 `vocab-quiz-v95` → `v96`.

남겨 둔 기존 문제 4개(`drain`·`beguile`·`counterpart`·`companion`)는 이번에도 손대지 않았다.

author: herurg123
body:
## Incident

Recovery run `35686440718` on current main
`86d0ecdc6508fd3b80737ea35d98509ae4bb06eb` successfully restored the paid
artifact from run `35676364066`, skipped full Research, then failed during
Coverage editorial completion with:

```
EditorialRepairError: editorial repair input changed: archive_sha256
```

## Root cause

P0 editorial repair journal v1 hashed the entire `automation/archive/index.json`
object. `bootstrap_archive.py` rewrites top-level `generated_at = now()` on every
run, even when the archive corpus is otherwise identical.

Production evidence proves this is the Sep22 failure:
- the restored v1 journal stores
  `archive_sha256=aab2217b89a785b74e0cebcbe7cde95ee16a06964ce4882728bf14dc4df9e810`;
- the exact saved `editorial-prompt-input.txt` archive context has
  `generated_at=2026-09-22T01:36:38+00:00` and its canonical full hash equals
  that journal hash exactly;
- tracked `automation/archive/index.json` is the same Git blob
  `8915ebafd38ed697ecc1be82809221946b4f5415` on the original production head,
  prior remediation main, and current failing recovery main.

## Fix

- bump editorial repair journal identity to v2;
- v2 archive identity excludes only top-level `generated_at`;
- all archive items, story records, source URLs, source/version metadata and other
  fields remain hash-bound;
- preserve v1 replay fail-closed by allowing an archive mismatch only when the
  exact saved editorial prompt proves the original full v1 archive hash and the
  saved/current archives are identical after removing only `generated_at`.

No retrieval, search allocation, Coverage policy, ranking or selected-story logic
changes.

## Mandatory public-entrypoint regression

Regression now executes the actual `run_editorial_repair.main()` entrypoint on a
production-shaped v1 `response_saved` state. It proves:
- saved response replays offline;
- provider callback is never invoked;
- timestamp-only archive rebuild is accepted;
- real archive item drift remains blocked.

Additional v2 tests prove `generated_at` is non-semantic while any item mutation
fails closed.

## Spend / boundaries

- no production API calls for remediation validation;
- no Terra/Web Search/page fetch/image call;
- existing search ceilings 24/25 unchanged;
- current production artifact remains the source of incident evidence;
- after green exact-head CI this PR is authorized for immediate merge by the
  owner's standing instruction in this incident thread.

The single-GPU benchmark now compares square domains with strips of the same number of points, to show that CG convergence depends on the longest dimension rather than on the problem size.

- Grids use 16 points per roughness period (`N = 128` per unit length) at unit height. Squares are `32n × 32n` and strips `32n² × 32`, for `n = 1, 2, …, 32` (`isotropic`) or `8` (`anisotropic`, `stretched`).
- `--Lx` is replaced by `--layout square|strip` and `--bumps n`; results are stored under `$layout/$n/`.
- `setup_grid` takes an `Ly` keyword. The strong- and weak-scaling benchmarks are unchanged.
- The CG iteration cap is raised from 10000 to 20000.

author: seong-yong-park
body:
## 요약

TTS 지연 1·2단계. 문장별 PCM 캐시 + 선합성 + 즉답 한 마디.

- **캐시**: 합성한 문장을 16 kHz PCM으로 `cache_dir`에 보관. 적중 시 ~10 ms에 발행 (CLOVA 왕복 0.3–1.4 s 대신).
- **선합성**: `PlanStep`이 도착하는 순간 그 step의 `say`를 `/cortex/tts/prefetch`로 보내 미리 합성(우선). 부팅 3 s 뒤 고정 문구·few-shot say 31개를 `/cortex/tts/warmup`(latched, 후순위)으로 드립 전송.
- **즉답**: LLM에 요청을 보내는 순간 `ack_phrase`("네.")를 말해 생각 시간을 채움 (idle 상태에서만).
- **버그 수정**: rclpy 로거에 `.exception()`이 없어 합성 워커 안의 모든 예외가 AttributeError로 바뀌어 스레드풀에 삼켜졌다 → 어떤 실패도 로그 없이 조용히 드롭. traceback을 남기도록 수정.

## 측정 (llm_demo `speech:=true`, 실제 CLOVA 키)

콜드 캐시 첫 계획: step 0만 miss(319 ms), 나머지 5 step은 선합성 hit 7–16 ms. 두 번째부터 전부 hit 4–24 ms.

```
say '네.':               cache hit,  +4 ms
say '냉장고로 갑니다.':    cache miss, +319 ms
say '냉장고 문을 엽니다.':  cache hit,  +9 ms
…
say '안녕하세요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?': cache hit, +19 ms
```

CLOVA vs Google Chirp 3 HD 비교(12문장 ×2, `llm-router-test/out/tts-clova-chirp`): TTFA p50 0.65 s / 0.54 s, p95 1.35 s / 0.77 s — 캐시 적중이 어느 쪽보다 압도적이라 제공자 교체는 캐시 미스(새 chat 문장)만 남는 뒤 판단.

## 테스트

pytest 31 passed · 오프라인 `llm_demo.launch.py speech:=true` 3회 (콜드/웜)

## Submission type

- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Submission status and current guidance

This PR is submitted under the [submission guidance](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) reviewed on 2026-09-23. Its diff changes only the relevant catalog entry's **Lean proof** and **Attribution basis** fields. The Lean source and build materials are hosted in the external repository pinned below. This is not a new source-code submission or a claim to a new priority date.

Mathematical review must pass before Lean acceptance. Solver registration or an award claim by the mathematical solver is not a prerequisite for Lean verification or Lean candidate registration. The two contribution types can be registered independently.

The [`lean-verify` self-check is optional](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/docs/verification.md#recommended-lean-pre-submission-check) under the current rules.

## Problem and proposed change

**Problem ID:** JSP-000051 (Erdős Problem #51).

**Current entry:** `Lean proof | No`. **Proposed change:** mark `Lean proof | Yes` (pending verification), link the pinned source below, and credit the formalization contributors. The undersigned is the catalog editor only, not the proof author — this PR records an existing third-party formalization; no authorship or award eligibility is claimed by this PR.

**Scope:** This PR changes only the Lean proof and Attribution basis fields. The current status, eligibility, and solver credit are unchanged. No bounty, award eligibility, or original authorship is claimed.

## Proof source

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e"
  }
]
```

- **Theorem/file:** `src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos51.lean` — see the repository for the full theorem list and supporting modules.
- **Formalization authors:** plby/lean-proofs (formal authors per file header: Codex, GPT-5.x). The undersigned is the catalog editor only; no authorship or award eligibility is claimed by this PR.
- **Build instructions:** standard Lean 4 project; see the repository's `lakefile`/`lean-toolchain` and README. Run `lake exe cache get && lake build` to verify.
- **Toolchain:** leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0, Mathlib v4.33.0 (as pinned in the source repository's `lean-toolchain`).
- **Axiom hygiene:** no `sorry`/`admit`/`native_decide` in the file or its supporting tree; `#print axioms` audited at source. Every audited theorem depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- **Problem mapping:** JSP-000051 = Erdős Problem #51

## Reproducibility

The pinned commit `8822f7ddef30` on branch `main` of `plby/lean-proofs` contains the complete formalization. To reproduce:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs.git
cd lean-proofs
git checkout 8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e
lake exe cache get
```

author: danielmartinez-maker
body:
Stacked on PR #31.

This slice makes FINAL-07 presentation preferences durable across native-client restarts without introducing simulation authority.

### Implementation
- Adds a versioned `HHUI1` codec for UI scale, reduced-motion preference, and all seven keyboard bindings.
- Decoding is transactional: malformed versions, invalid scales, duplicate keys, out-of-range keys, incomplete payloads, and trailing data are rejected without mutating the current settings.
- Adds atomic whole-map keyboard validation so legitimate binding swaps can be restored without transient duplicate-key failures.
- Persists preferences under the existing per-user Hotel Haven LocalAppData root using temp-file + replace/write-through semantics.
- Loads preferences before native window layout so persisted UI scale is applied from startup.
- Settings changes and successful rebinding/reset operations save immediately; write failures preserve the in-session change and report that persistence failed.
- Cancels stale keyboard-capture state when window focus is lost, when page navigation leaves Settings, or when supported controller input takes over.
- Adds regression coverage for round-trip persistence, key swaps, corruption rejection, and preservation of transient input modality.

No simulation/save-game state is mixed into this file. No merge requested.

author: raisfirdaus-sys
body:
Two real settled coupons now carry enough evidence to fix how legs are ranked — and the evidence contradicts the advice this tool gave last time.

## What 18 real legs show, split by line type

| Line type | Paid full | Retention of printed odds |
|---|---|---|
| Half (X.50) | 5 / 5 | **100%** |
| Whole (X.00) | 3 / 4 | 88% (one pushed) |
| Quarter (X.25 / X.75) | 3 / 7 | **64%** |
| 1X2 | 1 / 2 | 49% |

The sample is small, but the leakage is structural rather than luck: a half line has zero probability mass in the push and half-result buckets, by construction. A push pays 1.0× and deletes the leg's odds outright; a half-lose pays 0.5×.

## The fix

Leg efficiency was multiplying probability by a flat constant per line type, which cannot express how much push risk a *particular* whole line actually carries. It now ranks on the probability mass that pays **full** odds — full wins, plus half credit for half-wins, nothing for pushes and half-loses — discounted by the margin paid.

**This retracts a recommendation made in this repo.** The four-leg Champions League ticket proposed earlier was built on three whole lines. Under the corrected metric they rank 103rd, 130th and 131st:

| Leg | Raw probability | Pays full odds | Push risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| HT Villarreal 0.00 | 55.9% | **32.4%** | 42.0% |
| HT Atletico Madrid 0.00 | 55.9% | 34.1% | 38.9% |
| HT Under 2.00 | 55.8% | 40.3% | 27.7% |

The nine-leg tickets are now clean: zero push-exposed legs in the Champions League and Nations League sets.

## Second fix: stop selecting on fabricated edges

Ranking by expected value is only honest when a person entered the statistics behind that value. Ranking by EV over placeholder seeds made the selector hunt for edges this repo invented, and the club slate was advertising a nine-leg ticket at **+42% EV** — a number no bookmaker offers anyone.

Parlay building and the reality banner now force a full market anchor whenever no user-entered statistics exist for the slate, so the reported figure is the compounded margin instead:

| Slate | Reported before | Reported now |
|---|---|---|
| Club, 10–13 Oct | +42.0% | **−10.8%** |
| Champions League | −17.7% | −25.2% |
| Nations League | −46.6% | −46.6% |

A backstop warning stays in the parlay tray for any positive EV that appears without user statistics.

Tests pass. Verified in Chromium across all three slates with no page errors and no horizontal scroll at 390px.

author: panarch
body:
The workspace presents three bottom tabs, but the browser history was one list
that every move pushed onto. A route request now decides its own history
treatment from where it stands relative to the current one, read from the
parents already declared in the route schema.

- Reaching a screen below the current one adds an entry. Opening a Task, an
  Issue from its list, a commit from Log, PR Files from a PR, and a file from
  Review, Compare, Log, or PR Files all descend.
- Moving between screens at the same place replaces the current entry.
  Selecting another Task, Note, Settings section, Issue, or file, changing Log
  and GitHub pages, changing Compare or Review refs, changing Review axes, and
  switching between Conversation, Integrated Review, Git, and GitHub all stay
  at one entry.
- Leaving a screen rewinds the entry it consumed instead of adding another, so
  a visible Back no longer leaves a step that browser Back walks back into.
- A route arriving from outside the tab it lands in — an address the browser
  loaded, a notification opening its Task, a request naming another tab's page,
  a tab selection, or a native link crossing tabs — has that tab's own screens
  written in beneath it. Back walks up them instead of leaving the application
  or returning to what the arrival interrupted.
- Each tab keeps the screen it last showed, so selecting a tab reopens it at
  the depth it was left at. Settings now remembers its page as Tasks and Notes
  already did.
- A native link followed inside one tab stays a step in that tab's flow, so
  opening a Review file from a Task's conversation returns to that conversation.

Entries are written through the History API on both paths and carry each tab's
last route, so arriving at one restores what the tabs held. The Navigation API
now only reports arrivals and keeps a native link inside one document.

Bypassing the relation is kept for two requests: applying a notification's Task
route, and a correction where the subject a route named is gone.

author: focafunk
body:
## Qué cambia

Suma `doc/mcp/publicacion-en-directorios.md`: guía paso a paso para publicar el MCP de Trazalog en los directorios de **Claude**, **ChatGPT** y **Gemini**, en ese orden, para ir preparando los trámites antes del cutover.

## Por qué

Pedido del PM: cuando la versión de `develop` pase a producción, quiere tener los trámites listos y no arrancar de cero. Relevado el 2026-09-22 contra la documentación oficial de los tres proveedores y cruzado con lo que hay en `develop`.

Lo que la guía aclara primero: **no son tres directorios**. Anthropic y OpenAI tienen portal con revisión. **Google no tiene directorio público** — en Gemini Enterprise el administrador de cada cliente registra el MCP en su propio Google Cloud, así que lo que Trazalog prepara es una guía para el cliente.

## Lo que falta hoy, por severidad

| | Estado |
|---|---|
| **Política de privacidad y términos públicos** | ❌ no existen (404 en `trazalog.com`). Causa de rechazo inmediato en Anthropic, obligatorias en OpenAI |
| `openWorldHint` en las 20 tools + `readOnlyHint: false` en las 2 de escritura | ❌ OpenAI las exige explícitas; Anthropic y Google no |
| Refresh token | ❌ TTL 24 h sin renovación: el usuario reconecta todos los días. No bloquea, pero un revisor lo nota |
| Cliente OAuth estático para Google + su redirect URI | ❌ Google no hace DCR |
| UserInfo endpoint | ❌ solo para restricción por dominio de workspace en ChatGPT; no bloquea |
| DCR, PKCE S256, metadata RFC 8414/9728, tools separadas lectura/escritura, nombres ≤ 64 | ✅ |

## Cómo lo verifiqué

- Documentación oficial de Anthropic (submission, review criteria, authentication), OpenAI (plugins submission, guidelines, auth), Google (Gemini Enterprise custom MCP) y el MCP Registry — links en §9.
- Auditoría de las 20 tools de `develop` contra los requisitos de anotaciones y nombres.
- Auditoría del metadata OAuth de Dnato en `develop`: qué publica, qué redirect URIs acepta, cómo valida el DCR.
- Verificación de que las URLs de privacidad/términos no existen en `trazalog.com`.

> No pude verificar en vivo el transporte del MCP Server ni el PRM (`mcp.cloudtrazalog.com` no respondía desde acá). Del trabajo previo consta que es Streamable HTTP.

Va a `develop` porque la versión que se publica es esa.

author: endoryu
body:
ユーザー質問「forge以外の開発環境でconfluenceアプリは開発できる?」への回答。ヘッダー強制が基盤の乗り換えで回避できるかの確認でもあります。**コード変更なし。**

## 結論

**選べません。** Confluence Cloud のアプリを新規に作る基盤は Forge だけです。

| フェーズ | 実施 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| Phase One | **2025-09-17** | Marketplaceへの新規掲載はForgeのみ。Connect module を1つでも含むアプリは掲載不可 |
| Phase Two | **2026-03** | Marketplaceアプリの descriptor 更新不可。**Connected Apps 経由の新規 private アプリのインストールも不可** |
| Phase Three | 2026 Q4 | Connect は end of support 状態へ |
| End of support | **2027-01-31** | 当初の2026年12月から延長 |

本日(2026-09-22)時点で **Phase Two まで実施済み**です。Connect では新規掲載も private インストールもできません。

Connect module を含む Forge アプリ(Connect on Forge)も「Connectアプリ」として扱われるため、抜け道になりません(公式: "apps mixing Connect and Forge modules are classified as Connect apps until all Connect modules are removed")。

## アプリ以外の経路も代替にならない

1. 外部Webアプリ + REST API + OAuth 2.0 — ページ内にUIを出せません。自前ホスティングが要り、費用0原則と §3 に反します。
2. Forge + `remotes` — UIはForgeのままなのでヘッダーの制約は変わらず、§3 で恒久禁止です。
3. Data Center / Server の P2 プラグイン — 対象はCloudで、別製品線です。
4. ブラウザ拡張 — Marketplaceで配布できません。

→ **Forge の制約の内側で設計するほかありません。** §3.1 の選択肢表の Connect 行を「選択不能」へ更新しました。

author: serv-os
body:
Peter, through one evening: "its just gone offline again!", "clicking print wakes it back up and reconects it", "nothing has changed on the printer its been sat there the entire time".

## The diagnosis is his own evidence

**Ping answered while port 9100 refused**, later ping failed too, and **pressing print always brought it back**. That is a print server going to sleep, not a broken printer and not the wifi.

The live record agrees it is intermittent, not failing. Jobs needing a retry: **9 of 11** on 16 Sep, **11 of 32** on 17 Sep, then **zero of 12** on 20 Sep, then 2 of 17 and 4 of 9. A dying machine does not have perfect days.

## Three changes

- **Keep awake.** The till sends `DLE EOT` (the ESC/POS status query) every two minutes to each network printer. It prints nothing and uses no paper, and it is skipped whenever a real ticket has just gone out. Jittered per device so two tills never knock together.
- **One printer, one job.** The dispatcher fired every job in a batch at once (a `for` loop over an un-awaited async call), so one kiosk order opened **three sockets** to a machine that accepts one: one printed, the others timed out. Same printer now queues; different printers still run side by side. My own v5.9.27 made this fire far more often by sweeping in bursts.
- **A collision is not a dead printer.** `failed to connect ... after 5000ms` now gets six extra attempts. `out of paper` does not, because retrying does not add paper.

## Caught while writing it

The first version recorded printer contact in the broadcast path using a variable that does not exist there. It would have thrown on every fast print. Both paths now use their own.

23 new tests. 3441 pass, build clean.

author: chubes4
body:
## Summary

`extrachill_analytics_link_page_migration_table_ready()` had no way to know which side of a migration it was checking, and reused one error code for both column and index mismatches. On production this meant a **source**-side failure (blog 4, `unique_daily_link_click` **index**) was reported as *"An Analytics destination table does not match its owned column contract"* — wrong role, wrong mismatch kind, and no indication of which column or index actually differed.

Closes #286.

## Changes

- **Role is now explicit, not asserted.** `table_ready()`, `schema_ready()`, and `schema_for_blog()` all accept an optional `$role` (`'source'` / `'destination'` / `''`). Every existing call site already knows which side of the migration it's on (before vs. after `switch_to_blog()` to the destination), so each one now passes its role in rather than the function guessing. When no role is supplied the message stays neutral ("An owned Analytics table...") instead of defaulting to a specific claim.
- **Column vs. index mismatches are now distinguishable by code alone.** Column mismatches keep the existing `analytics_link_page_migration_schema_mismatch` code. Both index-shape failures (missing/extra index name, and index-content mismatch) now return a new `analytics_link_page_migration_index_mismatch` code. Read failures (`..._schema_read_failed`) are unaffected.
- **The differing column or index is named in both the message and the error data.** Added a small `extrachill_analytics_link_page_migration_first_difference()` helper that walks the expected vs. actual contract maps and returns the first key that's missing, extra, or changed. The column-mismatch error data gains an additive `column` key; the index error data's existing `index` key is unchanged in shape.

Error data shape is unchanged for existing keys (`table`, `index`) and purely additive (`column`) — the one call site that reads `get_error_data()` (the migration plan's readiness reporting) keeps working.

## Design notes / judgment calls

- Went with **explicit role pass-through** over neutral-only wording, since every caller in this codebase already knows source vs. destination at the point it calls into schema validation — passing it through gives strictly more diagnostic value than staying neutral everywhere, while the neutral fallback still covers any caller that doesn't know.
- Kept the **column mismatch on the pre-existing `_schema_mismatch` code** rather than renaming it, since the issue only asked for a new code to separate index failures out; renaming the column code would be an unnecessary second breaking change for any external consumer that already keys off it.
- The existence-mismatch branch (index present in one side but not the other) and the content-mismatch branch (index exists on both sides but its definition differs) share the same new `_index_mismatch` code — both are index problems from the caller's point of view, and both now name the specific index.

## Testing

`homeboy review test extrachill-analytics --placement local`: **444 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** (whole suite, including this contract test file).

`homeboy review lint extrachill-analytics --placement local` on both changed files: phpcs, phpstan, and eslint all pass with no findings.

Added tests to `tests/LinkPageStorageMigrationContractTest.php`:
- `test_source_and_destination_schema_failures_are_blockers` (existing test, extended): asserts a source-side schema mismatch found during the readiness flow says "source" and never "destination" — the exact regression from the production report.
- `test_column_and_index_mismatches_are_distinguishable_and_named` (new): drives a column mismatch, an index-content mismatch, and an index-existence mismatch through the real readiness flow and asserts each produces a distinct, correctly-coded error whose message and `get_error_data()` name the specific column/index.
- `test_table_ready_names_the_supplied_role` (new): calls `table_ready()` directly with `'source'`, `'destination'`, and no role, asserting the message names only the supplied role (or neither, when unspecified).

body:
## Summary

Reported as "reports are stale" — checked directly, and the underlying data isn't actually stale (`data/policy_briefs.json` was 3 days old at the time, well under the page's own 30-day staleness threshold; confirmed identically on production: "Last fetch: Sep 19, 2026"). But the pipeline-status badge read **"0 feeds · 274 alerts · 9 briefs,"** which reads exactly like a broken pipeline — 274 alerts materializing from zero feeds.

**Root cause:** `scripts/generate_policy_briefs.py`'s `meta` object has never included a `feed_count` field — only `generated`/`brief_count`/`source_alerts`/`methodology`. `fetch_google_alerts.py` tracks a real feed count at fetch time, but it's a separate script in the pipeline and that count never reaches `policy_briefs.json`. The page's `meta.feed_count || 0` has silently defaulted to `0` on every single run since this badge shipped.

**Fix:** only show a feed count when the data actually has one (`typeof meta.feed_count === 'number'`). Alert and brief counts are the real, populated signal that the pipeline ran, and stay in the badge either way. If a future generator run starts populating `feed_count`, the badge picks it up automatically with no page change needed.

## Test plan

- [x] `node test/policy-briefs-curated.test.js` — passes, unaffected
- [x] `node --test test/housing-news-leads-with-the-newest.test.mjs` — passes, unaffected
- [x] Verified the new logic directly against the real data shape: without `feed_count`, badge now reads "✓ Pipeline active · 274 alerts · 9 briefs" (no misleading "0 feeds"); with a hypothetical `feed_count`, it correctly includes it

## Implements

* Added stock transfer migration
* Added StockTransfer and StockTransferItem entities
* Added transfer status management
* Added repositories and DTOs
* Added StockTransferService and controller
* Added source and destination warehouse validation
* Added inventory availability validation
* Added automatic TRANSFER_OUT and TRANSFER_IN stock movements
* Added automatic destination inventory creation when required

## API Endpoints

* `GET /api/stock-transfers`
* `GET /api/stock-transfers/{id}`
* `POST /api/stock-transfers`
* `PATCH /api/stock-transfers/{id}/status?status=COMPLETED`

## Business Rules

* Source and destination warehouses must be different
* Both warehouses must belong to the selected company
* Products must belong to the company
* Source inventory must have sufficient available stock
* Completing a transfer creates TRANSFER_OUT and TRANSFER_IN movements
* Destination inventory is created when necessary
* Completed transfers cannot be changed
* Transfer processing is transactional

## Testing

* Maven test suite executed successfully

digest: `sha256:ed2be1d8a2bd56554e5cb1ddb451011adeed8d2cd3a7b9d15e3c17336b91cab2`
tags: `dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3.1-debian13-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3-debian13-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3.1-debian-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19-debian13-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3-debian-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19-debian-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3.1-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19.3-fips-dev, dhi/gitlab-runner:19-fips-dev`

## 卡

https://github.com/hawkeye-xb/P-Pass/issues/373 — [CI-17] changes 只输出一个 run_heavy，6 个 job 共用

closes #373

---

## 一句话

判据从「一个布尔管 6 个 job」拆成**按依赖面分的两个 lane**，让只改 `apps/**` 的 PR 跳过主 workspace 的重型编译，但 `architecture enforcement` 照跑。

## 第一步（卡面必答题）：`apps/**` 到底能不能影响主 workspace

卡面写了「实施者必须自己重跑一遍，不许直接采信」。重跑结果（在本 PR 的 base commit 上）：

| 检查 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `grep -rn "apps/" crates/ --include="*.rs"` | **7 处，全是注释 / doc-comment**（开卡时 6 处，期间 `platform/src/windows.rs:26` 新增一处） |
| `grep -rnE "include_str!\|include_bytes!\|fs::read\|File::open\|Path::new" crates/ --include="*.rs" \| grep -i apps` | **空** |
| `crates/daemon/build.rs` | 只读 `PPF_BUILD_VERSION` 环境变量，全文 7 行，不碰路径 |
| src-tauri 在主 workspace 吗 | **不在**（根 `Cargo.toml` 的 `members` 不含 `apps/`；其自身 `Cargo.toml` 头部：*Standalone workspace on purpose … depends on no internal crate*） |

**两处差点看成反例，都追到底了：**

1. `crates/daemon/tests/cli_flow.rs:70,97` 提到 src-tauri 的 `DAEMON_VERSION_MARKER` —— **反向**依赖。daemon 的 `--version` 输出是契约（DAE-08 #319 锁的），**src-tauri 消费它**。方向是 daemon → src-tauri，所以改 src-tauri 弄不红 daemon 的测试；反过来才会，而那种改动落在 `crates/**`，本来就判跑。
2. `crates/platform/src/windows.rs:26` 说 `DATA_DIR_NAME` **取自** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` 的 `identifier` —— 这是**值复制**，不是文件读取。实测全仓 `.rs` 里提到 `tauri.conf` 的只有两处注释，**没有任何代码读那个 JSON**（`the_directory_name_is_the_bundle_identifier` 那条测试是 `assert_eq!(DATA_DIR_NAME, "com.p-pass.desktop")`，两个写死的字符串比）。所以改 `tauri.conf.json` 不会弄红任何 Rust 测试 —— 本 PR 不引入 fail-open。

## 逐条论证 job ↔ lane 的映射

比卡面那张表多补了一列：**「谁来保证 `apps/` 的 Rust 仍被检查」**。少了这一列，跳过就是丢覆盖。

| ci-rust job | 必需 | 绑到 | `apps/**` 惰性的依据 | `apps/` 的 Rust 由谁检查 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `architecture enforcement` | ✅ | **`run_arch`** | ❌ **不惰性** —— `tools/arch-check.sh:64` 明写 `apps/** — scanned` | 自己 |
| `clippy (deny warnings)` | ✅ | `run_heavy` | 主 workspace clippy，编不到独立 workspace | `ci-desktop` 的 `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` |
| `test (nextest + windows cross-check)` | ✅ | `run_heavy` | 同上，且 crates/ 无一处读 apps/ | `ci-desktop` 的 `cargo test --lib` |
| `test (windows)` | ❌ | `run_heavy` | 同上 | 同上 |
| `fmt + actionlint` | ❌ | `run_heavy` | `cargo fmt --all` 只覆盖主 workspace 成员 | `ci-desktop` 的 `cargo fmt -- --check` |
| `license + dependency audit` | ❌ | `run_heavy` | `cargo deny` 读根 `Cargo.lock`；`deny.toml` 不提 src-tauri | ⚠️ **无人** —— 见下方「顺带发现」 |

## fail-closed：原有三处保留，另加两处

原有（#255 建立的，一个字没动）：
1. 两个 lane 各自仍是 **allowlist 反向写法** —— 只有改动**全部**落在自己清单里才跳过，漏路径 = 多跑一次；
2. 下游仍写 `!= 'false'` —— `changes` 挂掉时输出为空，条件成立 ⇒ 照跑；
3. `!cancelled()` 保证 `changes` 失败时下游仍执行，不被 `needs` 的隐式 `success()` 跳掉。

**本 PR 新加两处**（卡面没要求，但从卡面原则直接推出来）：

4. **未知 lane 一律判「要跑」。** `LANE` 打错一个字母（`rust-worksapce`）若被静默当成宽清单，就是本脚本存在的意义所要防的那件事。
5. **`decide` 步骤自检包含关系。** 宽 lane 的无害清单是窄 lane 的超集 ⇒ `run_heavy=true` 时 `run_arch` 不可能是 `false`。真出现只可能是判据被改坏，当场两个都改判要跑并打 `::error::`：

```bash
if [ "$heavy" = "true" ] && [ "$arch" != "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::包含关系被破坏（run_heavy=true 而 run_arch=$arch）——判据有问题，全部改判要跑"
  arch=true
  heavy=true
fi
```

## `ci-desktop.yml` 一行都没动

**默认 lane（不带 lane 参数）的语义与本 PR 之前逐字一致**，而 `ci-desktop.yml` 就是不带参数调的。这是**向后兼容契约**，测试第 1 节专门钉它（`expect` 走的就是不带参数那条路径）。卡面范围也明确写了不含 `ci-desktop.yml`。

这不是省事：`desktop (ubuntu-latest)` / `desktop (windows-latest)` 编的就是 `apps/desktop`，它们**必须**保持窄清单。

## 验收标准逐条回应

### 标准 1 + 3：测试覆盖四类断言 —— ✅ E1，33 通过 0 失败

```
==> 1. 正向判据 · 不带 lane 参数（ci-desktop.yml 的调法，语义须与 CI-17 之前一致）  7 条
==> 2. fail-closed 的命门：不认识的东西一律要跑                                      5 条
==> 3. CI-17：两个 lane 各自的判定                                                  13 条
==> 4. CI-17：未知 lane 一律判要跑                                                   3 条
==> 5. CI-17：包含关系 —— 13 组输入全部满足 run_heavy=true ⇒ run_arch=true          ✅
==> 6. 变异反证甲：allowlist 兜底改成全放行 → 3/3 变红                               ✅
==> 7. 变异反证乙：宽 lane 的 apps/* 改成永不匹配 → 3/3 变红                         ✅
==> 8. 异常路径：无 base 时两个 lane 都判要跑                                        2 条
────────────────────────────────
通过 33，失败 0
```

两个 lane 的判定矩阵（实测）：

| 输入 | 默认 lane | `rust-workspace` |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` | `true` | **`false`** |
| `apps/android/app/src/main/x.kt` | `true` | **`false`** |
| `apps/x.kt` + `docs/a.md` | `true` | **`false`** |
| `apps/x.kt` + `crates/y.rs` | `true` | `true` |
| `crates/daemon/src/main.rs` | `true` | `true` |
| `Cargo.lock` | `true` | `true` |
| `newthing/x.rs` | `true` | `true` |
| `tools/arch-check.sh` | `true` | `true` |
| `.github/workflows/ci-rust.yml` | `true` | `true` |
| `docs/a.md` | `false` | `false` |
| 空列表 | `true` | `true` |

### 标准 2：变异反证 —— ✅ E1，**两个**变异

卡面只要求一个。加了第二个，因为第一个证不了新东西：

- **甲**（原有）：`is_inert` 兜底 `return 1` → `return 0`（allowlist 变全放行）⇒ 「改了 crates/」等 3 条必须变红。**证的是「要跑」那半边不是恒真式。**
- **乙**（新增）：宽 lane 的 `apps/*` → `zzz-never-matches/*` ⇒ 第 3 节那些 `false` 必须全变 `true`。**证的是「可跳」那半边不是恒假式** —— 没有它，第 3 节的 13 条断言可能只是碰巧过。

两个变异都先 `grep` 确认锚点真的匹配上了，没匹配就直接判失败（否则「变异没生效」会伪装成「变异后没变红」）。

### 标准 5：并发槽对照 —— ⏳ 待探针 PR 实测，**不在这里估**

卡面要求「不许用估算」。本 PR 自己改的是 `.github/**` 与 `tools/**`，两者都不在任何无害清单里 ⇒ **本 PR 上 6 条全跑**（这本身就是负对照的一半：非惰性改动照样全跑）。

真实的「之后」数字要一个**只改 `apps/**` 的 PR** 才量得到，见下。

### 标准 4 + 6

- **标准 4（负对照）**：本 PR 自身即「改了非惰性路径 ⇒ 6 条全跑」。`BLOCKED` 那半边在探针 PR 上做。
- **标准 6（不许改 job `name:`）**：✅ 一个都没改。`git diff` 里 `name:` 零改动，必需检查列表不受影响。

## 探针 PR（卡面第四步）

马上另开一个**只改 `apps/**`** 的探针 PR，**base 设成本分支**（这样 `base.sha` 是本分支，diff 里只有那个 apps 文件，而 workflow 用的是本分支的新逻辑）。预期：

```
architecture enforcement   真跑
clippy / test / test (windows) / license+deny / fmt   skipped
mergeStateStatus = CLEAN
```

然后在同一个探针上追加一个 `crates/` 下必然失败的测试，验「6 条全跑 + BLOCKED」。做法沿用 #255 的探针 PR #271。**探针结果贴回本 PR 后再合。**

## 顺带发现，已单独开卡（未顺手修）

**#376（SEC-09）**：`cargo deny check advisories licenses bans` 只审主 workspace，**src-tauri 那棵 Tauri 依赖树从来没被审过** —— `deny.toml` 不提它，`ci-desktop` 也只跑 fmt/clippy/test 不跑 deny。

⚠️ **本 PR 没有引入这个缺口，只是让它显形**：正因为 deny 本来就不审 src-tauri，把 `apps/**` 划进它的无害清单才不丢覆盖。#376 不是本 PR 的回退。

## 自验

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `bash -n` 两个脚本 | 通过 |
| `bash tools/test-ci-needs-full-lane.sh` | **通过 33，失败 0** |
| `just ci-docs` | **green ✅** |
| `git diff --stat` | 4 个文件，与卡面范围逐字一致；`ci-desktop.yml` 未动 |
| `AGENTS.md` 行数 | 105 → 113（+8）。该文件自称「一页以内」，我先写了 11 行又压到 8 行；若仍嫌长可再删 |
| 未跑 `just ci` | 本 PR **零 Rust 改动**，Rust 门禁由 PR 上的 lane 全量跑 |

## 收尾检查

- [x] 卡面验收标准逐条回应，附命令 + 真实输出（标准 1/2/3 = E1；标准 5 明确标为待探针，**不估算**）
- [x] 故障/安全类附反证结果（两个变异，各 3/3 变红）
- [x] 范围外改动为零；2 项「实施中追加」（未知 lane fail-closed、包含关系自检）已显式登记
- [x] 发现的新问题已单独开 issue（**#376**），未顺手修

## Summary

Closes the pre-public checklist items that are not blocked on GitHub Support, now that name clearance and logo distribution rights are confirmed.

**The README would have embarrassed us on day one.** It told visitors to run `npm install --global noetherkin` and `npx noetherkin --help`. No such package exists, so the documented first step would 404 for every single person who tried it. The quickstart that follows also assumed a global binary on `PATH`. Section 2 now describes building from a checkout and defines the `noetherkin` alias the rest of the README already uses, so those examples stay valid. This is deliberately neutral on ACP-012 (#6), which proposes retiring npm entirely: it documents what works today and needs no revisiting either way.

**Remaining items.**

| Item | Done |
| --- | --- |
| Copyright holder and year | `NOTICE`, `Copyright 2026 Prince Agyei Tuffour` |
| `NOTICE` decision | Added and shipped in the tarball |
| `package.json` author | Was absent, now set |
| `CODEOWNERS` | Every path to `@nanaagyei` |
| Dependency-license policy | AGPL, GPL, SSPL denied in dependency review |
| Social preview | 1280x640 card prepared; upload is manual |
| Issues / Discussions / Wiki | Issues on, Discussions off, Wiki disabled |

A few of these involved a judgment call worth stating rather than burying:

- **`LICENSE` is untouched.** Its appendix still reads `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]`, which is the verbatim Apache "how to apply" template rather than a gap. Editing license text is discouraged, so the real notice lives in `NOTICE`.
- **`NOTICE` is in the `files` allowlist.** npm auto-includes `LICENSE` but not `NOTICE`, and Apache-2.0 requires it to travel with distributions. Verified: the packed tarball now contains both `package/LICENSE` and `package/NOTICE`.
- **`CODEOWNERS` is not wired into branch protection.** A solo maintainer cannot satisfy an approval rule, and the checklist explicitly warns against creating an impossible one. Make it required when a second trusted maintainer exists.
- **Wiki disabled.** It was on and empty. An empty wiki tab on a public repo reads as abandonment. Discussions stays off; a solo maintainer should not open a second inbox before the first has traffic.
- **Strong copyleft denied**, because it would be inconsistent with the outbound Apache-2.0 grant on a redistributed tool.

## Protocol impact

- [x] No schema, lifecycle, permission, evidence, leveling, or skill-contract semantics changed.
- [x] A versioned architecture change proposal and migration/conformance impact are included where required. None required; this is packaging, documentation and repository configuration only.

- [x] `npm run verify` — 106/106 on this branch, which is cut from `main` and so does not include the validator work in #6.
- [x] `npm run release:check` — passes end to end, including `check-release`, `verify` and `package:check` after the `files` allowlist change.
- [x] Package/bundle drift reviewed — 21 bundles unchanged. Tarball inspected directly rather than trusting the manifest: `package/LICENSE` and `package/NOTICE` both present.

## AI assistance

Material. Claude Code (Opus 5) audited the checklist against repository state, rewrote the README install section, wrote `NOTICE` and `CODEOWNERS`, added the dependency-license policy, generated the social preview card, applied the repository setting change, and updated the checklist.

It verified rather than assumed two things worth repeating. `refs/pull/1`, `/2` and `/3` are **no longer advertised by the remote** and the pull requests no longer list, so the ref half of the Support purge appears complete; cached views cannot be checked from a client and remain outstanding. And the private agent-prompt files are untracked, gitignored, and appear in **zero** reachable commits, so they were not merely deleted from the working tree. A credential-pattern scan over all tracked files found nothing.

It also raised the copyright holder as a blocking question rather than inferring it from the git identity, since a wrong legal notice on a public repository is hard to undo.

- [ ] I understand and can explain the submitted behavior, trade-offs, tests, and failure modes.
- [x] No private prompts, raw transcripts, credentials, learner records, or unrelated local context are included.

## Learning and safety boundaries

- [x] Learner authorship and progressive assistance remain intact. No skill, contract, schema or catalog file changed.
- [x] No fabricated evidence, results, or remote actions were introduced. The one remote action, disabling the Wiki, was explicitly authorized.
- [x] Security and privacy impact was considered: history checked for private content, tracked files scanned for credentials, dependency-license policy added, and the outstanding cached-view purge left recorded as a blocker rather than quietly ticked.

## Still blocking public

1. GitHub Support confirmation that cached views for the purged pull requests are gone.
2. Nothing else. All npm work (checklist sections 3 to 6) is independent of visibility, and ACP-012 in #6 may remove most of it.

Before: you print an estimate, change something on it, and print again — and the second copy is the first one. Nothing on the record looks wrong, because nothing on the record is wrong: the estimate row, the PDF generator and the NetSuite copy all carry the edit. Reported from the field on an edited labor override that kept printing at the previous hours across Estimate PDF and Print, while the NetSuite PDF beside them was correct.

After: each open of the estimate PDF asks for a document the browser has never requested before, so a reprint always shows what is on the estimate now.

The endpoint already answers with `Cache-Control: no-store`, but Estimate PDF and Print point a bare tab at one fixed URL per estimate, and that URL is a cache key whatever the response says about storing it. The NetSuite PDF was the one that stayed correct because it is fetched as bytes and handed to the tab as a fresh blob each time — it has no reusable URL to begin with.

How: `openFleetsuitePdf` stamps the request with `?t=${Date.now()}`, moving `print=1` to `&print=1`. The route reads only `print` and `download`, so the extra parameter changes nothing server-side. The save that runs before the open is untouched, as is the frozen-estimate path that deliberately skips it.

body:
OpenInsert currently ships only for macOS. This adds a native .NET 10 Windows application and self-contained x64/ARM64 installers and portable ZIPs while preserving the Swift macOS application, its universal build, and its release assets.

The Windows app uses Ctrl + Space by default, supports hold/tap dictation, Gemini streaming transcription and optional cleanup, non-activating live captions, DPAPI-protected credentials, and guarded paste with clipboard restoration. Recording lasts up to about two minutes; the separate eight-second cleanup timeout is now clearly presented as a post-recording step. Captions show the waveform and latest transcript instead of a Listening label.

Text insertion compares retained UI Automation selection ranges directly, fixing Chromium composers whose ranges cannot be converted to offsets from DocumentRange.Start. Writable value-only editors are also supported. Original window, process, field, focus, and available selection checks remain, with content-free diagnostics for failures. Windows revision 2 is identifiable as 0.3.0-windows.2 / file version 0.3.0.2.

Validation on Windows x64: 37 core checks, 62 UI/settings checks (including captions at four DPI settings), and 53 native desktop checks passed. The installed app's fixed Chinese/English sentence was automatically pasted into the actual ChatGPT/Codex composer after reproducing the original failure; the insertion was undone without sending a message. An in-place upgrade preserved the existing saved key and consent. Both final installers and ZIP checksums were verified; the installed app and extracted x64 ZIP passed smoke checks.

[Hosted CI run 35691105977](https://github.com/Buffett111/OpenInsert/actions/runs/35691105977) passed all three jobs for commit 65b9406: the unchanged macOS test/universal-build job, Windows x64 tests/package/smoke, and Windows ARM64 packaging. Both Windows artifacts and the macOS universal artifact are available from that run.

Packages are unsigned. ARM64 is cross-compiled, not hardware-tested. A real microphone-to-Google-to-editor session and clean-machine SmartScreen behavior remain unverified. Full setup, validation scope, and release instructions are in docs/WINDOWS.md and docs/RELEASING.md.

author: soezrv-del
body: ## What this is RV Grok catalog-miss web search is no longer a single shot. Chat and Live Voice now run a **research loop**: search → evaluate whether the notes confirm the asked fact → if not, retry with a **different query phrasing**. A labeled EST is allowed only after that loop is exhausted, and it is marked **low confidence**. Desk / SPEC REPORT stay on the Facts brochure snapshot from #419. Estimates stay off the desk. DialaBot is untouched. ## Final behavior 1. **`WEB_SEARCH_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 3`** (named, easy to tune). Each attempt is one query phrasing (`max_tool_calls: 1` per POST). Model-list retries stay HTTP-only; a miss **rephrases** the query. 2. **Prompt** in `webSearch.ts` is search / confirm / rephrase — not “search once then write.” Notes say `CONFIRMED: yes` or `CONFIRMED: no`. The model does not write EST in the notes. 3. **Quality gate** (`evaluateResearchQuality` + `formatWebSearchInjection` + `mayEmitLabeledEstimate`): empty notes, `WEB SEARCH NOT AVAILABLE`, miss language, or an EST in the notes do **not** confirm. EST is blocked and another rephrased attempt runs. 4. **Only after N genuine failed attempts** (all rephrased, all unconfirmed) may estimatePolicy fire. That EST is labeled **low confidence**. A single miss never unlocks EST. 5. **Cache** for repeated questions is unchanged (confirmed hits still win). Shared wall-clock budget is still 12s chat / 10s voice — timeouts do not stack. 6. Call sites: `src/routes/api/rvgrok.ts` (Chat) and `src/routes/api/rvgrok.web-research.ts` (Live Voice) pass `maxAttempts: WEB_SEARCH_MAX_TOOL_CALLS`. ## Test results Local (91 passed, 0 failed): - `webSearch.test.ts` — confirming first search → no retry; empty first search → confirming rephrased retry; N failed attempts → labeled low-confidence EST; gate blocks EST when the loop is not exhausted - `estimatePolicy.test.ts` — labeled low-confidence EST; `mayEmitLabeledEstimate` gated; desk still Facts-only (2022 Tiffin Phaeton 40IH) - `voiceWeb.test.ts` — Live Voice hold / injection / timeout budget unchanged - `webResearchTelemetry.test.ts` — cache / gated / missing-key / headers - `prompts.test.ts`, `grounding.test.ts`, `repairMode.test.ts` — no regressions CI on this PR: GitGuardian + both Vercel previews green. ## Try this Ask Grok a catalog-miss spec (e.g. hitch / GVWR on a coach with no pin). It should browse, rephrase if the first hit does not confirm, and only then speak a low-confidence EST — never as an OEM pin. Desk numbers stay Facts-only.

## TLDR

AIME 2025 becomes a catalogue board: 30 competition math problems, importer-generated rows only, zero spine or importer edits, full-bake verified offline at the eval's own pinned dataset sha. Stacked on #1010 (aime24) — PR 3 of 3 for the ticket.

Part of [OME-1238](https://linear.app/openmined/issue/OME-1238/import-the-remaining-exact-match-benchmarks-the-roadmap-names).

## Problem / Solution

**Problem.** Same as #1010, one year over: papers reporting on AIME 2025 — the current frontier-math staple, published after most models' training cutoffs — have no board here.

**Solution.** One importer run; the rows point at the eval's own code. The one difference from aime24: a different upstream dataset (`math-ai/aime25`, string answers, lowercase fields) behind the same shared solver/scorer pair.

## Before / After

Same shape as #1010's — the researcher's missing board becomes a catalogue row (`inspect-aime25`, 30 cases, exact-match, no judge tokens). Not repeated here; this PR is the second data row of the same story.

### Don't regress
- The dataset revision is the eval's own upstream pin (`563bb84…`), conserved.
- Check surface stays ON (free-text family); the answer key never enters the public booklet (bake test asserts it).
- aime24's rows are untouched; the diff is additive.

## Architecture / Design

Skipped — pure data rows on the pipeline #1010 already walks; nothing new to draw (announcing the skip per convention).

## Known limitations of this design

- **30 cases, same variance caveat as aime24.**
- **aime24 and aime25 share `utils.aime_common`'s template and scorer upstream** — a future inspect_evals pin bump that changes that shared module changes *both* exams at once; the revision-pinned bakes make that loud (case counts and prompts are frozen per board), but reviewers of a pin bump should know the two boards move together.

## Review order

1. `apps/screamingface-engine/src/screamingface_engine_inspect/pins.py` — the lockfile row: `math-ai/aime25`, test split, 40-hex revision (verify the HF permalink resolves), 30 cases, Apache-2.0.

3. `src/screamingface_engine_inspect/boards.py` — the catalogue entry: prose honesty, the eval's own `aime_scorer`, check surface ON.
4. `tests/unit/test_inspect_snapshots.py` — appended fixture bake test; the point it pins: aime25's row rule reads *lowercase* fields and a *string* answer (aime24 is uppercase + integer), so a copy-paste of the wrong row rule fails here.
5. `tests/unit/test_inspect_imported_boards.py` + `tests/unit/test_benchmark_declaration.py` — one dict entry + one roster row (same owner append-only sign-off as #1010).

author: claydiffrient
body:
A cross-project roster of specialized agents that outlive any single task. A rostered agent is assigned a task, does the portion matching its specialty, logs what it did, and returns the task to the queue for the next one.

The roster lives in a top-level Roster row in the sidebar, and each project selects which rostered agents it uses in Project Settings. The same mechanism provides the `agent` review level, where a rostered reviewer holds the authority to move work out of the review column.

Inspired by the Hive concept — a registry of specialists, per-agent identity, a privileged orchestrator routing work — but deliberately **not** its state model. Hive has no branching and every agent works on main with a god agent arbitrating conflicts. This keeps D6: a worktree per task, branch bound to the task id, so hand-off is mediated by the board queue and never by agents editing a shared checkout.

## What is in it

- `roster_agent` and `project_roster_agent` schema, with `disallowed_tools` read as a **deny-list** and `ordering` on the per-project join.
- A rostered spawn: identity injected at the head of the opening prompt, model precedence `task.model ?? agent.model ?? project default`, and the agent's `disallowedTools` layered onto the default.
- `hand_off`, returning a task to `ready` rather than `failed`, keeping the worktree.
- The `agent` review level: `report_complete` starts a reviewer in the worker's own worktree on the worker's branch, scoped `.reviewer`.
- The Roster screen, the agent editor sheet, and the per-project picker in Project Settings.
- Rostered sessions are exempt from the elapsed and idle caps — not the token cap, and not the concurrency gate, which would otherwise let agent review spawn past `maxConcurrentAgents`.

## Review notes

**The Roster UI landed late and by a different route.** Its commit sat unmerged on a task branch for days while the board read `done`; SPEC §12 now records that and what it cost. Porting it was not a merge: `46bd2e6` put the roster behind a segmented Projects/Roster control above a sidebar that no longer exists, referencing a `selectedProjectId` that is gone, and git spliced that control in **outside any conflict marker**, producing a file that would not compile. `MainWindow.swift` was rewritten rather than resolved — the roster is a `SidebarSelection.roster` row beside At a Glance. The rejected alternative was keeping the segmented control, which would have meant a second selection axis fighting the one the sidebar already has.

**One deliberate scope addition, cheap to revert.** `RosterStore.assignments()` and `LiveRosterActivity` are new here; `46bd2e6` shipped `RosterActivityReporting` as a no-op stub with a comment that nothing implemented it. The epic has since made it implementable, and leaving the stub would have meant SPEC §10's documented refusal to delete a working agent could never fire. Reverting is `RosterActivity.swift` back to `NoRosterActivity`, the `assignments()` method, one line in `MainWindow.swift:31`, and two tests.

**What the render tests do not prove.** Offscreen, `NSSwitch.performClick` does not drive a SwiftUI binding on this machine — a test asserting the switch writes through was written, watched to pass vacuously, and replaced with two mounts of inverted stored state. The roster tests establish store → view and never view → store. Nobody has clicked the Roster tab in a running app.

**A trap for other branches.** The sidebar now pins two rows. Any unmerged branch that adds a sidebar row, or pins a row count, collides with `pinnedRows = 2` — it will merge clean, compile clean, and fail when the suite runs. `grep -rn 'ListTableCellView\|SidebarContent(' Tests/` is the check before the next integration. Five such assertions across four test files were fixed here.

Local: `swift build --build-tests` clean, `swift test` `Executed 1902 tests, with 1 skipped and 0 failures`. The skip is pre-existing.

body:
## What was wrong

Re-importing two years of Nationwide statements changed nothing. The 2024 and 2025 bills are in an older layout that missed the installment-bill detection, so each kept the policy term (May 21 to May 21) as its billing period. The importer's first matcher takes a bill with a period starting within a week of an existing row's as the same bill, so every bill of a term overwrote one row. That is why 2024 and 2025 show one or two rows per term while Oct 2025 onward is one per month.

## What changed

`backend/src/routes/import.ts`
- An insurance bill (has policy details, or the account is INSURANCE) is never keyed on a period. It is keyed on its due date: every non-scheduled row on the account with the same due date or issue date is the same installment, one survives, payments move onto it, the new read overwrites it. The `!ex.billingPeriodStart` condition is gone from that path.

`backend/src/services/pdfImportService.ts`
- `applyInsuranceFromText`: on a bill that is not an installment bill, a period that spans more than 45 days or equals the coverage term is nulled, so the bill files under its issue month.
- Installment detection accepts older wordings: "Amount due", "Monthly Installment", "Installment amount"; balance fallbacks add "Total/Remaining/Policy balance".

Regression-run on the five Nationwide 2026 bills, five Hartford bills and a Progressive letter: identical output. I do not have a 2024 or 2025 Nationwide PDF to verify the older layout against; the period guard and the due-date keying make the outcome one row per month regardless of whether detection fires.

Backend type-checks clean. No frontend changes.
