author: claydiffrient
body:
`report_complete` filed two identical reports for 26% of completing sessions — 64 duplicate groups out of 249 on the live board today, up from 13% five days ago.

## Cause: a transport retry, not a double call

Reading each worker's own transcript against the report rows, all 183 sessions that ever filed a `complete` report split with no overlap:

- **118 sessions** — one `tool_use` block, one `tool_result` → one row.
- **64 sessions** — one `tool_use` block, **zero** `tool_result` → **two rows**.
- **1 session** — two `tool_use` blocks with two distinct bodies. The model genuinely called it twice; a different thing.

Every duplicating session emitted exactly one `tool_use`, so the model called the tool once. The duplicate is perfectly predicted by the missing response.

`WorkerToolHandler.call` awaits `events.workerCompleted`, which runs `claude stop` on the worker's own session, **before** returning the `ToolResult`. It kills the HTTP client waiting on that response. Sometimes the response wins the race; sometimes the kill does and the client resends.

## What the second call was doing

All of it, unguarded: `ReportStore.insert`, `TaskStore.move` back to `review`, `SessionStore.setState(.completed, endedAt:)`, `FileLockStore.releaseAll`, and under `afterEpicMerge` a second `EpicStore.setState(.done)` and `ArchiveSweep.archiveEpic`, then `runtime.stop` again. A resend could drag an already-accepted task out of `done` and back into `review`.

## The fix

`Board.complete` reads `ReportStore.completion(db, taskId:sessionId:)` inside its own write transaction and, if a report is already there, returns it with `wasAlreadyComplete = true` having touched nothing. Transactional rather than a check in the tool handler, so two concurrent resends cannot both pass it. `WorkerToolHandler` skips `workerCompleted` and `reportQueued` on a resend and returns the first report's id. Keyed on `(session_id, task_id)`, so a second attempt's worker still files its own report. Nothing is deduplicated at read time.

Both new tests are mutation-checked: with the guard deleted, they fail 11 assertions, including `("review") is not equal to ("done") - the retry moved a task it should not have touched`.

## Also fixed, one line in the same function

The success text said "The task is now in Review" even when the task landed in `done`. `Board.TaskCompletion` now carries the column the task actually reached, so it reads "in Done" under `afterEpicMerge`. SPEC §6's worker-scope row is updated for both the column and the idempotency. The tool *descriptor* still carries the same inaccuracy — deliberately left, as a separate string with its own audience.

## What this does not do

The retry still happens. This makes it harmless; it does not stop the client resending, and the worker still ends its life never told its report landed. The root-cause fix — answer first, stop after — is filed separately, because detaching the stop makes its ordering unobservable to the test that asserts the event sequence.

The scope of the retry is bounded, not general: a response is only lost for a tool that stops its own caller before answering. That is `report_complete` and `acknowledge_shutdown`, and the latter is already safe because `shutdown_delivery` has an `(order_id, session_id)` primary key.

The 64 existing duplicate pairs on the live board are untouched; this prevents new ones.

Local: `swift build` clean, `swift test` `Executed 1748 tests, with 1 skipped and 0 failures`.

author: kusui26
body:
> **問い: 人が実際のブラウザで、受付から退席まで通せるか。**

[Phase 2 プラン](docs/260921_plan_Phase2.md) の PR 6。React + Vite の SPA を `apps/web` に置き、`apps/server` が**同じ入口から**配ります。**成果物は 1 つのコンテナのまま**です（[ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-single-container-sqlite.md)）。

## 影響範囲

**ドメインロジック（`packages/core`）・スキーマ・運用パラメータの既定値は触っていません。** 実証実験中の挙動は変わりません。マイグレーションもありません。

変えたのは 4 つです。

| | 何を | 実証実験への影響 |
|---|---|---|
| 新規 | `apps/web`（画面 3 面） | **人が初めて触れるものができた** |
| 新規 | `apps/server/src/web.ts`・`app.ts`（静的配信と道の割り当て） | サーバが `/api/` 以外を画面に落とす |
| 変更 | `routes/index.ts` の守りを `/api/*` に限定 | API の返しは変わらない（テストで固定） |
| 変更 | `Dockerfile` が画面も組み立てる | イメージに `/app/web` が増える |

## ビューは状態を描くだけ（CLAUDE.md 3.1）

- **押せる操作はサーバが返す。** 画面は `actions` を並べるだけで、足しも引きもしません。何が押せるかは `routes/views.ts` が `dispatch` を空打ちして `core` に聞いています
- **期限の判定を書いていない。** サーバは絶対時刻の期限とサーバ時刻を返し、画面は残りを数えて出すだけ。**切れたときに何が起きるかは `tick` が決めます**
- **権限の判定を書いていない**（[ADR-0014](docs/adr/0014-permissions-in-core.md)）
- `pnpm check:arch` に「画面が状態を描くだけである」検査を足し、CI で落とします

## 静的配信（[ADR-0016](docs/adr/0016-serving-the-app.md)）

同じ入口に画面と API を載せると、**道ごとに 3 つを分ける**必要がありました。

| | API（`/api/...`） | 画面 |
|---|---|---|
| CSP | `default-src 'none'` | 自分の資材だけ（外部の配信網も解析も 0） |
| 取りこぼし | 契約どおりの JSON の断り | `Accept: text/html` のときだけ 1 枚目 |
| 置いてよい期間 | —— | 指紋つきは 1 年、名前が固定のものは毎回確認 |

**`/healthz` は画面より先に載せます。** あとに置くと、ブラウザから開いたとき（`Accept: text/html`）に健康の答えではなく画面が返り、**監視の目が塞がれていることに誰も気づけません。** この順序をテストで固定するため、道の割り当てを `src/app.ts` に切り出しました（`main.ts` は読み込んだだけで記録を開くので、テストから組み立て直せないため）。

## 実装中に見つけて直したこと

| | 何が起きるところだったか |
|---|---|
| `serveStatic` の `onFound` でヘッダが乗らない | 返しを組み立て**終えてから**呼ばれる仕様（`@hono/node-server` 1.19）。文書どおりに書いたら Cache-Control が全部 `null` だった。テストで実証し、後ろから付ける形に |
| 消えた資材に HTML を返す | 配り直し後、古い端末が消えた `/assets/index-<古い指紋>.js` を取りに来る。HTML を返すと「予期しない `<`」で止まり、**原因の見当がつかない壊れ方**をする |
| lint が `.tsx` を 1 行も見ていない | `files: ['**/*.ts']` のみ。画面のコードは検査ゼロだった |
| `check:links` がコードのコメントを見ていない | コード側に 40 本のリンクがあり、**この PR で書いた壊れたリンクが 1 本すり抜けた** |

いずれも**実装をわざと壊して**検査が落ちることを確認しています（サーバ 6 通り・画面 5 通り）。

## テスト（22 + 14 件）

- **7.3 の 8 状態すべて**が、色だけでなく文字で読めること
- **サーバが返した操作だけ**が出ること。「人数を変える」が取り消しにならないこと
- **時計を偽装**して、進んだ端末にも遅れた端末にも引きずられないこと。負の残り時間を出さないこと
- CSP が道ごとに別であること、`/healthz` が画面に飲まれないこと、消えた資材が 404 であること

`infra/smoke.sh` に、コンテナから画面が配られることの確認を 5 項目足しました。

## 計画書との食い違い（確認済み）

**shadcn/ui を入れませんでした**（[ADR-0017](docs/adr/0017-no-component-library-yet.md)）。利用者の 3 画面に要る部品はボタンとステッパーの 2 つだけで、そのために依存を 4 つ増やす（Radix・cva・clsx・tailwind-merge）より、素の `<button>`・`<output>` のほうが支援技術との相性がよいためです。**PR 13・14 で改めて判断します。** Phase 2 プランの PR 6 を「Tailwind」に修正しました。

あわせて、**画面の部品（`.tsx`）の行数の上限を 40 行**にしました（CLAUDE.md 4 章）。20 行は論理の量を測る目安で、JSX は論理ではなく組み立てです。実際、20 行に寄せようとして部品を割ったら、props の型注釈が数えられて**警告が 5 件から 7 件に増えました。** やるべき分割（重複の共通化・props の名前付き `interface` 化・送信処理の hook 化）はやり切ってあります。

## 品質ゲート

```
pnpm verify   lint / typecheck / test / check:arch / check:links
```

**すべて成功。エラー 0・警告 0・テスト 1949 件。**

**未確認が 1 つあります。** `docker build` は、手元の Docker デーモンが Docker Hub に届かず（ホストの curl は通るのにデーモンが `load metadata` で停止）**ローカルで通せていません。** 代わりに**コンテナと同じ構成**（`WEB_DIR` を `dist` の複製に向けてサーバを起動）で受付 → `CALLED`・席 T-01 まで通しで確認し、画面・SPA フォールバック・ETag の 304・CSP の分離・PWA の資材をすべて確かめました。Dockerfile 側の前提（`--frozen-lockfile` の整合・filter 名・`.dockerignore`・COPY 元）も個別に確認済みです。**イメージそのものは CI のコンテナジョブで検証されます。**

## 補足

- 画面のバンドルは 130 kB（gzip）。**`core` のドメイン実装は完全に落ちています**（中身は React・Router・Zod のみ）
- PWA のアイコンは `tools/make-icons.mjs` が生成します（画像の変換器を入れずに PNG を直に組み立て）。iOS の「ホーム画面に追加」向けに `apple-touch-icon` も置きました（6.6）
- 今後の宿題: 施設の `maxPartySize` を画面へ渡していないため、人数の幅は画面側の定数（10）です。本当の上限は `core` が判断するので先回りして断ることはありませんが、契約に足すなら PR 13・14 の設定画面と合わせるのが自然です

- `verify-interface42` PASS, including exact-head attack plus unit, MorphTile integration, and Assembly receiver replay.

body:
# Socle classements de joueurs (top records) — `5000` lu et borné à 8 octets, réponse `5001` à vide (« `TM_CS/SC_RANKING_TOP_RECORD` »)

Branche `hermes/packet-socle-classements` → `master`. Base : `master` = `ec76b218cd0bd7c6498d725f253abb8b431f0cd6`.
Tête publiée : `b50300822aa76cdc06cc42fb7ddf3338ed229ba3`. Fiche de référence : `docs/packet-specs/socle-classements.md`.

| Commit | Contenu |
|---|---|
| `5927a10` | `Add packet spec for the ranking top-record socle (5000/5001)` — la fiche (605 lignes, aucun fichier de code) |
| `be18400` | `Route the ranking top-record request and answer it empty` — code + tests |
| `b503008` | `Record the K1 decisions in the ranking socle sheet` — §9 : décisions prises là où la fiche laissait un choix, et état livré des points `A VERIFIER` |

---

## 1. Ce que fait le changement

Le client Epic 7.3 envoie `TM_CS_RANKING_TOP_RECORD` (`5000`, 8 octets fixes) depuis la commande UI enregistrée sous le nom `Ranking_Top_Record` (fenêtre `window_donation_ranking.nui`) et attend **une seule** réponse `TM_SC_RANKING_TOP_RECORD` (`5001`), sans `TS_SC_RESULT` et sans état d'attente de son côté (fiche §5.7). Jusqu'ici cet id tombait dans le `throw new Exception("Unknown Packet Type")` de `GameClient` (`GameClient.cs:846`). La branche livre le **socle K1** : le paquet est reçu et traité proprement, la réponse est écrite et bornée, aucune donnée de classement n'existe encore côté serveur.

| Fichier | Ce qu'il apporte |
|---|---|
| `Game/Network/Packets/Enums/GamePackets.cs:99-100` | `TM_CS_RANKING_TOP_RECORD = 5000`, `TM_SC_RANKING_TOP_RECORD = 5001` (aucune collision : les deux valeurs sont libres sur `master`) |
| `Game/Network/Packets/Game/GameActionPackets.cs:25` et `:262-272` | `RankingTopRecordRequest(sbyte RankingType)` et `TryReadRankingTopRecord` : `Length` **exactement 8** exigée, `ranking_type` lu en `sbyte` à l'offset 7. author: luisinho-cyber
body:
## Resumo

`packages/whatsapp` (interface + cliente da Meta com retry e limite por número) e `apps/worker` (laço de 30 s sobre `claim_due_actions`, backoff, varredor de ações presas). Toda mensagem ativa passa por um porteiro único de consentimento. Migração `0004` com a função `security definer` que desprende ações abandonadas. 17 testes novos, 156 no total.

⚠️ **Mexe em migração e função `security definer`** — pela regra combinada, não mesclo sem sua conferência.

## O porteiro de consentimento

`enviarAtivo` é o **único** caminho por onde sai mensagem por iniciativa do sistema. Sem `whatsapp_consent_at`, a mensagem não sai e a recepção recebe alerta para falar por outro canal. Um lugar só de propósito: se cada chamada decidisse sozinha, bastaria um esquecimento para a clínica mandar mensagem sem consentimento.

Responder a quem escreveu não passa por aqui — ali quem iniciou foi o paciente, dentro da janela de 24 h.

## Silêncio não libera horário

`marcar_risco` muda para `em_risco` e alerta a recepção. O horário **continua reservado**. O teste vai além de checar o status: tenta marcar outro paciente no mesmo horário e exige o erro `23P01` da constraint. Só libera quem apertou "não vou".

## Falha e backoff

| Situação | O que acontece |
| --- | --- |
| Falha temporária (429, 5xx, rede) | volta a `pendente` com 1, 5, 15 min |
| 4ª falha | `erro` + alerta **urgente** |
| Recusa definitiva (template errado, sem consentimento) | `erro` na hora, sem repetir |

Repetir um 400 gasta o limite do número da clínica e não conserta nada.

## Migração 0004 — e o bug que ela corrige

`claim_due_actions` marca a ação como `executando` antes de executar. Se o worker morre no meio, ninguém desmarca: **aquela confirmação nunca mais sai e o paciente não é avisado**.

Escrevi o varredor primeiro como `update` direto. **O teste falhou e mostrou por quê:** ele roda sem clínica na transação (não sabe de antemão quais clínicas têm ação presa), e a RLS de `scheduled_actions` bloqueia — rodava sem erro e devolvia zero.

`app.requeue_stuck_actions` é `security definer` pelo mesmo motivo do `claim_due_actions`, e **devolve só a contagem**: nenhuma linha de nenhuma clínica atravessa a fronteira. Há teste lendo do catálogo (`prosecdef`, retorno `integer`, `search_path` fixo, `execute` revogado de `public`) e um que prova a necessidade: update direto alcança **0** linhas, pela função alcança **1**.

## Fila do botão separada

Resposta de botão tem payload fixo e efeito decidido por `packages/core` (`interpretarResposta` → `efeitoDaResposta`). Vai para a fila `botao`, não para a `conversa` — senão o agente de IA da Fase 4 tentaria interpretar texto onde não há texto. Os payloads vêm de `PAYLOAD_BOTOES`; redigitá-los faria o envio e a interpretação divergirem.

## Testes com cliente falso (17 novos)

Os três obrigatórios — **confirmou** (vira `confirmado`), **cancelou** (libera, ranqueia a fila, envia oferta e agenda a expiração), **silêncio** (`em_risco`, horário intocado) — mais: bloqueio por consentimento sem envio; backoff com `due_at` no futuro; 4ª falha vira erro com alerta; recusa definitiva não repete; "quer remarcar" não libera o horário; texto livre não é tratado aqui; varredor devolve o preso e ignora o recente; webhook manda botão para a fila certa.

## Saída local

```
npm run typecheck  → exit 0
npm run lint       → exit 0
npm test           → 14 arquivos, 156 testes, exit 0
```

## Fora do escopo

O envio real depende de templates aprovados na Meta e do Embedded Signup — o cliente está pronto, mas nenhuma mensagem sai até haver número e template de verdade configurados.

author: neuromechanist
body:
Corrects a comment in `workers/osa-worker/wrangler.toml` that I introduced in #438 and that the first deploy after that merge proved false.

## What it said

The Trap 2 note concluded that zone access was not a concern here, on the reasoning that `secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` already provisions custom domains on `osc.earth` for the status and branch deployments.

## What is actually true

That reasoning does not transfer. Pages custom domains, zone DNS records and `Zone:Workers Routes:Edit` are three separate grants, and the token holds the first two but not the third.

[Run 35687023452](https://github.com/OpenScience-Collective/osa/actions/runs/35687023452), the first `Sync Worker CORS` after #438 merged:

```
Trigger configuration for "osa-worker-dev" was only partially updated:
  Routes:
    - A request to the Cloudflare API (.../workers/scripts/osa-worker-dev/routes) failed.
      - No access to the specified resource.
```

Two details worth recording, both non-obvious:

- The script upload succeeds, so the code goes live and only route reconciliation fails. The merged host-gating fix from #438 is verifiably running right now despite the red job.
- Pre-registering a route by hand does **not** make the job pass. Wrangler fails reconciling a route that already matches, which is why dev still fails even though `develop-widget.osc.earth/osa` works.

## This is documentation only

No behavior changes. The underlying permission gap is tracked as #439 and needs a token change, which is not something a pull request can carry.

Closes nothing. Related: #437, #438, #439.

author: dmnyc
body:
Fixes #346. **Stacked on #354** (→ #353 → #352 → #351 → #341) — the diff shown here is just this fix.

HTML5 drag-and-drop never fires on touch, so a touchscreen had no way to reorder attachments and a keyboard had none either. The steppers are the cheapest reorder that always works: small ◀/▶ buttons on each thumbnail's bottom corners (buttons — reachable by touch and Tab), splicing the same array the drag does, so everything downstream is identical either gesture. The ends hide their arrow rather than disabling it; a new `arrow-right` icon mirrors the existing left one rather than rotating it (the join reads wrong at 14px).

The steppers flush the ALT row before splicing (the drag's rule) and square with the remove disc in Werkstätte, whose circular-things exception list now includes them.

body:
## Manual hook configuration

The `Manual Claude Code Hook Configuration` section was a hand-copied duplicate of
`hooks/hooks.json`, 60 of the README's 259 lines.

It had already rotted. When #31 removed the `Notification` hook, this copy kept it, so
anyone following those instructions installed a hook that defeats the grace period.
That was only caught during the #28 rebase. It would have drifted again.

It now points at the file:

> Copy the `hooks` object out of `hooks/hooks.json` into your agent's hook
> configuration, and replace `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` with the path to your checkout.

`hooks/hooks.json` is the same file the plugin installs and is already covered by
`test/plugin-manifests.test.js`, so it cannot drift. It is also agent-neutral, which
matters now that more agents are supported than can each get their own JSON dump.

It also sat between the config table and the native backend notes, splitting the
Configuration section in half. It moves to a new `Advanced Installation` section near
the bottom, together with the Codex manual instructions that pointed at it. Both manual
paths now live in one place, and the Installation section stays short.

## Table of contents

Generated between `<!-- toc -->` markers by `npm run toc`, covering `##` and `###`
headings.

`test/readme-toc.test.js` keeps it honest with four checks:

- the committed table of contents matches the headings, with a failure that names
  `npm run toc`
- `slugify` matches how GitHub builds anchors, including the leading hyphen an emoji
  heading produces (`## 🎯 Installation` anchors to `#-installation`)
- headings are read outside fenced code blocks, since the bash examples contain lines
  starting with `#`
- every in-page link, inside the table of contents and outside it, points at a real
  heading

I verified the staleness check actually fails by renaming a heading and watching it
trip. It then caught the heading rename in the second commit for real, before I
regenerated.

## `Run without Claude Code` rewritten

That heading claimed one thing and the example did another: it ran `claude -p`. The
prose was Claude-specific too ("Claude can keep working while you sip coffee"), and it
said a session auto-cleans "after 15 minutes" without mentioning that `uncaffeinate`
now holds the lock for a grace period first.

It is now `Using the CLI directly`, framed as what it actually is: the hooks only run
these commands, so you can run them yourself for any long job nothing else covers, such
as a build, a migration, or an agent not listed above. The example uses a placeholder
script instead of one agent's CLI, and the timing text matches the current settings.

## Notes

- The README drops from 259 to 233 lines while gaining a 14-line table of contents, so
  the body is about 40 lines shorter.
- Lint now covers `scripts/`.
- `AGENTS.md` records the new command and both invariants.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` clean.
- 101 tests pass across every suite except `test/pid.test.js`, which fails with
  `spawn EPERM` in a sandbox. CI proved that suite green on #28 with 117/117.
- `npm run toc` is idempotent on the committed file.

The eight NOSTOS islands previously relied on sparse props and repeated ruins. This candidate gives each island an authored spatial structure while preserving all story IDs, dialogue, NPCs, memories and act ordering.

Circe and Cyclops gain inhabitable galleries and cave facilities. The remaining six add Ithaca's asymmetric courtyard house, the lotus orchard shelters and descending irrigation channel, continuous Siren rock strata and moored wrecks, Calypso's domestic and boatbuilding spaces, and restrained tidal/ritual terrain for the prologue and Nekyia. Shared changes add wall-segment collision, matching walk surfaces, sheltered weather, mobile controls, quality tiers and adaptive resolution.

The implementation includes the fine-grained R2 spec, a 34-item implementation matrix, 24 fixed-camera before/after pairs and six supplemental spatial views. Asset IDs, the active context, provenance and iteration records are updated. The design document's UTF-8 response is also fixed.

Validation: 181 unit tests, TypeScript, production and asset-workbench builds, library/context/asset audits; five browser checks covering the eight-act touch journey, ending/restart, three complete island-switch cycles, multi-touch/orientation and quality rendering. Warm geometry and texture counts remain stable. Reproduction commands and logs are in `games/nostos/runs/run-20260922-eight-islands-r2/verification.json`.

This is a review candidate. Human visual acceptance and iPhone 13 Safari / Pixel 6 Chrome sustained 15-minute performance remain unverified. Desktop samples are diagnostic evidence only. This PR does not merge or deploy to Pages.

body:
Fixes: https://github.com/emqx/emqx/issues/19114
Release version: 6.0.4, 6.1.5, 6.2.4, 6.3.2, 7.0.0
Introduced in: pre-5.8

## Summary

Test-only fix for two flaky cases in `emqx_utils_stream_tests`: `foreach_test/0` and `mqueue_test/0`.

Both asserted the **entire mailbox** of the EUnit process:

```erlang
?assertEqual([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], emqx_utils_stream:consume(emqx_utils_stream:mqueue(100)))
```

EUnit runs all plain test cases of a single run in the same process, so any asynchronous message left behind
by an earlier test case (in CI an `{ssl_closed, _}`) was consumed by `emqx_utils_stream:mqueue/1` and failed
the assertion although the stream functions behaved correctly.

Each case now tags the messages it sends with its own reference and collects only the messages carrying that
tag, so unrelated messages cannot fail it. The expected values and their order are unchanged: a missing
message, a duplicate, a message with an unexpected payload and a wrong order still fail the assertion.

Two new cases, `foreach_with_unrelated_messages_test/0` and `mqueue_with_unrelated_messages_test/0`, put an
unrelated message of each shape (a 2-tuple such as `{ssl_closed, Ref}`, and a non-2-tuple such as `'DOWN'`)
into the mailbox before it is read, so that their presence while the messages are collected is guaranteed;
they fail if the filtering is removed.

No production code changed, and there is no user-visible change, so no changelog entry is needed.

author: minimapletinytools
body:
Two commits against the notes added in `4ffe3fec`. Both are green on `pytest tests/` (1988 passed), `npx jest` (1198 passed) and `ty check` (48 diagnostics, unchanged).

## `220af7c9` — cheap wins, and three notes that were already done

Mechanical renames the notes asked for: `BoundingBox` → `AxisAlignedBoundingBox`, `_drop_real_hits_off_boundary` → `_drop_real_hits_if_not_on_boundary`, `LocatedGeometry` → `LocatedFeatureGeometry`, `_stations` → `_stations_global`, `Drawing.id_of` → `get_viewport_id`, and a `ViewportList` alias.

Three notes came off because the code already does what they ask:

- **`Measure` identity already carries the kind** — verified: a horizontal and a vertical between one pair have different identities. The paragraph explaining what that costs the editing flow had gone missing; it is back.
- **Anchors are already canonicalised** in `__post_init__`. Narrowed to what is actually open: whether to hoist it into a `CanonicalFeaturePathPair`.
- **`_drop_duplicate_derived` is correct, but not for the reason the note guessed.** Declared features do *not* come first — `_sort_feature_hits` ranks specificity above declaredness on purpose, so a derived EDGE sorts ahead of the declared FACE it came from. What saves it is narrower: `_names_same_geometry` only matches same-kind pairs, and within one kind specificity ties, so declaredness decides. Written down, with the suggested assert checking the precondition that actually matters.

Two renames deliberately **not** done, with reasons in the commit message: `locate` → `locate_simple_unbounded` (65 call sites, 20 definitions, and the name wants settling first), and the loft's `start_distance`/`end_distance` repo-wide (those names are declared independently on five primitives).

## `b247363f` — refuse a twisted loft

A `ConvexPolygonSimpleLoft` side joins two profile edges with straight lines, so it is a quadrilateral in space — planar only when its four corners are coplanar. The class documented twisting as allowed-but-undefined and paid for it: `locate()` declined for **every** side whatever its shape, so a tapered cheek could not be measured to at all.

`is_valid` now refuses it, via `_sides_are_planar`, measured against each side's own size so it means the same thing on a 2mm relief pocket and a 2m post.

**Audited before changing anything**, since this can only take things away. Hooking `is_valid` across the whole suite: 12 lofts get built, 2 have non-planar sides, and both are in tests that already assert `is_valid()` is `False` for other reasons. Every real loft — the six that come through meshing — is planar to exactly `0.0`. A per-axis taper stays valid, and so does one that leans the top profile sideways; both have tests.

The payoff: a side now locates to a `Plane`, built from three of its corners and verified against all four.

The test that pinned the old behaviour is updated rather than deleted — its loft is a pure taper, exactly the case that should locate now — and it gained a check that the plane actually contains the side's corners, which "returns None" never had to make.

`get_outward_normal` keeps its parametric derivatives. They are correct for a plane, just more work than one needs, and this feeds picking and CSG containment — there is a note rather than a blind change.

Also renames the loft's own `start_distance`/`end_distance` to `bottom_points_z_pos`/`top_points_z_pos`, on the loft only. This reached `blueprint.py`, which no test covers — it would have broken on the next OCP export.

author: ktwu01
body:
## What was happening

The daily radar run has failed since 2026-09-21 with:

```
RuntimeError: Refusing to publish templated descriptions: 16 records share the
summary 'this deposit serves as a long-term archive for the unprocessed raw data
behind the gujrolls2019 table...'
```

Zenodo mints a separate record, concept and DOI for every file an uploader archives. One depositor is archiving a dataset one file per record (`gujrolls2019-35` through `gujrolls2019-100`, 74 and counting, from an account with 1,827 deposits). They share a single description between them.

Nothing in `deduplicate` joins those records, because the titles, DOIs and URLs it keys on are all distinct. So they reached `published` as 16 separate findings, and `assert_no_boilerplate_summaries` correctly read one description repeated across 16 records as templated text.

The series is still growing, so every run keeps failing. It held 59 records at the start of this investigation and 74 by the end.

## The change

`collapse_batch_deposits` keeps the earliest deposit of each batch, keying a batch on one creator list plus one description. Both halves are required:

- a shared description alone would merge two groups that describe their work in the same words
- a shared creator list alone would merge a lab's genuinely separate deposits

A record that published no description is never batched, since absent text is not evidence that two records hold the same archive.

The surviving record carries a rationale line naming how many files it stands for, so the collapsed count is explained where a reader sees it.

## Trade-offs not visible in the diff

The survivor keeps its own download and view counts instead of absorbing its siblings'. Each record was scored on its own before this collapsed them, so summing would report one file's adoption as the whole archive's and score it higher than the pre-collapse feed ever did.

Choosing the earliest deposit rather than the newest keeps the survivor stable when the depositor uploads another file the next day.

## Verification

Against the live Zenodo API with this repo's six configured searches:

```
before: 20 records share one description -> RuntimeError
after:  21 collapsed to 1, guard green
        survivor 22882561 gujrolls2019-100
        rationale: One of 21 files this depositor archived together under one description
```

Full CI sequence run in a clean `--detach` worktree with submodules initialized.

Closes #889.

## What changed

Audit finding [#889](https://github.com/phynics/axoloty/issues/889) reported three interfaces that were set by file layout rather than by decision. This narrows each to its intended surface without changing wire behavior or public writer operations.

- **A1 `WireWriter` split primitives.** The `writeByte`, `writeBytes`, `writeByteSlice`, and `advancePosition` helpers were module-visible only because `WireWriter+Encoding.swift` sat in a separate file. The encoding extension is now colocated in `WireWriter.swift`, so those helpers are `private`. `@inline(__always)` and the no-allocation contract are unchanged, and every public writer operation is preserved.
- **A2 `ObjectEditor` stored state.** The eight stored properties and `init(source:)` were `@usableFromInline` only because `BoundedDynamicObject` reads them from the same file. They are now `fileprivate`, and `EditOperation` is file-scoped.

author: claude[bot]
body:
**Before:** CI went red four times in three days, each time with a different set of suites failing. Nothing in the repository said this happens, so each occurrence cost a fresh diagnosis — and the safe-looking reflex, re-running until it goes green, is indistinguishable from hiding a regression.

**After:** it is written down, with the evidence, as `KI-005` in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`.

**How:** one entry. Documentation only; no code, no test, no threshold touched.

### The evidence

| Run | Head | Failing suites | Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 212 | `3d070a8` on `main` | `test:freshness-boundary` | 98/99 |
| 256 | `ee4d404` on `main` | `test:ledger-auth` | 101/102 |
| 258 | `83abd54` on `chore/bump-0.1.2` | `test:sidecar-pe` | 101/102 |
| 262 | `b2c01c2`, same branch | `test:ledger-auth`, `test:sidecar-pe` | 100/102 |

The load-bearing fact is that both `main` failures ran a tree **byte-identical** to one that had already passed green on the pull request branch:

```
3d070a8^{tree} == fc836a21^{tree} == 1369cc5   (run 211 green, run 212 red, five minutes apart)
ee4d404^{tree} == ce6234f^{tree} == 2e77ca2   (run 255 green, run 256 red)
```

Same tree, one green and one red. The difference is not in the tree. Every suite in that table starts a real sidecar and talks to it over HTTP.

### Two in a row on one branch, answered directly

`chore/bump-0.1.2` (#42) is in that table twice, and two in a row is what a real regression looks like. It is not one, on three independent grounds:

- the same branch carrying the same lockfile change passed **four times** on 2026-09-21 — runs 234, 241, 249 and 253;
- `test:ledger-auth` also failed on `main`, which does not carry that change;
- the only mechanism by which a lockfile could reach a sidecar suite is the `bin` entries it corrects, and `executor/sidecar-harness.mjs:65` spawns `process.execPath` directly against `mnde-local-sidecar.mjs` rather than through any installed bin shim. A fresh `npm ci` from that lockfile links only `tsc` and `tsserver`, and runs 102/102.

### The mechanism, where it is confirmed

`test:sidecar-pe` names it. All three of its failures asked for a specific approval refusal code and got the runtime's instead:

```
[FAIL] PE mode + missing approval -> REFUSE APPROVAL_REQUIRED
+ 'ERR_RUNTIME_DEGRADED'
- 'APPROVAL_REQUIRED'
```

That is the sidecar's event-loop watchdog declining to evaluate policy because the runtime looked unhealthy — correct production behaviour, reached for the wrong reason. A shared Windows runner stalled past the degraded threshold, and the watchdog does not clear for the life of the process, so every later assertion in the suite failed behind it.

**`test:ledger-auth` and `test:freshness-boundary` are consistent with the same cause and do not prove it.** Neither prints a reason code, so each records a downstream effect: in `test:ledger-auth` the decision came back carrying no ledger metadata at all, and the proof read that depended on it then returned 404. The entry says confirmed for one and leading explanation for the others, rather than claiming all four.

### Why this is not KI-001

KI-001 is two suites contending for a fixed `127.0.0.1:8787`, and its own workaround is that `npm test` runs suites sequentially. Here each suite has the machine to itself and still loses the event loop — run 262's two failures were minutes apart in the same sequential pass, not concurrent.

### Why it is safe to defer, in contract terms

It turns green runs red, never red runs green.

And the reason that holds is worth keeping, because it is a property of how these suites were written: they assert the **specific** reason code rather than merely that a refusal occurred, so a degraded runtime makes them fail rather than pass for the wrong reason. A suite asserting only "this was refused" would have gone green here while measuring nothing. The entry records that so the next refusal assertion keeps the same shape.

### No remediation is proposed

Raising the watchdog thresholds is off the table — the threshold is the control. The two options that weaken nothing are recorded as unauthorised rather than taken:

- have the sidecar harness record the runtime-health transition and report it, so a red run says "the runner stalled" in one line instead of needing a log read;
- carry it as it is.

### What this costs you

With strict status checks and a required `Guardrails`, a run that lands on a stalled runner blocks a merge until the branch is updated and CI runs again. Worth budgeting for when dispatching the 0.1.2 release rather than reading it as a regression.

### Validation

Documentation only. Linux, Node 24.14.1: `npm test` **102/102**, `npm run check:whitespace` 493 tracked files.

author: chambm
body: ## Motivation I was working on a reentry prediction made in FAR in the editor scene, and validating its results against the same simulated path in the flight scene. The per-part areas reported by FAR differed by 3-8 % for reasons that had nothing to do with aerodynamics, which made every real 1-2 % effect unreadable. For example, a Mk2 spaceplane's main tank read 2692 m2 of voxel face area in the editor and 2900 m2 in flight, which has significant impact on reentry heating. The editor and the flight should voxelize the same vehicle the same way as much as possible: this PR improves the flight/editor voxelization parity by tweaking the way `VehicleVoxel` places and sizes its grid. ## The "bug" `VehicleVoxel.CreateVoxel` derives the voxel (cube) size from the vessel's bounding box - `ElementSize = cbrt(Volume / elementCount)` - and centers the grid on that box. The box is taken over every part, including the landing gear, whose extent changes without the vessel changing: deployed gear extends the box, and a KSPWheel gear's retracted mesh sits 0.9 m lower in flight than in the editor. When the box changes, two things happen to every other part of the vehicle: - the voxel size changes with the box volume, so every part's voxels get coarser or finer and its projected areas move with them; - the grid's center moves with the box, so the lattice slides under every part and each part's faces re-alias against the cube edges. The same vessel therefore voxelizes differently in the editor, on the runway and in flight, and differently again between gear states. The editor's static analysis, the per-part areas FAR writes into the stock drag cubes, and the projected areas any consumer reads all carry that. ## The fix One method, `CreateVoxel`: - The voxel and the grid's center come from the bounds of the parts that have no wheel module (`ModuleWheelBase`, KSPWheel's `KSPWheelBase`) - the same set `VehicleAerodynamics` already leaves out of the main-axis calculation. I tested doing the same for control surfaces but that did not improve results and in some cases made them worse. - The center is rounded to a whole number of voxels from the vessel frame's origin (the root part), so that a centimeter of joint sag or suspension travel between the editor and the runway moves the box but not the cube edges under the parts. - The grid's chunk counts are computed from the span needed to reach the full `min`/`max` from that center, so it still covers everything, gear included. A vessel that is nothing but wheels falls back to the full bounds. ## Validation Two builds differing only in this change - master (0.16.2) and this PR - on stock craft in stock KSP with FAR, MechJeb and Procedural Parts. I ran a lot of simulations in editor and flight scenes using a KSP UI test harness. I can post the non-stock craft files and telemetry CSVs if that's helpful. A gear cycle is deployed -> retracted -> deployed in the editor (the deploy animation re-voxelizes the craft) and three retract/deploy cycles at three pitch holds in flight. ### 1. Voxel size and the areas of the parts that do not move Four planes with retractable gear. "Fixed parts" are every part that is neither a control surface nor a wheel; their geometry does not change through the cycle. | craft | build | voxel size, gear down / up (m) | fixed-parts area, down / up (m2) | sum of per-part changes (m2) | |---|---|---|---|---| | PoofySkirt (7 m) | master | 0.1257 / 0.1197 | 139.9 / 139.6 | 3.4 | | | PR | 0.1197 / 0.1197 | 139.8 / 139.7 | 0.3 | | Aeris 4A (13 m) | master | 0.1345 / 0.1237 | 157.2 / 156.6 | 8.6 | | | PR | 0.1222 / 0.1222 | 157.6 / 157.6 | 0.0 | | Stearwing A300 (33 m) | master | 0.3325 / 0.3224 | 798.4 / 765.9 | 54.4 | | | PR | 0.3224 / 0.3224 | 764.9 / 766.0 | 2.4 | | Albatross 3 (37 m) | master | 0.2232 / 0.1973 | 584.6 / 590.4 | 36.0 | | | PR | 0.1973 / 0.1973 | 590.4 / 590.4 | 0.8 | On master the voxel size moves 5-13 % with the gear. On the parts that do not move, the gear toggle changes the voxel face area of half to three quarters of them by more than 2 %, a third by more than 5 %, small parts by 30-40 % (area-weighted mean 2.5-7 %). With the PR the voxel size does not move and those parts hold to 0.1-0.3 %; what remains is on the parts the gear legs touch (voxel ownership at the contact). The gear-up voxel size equals master's on three planes (the Aeris is 1.2 % finer: master's retracted wheel meshes stick out of its box). Flight repeats the editor: master's voxel size flips between the two values on every gear cycle, the PR's does not. On master the deployed-gear lattice is not repeatable either - two flights of the Albatross gave 576 and 590 m2 for the same parts; the same flights with the PR got 581.3 and 581.7. ### 2. What a player sees in the editor FAR's static analysis in the editor helps players when designing their plane: it reports drag, lift, and angle of attack the plane trims at, for the craft as built. Deploying the gear should change those numbers only by what the gear itself does - a little more drag, a small pitching moment from the legs hanging below the fuselage. Everything else about the plane is unchanged, so nothing else about the answer should change. On master it does. Because the deployed gear enlarges the bounding box, every other part is re-voxelized on a coarser, shifted grid, and the analysis for the *whole plane* moves. The table shows how much the reported numbers change when the gear goes from retracted to deployed, on master and on this PR (Mach 0.5, alpha 0). The "trim shift" column converts the pitching-moment change into what a pilot would notice: how many degrees the angle of attack at which the plane flies hands-off moves. | craft | build | drag change (Cd) | pitching moment change (Cm) | trim angle of attack shift | |---|---|---|---|---| | PoofySkirt | master | -0.3 % | -0.0062 | -1.10 deg | | | PR | +0.2 % | -0.0029 | -0.51 deg | | Aeris 4A | master | +2.0 % | +0.0057 | +0.20 deg | | | PR | +1.8 % | +0.0055 | +0.19 deg | | Stearwing A300 | master | -4.1 % | +0.0103 | +0.06 deg | | | PR | -0.7 % | +0.0063 | +0.04 deg | | Albatross 3 | master | +0.6 % | -0.0008 | +0.36 deg | | | PR | 0.0 % | -0.0003 | +0.15 deg | Take the PR's numbers as what the gear really does (it is voxelizing the same plane on the same grid both times), and the difference from master's numbers is the "bug". author: mikkoparkkola
body:
## What this repairs

The direct backend route writes an `idp_refuse` transparency-log entry carrying the propagation error, and the meta-route's `refuse` closure feeds the same log. Before this change that tamper-evident record could not tell **"this caller has no grant"** from **"this caller's grant was revoked"** from **"custody was momentarily busy"** — all three arrived as one `PropagationError::Refuse(String)` differing only in interpolated prose.

**The client-facing message and the `idp_refuse` log entry are repaired by the same change.** The log is the half that matters for a regulated buyer, and it is the half a crate-internal side channel would have left flattened while fixing only the visible one. That is why the side-channel option was rejected: it would also have created a second answer to "why did this refuse" on a credential path, which is exactly what `AccountService::connected`'s invariant — a storage failure is never reported as absence — exists to prevent.

## The defect

`AccountServiceError::ConnectOffer` already survived custody intact through `CustodyError::Account` (`#[error(transparent)]`). It was destroyed one hop later, where `VaultStrategy` mapped every `CustodyError` through a single `Refuse`.

## Widened past the named site, deliberately

The reported defect is one `map_err`. The mechanism is three. Per-site mappings are how a discriminant survives one hop and dies at the next, so fixing only the named hop would have left the same defect armed at two other boundaries in this file. All three now route through one `refusal()` helper — a smaller diff than three guards, and a strictly smaller surface to get wrong later.

## No renderer branch, deliberately

The first revision added one so the absence case would not be prefixed `"credential minting failed"`. It is gone. `Display` already carries `no connected account` into the same audit reason, so the distinction a consumer or the log can branch on survives without it — and the branch cost 29 lines in the worst size-ratchet offender in the repository. Decoration on top of the carrier, so it was deleted rather than given budget. **`invoke.rs` is byte-identical to its base and is not part of this change.**

## `#[non_exhaustive]`

Landed in the same change because this is the only free moment for it: it costs nothing during a major bump and is itself breaking in any later minor. Afterwards every future variant on this enum is non-breaking. The variant addition is breaking relative to the published `3.5.1`, which is ordinary major-version work rather than a semver violation.

## A diagnosis, not an offer

No consent URL, no offer object, no actionable invitation is surfaced. The gateway-brokered consent journey stays deferred (ADR-008 Slice C, MIK-6745), and inviting a caller into a flow the gateway cannot complete would be worse for them than a clean refusal. Absence also drops the boundary context: which custody call observed it is not informative for a state the store simply does not hold.

## Falsifier and its admitted-case control

`absence_is_distinguishable_from_revocation_at_the_propagation_boundary`.

The falsifier **pairs absence against revocation**, because asserting only that an absent grant refuses would pass for an implementation that refuses everyone identically — which is the pre-fix behaviour exactly. Revocation is produced through the real `store.revoke()` rather than a fabricated error value, and absence uses an initialized-but-empty store so `lookup` *answers* "absent" instead of failing. The two are asserted to differ by `std::mem::discriminant`, not by string: a string difference is not something a consumer or an audit record can branch on.

**Admitted-case control:** the existing, already-green `a_sole_operator_grant_is_leasable_end_to_end`, proving the same store, descriptor, backend and principal do lease and release when a grant exists. Without it every refusal assertion in the file would pass vacuously.

Red first, and it failed for the right reason — an assertion, not a compile error:

```
an absent grant must carry the absence discriminant across the custody boundary,
not be flattened into a generic refusal:
Refuse("managed account is not usable: account is not connected — connect the
account for this backend, then retry")
```

The remediation sentence was physically present, nested three prefixes deep in prose.

## Size ratchet

The first revision failed two rows. No baseline was raised and no test was relocated to a fresh file to dodge the count. The renderer branch was deleted (above), and prose was trimmed in `audit_identity_propagation`'s doc block — the paragraph narrating how audit used to be best-effort, and a restatement that a disabled logger is a no-op which the same block already made four paragraphs earlier. The redaction paragraph, both caller-obligation bullets and `# Errors` are untouched. The trim is local to the function this change's argument is about, not scattered through unrelated files.

`identity_propagation/mod.rs` now sits at **976, exactly at its ceiling with no headroom** — the next addition there will need its own trim.

**Ratchet baseline drift, for whoever maintains it:** `invoke.rs` at base measures 6276, not the 6281 recorded in `scripts/dev/file-size-baseline.txt`. Someone tightened that file after the baseline was written and the ratchet never noticed. Nothing here depends on the slack and the baseline is left alone.

## Gates

| Gate | Status |
|---|---|
| format check | 0 |
| lint, all targets, warnings denied | 0 |
| target falsifier | 0 |
| full test suite | 0, with zero `FAILED` or `panicked` lines in the log |
| size ratchet | 0, zero `FAIL` lines, neither file flagged |

### One gate reported as not run, rather than passed

The mandated pre-commit change-scope check returned `changed_count: 0, risk_level: none`. **That result is vacuous and was not counted.** The index is bound to the canonical checkout while these edits are staged in a separate worktree, so the tool answered about a different tree; a post-commit hook then confirmed the index is stale. A clean bill from a tool that cannot see the work is a false green, not a pass. Scope was checked manually against the staged diff instead.

Re-indexing properly requires the canonical checkout to be moved off its forked branch, which is out of scope here. Until then, `detect_changes` run from a worktree should not be counted by anyone; `impact` is unaffected.

## Three process notes worth more than the fix

**A stale green is the same failure mode as a piped one:** both are a status detached from the thing it claims to describe, one by a pipe and one by time. A full-suite exit 0 from before a cleanup was discarded for that reason. Two further variants turned up in the same session — a background wrapper's exit code standing in for the test run's, and `gh pr create`'s status read through a pipe — so the general defence is to read the status out of the output file, and to verify the artifact rather than trust the command that made it.

**An intermediate renderer draft said "not connected" three times in one sentence.** No gate would have caught it; it was caught by reading the diff. Shipping a repair for unreadable nested prose with a fresh instance of unreadable nested prose would have been bad in the same way.

**This branch has two commits rather than one amended commit.** The trim was landed on top instead of rewritten into the original, because the original was already pushed and nobody authorised rewriting published history — the force flag would have been a consequence of the author's convenience, not of any instruction.

Refs MIK-6745.JOURNEY.1

author: bitplorer
body: ## Why `native/src/lib.rs` used one `Unit` enum for two jobs: which door the plan is, and which check runs after extract. Every apply walk named every other family and skipped it. That gets worse as families grow. This tip is private organization only. No new Door A family. ## Layout `Plan` is one variant per family. The variant owns only that family's checks (`native/src/plan.rs`). - `Plan::Integer` / `Plan::Float` own `BoundUnit` / `BoundUnit` (`native/src/bound.rs`). One `scalar_miss` and one `compile_bound_plan` serve both. `apply_bound_units` takes `&[BoundUnit]`, so a length unit is a type error. - `Plan::String` / `Plan::Bytes` own `LengthUnit` (`native/src/length.rs`). Count stays at the FFI door (codepoints or bytes). One length walk. - `Plan::IntegerEnum` / `Plan::StringEnum` own the member set (`Arc>` / `Arc>`). - `Plan::Boolean` and `Plan::Decimal` are markers. No bounds, no scale. `apply_integer` matches `Plan::Integer`, clones that `Arc`, and detaches the bound walk (`native/src/lib.rs`). Other variants are named and return `RuntimeError` before the walk. A new variant fails to compile in each door. There is no `_ => None` arm and no mega-`apply`. Python still sees one frozen `Plan` (`PyPlan` is only the PyO3 shell; `#[pyclass(name = "Plan")]`). ## Unchanged - Public `compile_*` / `apply_*` names and signatures. Compile and apply stay separate doors. - `FailKind` discriminants and host wording. - Cap Door B stays off. - Date* / UUID / Path / Pattern stay HOLD. No Decimal bounds or scale. No `rust_decimal`. - L1 Python surface unchanged. Host `_select_*` unchanged. - Hot path is still one FFI apply: `Arc` clone, then the same compare or length or membership walk. No extra allocation on apply. Boolean / Decimal no longer allocate a one-element unit list at compile; apply does not clone an `Arc` because the variant has no checks. ## Behavior note for review Host never applies a plan through another family's door. A direct peer call that does (`apply_integer` on a string plan) used to succeed as a no-op. It now raises `RuntimeError` (`… plan family mismatch`) and does not walk. Same-family apply results are unchanged, including wrong Python types rejected at extract. ## Checks - `cargo clippy --manifest-path native/Cargo.toml --release -- -D warnings` clean - `python -m mypy` clean (53 files) - `python -m pytest` green (native peer included; CPython 3.14.7)

body: ## Description - Zoom pruning enumerates document ids from each host's recordings listing instead of re-crawling the connector and re-downloading every transcript. - Fixes two paths that deleted transcripts whose recordings still existed: meeting-ID discovery could not see past Zoom's 15-month cap, and a failed listing window reported an error that protected no documents. - A host's documents are removed only when Zoom answers that the user does not exist. Any other failure, including a missing scope, stops the prune and deletes nothing. - A prune that recognises none of its hosts now stops, because Zoom returns that same answer for a user who belongs to a different account, so a rotated credential would otherwise wipe the connector. - An incomplete listing from Zoom now fails the indexing attempt as well, so the poll window cannot move past recordings Zoom left out of a page. - The client keeps one method per endpoint: `get_transcript` becomes `get_recording`, and `list_meeting_invitees` becomes `get_meeting_details`. Stacked on #14884. Tests for this change are in the PR stacked on top of this one, so the Zoom suite is red on this branch alone. ## How Has This Been Tested? Unit and daily tests land in the stacked tests PR. Verified read-only against a live Zoom account: the slim ids covered every indexed id with no transcript downloads, a missing scope and a server error each stopped the prune, and an unknown host email was skipped without stopping it. ## Additional Options - [ ] [Optional] Please cherry-pick this PR to the latest release version. - [x] [Optional] Override Linear Check --- ## Summary by cubic Prunes Zoom connectors through a slim listing of recording IDs instead of a full crawl, so pruning no longer re-downloads every transcript, misses recordings past Zoom's 15-month instances cap, or deletes documents on a failed listing window. - A document is deleted only when Zoom answers that the user does not exist (404, code 1001), asked once before the walk; any other failure stops the prune and deletes nothing. - A prune that recognizes none of its hosts stops instead of wiping the connector, because Zoom answers the same code for a user of a different account; a number no session answers for counts the same way. - An incomplete, looping, or endless listing raises during indexing too, and a listing Zoom sent no `total_records` for is treated as incomplete, so the poll window cannot move past recordings Zoom left out. - The prune walks a host named by email and by Group only once, and asks every listed run for a series' host so a recording-less run cannot look absent. - The client keeps one method per endpoint: `get_transcript` becomes `get_recording`, and `list_meeting_invitees` becomes `get_meeting_details`. - Verified against a live Zoom account: the slim IDs covered every indexed ID without downloading transcripts, a missing scope and a server error each stopped pruning, and an unknown host email was skipped without stopping it. The test suite now follows the client rename on this branch, so Zoom tests pass without the stacked PR. Written for commit 964d152449282be78cb9cc3eee83eb2414587bc7. Summary will update on new commits.

author: azmartone67
body:
## What changed

`worker.js` (the api.dchub.cloud zone worker) keeps a KV response cache that is **shared per URL**: an entry written for a URL is served to later callers of that URL (STEP 1 fresh, STEP 3 stale), and `kvCacheKey()` drops the credential query params from the key.

- **KV writes are gated.** The proxy write (STEP 2), the Render failover write (STEP 2.5) and the Flask HTML lane write now require **both**:
  - the request carried no caller credential — `carriesCallerCredential()`, and
  - the origin's `Cache-Control` allows a shared copy (neither `private` nor `no-store`) — `originAllowsSharedStore()`.
- **One credential predicate.** `carriesCallerCredential()` covers X-API-Key and `?api_key`, `Authorization` in any scheme, the other credential headers and cookies the origin reads (matched by name shape so a new one is covered without a worker edit), and every query param `kvCacheKey()` drops (`KV_KEY_STRIP_PARAMS`, now shared with `kvCacheKey`).
- `hasApiKey` → `hasCredential` on that predicate, so the KV read, the edge `cacheTtl` and the public Cache-Control rewrite use the same rule.
- `WORKER_VERSION` → `4.9.73-kv-writes-only-credential-free`; version pin updated in `tests/test_seven_levers_shell.py`.

## Expected effect on cache hit rate

Honouring `no-store` also stops **traffic-driven** KV writes on routes whose credential-free origin response is `no-store`. Measured 2026-09-22 on credential-free, cache-busted GETs to api.dchub.cloud:

| route | origin Cache-Control (credential-free 200) | KV write after this change |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/facilities`, `/api/v1/gas-pipelines`, `/api/v1/stats` | public | yes |
| `/api/news`, `/api/v1/search`, `/api/v1/markets`, `/api/v1/deals`, `/api/v1/tax-incentives`, `/api/infrastructure/*` | `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` | no |

The cron seeder (`seedApiCache`) is unchanged and still fills its seeded routes. To keep the KV lane on a `no-store` route, have the origin send `public, s-maxage=N` for its credential-free response. Every Flask HTML lane path sampled (robots, sitemap, markets, system-status, AGENTS.md, …) returned `public`, so that lane is unaffected for anonymous traffic.

## Evidence

- New `tests/test_worker_kv_write_is_credential_free.py` **executes the shipped code** under node: the predicates, each write site's own statements pulled verbatim from `worker.js`, and the Flask lane's actual condition. It also scans every `request.headers.get(...)` / `request.cookies.get(...)` name in the backend and fails on any name that is neither detected nor explicitly listed as benign. The scan has floors (≥30 headers, ≥10 cookies) so it can't pass by finding nothing.
- Mutation run: **12/12 killed**. Each mutation was confirmed applied, and `worker.js` was restored byte-identical (sha checked before and after). The mutations: each guard removed at STEP 2 / STEP 2.5 / Flask lane (6), `hasCredential` reverted to the old two-channel definition, header regex narrowed, header regex widened to match everything, cookie regex narrowed, strip-param check removed, and the Cache-Control check forced true.
- All 40 test files that read `worker.js`: `635 passed, 4 skipped` (skips are environmental: live MCP probe, DB DSN, sibling checkout).
- `scripts/check_worker_version_bump.sh origin/main HEAD` → rc=0; `regression_lint.py --mode delta --base origin/main` → rc=0 (run on the commit).
- ESM parse: `cp worker.js wchk.mjs && node --check wchk.mjs` → rc=0.

## Deploy

**Merging does not deploy this.** `worker.js` goes live only when it is pasted into the Cloudflare dashboard for the api.dchub.cloud zone worker. Until then production serves 4.9.72. Verify after the paste:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "https://api.dchub.cloud/api/v1/stats?_=$(date +%s)" | grep -i x-dc-worker-version
# want: 4.9.73-kv-writes-only-credential-free
```

author: sukvvon
body:
## 🎯 Changes

`queryOptions.test-d` in `react-query`, `preact-query`, and `svelte-query` each had a `'should return the proper type when passed to QueriesObserver'` case:

```ts
const queriesObserver = new QueriesObserver(queryClient, [options])
expectTypeOf(queriesObserver).toEqualTypeOf<
  QueriesObserver<Array<QueryObserverResult>>
>()
```

This asserted nothing. `QueriesObserver`'s constructor takes `queries: Array<QueryObserverOptions<any, any, any, any, any>>` — five `any`s — so passing a real `queryOptions()` result vs. a plain object makes no difference to inference. `TCombinedResult` is only decided by the third constructor argument (`options.combine`), which none of these tests passed, so the assertion always resolved to the default `Array<QueryObserverResult>`: a tautology that can't fail from a regression.

`QueriesObserver` is a `query-core` class; its type behavior belongs in `query-core`'s own tests, not scattered across adapter `queryOptions.test-d` files. `query-core` now has `queriesObserver.test-d.tsx`, including a case that passes `combine` and asserts the inferred `TCombinedResult` actually changes — a real, breakable check. That makes these three copies redundant as well as dead.

Removed the three `it` blocks and the now-unused `QueriesObserver`/`QueryObserverResult` imports. `solid-query` and `vue-query` never had this case, and `angular-query-experimental`/`lit-query` have no `queryOptions.test-d` file, so no other adapter needs the same cleanup.

author: jonah-6
body:
## Summary

There was no continuous integration for the repository, so regressions in the router, MCP client, marketplace app, or the Soroban spending-policy contract could land without being caught. This adds a single CI workflow that gates every push to `main` and every pull request.

## Changes

- Added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with two jobs:
  - `node`: checks out the repo, sets up pnpm 10 and Node 22 with pnpm store caching, then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test` from the repo root via Turborepo, covering all workspace packages (`apps/*`, `services/*`, `packages/*`).
  - `contracts`: runs `cargo test` inside `contracts/spending-policy` using the stable Rust toolchain, with `Swatinem/rust-cache` for build caching.
- The workflow triggers on `push` to `main` and on `pull_request`.
- `concurrency` cancels superseded runs on the same ref, and `permissions: contents: read` keeps the default token scope minimal.
- Third-party actions are pinned to major version tags (`actions/checkout@v4`, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`).

## Issues

Resolves #3

## Verification

I read the root `package.json`, `turbo.json`, and each workspace package's `package.json` (`apps/marketplace`, `apps/mcp`, `apps/router`, `services/pdf`, `packages/types`) to confirm the `lint`, `type-check`, `build`, and `test` scripts referenced in the workflow already exist (added by the already-merged lockfile/lint/test PR). I also read `contracts/Cargo.toml` and `contracts/spending-policy/Cargo.toml` to confirm the Rust workspace layout.

I did not run `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, or `cargo test` locally. GitHub Actions did not exist in this repository before this change, so there is no way to validate the workflow's syntax and step ordering other than by running it on this pull request; I will watch the Actions run on this PR and push small follow-up commits if anything needs adjusting.

body:
# LMM API Pull Request

## 变更说明 / Summary

Status-page sorting returns NaN when reliability is missing or both first-token latencies are missing. JavaScript treats that comparison as a tie, leaving unknown reliability ahead of known data and bypassing the name tiebreaker. Normalize non-finite reliability to negative infinity and compare normalized values for equality before subtraction. Zero reliability remains valid, unknown metrics sort last, and name breaks missing-latency ties. No metric aggregation, API, translation, or monetary behavior changes.

author: oo11o
body:
## What

`openUrl` is split into `openUrlInNewTab` (unchanged behaviour) and `openUrlInCurrentTab`. The current-tab step navigates this tab instead of opening a new one — which kills the content script mid-chain — so the runner now suspends the remaining steps in the service worker (keyed by tab id) before navigating, and the next page's content script picks up and finishes the stack. This is what makes a logout → redirect → login-form stack possible in one chord.

## How to verify

- [x] `npm test` passes (139 tests, 13 files)
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [ ] Tried it in Chrome (`chrome://extensions` → reload → `⌃⌥8` on dzo.lh for the new Logout stack)

## Notes

- Two verbs instead of one step with a `target` flag: the contracts genuinely differ (chain continues vs. chain suspends), matching the existing `popup`/`popupJson` and `readBySelector`/`copyBySelector` precedent — no existing step takes a mode enum.
- Resume records are one-shot (removed before the resumed steps run, so a failure doesn't leave a record to refire) and expire after 15s (so a navigation that never lands can't fire a stack later on an unrelated page).
- Secrets are never persisted in a resume record — re-seeded from `chrome.storage.local` on the far side, same as a fresh run. Notes are redacted before being parked too, since a secret can otherwise leak through a note like `went to ...&run=$secret_x`. Both are covered by tests.
- Builtins (`$url`, `$title`, `$selection`) are re-seeded from the landing page, not restored — they describe the page, and after a navigation that's a different page.
- **Breaking**: an old `"type": "openUrl"` in a hand-edited config now fails loudly as `Unknown step type "openUrl"` rather than working. `public/config/stacks.json` is migrated in this PR.
- **Known gap, not fixed here**: `resumePending()` runs at `document_idle`. On a page whose target element is rendered client-side (e.g. a React login form) after that point, a resumed `inputToSelector` step can throw `No element for "..."` before the element exists. This needs a `waitFor`/poll step — tracked as the next item in `.claude/plan/plan.md`'s v0.5 entry, not addressed in this PR.

body:
## Summary

- `x?.isEmpty == false ? x! : fallback` was duplicated at 7 call sites across the importer/exporter/publication services.
- The plain `String.nonEmpty: String?` helper it depends on was independently, privately redeclared in 4 different files (`StructuredAIClient`, `EPUBProcessor`, `ReferenceLibraryStore`, plus a differently-named trimmed variant in `AIRequestModels`) -- one of those (`EPUBProcessor`'s `Optional<String>.nonEmpty` property) turned out to be dead code, never actually called.
- None of this was a correctness bug -- every force-unwrap was safe given its guard -- but it's fragile duplication: a future edit that changes one copy's condition without the others is exactly the kind of thing that turns a "currently safe" force-unwrap into a real crash.

## Changes

- New `AppSources/Kistulentz/Services/StringExtensions.swift`: `String.nonEmpty: String?` and `Optional<String>.nonEmpty(or:) -> String`.

- Removed the private duplicate declarations this superseded in `StructuredAIClient`, `EPUBProcessor`, and `ReferenceLibraryStore`.
- Renamed `ReferenceLibraryModels`' locally-trimmed variant (different semantics -- it trims whitespace first) to `nonEmptyTrimmed`, matching the name `AIRequestModels` already uses for the same trimmed behavior, so it no longer collides with the new shared name.
- Added `StringExtensionsTests.swift` covering the new shared helper directly.

body:
Bounties had a status column (`open`/`paused`/`closed`) but no control anywhere to change it, and no way to remove one. This adds both.

## Archive

- New `archived` status. Keeps the bounty and every submission, invoice and payout record.
- Hidden from the public list and detail page via RLS (same rule as `closed`).
- Moves to its own **Archived** tab on `/dashboard/bounties`.
- Unarchive sets the bounty back to `closed`, so it does not silently reopen for submissions. Reopen is one more click.

## Delete

- `DELETE /api/bounties/:id`, creator only.
- Refused with `409` and `archive_instead: true` once any submission has been approved, invoiced or paid. The cascade would erase payment history, so the UI offers to archive instead.
- Pending and rejected submissions delete with the bounty.

## UI

- New `BountyActions` menu (mirrors `GigActions`): pause / resume / close, archive / unarchive, delete, with confirm dialogs.
- Sits in the sidebar of `/bounties/:id` and on every row of the dashboard list (rows are no longer one big link).
- Archived bounties show a creator-only notice on the detail page.

## GitHub issue comment

When the bounty funds a GitHub issue, the status comment is flipped to "withdrawn" on archive or delete and restored to "posted" on reopen. The comment bodies now live in `src/lib/bounty-issue-comments.ts`.

## Database

Migration applied to the live project via the Supabase MCP and recorded as `20260922045204_bounty_archived_status`. It widens the status CHECK and rewrites the public SELECT policy. Both changes are backwards compatible with the code on master.

## Docs

`public/openapi.json` and `public/skill.md` document the new status, the DELETE endpoint and the 409.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `pnpm lint` 0 errors
- 38 bounty tests pass across 7 files, including 11 new ones for DELETE, the archive/reopen comment sync and the delete guard
- `pnpm build` exit 0

Noticed but not changed: `updateBountySchema` is `createBountySchema.partial()`, and the `payout_currency` default survives `.partial()`, so every PATCH also writes `payout_currency: "USD"`. Harmless today since every bounty is USD.

body: ## Summary Labhand’s first apply of the K3s chart hit two deploy bugs. This branch is off `main` at `65b8094` (includes #4 and the #6 chart at `dd9a3f0`). - **Caddy `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.** `caddy:2-alpine` ships with `setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep`. With `capabilities.drop: [ALL]` and no add, the kernel refuses to exec the binary: `caddy: Operation not permitted`, even though the site listens on `:8080`. The caddy container now keeps `drop: ["ALL"]` and adds `NET_BIND_SERVICE`. `asymetryk/agentinfra` `deploy/k3s/working-set-ui` was not readable from this workspace (GitHub 404), so this follows that homelab drop-ALL + add pattern rather than a copied snippet. - **Portable `sed`.** `apply.sh` used GNU-only `sed -i`. It now uses `sed -i.bak` and deletes the backup, which works on BSD sed (Howards-MacBook-Pro-2) and GNU sed. The temp-file trap also removes a leftover `.bak`. `vite.config.ts` `allowedHosts` and the CAHQ origin are unchanged. No auth key is in the tree. This agent did not `kubectl apply`. ## Labhand After merge, rebuild the image on asym-k1 and re-apply. The pod still needs the existing tailnet auth key in secret `mirmicode/mirmicode-tailscale-auth` key `authkey` (not in git): ```bash ./deploy/k3s/mirmicode/build-image.sh MIRMICODE_APPLY=1 ./deploy/k3s/mirmicode/apply.sh ``` ## Test - `bash -n deploy/k3s/mirmicode/apply.sh` - GNU `sed -i.bak` substitution on a temp manifest: image tag replaced, `.bak` removed - `apply.sh` dry-run exits 0 and does not call kubectl - `npm test`: 56 passed - `go test` in `deploy/k3s/mirmicode/proxy`: ok - No cluster apply. `kubectl` is not on this VM, so kustomize render was not run here.

author: swir
body:
## Summary
- make Enhanced Diagnostics resume a newly selected Recycle/Restore session transactionally
- validate the selected manifest, current safety contract and restored-evidence report before mutating active UI state
- prevent a failed resume attempt from falling through and re-adopting RELEASE_EVIDENCE from the previously active session
- add regression coverage for valid persisted evidence, stale evidence and failed-manifest isolation

## Why
The enhanced resume layer previously called the base resume method and then inferred success from `self.check` / `self.evidence_report`. The base window intentionally preserves the last valid session after a failed resume. That meant the enhanced layer could continue using stale state after an invalid new manifest selection and inspect the previous session's attestation. This patch removes that ambiguity and keeps session/evidence identity fail-closed.

## Safety
- no change to Recycle Bin deletion behavior
- no permanent-delete fallback
- no STATUS.md/progress change
- merge only after exact-head Windows CI is green

_Requested by **Zaeem** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01E5cAsiVq6JzYZCxFzuMj6E?thread=cmsg_01E5cAsiVq6JzYZCxFzuMj6EJa19w1q9VSYBGkAeUyoQKM)_

Closes gaps 1 and 3 from `docs/HACKATHON_PLAN.md`.

Before: cloning the public repo and running `npm ci` gave you a project that could not be built. `npm run build` died on an unresolved `../convex/_generated/api`, `npm run typecheck` reported 348 errors, and 11 of 36 test files failed to load, because `convex/_generated/` was listed in `.gitignore`. Separately, the live page carried no Open Graph or Twitter card tags and no favicon, so pasting the URL into X or LinkedIn produced a bare link with no title, description or image.

After: the ignore rule is gone, so the generated directory can be committed (see **One step left for you** below — it still has to be generated once). The page now carries a full set of link-preview tags and a favicon, and the build copies both new assets to the site root.

**Gap 1.** Convex's own CLI is explicit about this — `npx convex codegen --help` says the generated code *"should be committed to the repo (your code won't typecheck without it!)"*. That settles the open question the plan raised about whether the ignore was deliberate.

**Gap 3.** `index.html` gains `og:type`, `og:site_name`, `og:url`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image` (plus width, height and alt), `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`, a `theme-color`, and an icon link. Image URLs are absolute because crawlers do not resolve relative paths. Two new files under `public/`: `og-image.png`, a 1200×630 card built from the app's own type and palette (Fraunces/Inter, `#f7f4ee` paper, the three verdict chips), and `favicon.svg`, a lens mark that stays legible at 16px.

How: `.gitignore` loses one line; `index.html` gains a metadata block; `public/` is new. No application code, no Convex functions and no tests were touched.

### One step left for you

The `.gitignore` change alone does not put the generated files in the repo, and I could not generate them from here — `npx convex codegen` requires a Convex login, and the anonymous local-backend fallback failed downloading its binary through this environment's proxy. The offline-only path I could run got build passing and typecheck down to 5 errors, but it cannot resolve the `components` export that `convex/http.ts`, `convex/pipeline.ts` and `convex/rateLimits.ts` import, so I did not ship a half-generated directory.

On your Mac, on this branch or on `main` after merging:

```sh
npx convex dev --once          # regenerates convex/_generated and pushes the backend
git add convex/_generated && git commit -m "chore: commit Convex generated code" && git push
```

Use `npx convex dev --once`, not `npx convex deploy` — the latter targets the stray prod deployment.

Then verify the gap is actually closed, in a throwaway directory:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zaeem-rafiq/second-look && cd second-look
npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build   # all four should exit 0
```

### Gap 3 reaches the live site only after a rebuild

The tags are in the built HTML, so the site keeps its current markup until you rebuild and re-upload:

```sh
VITE_CONVEX_URL=https://friendly-retriever-712.convex.cloud \
VITE_CONVEX_SITE_URL=https://friendly-retriever-712.convex.site npm run build
CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT=dev:friendly-retriever-712 \
  node node_modules/@convex-dev/static-hosting/dist/cli/index.js upload --dev --component staticHosting
```

The upload will now carry five assets rather than three. Afterwards `curl -sS https://friendly-retriever-712.convex.site/ | grep -c "og:"` should print 8, and pasting the URL into the X or LinkedIn composer should show the card. Worth doing before the social post, since that post is a scored deliverable.

Verified here: `npm run build` exits 0, `dist/` contains `favicon.svg` and `og-image.png` at the root, `dist/index.html` carries all 13 new tags with the absolute image URL intact, and the favicon renders cleanly at 16, 32 and 64 px.
