## **User description** ## What this changes, and why Two related UI fixes on the amber+white Liquid Glass kit (post v1.9.15 / PR #60), plus a transparency pass on full-tile glass: ### 1. Full-tile Liquid Glass + centred logos Portal (and dashboard) module cards put frost only on the 60px logo chip while the card stayed flat white, and 3D marks sat high-left. `.glass-tile` now wraps the **whole card**; logos are centred; `ModuleLogo3D` anchors on a centred origin. ### 2. More transparent tile frost Tiles felt too opaque. `.glass-tile` fill is now see-through: white wash `rgba(255,255,255,0.14)`, tint mixes against `transparent` (18% / 7%), specular `0.2`, rim `0.45`, blur `14px`. Labels stay `text-ink-900` / `text-ink-500`. ### 3. Organization logo missing in the header After M-5, uploads store `logoPath` with an empty `logoUrl`. The header then depends entirely on an authenticated Storage fetch. When that fails, OrgMark painted WE EHS over a saved logo. - Upload writes a small JPEG **thumb** into `logoUrl`. - `useFileUrl` starts in `loading` for paths, retries, then falls back to the thumb. - OrgMark keeps a cream slot when a logo is configured but unresolved. - Org Settings backfills `logoUrl` from a resolved path-only logo. Preview: `docs/ui-preview/module-tiles-before|after.html`, updated `shell.html`. ## Security impact - [x] None of the above `logoUrl` remains a small data URL or empty string on `/organizations/{orgId}`. No permanent Storage download token (M-5 stays closed). ## Evidence it works - `fileToLogoThumb`, `useFileUrl` retries/fallback, `OrgMark` cream slot tests. - Screenshots: `module-tiles-before.png`, `module-tiles-after.png` (more transparent), `shell.png`. ## Anything deliberately left undone - Path-only logos get a thumb when an admin opens Org Settings or re-uploads. - Audit hub `icon-chip` tiles unchanged.
  
___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Center module logos on translucent full-card glass and preserve uploaded organization logos when storage is unavailable ### What Changed - Module cards in the portal and dashboard now use a translucent Liquid Glass surface across the entire card, with centered logos and clearer dark labels. - 3D module logos stay centered instead of appearing offset, while hover effects remain available. - Organization logo uploads now save a small inline preview, allowing headers to show the uploaded logo while storage access is delayed or fails. - Logo loading retries before using the saved preview, and configured logos show a neutral placeholder instead of reverting to the vendor mark. - Existing path-only logos can be backfilled with an inline preview when an administrator opens organization settings. ### Impact `✅ Centered module logos` `✅ Translucent module cards` `✅ Fewer missing organization logos`

author: jsnajdr
body:
Implementing an optimization idea from https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82821#discussion_r4069813495.

When `registry.subscribe` can't find the store to subscribe to, it used to register to the registry listener that receives all updates. That ensures that a future update from the store registered in the future is not missed. But it's inefficient, there are too many unwanted updates both before and after store registration.

Here is a more efficient implementation: when the store doesn't exist, add a pending listener to `pendingListeners`, and then wire it up in `connectPendingListeners` after a store is registered.

This removes a need for a special case in #82821. The old registry-wide listener was "tainted", and we must be careful to not store it permanently in `subscribeDeferred`. Now the fallback listener is perfectly fine, the only difference is an indirect wrapped `unsubscribe` callback.

author: harshitnub077
body:
Closes #10110

## Summary
Corrects the empty state action button label, aligns the TypeScript return type in `useGroupsService`, wraps branch loading in `LoaderGuard`, resets pagination across artifact changes, and fixes toolbar pagination widget IDs in `ArtifactBranchesTabContent`.

## Motivation
On the Branches tab of the Artifact details page, several inconsistencies were introduced during initial scaffolding:
1. When an artifact has no branches, the empty state displays "No branches found", but the primary action button reads "Create version" (while opening the Create Branch modal). It also lacked the resource owner authorization check present on the toolbar.
2. In `useGroupsService.ts`, `getArtifactBranches` was typed as `Promise<VersionSearchResults>` rather than `Promise<BranchSearchResults>`, conflicting with the `GroupsService` interface definition and returning incorrect model types downstream.
3. Rapid navigation across artifacts while on page > 1 did not reset the page number, causing empty table views when the next artifact had fewer branches. Branch fetching also lacked `LoaderGuard` request cancellation.
4. `BranchesTabToolbar.tsx` retained `"reference-list-pagination"` attributes on its pagination component.

## Proposed Changes
- **Empty State & Auth**: Updated button text to "Create branch" and added `owner={props.artifact?.owner}` to `<IfAuth>`.
- **Type Signature**: Updated `getArtifactBranches` in `useGroupsService.ts` to return `Promise<BranchSearchResults>`.
- **Lifecycle & Cancellation**: Wrapped the fetch in `newLoaderGuard()` and returned `guard.cancel()` in `useEffect` cleanup.
- **Pagination Reset**: Added an effect resetting `paging.page` to `1` when `props.artifact?.artifactId` changes.
- **Toolbar Attributes**: Renamed `widgetId` and `className` in `BranchesTabToolbar.tsx` to `"branches-list-pagination"`.

## Impact
- Clear and accurate empty state messaging for branch creation.
- Strict TypeScript alignment with the backend SDK OpenAPI models.
- Predictable table pagination and no leaked network promises when switching artifacts quickly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Artifacts without custom branches show an empty state button labeled "Create branch".
- [x] Clicking "Create branch" opens the branch creation dialog.
- [x] Ownership checks on the empty state match the toolbar actions.
- [x] Navigating from page 2 of an artifact with 15 branches to an artifact with 2 branches resets the view to page 1.
- [x] `useGroupsService.getArtifactBranches` resolves `BranchSearchResults`.

## Checklist
- [x] Linked issue has maintainer approval
- [x] No overlapping open PRs for the same issue
- [x] Checked the [Tried & Rejected list](https://github.com/Apicurio/apicurio-registry/discussions/8364)
- [x] Tests added for new code paths
- [x] Tested locally: UI builds clean with `npm run build`
- [x] All commits have DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`)

## Summary

The docs sitemap currently exposes generated fragments as standalone pages, while broad titles and a long FAQ make useful answers harder to find. This change publishes intentional landing pages, clearer Home Assistant titles, and a shorter FAQ whose structured answers come from the same Markdown as the visible text.

## Practical impact

- Add a screen comparison guide and practical guides for room controls, media, cameras, and voice, linked from the main navigation.
- Remove 18 generated URLs from the sitemap, keep useful card capabilities in Reference, and move runtime coverage into developer docs. Preserve retired Weather Forecast, generated-reference, and all 16 generated screen URLs with HTML redirects.
- Preserve all 60 FAQ question headings while shortening its source from 4,007 to 2,682 words. Correct reset/networking guidance and document dated firmware/integration status.
- Standardise EspControl branding and descriptive titles. Keep the support button below the content on mobile so it does not obscure the comparison table.
- Add rendered-site checks to the docs build, an optional Search Console verification tag, a measured pre-change crawl baseline, and maintainer setup instructions.

## Documentation decision

- [x] Updated public docs or release-facing notes for user-visible behavior/configuration.
- [ ] No docs needed because this does not change user-visible behavior/configuration.
- [ ] Docs follow-up needed before merge; explain below.

Docs notes:

The site changes are ready for review. Search Console verification, sitemap submission, and traffic exports require the owner's Google account and have not been performed. The ineffective project-path robots.txt is replaced by a ready-to-publish host-root template. The owner explicitly chose to keep the template and instructions rather than create a separate GitHub Pages repository. See `dev-docs/docs-discovery.md` for these account steps.

## Testing

- [x] Automated/local checks passed or were run where practical.
- [ ] Device testing is required before merge.
- [x] Device testing is not required; explain why in Notes for testing.

No firmware or device behaviour changes; no flashing required.

- `python3 scripts/check_dev_docs.py --check`: passed.

The automated testing guidance calls for judgement because this touches documentation build scripts. No physical display test is needed: these changes affect the docs site and its checks only.

Check out `improve-docs-discovery`, run `npm ci`, `npm run docs:build`, and `npm run docs:preview`. Open the preview's `/espcontrol/` path and:

author: justmumu
body:
Second and final wave of the audit remediation plan. Every finding is now
closed, including P6, which the plan had withdrawn as unshippable.

Six independent branches were developed in isolated worktrees and merged here
with no file overlap between them. Combined gate on this branch: `make check`
1767 passed, coverage above the 80% floor (main: 92.39%); `make docs-build` green;
`make test-integration` 874 passed with two pre-existing `FileNotFoundError:
'taplo'` failures in `test_asset_formatters_check_then_rewrite_without_node`,
reproduced identically on unmodified `main`.

## Findings closed

| Finding | Rating | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P3 | CRITICAL | fixed — running byte counter in traversal |
| P6 | HIGH | fixed — measured first, then a maintained counter |
| P5 | HIGH | fixed — same counter in both search pages |
| P9 | MEDIUM | 3 of 4 items fixed, 1 refused with data, 1 dropped as unshippable |
| B1 | MEDIUM | fixed — widens acceptance |
| B2 | MEDIUM | fixed — docs, now pinned against the catalog |
| E4 | LOW | fixed — rejects at every ingress path |
| E6 | LOW | fixed |
| B3, B4 | LOW | dead code deleted |
| B5 | LOW | fixed — **breaking** |
| B6 | LOW | fixed — latent, no client behaviour changes |
| P10 | LOW | search half fixed |

## P3 and P5 were real, and large

Bytes handed to `canonical_json` by one call:

| | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `kb_neighbors` 300 edges | 8 925 600 | 58 733 |
| `kb_neighbors` 1000 edges | 98 585 355 | 195 509 |
| `kb_search` limit 100 | 5 691 350 | 132 500 |

Pre-fix is 1 : 8.85 : 97.75 for 1x : 3x : 10x edges — quadratic, as the finding
claimed. `make benchmark-kb SCALE=smoke BENCHMARK_PHASE=corpus` p50: traversal
106.38 ms -> 6.33 ms at `max_edges=300`; a wider sweep gives 1263.7 ms ->
23.1 ms at 1000 edges.

The host was shared with sibling worktrees during measurement, so the
load-bearing numbers above are serialized-byte counts, which are load
independent. Wall clock is reported alongside, not instead.

### The three limits are kept, not unified

The five sites measure different things, so one number would mean five different
real headrooms. Each is now a named constant carrying the headroom it leaves
below the true outer bound, `bounded_response` (`responses.py:115`): 262 121
bytes of `data` after the 23-byte envelope.

- `traversal.RESPONSE_BYTES = 200000` — excludes `frontier`, bounded by
  `max_nodes` UUIDs (~39 001 bytes). 62 121 spare.
- `search.RESPONSE_BYTES = 245000` — excludes `cursor`, bounded at 4096 base64
  chars. 17 121 spare.
- `graph.RECORD_RESPONSE_BYTES = 250000` — counts the whole `Graph.get` output.
  12 121 spare.
- `graph.ASSOCIATION_RESPONSE_BYTES = 245000` — items only; the view key and
  `next_cursor` live in the spare.

Accounting follows `_Matches.add` (`storage/fulltext.py:99-105`), an exact
per-item cost, not `_list_jobs`'s hardcoded 4096-byte envelope estimate. One
array member costs `len(canonical_json(member).encode("utf-8")) + 1`, which
over-counts a non-empty array by exactly one byte, so a page can stop at most
one byte per array earlier and can never exceed its declared limit.

### The truncation boundary did not move

Theoretically earlier by <=1 byte per array. Measured against `main`@74d3982's
`src/` under `PYTHONPATH`: the real-corpus traversal truncates at 1016 edges on
both trees, and twelve near-boundary item sizes across the three mocked sites
give identical item counts. The plan asked for this to be stated in
`CHANGELOG.md` rather than leaning on the existing 262144 ceiling assertion as a
control; it is, and the tests assert the moved boundary explicitly.

## E4 reached three of eleven ingress paths

The check is on the `RecordID` alias (`models.py:20`), not in
`validate_record_id`. Only `GetRequest.ids`, `DeleteRequest.ids`,
`ReindexRequest.ids` and the decoded-cursor `owner_id` reached that function;
`NodeRef`, `Mutation`, `SearchRequest`, `NeighborsRequest`, `JobsRequest` and
the six tool signatures enforced width or a bare `UUID(...)`, and `TargetRef.id`
enforced nothing but length. Placing the check in `validate_record_id` alone
would have made `kb_reindex` stricter than `kb_get`, which is what the plan
warned against.

Two deviations, both deliberate:

1. **`RecordID` / `StoredRecordID` split.** The alias was also on the response
   models, where the check is dead weight and measurably expensive:
   `NeighborsResult.model_validate` on a maximal payload measures 7.95 ms, and
   checking its ~12 000 identifiers costs 5.4 ms with a compiled grammar and
   39 ms with the `str(UUID(v))` roundtrip. Response models keep the width-only
   rule. Published tool input and output schemas are byte-identical, verified by
   diffing `list_tools()` across both trees.
2. **Two shapes for one rejection.** For the six tool-argument paths the refusal
   now happens one layer earlier, at FastMCP signature validation, as
   `is_error=True` with no structured envelope — exactly how a wrong-length
   identifier is refused today. Below the signatures it carries `INVALID`.
   Closing that needs `tools/*.py`, which this work does not own; it is stated
   in `CHANGELOG.md` rather than left for a reader to discover.

`validate_graph_id` uses a compiled grammar rather than the roundtrip
(3.3 us -> 0.45 us). Equivalence is not asserted by inspection:
`test_the_grammar_accepts_exactly_what_the_uuid_roundtrip_accepts` holds the two
against each other over a generated corpus of 100+ values — case variants,
hyphen-stripped, brace- and `urn:uuid:`-wrapped, and every single-character
substitution at every offset.

## B1 is solved by asking the catalog, not by restating it

`_cross_field_txt_record` no longer carries a grammar of its own. It diverts only
when the dedicated type's own `value` rule, read from the catalog at call time,
accepts the value. The two acceptances are therefore complementary by
construction: no value can be refused by both, none accepted by both, and the
rule cannot drift from the type it mirrors. `_ensure_cross_field_contract` fails
at import if a diverted tag names a type with no `value` rule.

Ten spellings had no home and now have one, among them
`v=spf1include:_spf.google.com ~all`. Nothing accepted before is rejected: the
new diversion set is a strict subset of the old one.

While there, two further doc corrections: `docs/tools/graph.md:92-101` described
a policy the code did not implement, and the `v=STSv1` sentence at `:300` was no
longer true of a leading tag.

## B5 is breaking, and it landed where measurement said it must

In `canonicalize_record` (`catalog.py:610`), not `identity.py` as the plan
guessed and not `catalog.py:1019`. The natural declarative form — adding
`"case_insensitive": ["name"]` to `_CAA_ORDER` — moves `CATALOG_FINGERPRINT`
from `d25e5c37...` to `50944b98...`. `SchemaGuard.check` compares that for exact
equality and this tree has no workspace upgrade path, so the declarative form
would brick every existing workspace. Folding only the hash input was rejected
separately: it would leave the identity saying one fact while the stored
`parameters[].name` changed underneath it.

Only ASCII names fold. `"K".lower()` is `"k"`, so folding a non-ASCII tag would
admit a spelling `_valid_caa_parameters` rejects today, and canonicalization
runs before validation and must not widen it.

The migration note was measured across versions, not reasoned: a v0.2.0
workspace built on the pre-fix tree and reopened on the fixed tree opens
normally, an existing fork does not merge itself, and a workspace holding only
the upper-case spelling gains a second edge on the first write after the
upgrade. Patching a stale edge by `id` does not repair it — `_preflight_row`
keeps the existing row's `key` for an id-patch, leaving folded properties under
a key that no longer matches them. Delete and re-write is the only correct
repair. `CATALOG_FINGERPRINT` is unchanged and the existing pin passes
untouched.

## P9: three fixed, one refused, one dropped

- **`

author: yurisismotto
body:
`cargo audit`, run for the first time as part of Security Certification v1 gate **SEC-DEPS-01**, found a real vulnerability. Per the certification brief, that **stops the certification** and gets fixed on a dedicated branch rather than written up as a finding.

```
Crate:     rustls
Version:   0.23.43
Title:     TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across
           encryption level boundaries
ID:        RUSTSEC-2026-0285
Severity:  5.3 (medium)
Solution:  Upgrade to >=0.23.45
```

## Why this one matters here

It is directly relevant, not incidental. OmniBridge speaks **TLS 1.3 and nothing else** — `core/src/tls.rs` builds both configs with `TLS13_ONLY`, and the `tls12` rustls feature is not even enabled, so the 1.2 code is not compiled in. An advisory about TLS 1.3 handshake message handling therefore lands on the code path **every peer session uses**.

SEC-9's letter only *requires* action on High/Critical, and this is Medium. Fixed anyway: it is a patch-version bump in the library the entire trust model rests on, and an evidence-backed exception would cost more to justify than the fix costs to apply.

## The change

The floor in `core/Cargo.toml` moves `0.23.43` → `0.23.45`, not just the lockfile, so a later resolution cannot quietly drop back below the fix.

```diff
-rustls = { version = "0.23.43", default-features = false, features = ["std", "ring"] }
+rustls = { version = "0.23.45", default-features = false, features = ["std", "ring"] }
```

Two lines in `core/Cargo.toml` (normal + dev-dependencies) and the lockfile. Nothing else.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo audit` | **clean**, 282 dependencies scanned |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -j 2 -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test --workspace -j 2` | **1016 passed, 0 failed**, 24 ignored |

## Scope

Deliberately minimal — this branch is the fix and nothing else.

Adding `cargo audit` to CI belongs with SEC-DEPS-01 in the certification itself, not here. But it is worth recording that **the gate found something real the first time it was ever run**, which is the argument for it being a standing CI check rather than a one-off certification step.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: maldoteth
body:
**Intent** — the site ships 110 UI locales and, on the two pages everything else is judged on, exactly one indexable language. Both said `lang="en"`, neither carried hreflang, and there was no localised URL, so all 110 translations were duplicates of the English page rather than variants of it. The content already exists; it just wasn't reachable.

**Constraints** — `?hl=` rather than a path prefix, for the reason already in the worker: four locale codes (de, ha, no, uk) are registered usernames whose profiles live at those paths. hreflang accepts ISO 639-1 codes only, so the 27 locales without one take the nearest standard language — those are UI strings, not crawler variants, and they stay out of the cluster. Both pages render outside the marketing branch, so each needed wiring of its own.

**Result** — `/` and `/docs` now answer `?hl=<code>` with a translated title, description, share card and `<html lang>`, self-canonical, naming every sibling plus `x-default`; 83 languages each. `/converter` and `/migrate-youtube` are wired too — their translations were already in the locale files with no route mapping. Watch Search Console's international targeting report for the new clusters, and check a `?hl=es` fetch of `/` after deploy returns Spanish head tags.

author: qigao
body:
Implements #47.

This is a focused editorial pass: replace prose-first motivation with small embedded C examples, without changing the three-Part architecture or adding new primitives.

### Chapter 1
Reviewed and intentionally unchanged. It already opens with repeated compare implementations, then macro reuse, then repeated type facts/X-Macro data. It already satisfies the embedded-C-first rule.

### Chapter 3 — callback → Callable
- now opens with a conventional `task_fn + void *ctx` callback API
- shows a concrete `square_ctx` callback before discussing signatures/capture/dispatch
- makes the problem explicit: once behavior is erased into `fn + void *`, the library no longer knows input/output/capture/composition semantics
- keeps plain function pointers as the baseline; Callable appears only when saved/composed/analyzed behavior needs more contract

### Chapter 10 — switch → typed Machine
- now opens with a complete hand-written connection-state `switch(state) / if(event)`
- shows exactly where Event payload typing, guards/actions, ambiguity, terminal rules, atomic commit and serialized ownership begin to escape ordinary switch conventions
- Machine is introduced as the smallest way to turn those repeated conventions into typed, validated program data
- Lean remains after the small-step semantic question exists

### Chapter 11 — shared mutable state → Actor
- now opens with a normal C11 `mtx_t` protected account object
- shows that the issue is not that mutexes are “wrong”, but that lifecycle/admission/stale references/shutdown/execution-context rules get repeated across public operations
- Actor is framed as changing the ownership model to many producers → bounded mailbox → one serialized mutable owner
- domain transition semantics remain owned by Chapter 10 Machine

### QA
- Chapter 1/3/10/11 each have exactly one H1
- numbered H2 sections remain continuous
- no label-only H2 headings introduced
- no new snapshot API claims were added; the new code is plain/conceptual C that motivates the later snapshot-grounded implementation sections

body: Fixes GigaChat OAuth/completion TLS failures on Windows when the OS/browser trusts a certificate chain that httpx/certifi does not. The packaged bridge now includes truststore and uses the native Windows certificate store by default. Custom PEM/CRT CA bundles still take precedence, and SSL verification is never disabled automatically. Error messages now explain how to handle antivirus/corporate interception if system trust still fails. Python/Ruff/Pytest, desktop TypeScript/Vite, packaged bridge smoke test and full Windows Tauri/NSIS build are green.

author: guillaumedespaux
body:
…upprime (essai d'abord)

Demandé le 2026-09-22 : « vérifie chaque entreprise ; rien trouvé, supprime-la ; sinon complète-la avec ce que tu trouves sur Pappers ou societe.com ; s'il y a déjà quelqu'un de rattaché, n'y touche pas ». Aucun SQL n'est joué d'ici (CLAUDE.md 2.1) : c'est un outil, que l'utilisateur lance sur le serveur, sur le modèle des scripts de chiffrement.

LA SOURCE : l'API officielle « Recherche d'entreprises » (annuaire des entreprises de l'État). Pappers et societe.com republient ces mêmes données (Sirene, registre national des entreprises) ; l'API les donne sans clé et son usage automatisé est permis, quand Pappers exige une clé payante et que societe.com interdit l'extraction de ses pages. Quatre cent soixante et onze fiches ne se vérifient pas à la main dans un navigateur.

LES RÈGLES (src/api/lib/registreEntreprises.js, tranchées par l'utilisateur) :
  · rien au registre : supprimée ; radiée : supprimée aussi (réponse de l'utilisateur) ;
  · active : complétée, seulement ce qui est VIDE (SIRET, NAF, adresse, code postal, ville, forme
    juridique, date de création, référent et sa fonction). Ni e-mail ni téléphone ni OPCO : aucun
    registre public ne les porte ;
  · sans SIRET, on ne complète que sans ambiguïté (une seule entreprise active de ce nom au même
    code postal) ; plusieurs candidates, un nom voisin, le même nom ailleurs, un SIRET faux, un
    établissement fermé d'une entreprise vivante : la fiche attend un humain ;
  · une panne du registre n'est JAMAIS un « introuvable ».

« RATTACHÉE », AU SENS LARGE : stagiaire, inscription, facture, document, vente de matériel, compte de représentant, cachet, ou stagiaire dont l'e-mail est celui de l'entreprise. Les clés étrangères sont en ON DELETE SET NULL : supprimer une fiche rattachée ne lèverait aucune erreur, elle détacherait en silence factures et documents. Une fiche rattachée ne part même pas au registre.

EN DEUX TEMPS, RÉVERSIBLE : l'essai (le défaut, parce que le script supprime) n'écrit rien et dépose plan et rapport ; --appliquer exécute CE plan (ce qu'on a relu), après avoir sauvegardé les fiches visées, et saute toute fiche modifiée ou rattachée depuis l'essai (empreinte, et gardes dans chaque écriture) ; --restaurer remet les supprimées et retire l'ajouté, sauf ce qui a été corrigé depuis.

Vérifié sur le vrai registre, sur des entreprises publiques : SIRET connu (complétée), SIREN seul (complétée, SIRET du siège), radiée (supprimée), inconnue (supprimée), homonymes au même code postal (à vérifier), déjà complète (rien). Quinze défauts réintroduits un à un : chacun fait virer entreprises-registre.test.js au rouge. Tests : 1707 — 1700 réussis, 0 échec, 7 ignorés. Lint : 0 erreur (l'outil, hors du périmètre du lint de l'API, a été vérifié par une copie).

author: aqm857886159
body:
# 测试：核心流程冒烟三道防线（empty 每次必跑 / 真实状态夹具 / 合后验 main）

## 解决什么

09-22 main 上同时出现三处故障：选中图片节点后生成浮框（composer）不出现、点卡片上的「2 版」不弹结果托盘、编组框删不掉。**当时 CI 全绿，一条测试都没报出来。**根因是画布 `data-dragging` 标记在平移后卡住（#836 `accc93b82` 已修）。

测试没拦住，是四件事叠在一起：

1. 核心走查 `tests/ux/node-params-and-version-pill.walk.mjs` **没有进任何 CI 套件**——写了等于没跑。
2. 分类器 `scripts/validation-policy.mjs` 只在改到 `src/workbench/generationCanvas` 时才开画布套件；这次坏的是**共享 CSS 开关**，于是没触发。
3. 所有走查都在隔离的空 profile、空项目里跑。用户实际是滚轮平移档、1280×800 小窗、Agent 面板开着、项目里几十张卡——这些状态一条都没覆盖。
4. PR 合入后，没有人在 main 的 merge SHA 上确认核心流程还是好的。

本 PR 不改产品行为（唯一例外见「单列的生产改动」），只把上面四条变成机器强制的三道防线。方案：[`docs/plan/2026-09-22-core-flow-smoke-three-defenses.md`](docs/plan/2026-09-22-core-flow-smoke-three-defenses.md)。

## 三道防线

### ① 核心冒烟每次必跑，分类器不许降档（对应原因 1、2）

- **唯一场景清单** `CORE_SMOKE_SCENARIOS`（`tests/ux/core-smoke/scenarios.mjs`）：`node-params-and-version-pill` + `canvas-drag-pan-gestures`。结构自检拒绝「只在某种夹具跑」这类后门字段，id/cases 必须规范，脚本不存在就红。
- **分类器**：`coreSmoke = !docsOnly`，**没有第二条降档路径**。fail-closed 分支（空 diff、删除/改名、手动全量）同样开启；main push 按真实 `before..after` 走同一条规则。改 `tests/ux/core-smoke/**` 算验证基础设施，自动全量。
- **CI**：新 job `Core Flow Smoke (empty)` / `(used)`（matrix，`fail-fast: false`），唯一开关是 `needs.scope.outputs.core_smoke`。汇总判定里，**只有 `core_smoke=false` 且 `reason=docs_only` 才接受 skipped**，其余一律要求 success。
- 依赖登记表 `needs.mjs`：写了未登记的依赖，runner 在**起进程之前**就报「缺依赖」而红，不会静默跳过（登记即放绿是假绿，R17）。

### ② 用真实状态的夹具跑两遍（对应原因 3）

前置状态不灌 store，而是**写 App 自己持久化的 `.nomi/project.json`，再从项目库卡片用 UI 打开**——加载、迁移、规范化、渲染走的都是真实路径，等于「用户打开昨天的项目」。被测动作全部由真实鼠标、键盘、滚轮驱动。

- `empty`：空白起点（1440×831）。
- `used`：24 张真实卡（取自仓库里的真实项目快照，含真实提示词、标题、多版本 history）、2 个带成员的编组 + 1 个空编组框、时间轴 clip 并展开、Agent 面板打开、1280×800。夹具打开项目后**用 UI 做前置断言**，任何一条不成立就红。
- `profile-copy`（仅本地，不进 CI）：`cp -R` 深拷贝用户真实 userData 与项目根，只在拷贝上跑、跑完删除，并对原库关键文件做指纹比对，原库零写入。
- runner 断言冒烟**前后 `git status --porcelain` 一字不差**，CI 上另外要求工作树为空。
- 两条走查都支持 zh-CN / en（本 PR 把 `canvas-drag-pan-gestures` 写死的 `zh-CN` 参数化，改成与 node-params 同一套约定）。

### ③ 合入后立刻验 main（对应原因 4）

`delivery:verify-merged` 读 merge SHA 相对第一父提交的 diff，用**同一个分类器**判断：

- 非纯文档 merge：**阻断档**的核心冒烟必须**恰好是 success**。skipped / neutral / 缺席一律拒绝，报错点名是哪一份、实际什么结论。非阻断档抄结论进收据的 `coreSmoke.advisory`，不参与判定。
- 纯文档 merge：不要求，收据写 `coreSmoke: { required: false, reason: "docs_only" }`。
- 纪律进了 `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `docs/release-process.md`：**上一个合入没有收据，就不合下一个**；冒烟红了**不自动回滚**，由人决定修还是 revert。

## `used` 暂为非阻断（2026-09-22 用户拍板）

交工前按验收门实测，结果分两半：

- **阳性对照通过**：把 `data-dragging` 的三个 owner 回退到 #836 之前，两种夹具都红 0/2，红的条目**逐条对上**用户报的三件事，`used` 还多抓到一条 `G6`。
- **`used` 不稳**：修复在位、**生产代码逐字未变**（`git diff -- src/ electron/` 为空）的前提下，`used` / zh-CN 连跑 5 次只有 1 次全绿。

三种失败全部出自下面「只记 TODO 的三条」里那几条**本 PR 没修的小窗布局问题**，归因依据是 Playwright 报出的拦截者 DOM 原文，不是推测：

| 失败 | 拦截者原文 | 归属 |
|---|---|---|
| 点「适应视图」超时 | `<div role="toolbar" data-batch-dock="true" aria-label="Canvas batch generation" …> subtree intercepts pointer events` | T-CV-19。**英文更容易撞**：`Images ×9` 比 `图片 ×9` 宽，居中的栏铺得更开 |
| `P4 第 1 版缩略图`点不到 | `它的中心点 {"x":85,"y":179,"width":11,"height":11} 上画的是 button.grid.size-8.min-h-8，不是它自己` | T-CV-20。卡被「适应视图」挤到左缘，托盘 clamp 回视口后与卡自己的浮动工具条相叠 |
| 关设置弹窗超时 | 等 `getByRole('dialog', { name: '设置' }).locator('[data-settings-close]')` | T-QA-21。走查的 `clickPastToasts` 兜底本身时序相关，会间歇失手 |

**拍板**：先落防线。`empty`（zh-CN / en）是阻断门；`used` 照跑、照传证据、红了照样亮红给人看，但不拉垮汇总判定、不拦合后收据。理由：一条 5 次绿 1 次的必过门会让后续每个 PR 和每张合入收据都押在掷骰子上，红灯一旦不可信人就开始绕过它——那正是本方案要根除的东西。

**升阻断条件**：T-CV-19 / T-CV-20 / T-QA-21 三条修完，且 `used` 连跑 5 次全绿（跟进项 T-QA-23）。
**怎么升**：只改 `scripts/validation-policy.mjs` 的 `CORE_SMOKE_BLOCKING_FIXTURES` 一处，CI 的 `continue-on-error` 与合后收据都从它派生。

## 单列的生产改动：⌘Z 归属（「用过的项目」夹具第一次跑就抓到的）

方案写明「生产代码原则上不动」，这是唯一的例外，因此单列：

**现象**（1280×800、时间轴展开）：在画布上删掉编组框后按 ⌘Z，什么都没回来。时间轴展开后它的 window 监听先注册，把 ⌘Z 吃成了时间轴撤销；去过一次预览页也一样，因为 keep-alive 的那条隐藏时间轴还在抢键。时间轴收起时同样的 ⌘Z 正常。**这是 main 上用户真的会遇到的正确性 bug。**

**修法**：`src/workbench/shortcutSurface.ts` 成为唯一的归属规则——看不见的面绝不认领快捷键；同屏两面时，归最近一次 pointerdown 落下的那一面。画布与时间轴两边的键盘门都改成先问它（`dispatchTimelineShortcut` 的 surface 参数是必填），原来画布单边的 `offsetParent` 检查删除。新增一个面只需要加 `data-shortcut-surface` 属性并调同一个函数；监听注册顺序不再决定结果。

根因合同：[`docs/fixes/2026-09-22-keyboard-shortcut-surface-ownership.root-cause.json`](docs/fixes/2026-09-22-keyboard-shortcut-surface-ownership.root-cause.json)（含门表）。单测：`src/workbench/shortcutSurface.test.ts`、`useCanvasShortcuts.test.ts`。

## 没改产品、只记进 TODO 的三条

| 现象 | 处理 | 登记 |
|---|---|---|
| 小窗下底部居中的批量生成栏压住左下角缩放条 | 走查像人一样先点 × 收起它 | T-CV-19 |
| 选中卡的浮框 / 结果托盘被停靠物挤得放不下，clamp 后盖住卡和握把 | 走查先收起碍事的两样 | T-CV-20 |
| 常驻的模型不可用警告 toast 浮在弹层之上，压住设置弹窗关闭钮 | 走查先点掉 toast | T-QA-21 |

三条现在都**挡着 `used` 升阻断**，已在各自备注里注明并附证据路径。花钱路的冒烟场景由「Draft PR 代码审查与整合」会话登记（T-QA-22）；本 PR **刻意不放占位条目**——占位就是空跑的绿。

## 与 main 的合并：`real-media-fixtures.json` 按并集解

合 `origin/main`（#839 等 20 个提交）时 `tests/ux/real-media-fixtures.json` 冲突。两边都是**纯追加、条目零重叠**：main 加 `shot-cut-aug12-hevc` / `video-fastcut-derived` 与 `shot-cut-coverage` 类；本分支加 `video-ai-shot-640x360` / `image-ai-shot-frame-png` 与 `core-smoke` 类；`requiredClasses` 两边都没动。

解法是并集，并且是**程序化合出来的**：先断言「同名但内容不同的条目为空」和「`requiredClasses` 两边一致」，不成立就停；再以 main 那版为底插入本分支独有的条目；最后回验两边条目一个都没丢。`check:real-media-fixture` 与 `check:quality-gate-workflow` 合后都绿。`package.json` 两边各加一行 script（`test:core-smoke` / `test:real-media`），git 自己 auto-merge，已复验两条 script 都在且逐字正确。

**顺带一提，#839 和本 PR 的理由是互相印证的**：#839 把真素材腿分出自己的车道，理由是「CI runner 上没有那 1.38GB 素材，放进来只会让每个 PR 红在一件与改动无关的事上，红灯一旦不可信，人就开始绕过它」。本 PR 为 `repoPath` 素材做的偏差、以及把 `used` 降为非阻断，用的是同一条推理——**一条不可信的红灯比没有红灯更糟**。两边是同一个判断在两处落地，不是打架。

## 对拍板的一处偏差（等确认）

用户拍板「只用 `NOMI_REAL_MEDIA_DIR` 里登记过的真实素材」，同时要求每个 PR 都跑。但 CI 上没有那 1.38 GB 素材，而缺素材必红（这个行为是对的，不许 skip），两条放一起冒烟在 CI 上会恒红。

处理：登记表新增一类 **`repoPath` 素材**，指向公开仓库里**已有的真实 AI 镜头** `tests/ux/fixtures/real-shot-640x360.mp4`（09-06 起就被 `editing-real-user-pass` 等走查当真实素材用）。缺文件照样红，门岗照样按身份扫描，并新增「repoPath 与 relativePath 互斥、文件必须在仓库里」两条判据。备选是把用户的 4K 私人素材放进公开仓库——有隐私问题，不采用。代价：冒烟测不到 4K HEVC 的解码成本，那条仍由性能腿负责。

## 验收门逐条对应证据

全部原始数据：[`docs/evidence/2026-09-22-core-smoke-negative-control/`](docs/evidence/2026-09-22-core-smoke-negative-control/)

| 门 | 结果 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|
| 1. 阳性对照：回退 #836 的生产修复后两遍必须红 | ✅ **通过** | 按文件回退三个 owner 到 `195bf3a2c`（−59/+6，未提交，跑完恢复、树验回原值）。`empty` **0/2**（122.2s，node-params 13 条失败）、`used` **0/2**（131.5s，14 条）。红的条目逐条对上三件报障：composer（P1/P2 五条）、「2 版」托盘（P3/P4/P5）、编组框（F2 三条），外加根因 G2/G3；`used` 多一条 G6 |

author: tkaunlaky-e6
body:
## Problem

Freshworks Power BI queries that `SELECT … FROM <view>` where the view uses `EXPLODE(FROM_JSON(col, 'array<struct<…>>'))` fail at parse time with:

```
Lexical error at line 1, column 14. Encountered: "\" (92), after : ""
```

(Confirmed in the planner logs — the query is transpiled `databricks → E6`, then `tryParseWithE6` dies on the backslash.)

## Root cause

`FROM_JSON`'s 2nd argument is a **type descriptor**, not a normal string value. The engine parses it at SQL-parse time via `DataTypeParser.parseJsonSchemaString()`, which spins up a **`JsonSchema()` sub-parser over the raw string body** (so it resets to line 1). That lexer skips whitespace but has **no rule for a backslash**.

The views write the schema multi-line for readability, so the source string literal contains real newlines. e6 escapes those newlines as `\n` (backslash-n) on output, and the sub-parser dies on the `\` — at **column 14**, which is exactly the char after `array<struct<` (13 chars).

## Fix

Whitespace is insignificant inside a type descriptor, so when rendering a `FROM_JSON` string arg (`anonymous_sql`), collapse it with `" ".join(val.split())`. That drops the newlines that would otherwise be backslash-escaped, so `array<struct<\n    id:string…` becomes `array<struct< id:string…` — backslash-free, and the sub-parser skips the spaces and derives the identical type. Already single-line schemas are unchanged (idempotent), so nothing else in the workload shifts.

## Tests

Adds `test_from_json_schema_newlines`: a multi-line schema transpiles to a clean single-line, backslash-free descriptor; a single-line schema is left untouched. The existing `test_json_extract` (`value:` → `` `value` `` rewrite) still passes.

`make check` is green — style (ruff, ruff-format, mypy), `test` (1010) and `test-rs` (1010).

author: valstan
body:
## Summary

Шаг 7 из девяти в пакете владельца 22.09 (план — `docs/plans/owner-package-2026-09-22.md`).

Владелец: «модуль печати бирок на двигатель: выбрать несколько двигателей, бирки распечатались на листе А4 — 6, 4 или 2 штуки. Проработай все три варианта и сделай в печатной форме, чтобы оператор мог выбрать. Бирки растягивай, чтобы весь лист заполнить, шрифты увеличивай-уменьшай. Обозначения — меньше шрифт, наименования и номера — больше».

- **Три раскладки:** 6 это 2 на 3, 4 это 2 на 2, 2 это 1 на 2. Высота ячейки считается от печатной области листа, а не подбирается на глаз, поэтому лист заполняется целиком в любом варианте.
- **Кегли** собраны одной таблицей констант: чем меньше бирок на листе, тем крупнее номер и марка. Номер двигателя самый крупный, подписи полей мелкие и приглушённые.
- **Листы режет сам генератор**, а не браузерная сетка: число листов детерминировано и совпадает с тем, что диалог показывает оператору.
- **Диалог** с переключателем и живым предпросмотром листа А4, счётчиками выбранных двигателей и листов. Последний выбранный вариант запоминается.
- **Печать по выделенным строкам**, а не по фильтру — этим бирки отличаются от печати этикеток рядом. При пустом выделении программа говорит об этом, а не печатает молча весь отфильтрованный список. Точки входа: кнопка в тулбаре, пункт контекстного меню для выделенных, кнопка «Бирка» в карточке двигателя.

## Про две даты, которых нет в базе

Владелец сам предложил их вычислять. Окончание ремонта по договору — дата поступления плюс срок ремонта контракта, он приехал шагом 5. Дата окончательной технической приёмки считается от него отдельной именованной константой запаса, сейчас 10 дней: меняется одним движением, если владелец назовёт другое число.

Пустое значение печатается прочерком: на бирке пустое место читается как «забыли». Реально пустыми бывают договор (у двигателей без него) и обе вычисленные даты, когда не заполнена дата поступления — считать не от чего.

## Test plan

- `pnpm -r typecheck` (7 пакетов), `pnpm -r lint` — зелёные. Тесты electron-app **1209** — зелёные.
- Новое: 7 тестов генератора (6 бирок при варианте 6 дают один лист, при 4 — два, при 2 — три; 7 бирок при 6 — два листа; все поля и все четыре даты попадают в лист, включая вычисленную приёмку; пустые значения дают прочерки; три раскладки дают строго растущие кегли; сетка и высота ряда считаются от печатной области). Плюс проверки в стороже списка: набор берётся из выделения, а не из фильтра, и этикетки по-прежнему от фильтра.

author: sirtheo
body:
## Problem

Of the three release targets, `dot` declares a bundle and `window` does not, so releasing the window leaves a bare `bin/sailor-desktop`: a file nothing launches by name. What a person opens is an application bundle, and no release has ever written one — the bundle in use was assembled by hand on 04/09, outside the loop entirely. The cost is measurable: the stamp `state/window-binary-commit` still names a commit of 05/09, while 383 commits touching `desktop/` have been merged since, and the CLI target was released the same morning as this was found.

No issue: No issue covers it: the gap was found by measuring why a released window trails the trunk, not from the register.

## Behaviour

The `window` target now declares the bundle it needs: `bin/Sailor.app`, carrying `desktop/src-tauri/bundle/Info.plist` and the icns beside the binary and signed like the dot's, with the binary installed at `Contents/MacOS/sailor-desktop`. The plist lives out of `src-tauri/` itself, where Tauri's own bundler would merge it into what `cargo tauri build` produces. Nothing else names `bin/sailor-desktop`, so no caller changes.

## Verification

`every_bundle_names_the_binary_it_starts` is new: it reads the plist each bundled target carries and refuses a `CFBundleExecutable` that is not the file installed in `Contents/MacOS` — the failure that assembles, signs and installs a bundle which opens nothing. Both mutants go red with the fact named: a plist starting `Sailor`, and a binary placed outside `Contents/MacOS`. Before writing the judge I assembled the bundle by hand from a debug binary and signed it with the same gesture: `codesign --verify` reports valid on disk and satisfying its designated requirement, and opening it starts the process. `cargo test -p release --lib` 25 green, `every_release_target_names_a_real_binary` 4 green, the comment ratchet 7/7 with the `release` seed lowered from 411 to 410.

## Use case
Copy selected text from a PowerPoint (.pptx) slide and paste it into Lumi to edit or use in a prompt. PowerPoint places multiple representations of the same selection on the clipboard: plain text, rich text/HTML, and PNG/bitmap images. The reported clipboard sample contained valid Unicode text alongside image formats, but Lumi attached an image instead of inserting the text.

**Expected:** paste the text into the composer at the caret/selection, without adding an image attachment.

## Fix
- Move the existing nonempty-text insertion block before image decoding in `OnClipboardPasteRequested`.
- Reuse the existing text insertion, file handling, and image decoding paths; no new abstractions, dependencies, settings, or Strata changes.
- Preserve Lumi chat-context and file paste priority. Image-only payloads (including screenshots) still attach normally.

## Validation
- The mixed text/image regression reproduced the original bug before the fix.
- Debug build succeeded. All **8 focused tests passed** (5 clipboard cases plus 3 existing composer tests).
- Clipboard coverage: text + image, plain text, image-only, empty text + image, and file + text + image. Also verifies selection replacement and image file decoding.
- Isolated Debug Lumi verified via Lumi/Avalonia MCP: a native Windows clipboard containing both text and an image inserted the exact text with no pending attachment; **zero binding errors**. No message sent. Restored the original clipboard.
- `git diff --check` passed.

```powershell
dotnet test tests\Lumi.Tests\Lumi.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ChatViewClipboardTests|FullyQualifiedName~StrataChatComposerSendTests"
```

Local NuGet.org TLS access failed, so restore used the existing local package cache and vendored SDK via a session-only config; repository dependency configuration is unchanged. Existing build warnings remain.

Based on `origin/main` at `043a852`; branch pushed through the configured `yanivlavi` remote.

- Fresh `origin/main` fetch and GitHub main both resolve to `043a852da994f29e80a2794e5f61f1efa5aa144e`, already this branch's base. `git rebase origin/main` therefore completed as a no-op; no artificial history rewrite.
- Investigated original Windows CI run `35717946181`, job `106713768863`. All five clipboard cases passed, but their Skia renderer shared a test host with drawing-free headless tests, causing four `ChatMotionTests` failures (`HeadlessPlatformTypeface` to `SkiaTypeface`) and a later host hang/abort.

- Validation after the CI correction: **Release build succeeded**, **5/5 real-image clipboard cases passed**, **3/3 composer cases passed**, and the **updated affected CI batch passed 225 tests with 2 existing opt-in skips**. All three test runs used fresh hosts as CI now does. Test-project build has existing warnings, no errors.
- UI/runtime code is unchanged by this follow-up and the no-op rebase, so no new live Lumi instance was launched. The original MCP verification above still describes the same production code. No daily-driver instance, profile, or settings touched.
- Strata recorded and checked-out revision: `efffea664ce6f0142f1bac2054d0d38b35c077ec`.

**Plan**: [349, One path editor, and a goal that never needs renaming](https://github.com/UpSpeech/upspeech/blob/main/plans/349-one-path-editor-and-a-goal-that-never-needs-renaming.md), stages 1 and 2 of 4. Tracking issue: UpSpeech/upspeech#270.

The therapist's learning path tab had two implementations of the same screen. This is the translation half of collapsing them to one.

## Added

- `learning_path.editor.no_steps_title` and `no_steps_description`, the empty state for a path that exists with no steps. That case previously fell into the milestone branch and drew 43 greyed-out curriculum steps the patient has no relationship to.
- `learning_path.editor.rename_goal_hint`, screen-reader text pointing at the rename button now beside the goal title.
- `learning_path.editor.move_goal`, the label for the reduced goal menu.
- `learning_path.goal_actions_batch`, the per-goal batch menu.

## Removed

- `learning_path.editor.add_goal` and `learning_path.editor.new_goal_name`. The Add a goal button wrote a row titled "New goal" and left the therapist to find Rename in a submenu. The composer already creates a named goal in the same call that writes the step.
- `learning_path.editor.write_step`, merged into `editor.add_step`. Two labels opened the same modal.
- `learning_path.milestone_actions`, whose menu is gone.

## Changed

`learning_path.editor.goal_settled` drops its rename clause: "started, so it cannot be renamed or moved" becomes "started, so it cannot be moved". Settling protects the order of the path. It has no reason to freeze what a goal is called, and today it is what makes an accidental "New goal" permanent.

## Benchmark PR check

One updating table. Correctness gates the check; performance is advisory.

- [x] Measure the PR's JVMD revision only in ordinary runs.
- [x] Reuse compatible main results; never rerun main for a PR.
- [x] Keep compact results in GitHub Checks, outside git.
- [x] One renderer for the check, Actions summary and updating PR comment.
- [x] Green/red signed deltas; failed results have no improvement percentage.
- [x] Preserve completed run/attempt records; guard against stale publishers.
- [x] Separate read-only measurement from trusted publication.
- [x] Keep JDTLS, attribution and overhead as manual modes.
- [x] Remove dashboard/bundle flow, obsolete test launcher and all nested READMEs.
- [x] Reporting regressions pass locally and in GitHub.
- [ ] Activate the publisher on main.
- [ ] Verify live comment updates, baseline reuse and failure publication after activation.

### Current revision

`a8c0cdbf9e7d3f2760947de0fc5bac089217360d`, tree `ed30581ab9c2181a98771e8ac69770148ed5e509`.

Follow-up: deleted all five nested READMEs and the root Performance section; repaired deleted-guide links. API documentation remains. Distributions now builds merged PRs to main, not open PR updates or unmerged closures; version-tag releases remain supported. Documentation and CI changes are separate commits. API schema verification and deleted-reference checks passed; merged-event execution awaits merge.

All CI passed before the documentation/trigger-only follow-up: [Measurement](https://github.com/maxjay/jvmd/actions/runs/35754888596), [Checkpoints](https://github.com/maxjay/jvmd/actions/runs/35754888511), [Distributions](https://github.com/maxjay/jvmd/actions/runs/35754888836), and [Merge Review](https://github.com/maxjay/jvmd/actions/runs/35754888790). Measurement verified all 1,725 JVMD requests across five processes and passed 15 reporting/harness tests.

### Behaviour

Main publishes reusable check records. PR runs select the nearest compatible result in the searched base history. Missing/incompatible baselines show unavailable, without inventing a delta.

The comment is updated in place for the current head/run. Each completed attempt retains its own check record. Agents read the JSON in the check's `output.text`; the API link is in the table footer. No routine archive download.

GitHub check retention: 400 days, followed by 10 days archived. Seven-day artifacts are only the internal JSON transfer and explicitly requested profiles. No generated branch, release assets, source-tree results, new service or dependencies.

### Validation and activation

15 local tests pass, covering independent oracles, partial references, sample attribution, advisory colours, incompatible baselines, invalid measurements, missing-result failures, reruns, immutable records and stale attempts/heads.

**GitHub only activates `workflow_run` when the publisher exists on the default branch.** This is why end-to-end automatic publication cannot yet run from this unmerged PR. Its trusted code deliberately comes from main, never from the measured PR. Measurement CI passed on the published revision; publication acceptance remains unchecked until activation. A real rerun of the preceding revision was cancelled when superseded by the newer head, as intended. Live rerun/comment and failure-publication checks still require activation.

### Benchmark implementation reduction from `08164d7` (before the follow-up below)

- Production/integration: unchanged.
- Benchmark infrastructure: +289 / −325 lines across 8 files.
- Tests: +81 / −63 lines across 3 files.
- Durable documentation: +69 / −127 lines in the existing guide.
- Generated evidence in source: unchanged; none added.

**Net executable reduction: 18 lines**, separately from 58 documentation lines. The reduction is modest because safe publication and baseline selection replace the removed presentation code.

Deleted: `dashboard.mjs`, its obsolete tests, the separate `test.py` launcher, dashboard aggregation/link construction, and per-request estimates derived from process samples. Normal CI no longer downloads JDTLS or automatically profiles/runs overhead experiments. Existing production correctness tests and standard JFR/Perfetto exports remain.



Follow-up reduction: documentation +4 / −364 lines across 8 files (5 deleted); workflow +6 / −10 lines in one file. Production, benchmark implementations, tests and generated evidence unchanged.

### Review fixes

Six confirmed findings fixed: publisher coverage/count invariants, shim workflow triggers, URI normalization (including readiness diagnostics), nested dispatch tracing, task-exit sampling, and hidden project configuration identity. JDTLS URI finding disproved by a fresh pinned-server run: attached sources use `/offset-1.jar/external/Offset.java`; `Offset.class` is in the query. Regression checks retain source-content, declaration-range and version verification.

21 Python tests and both enabled/disabled Java tracing tests passed. Fresh space/Unicode-path comparison: 60/60 requests correct per server; independent verification passed with equal fixture identities. The earlier JDTLS readiness timeout remains in local run output. [Current measurement CI](https://github.com/maxjay/jvmd/actions/runs/35757008437) passed build, regression tests, measurement and independent verification; other CI remains pending/in progress.

Review-fix growth: production instrumentation +1/−1 (1 file); benchmark/CI +50/−13 (6 files); tests +96/−0 (3 files); docs/generated files unchanged. No dependencies or new executable paths.

### CI simplification

Removed Merge Review and its base rebuild/component artifact job. Ordinary PR workflows are Tests and Benchmarks. Pinned toolchains and third-party Maven artifacts are cached; local dev.jvmd artifacts, compiled outputs and benchmark workspace state are excluded. Cache misses still perform normal downloads and builds. Publisher/release name references updated. YAML/shell syntax and all 21 harness tests pass; first cache-populating CI run is pending. author: hyperpolymath
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `CodeQL Security Analysis` + `Hypatia Security Scan` `startup_failure` that has blocked both workflows on `main` since 2026-09-22 03:06 UTC (first failing run: #94's branch; every run since).

## Root cause

The grouped dependabot bump **#94** moved `github/codeql-action` **v4.38.0 → v4.38.1** in `codeql.yml` (`init`/`analyze`) and `hypatia-scan.yml` (`upload-sarif`). Since that merge, every run of those two workflows fails at **startup** (0 jobs ever dispatch — no job logs exist). The same signature now reproduces estate-wide, keyed exactly on the codeql-action version:

| repo | ref | latest codeql/hypatia status |
|---|---|---|
| vexometer | `@v4.38.1` tag | 🔴 startup_failure (since 09-21) |
| hypatia | `@1c5b675` (4.38.1 SHA) | 🔴 startup_failure |
| rsr-template-repo | `@1c5b675` (4.38.1 SHA) | 🔴 startup_failure (since ~09-15) |
| **nexia-list** | `@v4.38.1` tag | 🔴 startup_failure (since #94) |
| affinescript | `@v4.38.0` tag | ✅ green 09-21 |
| boj-server | `@v4.34/4.38.0` | ✅ green 09-21 |
| deed-ecosystem | `@b96794f0` (4.38.0 SHA) | ✅ green 09-21 |

The v4.38.1 **tag object exists** (peeled `1c5b675653bb…`) — verified via `ls-remote`/API — but GitHub refuses it at workflow startup (tag *and* SHA form, per hypatia/rsr-template). Byte-identical replicas of the failing workflows under a **new path** on a scratch branch *do* start and execute, so the YAML/content itself is valid; v4.38.1 resolution is rejected by GitHub's actions catalog/policy layer on default-branch-evaluated runs. Exact GitHub-internal reason is not visible from the API (startup_failure runs expose no error text); the behavioural fix is unambiguous: stay on the last green release.

## Changes

- `codeql.yml`, `hypatia-scan.yml`: pin `codeql-action/*` to `@b96794f015dfd88f77b49b1c93e0fa7110f94c63` (**v4.38.0**, SHA-pinned — satisfies this repo's `sha_pinning_required` policy and matches the green `deed-ecosystem` configuration).
- `actions.lock`: re-keyed to the SHA pin. This also fixes today's **`Workflow security linter`** failure ("lock lists github/codeql-action@v4.38.0 but no workflow uses it") — dependabot bumped `uses:` without regenerating the lock; the estate's locked-actions gate caught it exactly as designed.
- `dependabot.yml`: `ignore` rule for `github/codeql-action@4.38.1` so the daily grouped actions update can't re-merge the same broken bump overnight.

## Verification

The PR itself is the live test: `pull_request` runs of CodeQL and Hypatia on this branch should **dispatch jobs** (rather than startup_failure). Watch runs above. If either still fails at startup, the remaining levers are owner-side (delete+recreate workflow files to clear the poisoned registration, or repo Settings → Code security / Actions policy review), but the version discriminator evidence says this rollback is the fix.

## Follow-ups (estate-wide, not in this PR)

- Same rollback needed in **vexometer**, **hypatia**, **rsr-template-repo**, and any other repo that merged the 4.38.1 actions bump (dependabot auto-merge reproduced the break within hours per repo).
- Standards canonical `codeql-reusable.yml` / `hypatia-scan-reusable.yml` currently pin the **4.38.1 SHA** (`1c5b675…`) and should be re-pinned to v4.38.0 SHA until upstream clears 4.38.1.

---

*Rollback of the codeql-action portion of #94; all other bumps in #94 are untouched. See issue #49 for the CI-honesty context — this is precisely the class of failure that used to be invisible.*

The macOS computer-use provider created a temporary socket directory before setting permissions, writing its token, and launching the helper. If any setup step failed synchronously, the directory remained behind. Setup failures now remove it before returning the error.

author: rogeriochaves
body:
## What a search does when the model behind it is missing

A sentence classified as a judgement was rewritten into a judge question by the project's FAST model. When that model was missing or refused, the router quoted the sentence and searched it as a literal phrase, silently: `frustrated users` became `"frustrated users"`, "Nothing matches these filters", and nothing on screen said why. The server already computed a `fellBackFrom` signal for exactly this and no client read it.

Two changes.

**The judgement still runs.** A sentence that describes a judgement describes one whether or not a model is there to sharpen it, so the fallback is now the sentence judged exactly as typed, the way a chip typed by hand already is: the question as it stands, no criteria, no model between Enter and the estimate. Matching those words literally is a different search that answers a question no one asked.

**One line under the bar says what happened.** What the sentence was read as, which of the two model problems it was (none connected, or the one connected failed), the handled code it failed with, and that the words were used as typed. Beside it, a button to the model provider settings, which can be dismissed per project; the line stays, because it is how a reader learns the search ran degraded. The question is not repeated there, since the chip and the progress bar over the table both already carry it. The once-per-page-load "connect a model for smarter search" popover goes with it: one affordance, attached to the search that just ran, instead of a popover that fired once and then went quiet for the rest of the session.

A router call that fails outright now also says so, with a warning toast, instead of requoting the words with no explanation.

The router's log line names the cause inline (handled code, model, status). The log collector ships only the `msg` field, so a cause carried beside the message never leaves the cluster. On the stack below that line reads:

```
Instant Eval question could not be written; judging the sentence as typed
(ai_query_provider_error openai/gpt-5.6-luna-retired openai HTTP 404)
```

## Test Connection sends a real generation

Same shape of problem on the settings page. Listing models proves a key is shaped right and reaches the vendor, and nothing else:

- an account with no credit left lists its models happily and refuses the first completion, so the row said "Connection works"
- a plan-billed lane with no listing endpoint (Codex on an OpenAI account) was reported as "can't be tested automatically" while working perfectly

Test Connection now sends one generation of one token down the same road the product uses at runtime: the nlpgo proxy for the OpenAI-compatible lanes, the AI gateway for Codex. It runs the cheapest chat model the provider lists, against the credential on the row that was asked about rather than whatever the provider key collapses to when an organization row and a project override both exist. A credential the listing already refused is not asked twice.

Two new coded refusals, because they are two different things to do about it: `provider_out_of_credit` (top it up) and `provider_usage_limit_reached` (wait for the window). Neither sends the reader off to replace a key that is fine.

A third verdict was wrong until the dogfood caught it: a generation that never reached the provider was reported as a refusal, saying "it answered, but wouldn't confirm the key" about an address that was never opened. The rule was matching words in the failure message, and the AI SDK says `Cannot connect to API` where undici says `fetch failed`. It now decides on whether anything came back, an HTTP status or a response body, which also covers a ping that runs out of its 20 second budget.

## Deployment impact

No migration, no new configuration. Test Connection now spends one token per click on chat providers, inside the per-organization egress budget that already gated it.

## Dogfooded

On a local stack against a project of 5,310 traces, with the AI gateway running so the Codex lane has something to reach, and the project's search model pointed at one the vendor answers 404 for.

The sentence is judged exactly as typed, one line says what it was read as and what failed, and the judgement finds what it was asked for: 63 of the first 500 rows, every one a customer complaining.

![judged as typed, with the line and the way to fix it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b31f0238-bcb7-4f01-b7e5-86d0c58f878a)

![63 matched while judging](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a083dd5-4ebb-4d1c-9bc1-5c850f7cc4bc)

Test Connection on the Codex row, which before this change reported that it could not be tested:

![Codex verified by a real generation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8608cba4-e8d9-47ad-a86c-f653111aefc6)

The full run, the dismissal sticking, and the rest of the stills are in [this comment](https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/pull/8268#issuecomment-5777570065).

## Verification

- `pnpm test:unit` on the search router and the model providers, `pnpm test:component` on the search bar and the Explorer page
- `pnpm typecheck:all`
- `check:feature-parity` on `specs/traces-v2/search.feature` and `specs/model-providers/credential-validation.feature`


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added Test Connection support for model providers, with clearer results for invalid credentials, unreachable providers, insufficient credit, and usage limits.
  - Search now shows in-context notices when model-assisted interpretation is unavailable, with model configuration guidance and dismissal controls.
  - Search fallbacks distinguish between no configured model and model failures.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved fallback behavior and warning messages when search routing fails.
  - Questions can now be evaluated as written when model-generated criteria cannot be created.

body:
## What this adds

**Coach Voice** for Spread Out! — the device's built-in speech engine (Web Speech API) reads the coach aloud, so kids who are still learning to read can play on their own. Nothing leaves the device and it works offline, keeping the game's "we collect nothing" promise intact. (Same approach as Football IQ's read-aloud, so the two games match.)

- Speaks the in-play coach hints, throttled so it says one useful line every few seconds instead of chattering as hints flip
- Speaks the position prompts in Where Do I Stand?, the kickoff formation lesson (interrupting anything in progress), and celebrations (goals, perfect passes, stars, level-ups)
- 🗣️ toggle as a menu pill and an in-game top-bar button, remembered on the device; mute silences the voice too
- Coach Corner gets "Read aloud" buttons for the practice plan and tips, which work even when the toggle is off (explicit tap)
- Emoji are stripped and dashes/line breaks turned into natural pauses; picks a natural English voice when the device has one
- On devices without speech support the controls hide and the game plays as before

Only `spread-out/` changes (game file + PRD note). No deployment changes.

## Testing

Automated browser runs with the speech engine stubbed: intro and hints are spoken at a calm pace (2–3 lines per 8 s of play), emoji never reach the voice, position prompts and the kickoff lesson speak, toggling off is silent and persists across reload, read-aloud reads a card's text without its button label, and a browser with no speech support shows no errors. Zero page errors across all game modes.

author: grintzdel
body:
> Empilée sur #52, elle-même sur #51. GitHub rebasera les bases au fil des merges.

L'application mobile n'a pas d'écran d'inscription : on y arrive avec un compte, qui a ou n'a pas d'adhésion. Sans adhésion, l'API ferme la semaine de la machine — et il fallait ouvrir le navigateur pour en sortir. Cette PR porte `/bienvenue` sur mobile, et montre ses ateliers dans Compte.

## Ce qui bouge

- Écran `/onboarding` : choisir un atelier dans l'annuaire trié par proximité, cocher ses pratiques, rejoindre. Mêmes deux règles que le web — un atelier, au moins une pratique.
- Compte : « Mes ateliers » (`GET /me/ateliers`), ou un encart pour en rejoindre un quand la liste est vide. Chaque ligne pousse vers la fiche.
- Annuaire : le même encart en tête quand `memberships` est vide, parce que c'est là qu'on comprend pourquoi la semaine est fermée.
- `IIdentityPort` gagne `myAteliers()` — `user.memberships` ne porte qu'un `atelierId` et un rôle, jamais un nom.

## Trois choix, dits explicitement

**Rejoindre n'est pas une garde.** Un `Stack.Protected` sur `memberships.length === 0` enfermerait un membre dans un formulaire sans issue. C'est un encart, pas un péage.

**`SessionProvider` sait se rafraîchir.** Sans cela `user.memberships` reste périmé après l'adhésion : l'encart ne disparaîtrait pas et la semaine resterait fermée jusqu'au prochain démarrage. L'adhésion appelle `refresh()` et invalide **tout** le cache TanStack — rejoindre un atelier change ce que l'application entière a le droit de voir, pas une liste.

**`AtelierHttpAdapter` cesse d'être entièrement public.** L'annuaire et les fiches restent anonymes ; `POST /onboarding/complete` part avec le Bearer. C'est le même découpage en deux clients que le web, et `CLAUDE.md` est corrigé — il affirmait le contraire.

## Ce que je n'ai pas fait

Les adapters in-memory d'`apps/mobile` ne sont construits nulle part. Plutôt que de les remplir de fiction pour satisfaire les deux nouvelles méthodes de port, je les ai implémentés fidèlement (`seedAteliers` sur l'identité, comme `seedAvailability` sur le booking). Le ménage de ce code mort reste à faire, ailleurs.

## Vérifié

`pnpm check` vert. `expo export --platform ios` passe, et `/onboarding` apparaît dans les routes typées générées — la coquille est bien vue par le router.

Les écrans ne sont pas testés, comme les sept autres.

author: chandra-glitch
body:
## Problem

IRONWALL produces risk measurements, but `main` has no deterministic way to compare selected non-negative metrics with approved upper bounds. Manual comparisons can obscure utilization, remaining headroom, and breaches—information the ECB describes as part of effective risk dashboards: https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/ecb/pub/pdf/ssm_supervisory_statement_on_governance_and_risk_appetite_201606.en.pdf

## Solution

- add a generic upper-bound risk-limit evaluator for selected metrics
- report utilization, signed headroom, per-metric breach state, and an aggregate status
- keep equality at 100% utilization without treating it as an exceedance
- sort results deterministically and preserve strict-JSON output when a ratio exceeds floating-point range
- reject invalid names, missing observations, non-finite inputs, negative values, and non-positive limits
- document units, horizon matching, governance assumptions, and limitations
- add focused regression tests

The change is isolated to three new files and does not overlap the files changed by open PRs #2–#24.

## Checks performed

- `python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"`
- `ruff check .`
- `ruff format --check .`
- `pytest` — 72 passed
- `python -m build` — source distribution and wheel built successfully (the build frontend was installed only in the validation environment because PR #5 already owns the pending development-dependency change)
- installed-wheel import, strict-JSON, and CLI smoke test
- 1,000 deterministic invariant cases

Prepared by the scheduled IRONWALL improvement workflow. This PR is intentionally left unmerged for review.

author: ztein
body:
Three decision records from today's quality review of the March 2026 PPR run (three models, two figures read by hand against the image):

- **T-082** — the quality measure is *utility*: how many factual questions (incl. figure-only facts) a downstream LLM answers correctly from figmark's output. A preference judge on this corpus tracked description length and called panel-naming pedantry a factual error; wrong criterion for this product.
- **T-087** (new, High) — the diagram prompt is a screen-reader artefact: all three models spent a section on colours/line styles and all three missed the main scenario's 2027 dip. Figures are also read without their caption / source line / referring sentence, which is the author's own reading instruction.
- **T-088** (new, High) — vector charts are rasterised and values guessed from pixels while the PDF holds the series as polylines (41 on the probed page) and the ticks as positioned text. Bench first: share of the PPR's 49 regions that are reconstructible.

author: mkm29
body:
## Description

Renovate now updates the digest along with the tag for Docker images pinned as `image:tag@sha256:<digest>`.

- **`zarf.yaml` `images:`**: capture an optional `currentDigest`. Previously a digest-pinned ref was misparsed (`depName=image:tag@sha256`, `currentValue=<digest hex>`), so lookups failed.
- **Helm value override (`# renovate: image=`)**: capture an optional digest. Also fixes the tag being read as the digest hex, single-quoted values keeping a trailing `'`, and a trailing comment containing `:` producing an empty tag.
- **Playwright (`tasks/test.yaml`)**: capture an optional digest so tag bumps no longer leave a stale digest.
- **New packageRule**: `autoReplaceGlobalMatch: false` for `custom.regex` Docker deps, so a hex-only tag (e.g. `17`) isn't also replaced inside the digest ([docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#autoreplaceglobalmatch)).

Renovate's default auto-replace swaps `currentDigest` for `newDigest`, so no `autoReplaceStringTemplate` is needed. Images without a digest are unaffected (`pinDigests` stays off).

## Checklist before merging

- [x] ADR proposed if making an architectural change to the repo (N/A)
- [x] Tests run, docs added or updated as needed
  - New regexes checked against sample refs (plain, quoted, registry port, trailing comment, digest); `renovate-config-validator --strict` reports no new errors vs `main`

author: udene1
body:
## Purpose

Cashflow OS is an environment, not part of Cognitia.

This adds a read-only observation feed so an external cognitive system can observe work happening in the environment without being coupled to the Cashflow UI.

## Observations

The feed exposes existing operational records as observations:
- lead state
- structured research
- sales activities
- MCP tool calls
- outreach state

Each observation preserves source, kind, timestamp, interface, and raw content.

## Boundary

This does not add Cognitia logic, autonomous action, or product-specific cognition.

It also does not claim to know whether the underlying actor was human or agent. Actor is currently recorded as unknown; the interface indicates whether the record came through REST/research API, MCP, or Gmail.

The environment remains disposable: Cognitia can consume observations without knowing Cashflow-specific semantics.

## Before submitting

## Language(s)

Spanish - both `values-es` (generic) and `values-es-rES` (Spain)

## Summary

The **Woodcutting** skill and everything it puts on screen, in both Spanish locales. This is the skills-and-items half of the Woodcutting batch; the Woodcutters Guild is a separate PR.

- **Skill screen** (`strings.xml`): the armory stat, the `Lv. %1$d  •  %2$s XP/tronco` session row, the three prestige paths, the Master Woodcutter title and its requirement, and the axe equipment slot.
- **Trees** (`strings_skills.xml`): all 11 `tree_*_name` entries, from the basic `Árbol` to the Elder Isle `Pino Costero`, `Roble del Bosque`, `Árbol Abisal` and `Árbol Estelar`.
- **Items** (`strings_items.xml`): the seven log names that were still English in `values-es` (`Logs`, `Oak Logs`, `Willow Logs`, `Maple Logs`, `Yew Logs`, `Redwood Logs`, `Magic Logs`), mahogany and teak, the four missing axes (Divine, Dwarven, Ironwood, Sanctum), the Heirloom Axe, the two Woodcutting capes, and the four Elder Isle logs and tree items.
- **Quest objectives** (`strings_quests.xml`): the six `quest_woodcutting_N_objective` entries and the four `quest_daily_wc_*_objective` entries.

## Detailed changes

| File | Lines |
| --- | --- |
| `values-es/strings.xml` | 14 |
| `values-es-rES/strings.xml` | 17 |
| `values-es/strings_items.xml` | 21 |
| `values-es-rES/strings_items.xml` | 15 |
| `values-es/strings_skills.xml` | 11 |
| `values-es-rES/strings_skills.xml` | 11 |
| `values-es/strings_quests.xml` | 10 |
| `values-es-rES/strings_quests.xml` | 10 |
| `values-es-rES/strings_game.xml` | 1 |
| `values-es-rES/strings_weekly_quests.xml` | 6 |

Terminology reuses what the repository already uses in Spanish: `Tala de madera` for the skill, `troncos` for logs, `hacha` for axe, `roble`/`sauce`/`arce`/`tejo`/`secuoya`/`mágico` for the species, `Maestro Leñador` for Master Woodcutter, `Santuario Corrupto` for the Corrupted Sanctum and `Ruinas del Bosque Antiguo` for the Ancient Forest Ruins.

Three notes on naming:

body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical runtime `ReferenceError: process is not defined` on the deployed website (Cloudflare Pages) that prevented the interactive terminal playground from loading, and updates Playwright testing to run against both `dev` and `production` builds.

### Root Cause

1. In PR #66 (`042bcf5`), terminal width cache invalidation listeners were added to [src/utils/terminal.ts](file:///Users/nemesis/Projects/my-projects/cxstatusline/src/utils/terminal.ts) at module top level (`typeof process.stdout?.on === 'function'` and `process.platform !== 'win32'`).
2. In browsers (like Safari/Chrome on the deployed landing page), `process` is not a declared global. Evaluating property access on an undeclared identifier (`process.stdout` or `process.platform`) throws `ReferenceError: process is not defined` immediately when `src/utils/terminal.ts` is evaluated.
3. Because `terminal.ts` is imported by `TerminalWidthWidget` -> `catalog.ts` -> `website/src/playground.tsx`, the dynamic import `import('./playground')` threw this `ReferenceError`, caught by `syncViewport()` which displayed "The playground could not load. Try again.".

### Why Playwright Tests Passed Previously

- `website/playwright.config.ts` was running `webServer: { command: "bun run dev ..." }`. In Vite dev mode, Vite injects dev client mocks and shims `process`, so the error never surfaced during dev-server test runs.
- In production builds (`astro build` -> static output on Cloudflare Pages or `astro preview`), Vite does not inject dev client mocks.
- Furthermore, `website/test/edit-preview.spec.ts` was using `fetch("/src/sample-settings.json")` (a dev-server-only path), which failed on static preview builds.

### Fix

1. **Guarded `process` in [src/utils/terminal.ts](file:///Users/nemesis/Projects/my-projects/cxstatusline/src/utils/terminal.ts)**: Wrapped all top-level listeners and functions with `typeof process !== 'undefined'`.
2. **Hardened [website/astro.config.mjs](file:///Users/nemesis/Projects/my-projects/cxstatusline/website/astro.config.mjs)**: Added defense-in-depth defines for `process.stdout`, `process.on`, `process.pid`, and `process.execPath`.
3. **Defense-in-depth Fallback in [website/src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro](file:///Users/nemesis/Projects/my-projects/cxstatusline/website/src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro)**: Added an inline head fallback shim `window.process ??= ...` ensuring browser modules touching `process` will never throw ReferenceError.
4. **Dual Playwright Testing (`dev` and `production`)**:
   - Configured `website/playwright.config.ts` with `PLAYWRIGHT_MODE` switching between `bun run dev` and `bun run build && bunx astro preview`.
   - Added `test:e2e:dev`, `test:e2e:prod`, and `test:e2e` (runs both sequentially) to `website/package.json` and `test:website:e2e` to root `package.json`.
   - Added Playwright install and `test:website:e2e` to [.github/workflows/ci.yml](file:///Users/nemesis/Projects/my-projects/cxstatusline/.github/workflows/ci.yml).
5. **Fixed Test Fixtures & Types**:
   - Changed `website/test/edit-preview.spec.ts` to use imported `defaultLayout` directly instead of dev-only `fetch("/src/sample-settings.json")`.
   - Typed `serverEnv` and `page.evaluate` parameter objects cleanly for strict TypeScript checking.

## Verification

- `bun test ./test ./src`: 816 passed, 1 skipped (0 failures)
- `bun run typecheck`: Clean (0 errors)
- `cd website && bunx tsc --noEmit`: Clean (0 errors)
- `bun run test:website:e2e`: All 20 tests passed (10 on dev server, 10 on production preview build)
- `bun run check:package`: Passed

## Summary
- Adds a repeatable `--nameserver <IP|host>` CLI flag that feeds `EpConfig.uaConfig.nameserver` before `libInit`
- Enables PJSIP's RFC 3263 resolver so SIP URIs go through SRV (and NAPTR when present) lookups instead of plain A/AAAA

voip_patrol --nameserver 8.8.8.8 --nameserver 1.1.1.1 -c conf.xml ...

Target URIs must be `sip:user@domain` (no explicit port or `;transport=`) for SRV resolution to kick in.

author: jobordu
body:
Two things, and **the second pre-dates the first**.

## 1. The issuer travels on the card and was not used

EF 2F02 holds the device certificate followed by its issuer's. The trust-anchor README says so, and
says not to copy the issuer into the trust directory *because of it*:

> **Do not add the Device Issuer CA here.** `DEDINK0400001` travels on the card itself, in EF 2F02
> after the device certificate.

Nothing acted on that. Against a real DENK0404144:

```
CVC_ELEMENTS=2
CVC_ELEMENT_1=0x7F21 CV Certificate
CVC_ELEMENT_2=0x7F21 CV Certificate
[Warning: File DEDINK0400001 not found]
CVC_CHAIN=failed
```

It parses both elements, then looks the issuer up as a **file** and fails.

`GoldenNitrokeyDevautTest` passes only because the **test** extracts that element itself and writes
it into a temporary trust directory. So the tested path was not the path a card takes, and the
production one failed closed in a way that reads as a chain problem rather than a missing manual
step.

## 2. A self-signed card certificate was its own anchor

The walk terminated on `car == chr_` — a certificate that verified against itself — and returned
success **without consulting the trust directory at all**.

Measured on the **committed** version, with a real Pico HSM certificate
(`CHR == CAR == ESP41D722E200001`) and an **empty** `--trust-dir`:

```
CVC_CHAIN=verified
```

A card vouching for itself is not a chain. `--require-external-car` refuses `CHR == CAR` when a
caller asks for it, but a caller that passed a trust directory and read `CVC_CHAIN=verified` was
told its card chained to an anchor it had never seen.

The terminating certificate must now be a file in `--trust-dir`. That check is also what makes the
first change safe: carried certificates are a **lookup path, not a trust store**, so a card
carrying its own root still cannot terminate the walk.

## Verified on hardware

With only `DESRCACC100001` in the trust directory — the documented posture — a freshly generated
key on DENK0404144:

```
DEVAUT_CHAIN=verified
ATTEST_CAR=DENK040414400000
DEVAUT_CHR=DENK040414400000
ATTEST_SIGNATURE=verified
ATTESTED_POINT_MATCHES=yes
```

That is the first end-to-end run of `hsm-key-attestation-verify.py` against a card that this
repository records — and it is the provenance source regalia#447 needs, now that `CKA_LOCAL` is
known to track the certificate rather than the key's origin.

## Tests

Four new rows, and the self-signed fixture is a **real Pico certificate** because it is the only
one that exercises the terminal case with bytes that came off a card. Mutation-checked: not using
the carried issuer, dropping the anchor check, or letting carried certificates shadow the anchors
each fail the suite.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Enhancements**
  - Certificate verification now uses issuer certificates carried on a device to complete the certificate chain.
  - Verification still requires the operator-provided root certificate as the trust anchor.
  - Self-signed device certificates cannot establish trust by themselves, and an issuer without its root is rejected.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved certificate-chain validation for missing, unrelated, or incomplete trust configurations.
  - Added coverage for successful and failed verification scenarios.
