author: 0muji4
body:
Closes #44

#43 に積んでいる。マージは #43 のあと。

## 設計意図

#43 で `shared` に入れたロジックを画面につなぐ。DD §3.3 / §3.5 / §4.4 / §4.5 の設計をそのまま実装した。

**不変条件は 1 つ：`selection` が `Traveling` であることと、移動のコルーチンが走っていることは同値である。** これを保つのは `GraphCanvasState.dispatch` だけで、イベントを送る側はこの条件を知らなくてよい。`Traveling` に入ることと出ることを 1 か所で判定している。崩れると、選択を解除したあとも地図が元の移動先へ寄り続ける。

`camera` は段階 02 のまま `mutableStateOf` で持ち、pan / zoom の経路を 1 行も変えていない。`focus` は同じ型に持たせたが、遷移のときにしか変わらないので合成の中で読んでよい。Compose の購読は `MutableState` ごとなので、camera の毎フレームの更新では再構成されない。

## DD の訂正を同梱

DD §4.4 は「全体表示は状態機械を通らないが、移動だけ止める」と書いていた。**これは実装できない。** 止めるだけだと走っている移動が無いのに `Traveling` が残り、`Arrived` が永久に来ない。`TouchDownWhileTraveling` を送ってから fit する形に直した。CONTRIBUTING の「同じ挙動の文書と実装は 1 つの関心事」に従い同じ PR に入れている。

## 実装で判断が要った点

**破線は `drawLine` ではなく `drawPath` で描く。** ハードウェアアクセラレーションの canvas は、線に対する `PathEffect` を API 28 になるまで無視する。minSdk は 24 なので、`drawLine` で書くと API 27 以下の端末で ENTITY_RELATION と SEMANTIC_BRIDGE が実線になり、R3 の「種類ごとの線種」が成り立たない。効果だけが黙って落ちるので、ビルドでもテストでも捕まらない。手元の SDK には API 37 の system image しか無く、**API 27 以下での確認はできていない**。

**edge のラベルの幅は `remember(scene)` で測り置く。** member を指すと 117 本すべてにラベルが付く。段階 02 が「毎フレーム文字を測らない」として決めた形をここでも保つ。

**`LabelPaints` は構築後に変更しない。** 名前を描く node の濃さは常に 1 で、薄く描く ghost には名前を描かない。段階 02 の KDoc にあった「段階 03 が濃さを変えるときは `Paint.setAlpha`」という見込みは外れたので、不変条件として書き直した。

**名前の左端は倍率を掛けた半径から取る。** 掛けないと root（1.45 倍）と移動先（1.25 倍）の円が自分の名前に食い込む。

## テスト

`GraphCanvasStateTest` を 9 件から 29 件に、実データに対する `SceneDataTest` を 8 件追加。移動は時計（`TravelClock`）を差し替えて刻むので、合成なしで割り込み・停止・到着まで固定できる。

とくに `show_all_during_the_travel_leaves_the_traveling_state` は上の不変条件の回帰テストで、ここが落ちると `Traveling` が残る。

`SceneDataTest` は `GraphCameraFitTest` の方針に倣い、データから決まる数値そのものは固定しない。117 本や次数はデータを足せば変わるので、守るのは規則だけにしている。

## 実機で確かめた

Pixel 8a（1080×2400・density 420・60 Hz・release ビルド）で R1〜R5 を 1 つずつ。タップ位置は `Camera.fit` から計算して指定したので、どの node を押したかが曖昧にならない。

| 操作 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| member を 1 回タップ | edge 117 本がラベル付きで出る。**地図は動かず他の node も薄くならない** |
| 同じ位置をもう一度 | camera が (47%, 48%) へ移動、1-hop が前景、**edge は 0 本** |
| 前景の node を 1 回タップ | その node の edge が出る。白い実線と**緑の破線**が描き分けられている |
| target を root にして前景の node を 1 回タップ | **地図の領域が 1 バイトも変わらない**（画像比較で確認。差分はステータスバーの時計 34 行だけ） |
| ghost を 1 回タップ | 薄さが和らぎ名前が出る。edge は増えない |
| 移動中にタップ | その位置で root が確定。移動先（508, 1152）ではなく元の位置（344, 1076）に留まる |
| 選択解除 | 全体に戻り camera は動かない |

4 番目と 5 番目は**「押しても見た目が変わらないのが仕様どおり」**の箇所である（プロトタイプの `persistentTargetRoot` 優先）。不具合と取り違えないこと。

## 性能（段階 02 が残した宿題を閉じる）

段階 02 の DD は R4 を「エミュレータでしか測っていない。**実機では確かめていない**」と断っていた。同じ Pixel 8a で測った。

| 状態 | frames | jank | p50 | p90 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 全体地図（edge 0 本＝段階 02 と同じ負荷） | 944 | **0** | 6 ms | 8 ms | 9 ms |
| member を 1 回タップ（edge 117 + ラベル 117） | 952 | **0** | 7 ms | 8 ms | 11 ms |

締切 16.67 ms の超過は 0 件。edge とラベルの追加分は p50 で 1 ms、p99 で 2 ms だった。画面外カリング（段階 02 DD §4.4 が予告）は要らない。

確かめたのは 1 機種の 60 Hz での 1 回であって、すべての端末を代表しない。測定条件は DD §4.6 に残した。

## 確認

`./gradlew spotlessCheck :shared:allTests :androidApp:check` が通る。

author: macbuchi
body:
## The finding

**11 of the 13 entries in the KW39 error digest were the same thing:** `AuthRetryableFetchException(statusCode: 504)` from requesting a password reset, spanning versions 1.154.2 through 1.171.0.

A 504 means the gateway did not answer. `looksOffline` treats exactly that as a lost connection everywhere else in the app — `looksLikeGatewayTimeout` was added for it in September.

## Why it got through anyway

A `logError` with its own context reports **everything**. `worthReporting` deliberately does not touch it, on the grounds that the caller decided to report. That is right in general and was too broad here: this path filtered only the 429 rate limit and reported the rest, including the case the rest of the app calls "no signal".

The source is known and documented in CLAUDE.md: Google's review robots click through the login screen, the Play test address sits in the console as an app access, and the mail rate limit is deliberately 3/h. A normal event leading the digest crowds out the real findings — the same lesson as #124 (37 reports for a sign-out) and #136 (193 for cancelled tile jobs).

## The change

Both reset handlers now skip `looksOffline` as well as the rate limit. **Nothing changes for the user:** the screen keeps giving the one answer it always gave, because a visible failure would be an account oracle.

## Counter-proofs, both directions

- Removing the new condition fails the 504 test.
- A genuine auth failure (400 `validation_failed`) still reports, with its own test — so a filter that swallowed everything would not pass either. That matters: without it nobody would see the reset actually breaking, which is the #80 lesson.

No user-visible change, so the current changelog block's version line is extended rather than a new block added.

author: philfreshman
body:
Follow-up item 2 from the #71/#72/#73 handoff.

`writing` asked `admitting` for an entry's full weight before `write` had done its head, and `write` skips a blob that is already at its pathname. So a put for an entry the store already holds could evict other comparisons to make room it then never used: the cache ends up smaller and holding what it would have held anyway.

Sharper than wasteful. The entry being put is in the listing the sweep reads and may be the oldest thing in it, so the room it asks for can be freed by deleting the very blobs the write is about to skip. Against a store that forgets a blob immediately the two halves cancel — the head then misses and both blobs are rewritten — which is why nothing saw this. Against the real one they do not: a delete takes up to a minute to propagate, so the head can still see a blob on its way out, skip the write, and leave the entry gone once the delete lands.

### The seam question the handoff raised

Of its two candidates I took **head before admit** rather than **exclude the incoming `diff_id` from the sweep candidates**. The second stops an entry deleting itself and still lets a re-put evict its neighbours, which is the defect as stated; the first covers both shapes.

Considered and rejected: reusing the listing `admitting` already takes, to weigh and to check presence from one snapshot. It costs no extra requests and makes "the sweep will not delete what the write skips" true by construction — but a list is staler than a head, and a stale "present" is a blob skipped that is not there, which is a *new* way to write half an entry. A head is the read this module already trusts for exactly this question.

**The head inside `write` stays**, and is not the first one repeated: a sweep happens between them, long enough for another invocation to land the blob this one is about to write, and the head immediately before the put is what keeps that from resetting an `uploaded_at` eviction orders by. The cost is a head per blob on a write that goes ahead — on work the runtime drains after the answer has gone, that no caller waits on — against a listing and every delete saved on a write that does not.

A blob whose pathname the store cannot answer for now abandons the whole write rather than its own half. Writing the rest of the entry around it is how a `patches.json` ends up without the `meta.json` that names it: an orphan nothing reads and the budget counts forever.

### On the test seam

The handoff expected this to need an adapter whose deletes are delayed, on the `losing_deletes` precedent, and said to put that to Phil rather than assume it. **It does not need one, so I am not asking for one.** That expectation assumed the test has to reproduce the eventually-consistent race. It does not: what the fix does is *not sweep*, and a sweep that did not happen is visible against the immediate-delete store as the neighbour that survived and the `uploaded_at` that did not move. `Memory::uploaded_at` is already there for the second.

Both tests are at the wire, through `Memory::losing_reads` — which is what a lookup that failed and two invocations racing one comparison both look like, staged rather than raced. Both red first, for the two shapes above.

`./scripts/checks.sh` green.

author: eeiaao
body:
## What changes

`FixInitiator::loggedOn_` was only ever cleared at the top of `connect()`
and set true after a Logon reply. Every session-loss path -- EOF, a write
failure, `HeartbeatMissed`, a counterparty Logout -- reported its reason
through `setSessionDown()` but never touched `loggedOn_`. If the transport
never comes back up, `connect()` never runs, and `loggedOn()` reports true
for the whole outage; a caller judging reachability by the flag keeps
sending into a socket that is already gone.

The fix moves `loggedOn_ = false` into `setSessionDown()` itself, the one
place all four loss paths already funnel through (directly, or via the
public `logout()` a caller invokes on EOF or a write failure). A future
fifth path inherits the reset automatically instead of needing its own
call site.

## Test

One scenario per loss path, in `tests/test_fix_initiator.cpp`
(`test_logged_on_false_after_session_loss`), against a scripted in-memory
counterparty:

| Loss path | Test |
|---|---|
| EOF (transport close reported via `logout()`) | `test_logged_on_false_after_session_loss` |
| Write failure (reported via `logout()`) | `test_logged_on_false_after_session_loss` |
| `HeartbeatMissed` (`onTick()`, TestRequest unanswered past 2.4x `HeartBtInt`) | `test_logged_on_false_after_session_loss` |
| Counterparty Logout (`onFrame()`, `35=5` while logged on) | `test_logged_on_false_after_session_loss` |

Also extended with the same `loggedOn()` check, against the real venue

- **New information needed** — the household has different/additional issues after the last contact
- resolved households still retain their contact history

The selected household shows:
- latest contact timestamp
- recipient
- operator snapshot
- up to 5 recent contact-history entries

### Diagnostics used
The composer reuses existing sources of truth:
- missing/invalid email
- missing phone
- missing/invalid name
- missing unit reference
- same-household **Shared email / Shared phone**

Internal-only signals such as Possible duplicate, Patronato workflow state, or Activation Queue status are deliberately excluded from resident messages.

### Integrity / security
- the server action recomputes the live household diagnostics before recording contact
- recipient is identified by current resident position, avoiding ambiguity when two residents share a phone
- contact history is append-only
- public/anon/authenticated have no direct table access
- contact RPC is service-role only
- service_role has SELECT + INSERT only on history; UPDATE/DELETE are explicitly revoked
- preview remains read-only
- no WhatsApp delivery/read status is claimed; the operator confirms sending manually

### Backend
Adds:
- `community_registration_contact_events`
- `record_community_registration_whatsapp_contact_v1`
- audit event `internal_correction / whatsapp_contacted`

### Live QA
- migration applied successfully to hosted Supabase
- RPC exercised against real Andalucía data inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK
- rollback verified: no QA contact row remained
- anon/authenticated RPC execution denied
- service_role RPC execution allowed
- history table verified SELECT/INSERT=true, UPDATE/DELETE=false

### Scope
No WhatsApp Business API integration.
No automatic send/delivery/read claims.

author: jeffreytwin
body: Six things from 2026-09-22, plus what the build probes turned up on the failing connections. ## Builder Connections is a Floor Plans tab Beside Changes and Email Campaign, rather than an item under Settings — it is where the work is, not configuration someone sets once. `/dashboard/settings/builders` redirects to `/dashboard/floor-plans/connections`, so bookmarks and the Floor Plans banner link still land. ## A failing connection is a number on the menu, and the character says so New `GET /api/internal/floorplans/connections/troubled` returns the same set the Floor Plans banner already shows — active connections of active builders whose last run failed and nobody dismissed — without the whole builders list behind it. The sidebar badge and a new `BuilderAlertMonitor` both read it; the monitor seeds what is already failing on first load, so old news makes no sound, and names the connection in the `builder_error` event so all four characters can say which one went dark. A nav item can carry several badges (Floor Plans now has three), and each was pinning itself to `right: 10px`, so they stacked on top of one another. They sit in a row now — a pre-existing overlap this change would have made visible. ## The half-written plan list — Ryan Homes and Pulte Two connections were dying on `(input.plans ?? []).filter is not a function`: Ryan Homes' Amber Creek and Pulte's North River Ranch. Neither page has anything wrong with it. The cause is the *answer* running out of room. The list read had 8k tokens to reply in, and a community page whose plans each carry a dozen pictures with long URLs fills that before the end, so the tool call arrives half-written and its list of plans is no longer a list. Saying so is not enough when it is taking connections down, so the read now asks again with room to spare — 16k to begin with, 32k on the second attempt — and only gives up if a page will not fit even then, where it names the reason rather than failing on the shape of what came back. Every list off a tool call also goes through one guard, so a string where pictures belong can no longer be spread into single letters. Ryan's quick move-in was never a separate problem. The probe confirmed it reads perfectly in the engine's own distillation: > `1 Quick Move-In Home Available [LINK .../specs/31336/...] [IMG ...] Mayport $324,990 Available in October 2026 3 Bed 1,674 Sq.Ft. 2 Bathroom 1 Half Bath 1 Car Garage` ## Pictures a page carries but never draws — Perry Homes Perry's plans came through and their interiors did not, though the photographs are right there on the page. They are — but not in any ``. Perry's section pages draw a hero and four thumbnails and keep the whole gallery in the Next.js payload: the 50' section carries 23 photographs of its model home, the 90' carries 18, and not one is drawn. Distillation only understands ``, and the galleries can't be read off the headings either, because Perry has no gallery heading — every picture falls under "Become a Perry Insider!" at the foot of the page. So `payloadGallery` reads the media-library records out of a page's own payload, in payload order — but only as a *fallback*, when the headings yielded no gallery, so a page that does draw its galleries is still read from what it draws and a plan never inherits the community's other pictures. Those records also say what each picture is (`"type":["interior"]`, with the design and section), which settles the sorting: a picture the page itself calls an outside view is marked as one and goes last, and the lead becomes the first *room* rather than the front of the house. The rooms keep the page's own order, which is the photographer's; the edit overlay's sorting button takes it from there. Held to the live pages: 23 off the 50' section with its one exterior named, 18 off the 90' including two the page labels nothing at all, which are kept rather than dropped. ## A browser, for the builders whose pages are empty without one Richmond American's site is a Blazor app. Every page of it — the community, all eight plans, all eleven homes named in its own sitemap — fetches as ~240KB of shell and fills itself in afterwards over Blazor's wire. There is nothing in the HTML to read, on any page. So the generic engine gains a second way of getting a page (`render_claude`, headless Chromium via `puppeteer-core` + `@sparticuz/chromium`). Everything after that is unchanged — the same distillation, the same reads, the same gallery ordering, the same diff. A builder is switched between them from the Builder Connections tab ("use a browser"); only a builder already on a generic engine can be switched. A page gets up to twenty seconds to draw itself, and what counts as drawn is the same test that tells the plain engine a page was never readable: a price, a size or a bed count anywhere. One browser serves a whole run and is given back at the end of it, well or badly. Both ends are bounded, because renting a browser is slow: - a run may spend ~170s in the browser, after which a page is refused rather than the run being killed with nothing written down — the list pages are read first, so what a slow community loses is a plan's extras, which were always optional; - the nightly tick will not *start* a rendering connection without most of its budget left, and waits for the next tick, where it goes first. Verified end to end against a page shaped like Richmond's — chrome at first, plans and prices three seconds later. The renderer waits it out and returns all of them. Also: a run that finds nothing on a page carrying no price, no size and no bed count now says the page draws its plans after loading, rather than blaming the run. `pageLooksUnrendered` is pure and tested, does double duty as the renderer's wait condition, and leaves a page that *did* render alone — including a sold-out community that still prices what it had. ## Tests 838 passing, including `payloadGallery` against Perry's real payload text (escaped quotes, records split across script chunks, unlabelled pictures) and the new lead-with-a-room ordering. Typecheck clean, lint clean on the touched files, and a full `next build` succeeds locally with the new dependencies. Both build probes are retired and their `prebuild` steps removed. Once this is live, Richmond's builder needs switching to "use a browser" from the Builder Connections tab (or I'll set it) before its next run. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_013Rq42NS54r9rwKfYVi77jx

author: srosro
body:
Closes #90

## Problem
On 2026-09-22 the priority desk wrote a precise reason to `run/desk-priority/notes.json` (wiki 401 on every retry) but no section. `render_edition.py`'s `ensure_priority_desk` filled the slot with hardcoded bilingual copy ("not built in time"), and the page also suppressed `could_not_source` on the priority desk — so the desk's reason could not have printed even if it had been written. Four places owned the message (renderer copy, pt-edition/SKILL.md, pt-priority/SKILL.md, desks.md).

## Design
- **Deleted:** `PRIORITY_UNAVAILABLE`, `_unavailable_priority_section`, `ensure_priority_desk`, `_priority_configured`, and the gap-card tests.
- **Renderer:** `priority_desk_missing()` — priority configured + paper batch (weather/calendar) + no priority section → `sys.exit` with a named error (the 2026-09-18 tripwire stays loud instead of being papered over). A priority section with no card must carry a non-blank `could_not_source`. The priority desk now prints `could_not_source` (sources stay hidden).
- **Desk (pt-priority):** when it cannot publish, writes `notes.json` `could_not_source` with what failed and why.
- **Edition (pt-edition):** no complete checkpoint → writes the unavailable section, copying `could_not_source` verbatim from the desk's notes. A noncanonical paper with no notes says today's scheduled paper has not published the card.
- Alternative considered: the desk writes a whole section file the edition copies. Rejected — one more file shape; notes.json + could_not_source is the convention every other desk already uses.

## LOC
Target ≈ −50 to −70. Actual: `7 files changed, 94 insertions(+), 127 deletions(-)` (net −33). Short of target because review asked for the no-reason gate (+validation, +parametrized test), which keeps "no placeholder" enforced rather than instructed.

## Verified
- `just test`: `660 passed`.
- Tests drive `main()` and assert rendered HTML/chat: configured paper without the desk exits loudly; unconfigured / one-topic edition renders without it; unavailable section prints `Couldn't source: <reason>` in HTML and chat; blank/empty reason is refused.

## Unverified / follow-ups
- Not run against a live agent. Stale "gap card" wording remains in files outside this PR's touch set: `runtime/SOUL.md:341`, `pt-dashboard/scripts/register_crons.py:179,243`, `pt-research/references/desks.md:28` (owned by another PR), `pt-shared/SKILL.md:63`, `pt-shared/scripts/owner_language.py` docstring. Their meaning now reads as "the unavailable card the edition writes".
- `page_rules` does not scan `could_not_source`, so a reason naming a script (e.g. `wiki_setup.py`) prints as-is — intentionally, so the desk's exact diagnosis is not refused.
- Declined roborev low: a mixed `[" ", "reason"]` list renders a stray separator — pre-existing for every desk.

author: ryanhill1
body:
Closes #1421

### Problem

`_parse_gates` resolved a single-qubit gate's register by scanning `program_qubits`
with a `for` loop and no `else`. A name that never matched left `qubit_values` empty
and the gate was dropped:

```qasm
qubit[4] q;
let a = q[0:1];
h a;
x q[3];
```
```
[{"gate": "x", "target": 3}]      # the h is gone, no error
```

The converted circuit computes something different from the program, with nothing
downstream able to tell. The adjacent multi-qubit branch already rejected this — #1405
gave it an explicit check — but the single-qubit one did not.

### The decision worth arguing about

This makes the failure loud. It does **not** make aliases work, and that is deliberate.

The tempting alternative is to let pyqasm resolve the alias, since the public
`qasm3_to_ionq` wrapper already retries through it. But pyqasm's alias ranges are off
by one:

```
let a = q[0:1]      -> h q[0]                    (expected q[0], q[1])
let whole = q[0:3]  -> h q[0], h q[1], h q[2]    on a 4-qubit register
```

OpenQASM 3 ranges are inclusive, so aliasing a whole register should cover all four
qubits. Leaning on that would trade a dropped gate for a quietly wrong one, which is
the same class of bug this PR exists to remove. Reported upstream separately.

So after this change an alias program raises rather than converting. That is a
regression in reach and an improvement in honesty; it can be revisited once pyqasm's
ranges are fixed.

### Caveats

- The public `qasm3_to_ionq` path still converts alias programs, via pyqasm's retry,
  and still produces the off-by-one result. Catching that would mean detecting aliases
  before pyqasm consumes them, which is a wider change than this bug.
- `tests/transpiler/qasm` 165 passed; the converter sweeps CONTRIBUTING mandates
  (`test_measurement_coverage.py`, `test_measurement_semantics.py`) are green.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - IonQ conversion now reports an error when a gate references an unresolved qubit register instead of silently omitting the gate.
  - Single-qubit gates on directly declared registers continue to expand across the register’s qubits as expected.

- **Documentation**
  - Added an unreleased changelog entry describing the conversion behavior and error handling.

      批700(PR #80)它判了 293 站的生死自己從來沒有一條檢 → 格子第一次有了自己的自測
  兩批的新律排在一起,配方就露出來了:

      LL364 排除要逐條印出吃掉幾支:讓過寬的排除以數字現形,不要以沉默現形

照配方對照「VCGC/VDF/VRN 全部成功」,第一個問題就爆了

      VCGC 受治理家族         364

     不是壞掉,是寫死的數字過期了(LL372 同一族)。
     修:不釘數量——件冊讀得到、今天每一包都 INTEGRATED、今天零包就是 NODATA。

author: scala-steward
kolisachint
body:
A hoocode canvas. The person drags, connects, labels and styles shapes in their
browser; the agent adds, updates and deletes cells by id through six actions;
each sees the other's changes as they happen.

```
/canvas open drawio-canvas
```

## The constraint that shaped it

A canvas has to be enough on its own: nothing to install, no service to run, no
third-party origin in the page, nothing fetched from the network. So the editor
is this canvas's own rather than an embedded draw.io, and there is no
`package.json` and no `node_modules` anywhere — the SDK import is host-resolved,
and a local install would shadow it.

What that costs is rendering fidelity, and the bargain is stated rather than
hidden:

> **Rendering degrades. The document does not.**

About eighteen shape families draw properly (rounded boxes, ellipses, rhombus,
hexagon, cylinder, cloud, note, document, process, step, card, actor, swimlane,
text…), with fills, strokes, dashes, opacity, fonts, and edges with waypoints,
orthogonal routing, six arrowhead styles and labels. Anything else — an AWS
icon, a UML stencil — draws as a labelled rectangle in its own colours, while
its style string, custom attributes, children and relationships survive every
edit untouched. There is a test that opens an AWS-stencil file, edits it, saves
it and asserts the stencil, the `UserObject` attributes and `points=[[0,0,0]]`
are all still there.

## Two decisions carry the collaboration

**Edits are cell-addressed in both directions.** The page sends the same
`{operation, cell_id, new_xml}` operations the agent does, so moving a box and
adding a node are not a conflict at all — they touch different cells and both
land. Only edits to the *same* cell race, and there the later one wins. A
document-at-a-time protocol would make every concurrent edit a conflict, and the
edit discarded would usually be the person's, because the agent writes faster.

**The agent has to look before it writes.** `edit_diagram` is refused when the
document has changed since the agent last read it, and the refusal says to call
`get_diagram` and retry. A content fingerprint, not a lock and not a timeout —
so a slow turn is fine and only a stale one is stopped. The person is never
blocked: they are looking at the diagram, so they cannot be working from a stale
copy of it.

## Structure

The XML parser, document model, style reader and renderer are loaded **by both
halves** — the extension process and the page — from the same files. That is the
main structural decision here: a canvas whose server understood a slightly
different document than its page would lose someone's work, and the loss would
look like a rendering bug.

```
extension.mjs     the host-facing surface, and nothing else
lib/canvas.mjs    the canvas declaration and the six action handlers
lib/xml.mjs       XML parser and serializer, non-destructive by design   <- served to the page too
lib/model.mjs     the .drawio document: pages, cells, operations         <- served to the page too
lib/style.mjs     draw.io style strings                                  <- served to the page too
lib/render.mjs    the document as SVG, as a pure function                <- served to the page too
lib/session.mjs   one open document: versions, history, the edit gate
lib/files.mjs     reading and writing .drawio, and the workspace rule
lib/server.mjs    the loopback server, the token, and the event stream
ui/               the editor
```

Because `render.mjs` is pure, one renderer serves three callers: the live
canvas, `save_file`'s `.svg` output, and the history thumbnails.

## Details worth a reviewer's eye

- **The token is the first path segment**, not a query parameter. The browser
  drops the query string when resolving an ES module import, which would leave
  the page's own modules unauthenticated; a cookie is worse, because on
  `127.0.0.1` cookies are shared across ports and would hand the token to every
  other local server the browser talks to.
- **Every file path is resolved on its real path** inside the session's working
  directory, so neither `../` nor a symlink reaches out. Only `.drawio`, `.xml`
  and `.svg` are written.
- **draw.io's compressed page format** (URI-encode, raw deflate, base64) is
  decoded on the way in and written back plain.
- **A document survives `reload_canvas`.** Reload re-forks the process, so
  iterating on this canvas's own code would otherwise throw away the diagram the
  person is looking at. Parked documents have a 60-second freshness window, so
  one can never resurrect under an unrelated later instance.
- **Labels take their colour from the shape they sit on**, not from the page —
  otherwise every pastel-filled shape gets near-white text in dark mode.

## Checked

97 tests, no dependencies:

```bash
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

They include `test/protocol.test.mjs`, which forks `extension.mjs` as a real
child process and speaks the canvas wire protocol to it — resolving the SDK
import the way a host does — so the thing under test is the extension as a host
sees it. It also fails the build if a `package.json` or `node_modules` ever
appears, or if a `node:` import lands in one of the four modules the browser
loads. `test/browser.test.mjs` drives the editor in Chromium against a live
canvas (10 of the 97; it needs a driver installed outside the repository, which
the README explains).

Separately, exercised end to end against hoocode itself: discovery from
`~/.copilot/extensions`, the workspace-trust gate, `/canvas list` and
`/canvas open`, `list_canvas_capabilities`, `invoke_canvas_action`,
`reload_canvas`, and close releasing the port.

## Needs a follow-up

The CI workflow is **not** committed — the session that wrote this had no
`workflow` scope, and the push was rejected with it. The YAML is in the README,
ready to paste to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

The two file actions need hoocode with canvas session context
(kolisachint/hoocode#255, released in v0.5.81); without it the canvas still
opens and says so in its status, or `DRAWIO_CANVAS_WORKSPACE` names the
directory instead.

`main` is a single empty commit, created only so this arrives as a reviewable
diff rather than as an initial import nobody can read. The repository's default
branch still points at this feature branch; worth switching to `main` before
merging.

body:
## What

Task: #1670

**Exact paths touched:** `src/routes/worldEvents.js` (new `POST .../suggest-names` route), `frontend/src/pages/EventPackagePage.jsx` (Basics section control), `frontend/src/pages/EventPackagePage.css` (new rules), `tests/unit/routes/world-cluster-tier-promotion.test.js` (F-AUTH-1 CP3 lock-count update, see note below).

## CI fix note

The first push's `Tests` check failed — not a flake. `tests/unit/routes/world-cluster-tier-promotion.test.js` is the F-AUTH-1 CP3 confirmation-sweep test; it hardcodes exact `requireAuth`/`aiRateLimiter` counts for `worldEvents.js` and the CP3 zone aggregate. My new route legitimately adds one more `requireAuth`-gated, `aiRateLimiter`-gated AI POST handler (exactly the D4 pattern the test itself enforces), which correctly shifted those locked counts by one. The test file already documents this exact scenario happening once before (a comment citing Task #1642 doing the same thing to the same counts), so I followed that same precedent: updated `worldEvents.js`'s count 63→64 (with a comment citing Task #1670), the "AI handlers" count 4→5, added an explicit named test for the new route matching the file's existing per-route test style, and the CP3 zone aggregate 106→107 — all with updated comments, not silently. Verified locally (43/43 pass in that file) plus the two other `worldEvents.js`-referencing test files (21/21, unaffected) before pushing.

## Do #1 — checked first: existing title generation

`episodeGeneratorService.js:519-554` already generates an AI **episode** title (not an event name) — `new Anthropic({ apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY })`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, a plain-JSON-in-prompt response parsed via `/\{[\s\S]*\}/` regex + `JSON.parse`, no retry loop (single try, falls back to the event name on any error, `:581-583`). `eventGeneratorRoute.js:16-73` generates full **events** (a different thing — bulk event library creation), using `new Anthropic()`, model `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and the `MODELS` array + per-model retry pattern CLAUDE.md's own AI convention names. `src/routes/memories/interview.js:99-130` has the fullest version of that pattern: an outer loop over `MODELS`, an inner up-to-2-attempts-per-model loop with a 2s backoff on 529/503, falling through to the next model on repeated overload or a 404.

**Model chosen: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`** — the cheapest tier (`aiCostTracker.js:33`, $0.80/$4 per 1M vs. Sonnet's $3/$15), matching the episode-title precedent, appropriate for a short, low-stakes, three-short-strings task. No new Anthropic client wrapper added — `new Anthropic()` reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment the same way `eventGeneratorRoute.js` does, and `aiCostTracker.js` monkey-patches the SDK's `Messages.create()` globally at app startup (`app.js:19`) — every `new Anthropic()` instance anywhere in the app is already cost-tracked and budget-gated with zero extra wiring, confirmed by reading `aiCostTracker.js`'s own header comment. Retry pattern reused verbatim from `interview.js`'s two-attempts-per-model loop.

## Do #2 — the endpoint

`POST /api/v1/world/:showId/events/:eventId/suggest-names` (`worldEvents.js`, right after the single-event GET). Loads the event by raw SQL (same query shape as the existing GET, `:137-140`), writes nothing — no `INSERT`/`UPDATE` anywhere in the handler.

**Fields used, and where each comes from:**
- Show name — `models.Show.findByPk(showId)`.
- Host name + archetype — the linked `SocialProfile` via `source_profile_id` (same durable FK the GET route already reads, `:158`), giving both `display_name`/`handle` and the psychological `archetype` ENUM (humanized: `polished_curator` → "polished curator"); falls back to the event's own legacy `host` text field when there's no linked profile.
- `category`, `format`, `venue_name`, `event_date`, `event_time`, `dress_code`, `prestige` — read directly off the event row.

**What happens when most are empty** (true of most events today, per the census this issue itself names — 53 events with almost no venue/category/format): every fact line is individually conditional (`event.category ? ... : null`, filtered), so the prompt only ever contains what's actually set. When *nothing* beyond the event existing is available, the prompt explicitly says so ("No details recorded for this event yet beyond it existing — do not invent any") rather than silently degrading to a generic, unguided prompt. Either way the prompt tells the model directly not to invent a venue, guest, theme, or location it wasn't given — so today's sparse events get names that lean on host/category/format/tone rather than fabricated specifics, and get noticeably richer once venue (piece 2) and category/format (already landed, per `docs/EVENT_EPISODE_FLOW.md` §8(k)/Task #1640) are actually filled in.

## Do #3 — frontend: Basics section control

A "Suggest names" button in the Basics section header (`epp-section-header`, matching the same pattern already used for People's "Change Host", including the same `!used` gate — an event already turned into an episode can't be renamed this way). Clicking it opens a panel: three suggestion buttons (pick one → saves immediately), a Regenerate button (re-calls the same endpoint), and a free-text input + Save button, Enter-to-save included.

**Confirmed: `name` is already in the existing update route's allowlist** — `worldEvents.js`'s `PUT /world/:showId/events/:eventId` `allowedFields` array includes `'name'` as its first entry (`:389` at this basis). Picking a suggestion or typing a custom name both call that existing route directly (`api.put(..., { name })`), matching the same pattern `selectHost` already uses for `source_profile_id`/`host`. No new write endpoint was added.

## Do #4 — no automatic renaming

Nothing calls `suggest-names` on mount — `openNameSuggest` only runs from the button's `onClick`, and the event's own `useEffect`s (page load, toast timeout, host-picker debounce) never reference it. An event is renamed only through `saveEventName`, itself only reachable by clicking a suggestion or the Save button. Confirmed by click-test (below): zero calls to `suggest-names` and zero `PUT` calls before any click on a fresh page load.

## Do #5 — length and no invented facts

Enforced twice: the prompt itself states both rules ("under 40 characters," "No quotation marks," "Do not invent facts... the details above don't give you"), and the response parser defensively re-enforces length and strips quote characters regardless of what the model returns (`.replace(/["'‘’“”]/g, '').trim().slice(0, 40)` — straight and curly, single and double quotes) rather than trusting the prompt alone. The free-text input also has `maxLength={40}` for a typed name.

## Click-tests at 900×1000 (mocked dev server, Playwright)

`event-name-suggest-clicktest.js`, 13/13 pass:
```
PASS — no suggest-names call on page load
PASS — no PUT call on page load
PASS — name shown as-is on load ("sasha's Event")
PASS — suggest-names called exactly once after clicking
PASS — three suggestions shown
PASS — suggestions match the first mocked batch
PASS — regenerate called suggest-names again
PASS — regenerate shows a different batch
PASS — picking an option PUTs the existing event route with that name
PASS — the page title now shows the picked name
PASS — the suggest panel closes after saving
PASS — typing a custom name PUTs it via the same route
PASS — the page title now shows the typed name
```

Regression check against the two prior click-test suites for this page/its shared component (`EventPackagePage.jsx`/`.css` touched again by this PR, after #1654/#1656/#1658/#1668) — both still fully pass, 12/12 and 14/14.

```
$ node -c src/routes/worldEvents.js && echo OK
OK

$ node scripts/validate-routes.js
Route files scanned: 132 · Source files scanned: 710 · Warnings: 10 (all pre-existing, none in touched files)
EXIT: 0

$ bash scripts/lint-silent-catches.sh

author: ross
body:
W2 of the `hacc` stack (stacked on #288): the component itself — `ComponentKind::HttpAccess`, graph rule 60, `crates/logit-transforms/src/http_access.rs`, the registry arm, the regenerated schema.

**What it does** (ADR `http-access-normalization`, plan `http-access-normalization`): a web server logs the raw value under the OTel semconv name (`"url.original":"$request_uri"`, `"http.response.status_code":"$status"`), and one component rewrites the line into its conformant form plus a bounded derived set, in nine steps, best-effort per field:

0. **De-alias** the dashed spelling (`url-path` → `url.path`) from a fixed pre-interned table — what lets HAProxy use `%{+json}o`, whose item names can't contain `.`.
1. **Decompose** `http.request.line` / `url.original` into whichever atomic fields are absent.
2. **Coerce** sizes/ports/status to `I64` (`"000"` → `0`); an unparseable value is left in place, counted `invalid{field}`, and (for status/duration/request line only) diagnosed once.
3. **Durations** `_s|_ms|_us|` unsuffixed-ns → `http.request.duration_s` (same for `upstream.{duration,connect,header}`).
4. **Method** onto semconv's known set, else `_OTHER` + `http.request.method_original`.
5. **Version** `HTTP/1.1` → `1.1`, `2.0` → `2`.
6. **Query**: strip `?`, redact semconv's sensitive keys (+ `redact_query`) → `REDACTED`, before capping.
7. **Cap and clean** every `CAPPED_FIELDS` entry by chars; control bytes → `_`, length-preserving.
8. **Classify** `user_agent.class` (uncapped value, ordered built-in table, config rules first; crawler/scanner also `user_agent.synthetic.type: bot`) and `http.route` (capped path, `routes:` rules + `assets`/`well_known`/`probes` built-ins, `route_other` fallback, else nothing).
9. **Derive** `error.type` (5xx), `span.status` (`error` for 5xx/0, else `unset` — never `ok`), `span.name` (`{method} {route}` / `{method}`, `HTTP` for `_OTHER`), `span.duration_s` mirror when the line carries no span timing, and `client.address` from XFF's first hop under `forwarded: {trust: true}`.

Every classification value comes from config or a built-in table, never from the input — the review question for any change here. Never drops an event, never invents an absent field, never touches `log`/`metrics`/`span`/`timestamp`/`Resource`. Events with no log record pass through untouched.

**Rule 60** compiles every `match` at validate time (rule 31's reasoning) and rejects empties, `builtin`+`match` together, a duplicate built-in, a `max_length` key that names nothing this component caps (the error lists the valid keys), `max_length: 0`, and `forwarded: {trust: false}`. A bare `type: http_access` is valid and meaningful, so there is deliberately no no-op clause. `CAPPED_FIELDS` lives in `logit-config` so the rule and the transform can't disagree; the CLI hands the transform the resolved caps.

**Tests:** 80 added (53 in the transform, 18 rule-60, 8 config round-trips, 1 registry run-it). Workspace: 4022 passing, clippy clean.

**Deliberately deferred:** the built-in UA/route tables are the plan's first cut — W3 replaces them from a sourced corpus. Allocation pins and the `memory.md` rows land in W4. The file is 2100 lines (1228 code + tests); left as one file rather than split pre-review.

body: ## Scope First consumer under RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#61, paired with #24 and RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#67. This migrates Enhanced Cover from its repository-local Release Please/publisher/recovery state machine to the shared Profile B contract while preserving product-specific release evidence and optional WordPress.org deployment. ## Release architecture Before: ```text Quality → repository-local workflow_run publisher → local RP lifecycle / merge geometry / label reconciliation → local draft creation + --clobber asset replacement → local immutable publication/readback → manual mutable recovery lane → optional WordPress.org deployment ``` After: ```text Quality → exact ZIP/checksum + promotion manifest → shared Profile B @ aa88eb65d67f26ef7c73a87ba8b43f7eb7f2c0c2 → Release Please owns version/changelog/release PR/tag/draft identity → exact run/attempt asset promotion → immutable GitHub release/readback → separate exact-successful-Profile-B WordPress.org adapter when enabled ``` Deleted/superseded: - repository-local RP/publisher state machine; - manual rebuild / mutable `--clobber` recovery; - local lifecycle-label reconciliation; - manual deployment bypass of `wordpress-org/deployment.json`. Retained: - deterministic ZIP/checksum/repository manifest construction; - exact runtime archive verification; - WordPress 6.5/current compatibility + fresh ZIP install; - Plugin Check; - protected `wordpress-org` environment and SVN adapter; - WordPress.org deployment remains disabled by committed contract and is downstream of the canonical immutable GitHub release; - listing-artwork synchronization is source-controlled through `syncListingAssets` rather than a manual deployment bypass; - downstream deployment is authenticated from the completed canonical `Release Please` workflow run and exact main SHA, avoiding reliance on a secondary `release` event suppressed by `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The public Profile B promotion manifest names only the ZIP and checksum. The richer repository manifest remains CI evidence and is not promoted as an additional GitHub release asset. ## Quality command mapping This branch stages the bounded command contract currently proposed by RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#69: | Before | After | Enforcement | |---|---|---| | `composer lint` | `composer lint:syntax` | required ordinary check | | `composer phpcs` | `composer standards` | required ordinary check | | `composer phpcbf` | `composer standards:fix` | fixer, same PHPCS rules/scope | | `composer test` | `composer test:integration` | required WordPress/database CI lane | | `composer check` = PHPCS only | `composer check` = syntax + standards | required ordinary aggregate | | pnpm PHP wrapper aliases | removed | canonical Composer names used directly | The syntax runner now fails closed if file discovery itself fails; Quality includes a negative fake-`find` contract check. No PHPStan, analysis floor, style rewrite, production API change or integration weakening is included. ## Qualification The command-contract dependency has landed: RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#69 merged as `521aa11f5246e858502b4daba5241f6ee2f1a690`. Its final reviewed contract matches this branch's command semantics. Exact PR head: `aad30a1153927f7e7aa886d57b81a0c33d6e42fc` Fresh exact-source Quality: run **35768697544 / attempt 1**. Successful lanes: - shared WordPress Plugin Quality baseline; - exact-source release artifact build and Profile B promotion manifest; - WordPress 6.5 / PHP 8.0 integration + fresh ZIP install; - WordPress current / PHP 8.3 integration + fresh ZIP install; - Plugin Check; - terminal `quality`. Artifact **10712609392** (`ran-enhanced-cover-release-35768697544-1`) binds both `quality_commit` and `source_commit` to the exact PR head. The public promotion set is only the ZIP and checksum. The pinned shared Profile B workflow at `aa88eb65d67f26ef7c73a87ba8b43f7eb7f2c0c2` has the same workflow blob as current `.github/main`; #69 changed documentation only. **Do not merge solely on this evidence.** Independent code/security review is still required. After an authorised merge, the live post-merge path must prove Release Please candidate qualification, exact tested ZIP/checksum promotion, immutable GitHub publication/readback, and the downstream WordPress.org observer must no-op while its committed deployment contract remains disabled. Refs RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#61, #24, RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#67, RocketsAreNostalgic/.github#66. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: arminomari
body:
## Gemensam statustidslinje för creator och företag

Idag ligger statusen utspridd: uppdraget har en status, varje video en annan, utbetalningen en tredje. Ingen av parterna kan se på ett ställe vad som faktiskt väntas på, eller av vem.

### Regeln (`Domain/Common/AssignmentProgress.cs`)
Ett uppdrag, kampanj som kran, går genom samma steg:

**Antagen → Video publicerad → Godkänd av företaget → Views verifieras → Ersättning → Avslutat**

Varje steg bär `state` (klar, pågår, kommande, stoppad), `waitingOn` (creator, företag, VYRLE, TikTok, ingen), en förklarande rad och vid behov en deadline. Inget lagras: allt härleds ur uppdraget, dess videor och utbetalningsliggaren vid varje läsning, så statusen kan aldrig hamna ur synk med verkligheten.

Vad stegen läser:
- **Video**: finns en inskickad eller godkänd video? Är alla nekade hamnar uppdraget tillbaka här, med företagets motivering som hjälptext.
- **Godkänd**: en video som väntar på beslut ger `waitingOn = Brand` och deadline från `ReviewPolicy` (auto-godkännande).
- **Views**: godkänd video men under kampanjens tröskel ger `waitingOn = TikTok` och "400 av 1000 views. Hämtas från TikTok en gång per dygn."
- **Ersättning**: följer utbetalningsliggaren. Ej begärd och klar → creatorns tur. Begärd, under granskning, godkänd eller misslyckad → VYRLE. Nekad → creatorns tur.
- **Avbrutet eller diskvalificerat** stoppar tidslinjen istället för att låtsas att den fortsätter. En kran får aldrig steget "Avslutat", den är löpande.

### Samma sanning, två röster
`CreatorHeadline` och `BrandHeadline` ger samma steg olika formulering: creatorn ser "Väntar på företaget", företaget ser "Er tur: godkänd av företaget". Båda läser exakt samma stegslista.

### API
`AssignmentDetailDto.Progress` bär hela tidslinjen, `AssignmentListDto` bär det aktuella steget plus `waitingOn` och rubrik, så listraderna kan visa "Din tur" utan ett extra anrop.

### Frontend
Ny `ProgressTimeline` (`components/app`) renderas överst på creatorns uppdragssida och på företagets creator-sida, med rollen som enda skillnad. Vertikal tidslinje med bockar, pågående steg i accentfärg, deadline som "senast om 2 dagar".

### Tester
- `dotnet test`: **506 passed**. Tre nya: tidslinjen pekar ut rätt part i varje läge, ersättningssteget följer liggaren, och ett avbrutet uppdrag stoppar tidslinjen.
- Playwright: `timeline-creator` och `timeline-brand` på 1440 och 390, överflöde och axe gröna.
- Fixade en kontrastmiss som sviten fångade på köpet: utgående chattbubblans tidsstämpel låg under AA.

### Screenshots
`docs/screens/pw/timeline-creator-*.jpg` och `timeline-brand-*.jpg`.

author: musiker15
body:
Die Anlagenstruktur aus Abschnitt 3.2 lässt sich jetzt füllen. Die Tabellen gab es seit Phase 0, eine Oberfläche nicht.

**Im Büro.** An der Anlage stehen ihre Verteiler, jeder hat einen eigenen Bildschirm (`/verteiler/...`) mit seinen Feldern und Stromkreisen, ein Stromkreis einen mit seinen Betriebsmitteln (`/stromkreise/...`). Alles lässt sich anlegen, ändern, verschieben und löschen. Je Stromkreis gibt es Verbraucher, Schutzeinrichtung mit Art, Charakteristik und Nennstrom, RCD mit Typ und Bemessungsdifferenzstrom und die Leitung mit Typ, Aderzahl, Querschnitt, Länge und Verlegeart. Jeder Wert darf leer bleiben. Die Charakteristik muss zur Schutzeinrichtung passen (B bis Z zum Schalter, gG und aM zur Sicherung), das Formular bietet nur an, was passt. Aufgelistet wird wie auf dem Verteiler, F2 vor F10.

**Auf der Baustelle.** Am Auftrag stehen die Verteiler seiner Anlage. Man kann einen Stromkreis nachtragen, die Angaben eines vorhandenen ergänzen oder ein Betriebsmittel dazuschreiben, alles ohne Netz. Verschieben und Löschen bleiben dem Büro.

**Das Stromkreisverzeichnis.** `GET /installations/:id/circuit-chart` druckt alle Verteiler der Anlage, mit `?board=` einen, im Querformat mit einem Verteiler je Seite. Oben stehen der Betrieb mit Telefonnummer und der Tag der letzten Änderung. Es wird bei jedem Abruf gedruckt und nicht gespeichert, weil es anders als ein Beleg keinen Vorgang festhält (Nachtrag in ADR 0007). Mit dem echten Renderer geprüft, sieht sauber aus.

**Zwei Dinge, die dabei aufgefallen sind:**

- PostgreSQL prüft Fremdschlüssel an der Row-Level Security vorbei. Unter der Anwendungsrolle ließ sich ein Verteiler an die Anlage eines anderen Betriebs hängen, wenn man ihre Kennung kannte. Migration 0030 lässt die vier Tabellen deshalb über Betrieb und Kennung zusammen auf ihre Eltern zeigen. Der Abgleich fragt den Elternteil vorher unter der Policy ab und lehnt einen fremden oder gelöschten als Konflikt `record_missing` ab, damit nicht die ganze Übertragung scheitert (Nachtrag in ADR 0003). Die übrigen Verweise im Datenmodell haben dieselbe Lücke. Das ist nicht Teil dieses PR, ein eigener Vorschlag dafür liegt bereit.
- Gelöscht wird durch Markieren, die Kaskaden der Schlüssel laufen also nie. Ein gelöschter Verteiler ließ seine Stromkreise unsichtbar stehen. Jetzt markiert ein Trigger mit, was darunter hängt (Nachtrag in ADR 0005). Nebenbei behoben: der Schlüssel vom Stromkreis zum Feld leerte beim Entfernen auch den Verteiler, ein Feld mit Stromkreisen ließ sich deshalb gar nicht entfernen.

Im Konzept kommt die Aderzahl dazu, Feature-Gliederung v2.14.

Geprüft in der Vorschau: Verteiler im Büro angelegt und angesehen, auf der Baustelle einen Stromkreis nachgetragen und die Werte in der Datenbank kontrolliert, falsche Zahlen im Formular abgelehnt, das PDF mit dem lokalen Renderer gedruckt. Die Beispieldaten haben jetzt zwei Verteiler im Zählerschrank der Familie Berg. Tests: domain 253, server 592, web 246.

Closes #70

body:
## Summary
- Add `` `<base>` `` alongside `"the base branch"` and `` `<default>` `` in the base-branch substitution instruction (14 generated SKILL.md files, sourced from `scripts/resolvers/utility.ts`). Skills already use `<base>` interchangeably in later commands (e.g. `git diff <base>...HEAD`), so accepting it in the placeholder list matches actual usage.
- Route `gh pr merge` through `-R "$PR_REPO" "$PR_NUMBER"` in `land-and-deploy/sections/merge-and-deploy.md.tmpl`. Without `-R`, `gh` runs `git checkout <base>` locally after a successful server merge; when `<base>` is checked out in a sibling worktree (Conductor and other multi-workspace setups), that fails with `fatal: '<base>' is already used by worktree at ...`. The server merge still lands, but `--delete-branch` does not run, leaving an orphan head ref. `-R` routes every step through the API and skips the local git operations, so it's strictly safer even outside worktree setups.

## Relationship to prior PRs
- Reopens the placeholder-polish change from #2872 (closed 2026-09-20 to keep it local for a while); resubmitting now.

author: cheeezis
body:
## Summary
- Dokumentiert alle Netzwerkpfade der Anwendung (Browser → Review, Worker/Review → Postgres/Storage/Key Vault, lokaler Zugriff, CI/CD → Azure) in [docs/networking.md](docs/networking.md).
- Analysiert, was öffentlich erreichbar ist und warum: Postgres, Storage und Key Vault haben öffentliche Endpunkte, weil die Container-Apps-Consumption-Umgebung keine feste ausgehende IP hat und Azure dafür kein Service-Tag veröffentlicht (geprüft).
- Bewusste Entscheidung dokumentiert, keine VNet-Integration/Private Endpoints einzuführen: würde ~20+ EUR/Monat zusätzlich kosten, für dieses Projekt (keine Daten Dritter, keine Compliance-Vorgabe) nicht gerechtfertigt. TLS + RBAC/Passwort tragen die eigentliche Zugriffskontrolle.

## Todo-Stand (Phase 11 der Roadmap)
1. Terraform State in Remote Backend verschieben — bereits in Phase 10 erledigt (vorgezogen, da CI es brauchte)
2. State-Dateien nicht versionieren — bereits erfüllt (`*.tfstate` seit je in `.gitignore`)
3. Netzwerkpfade dokumentieren — erledigt (dieser PR)
4. Prüfen, welche Dienste öffentlich erreichbar sein müssen — erledigt (dieser PR, Analyse in docs/networking.md)
5. Datenbankzugriff einschränken — bewusst nicht weiter eingeschränkt (dieser PR begründet warum); TLS + eingeschränkte App-Rolle bleiben der eigentliche Schutz

## Test plan
- Keine Infrastrukturänderung in diesem PR, nur Dokumentation — kein `terraform plan`/`apply` nötig.

author: zz-plant
body:
**What changed, and why.**

A goal that named none of the curated tree's words had no route in. The roadmap listed this as §5's gap. `ambit goal "<sentence>" --judge[=url]` closes it using a Jev-compatible model on this machine.

- **When it asks.** It asks only when the vocabulary cannot recommend. A goal the words already cover never opens a socket. Without `--judge`, nothing is ever contacted, whatever `AMBIT_JUDGE_URL` says.
- **What it asks.** The sentence goes out as one Choice question over every curated node, using each node's name and one-line description. It is sent to `/v1/systemone` in TypeSafe's wire format.
- **What it returns.** A suggestion with its probability, plus the three likeliest nodes. If no node reaches even odds, it lists the likeliest and suggests nothing. An answer naming a node the tree doesn't have is treated as no answer. A judge that errors or isn't running produces a message, not a crash.
- **What it writes.** Nothing. A test compares `ambit status` before and after.

**Where it may ask.** The new `judgeUrl` in `src/engine/judge.ts` parses the URL instead of matching a prefix. It accepts only `http://` to `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]`, with no credentials. A prefix test would pass `http://127.0.0.1:1@host`, and every HTTP client reads that as a request to `host`. The default is Kev on `127.0.0.1:8009`, overridable with `AMBIT_JUDGE_URL`, and `AMBIT_JUDGE_MODEL` names a model if the server needs one.

This makes `goal --judge` the fifth command that opens a socket. The security-invariant sections of the README, SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md now list it, and so does the FAQ's egress table, with exactly what is sent. The CLI help, the deep dive's CLI surface, the roadmap, the changelog and `llms.txt` describe it. The MCP `ambit_goal` tool does not offer it yet, and the roadmap says so.

**A formatter fix it needed.** The text view stopped one level into nested objects, so it printed that a suggestion existed but not what it was. `ambit can` lost fields the same way once. Nested blocks now render all the way down. A nested `id` does not get promoted to a headline, so existing output reads as it did, and the README's captured console blocks are unchanged.

**Tests.**
- `src/engine/judge.test.ts` has ten tests. They cover the URL rules, the question's shape, suggesting at even odds or better, listing below it, ignoring answers outside the tree, error handling, writing nothing, never asking when the words recommend, opening no socket without `--judge`, and refusing a host off this machine before sending anything.
- `src/engine/cli/output.test.ts` holds the recursive rendering.
- Removing the loopback test, the credentials test, or the only-when-unmatched condition each fails the test written for it. The formatter test fails against the old formatter.
- I also ran the real `./cli.js` against a fake local judge, both with a suggestion and with a refused host and an absent server.

Verified locally: `lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `test:coverage` (476 passing), `demo:check`, `docs:examples:check`, `prose:check` (8.18 dash/1k, 2.77 rather-than/1k), `assets:check`, and a link and anchor check across every markdown file.

**Checks.** CI runs [the same gate](https://github.com/zz-plant/ambit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-checks-ci-runs) on every push; running it locally first is faster than a round trip.

- [ ] If this touches `src/server/api.ts`: it still binds loopback only. The origin check and the no-entry-creation rule have tests; the bind address does not.
- [ ] If this touches where the graph is stored: the engine, MCP server, and visualizer API all resolve `src/shared/db-path.ts`
- [ ] If this edits `src/engine/techtree.json`: it links the capability-model issue where the era or prerequisite was argued
- [ ] If this adds a runtime reader or a declared check: it ships with a test

body:
Stacked on #78 (the #77 Soft Paper foundation — this branch builds on it; merge that first).

## What (decision #72, validated in issue #72's resolution)

**URL scope.** `#/highlights?article=<id>` — minimal query-param support in `parseHash` (`#/path?k=v`); only `article` on the review route; tag/confidence/sort stay component state. Deep-link, reload, and browser-Back all behave, including a scope that outlives its article.

**Scoped UI (one slot, two states).** While scoped, the article combobox is replaced by a removable pill scope chip (inside-× clear → navigates to `#/highlights`, a real history push so Back returns to the scoped URL); the "article" sort option is absent while scoped; clearing never leaves a hidden combobox filter behind. A vanished scope renders the calm "(deleted article)" chip, keeps its orphan rows (never-drop, badged "Article missing"), and shows the honest back-to-all empty state when zero rows remain.

**Entries (one per surface, gated at ≥ 1).**
- Annotations drawer: "Review highlights" next to "Export highlights" (hidden at 0).
- Library rows: a highlights anchor in the icon cluster with the count in the aria-label (chapters yes / books no) — driven by THE per-article highlight-count fold on the LibrarySnapshot.
- Review combobox (unscoped): every article findable incl. zero-highlight ones, counts in the suggestion labels (native select — the shared TagPicker-pattern combobox can replace it deliberately when #75 lands).

**Honesty.** The review mount's shared back affordance relabels to "Back" (entries arrive from article pages as often as from the library); article page keeps "Back to library".

## Verification

- `npm run lint` ✅ · `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · unit **2,443 passed** (14 new)
- New `tests/e2e/review-panel/scope.spec.ts` (7 tests: entries, scoped UI, chip-clear + Back round trip, reload survival, deleted-article orphan rows, vanished-scope empty state) — green on chromium/firefox/webkit, alongside every touched suite (review-panel, back-nav, panel-keyboard, card-actions, metadata-edit, library-restore, a11y, reduced-motion, forced-colors, header-geometry, tag-popover): **232 passed on firefox+webkit, full chromium pass on the touched set**.
- Full three-engine suite: the only failures are **pre-existing on pristine main** (verified by identical runs against 6618aba: epub/pdf intake, the two portability journeys, imagery geometry, annotation span specs, toc/shell-nav singletons). The e2e rot that blocked gating at all — 11 suites' fixture sentinel + the round-trip rate literal — is repaired in this PR's tail commits.

author: puemos
body:
## Problem

In the work layout, the title of a pane starts at a different distance from the left edge on each surface, so the title jumps as you move between a session and a space page.

- A session title with a breadcrumb starts 12px from the pane edge.
- A session title with plain text starts 4px from the pane edge, left of the page under it.
- A work-layout space page starts 24px, because it adds its own `pl-5` to reach the inset its body uses.

The pane title bar asks `ChromeBar` for `inset="control"` (4px), which assumes the title starts with a button. Each view then makes up the difference, or does not.

## Changes

- Every pane title now starts 24px from the pane edge, on the same line as the page under it.
- `ChromeBar` gains a `title` inset and exports `PANE_INSET`, the one value a title bar and its body share.
- Title content that starts with a small button (`ChannelBreadcrumb`, `ReportBreadcrumbs`) cancels that button's own padding with `LEADING_BUTTON_PULL`, so a breadcrumb title and a text title land on the same line.
- The local `pl-5` in the space page and the spaces list goes away, so a view no longer states the inset itself.

The alternative was to keep the 4px bar and give each view the padding it needs. That is the state this PR removes: the value lived in five places and three of them disagreed.

Left edge measured in the browser, in device pixels. The pane border adds 1px, so 25 is the 24px inset.

| Surface | Title inset before | Title inset after | Body inset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session, breadcrumb title | 13 | 25 | 25 |
| Session, plain title | 5 | 25 | 25 |
| Space page | 25 | 25 | 25 |
| Spaces list | 25 | 25 | 33 (list rows) |

Session, breadcrumb title:

![compare-session-breadcrumb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/c3e247a0d4e67f4574ef14607d5365ee5c69b6de/2026/09/155ca19d-b7a5-42e0-90f5-1e7436b33fb2.png)

Session, plain title:

![compare-session-plain-title](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/4dc36fd647817947733635c163bbf0112061d108/2026/09/843953b1-8c36-45ce-be7e-3ca1fd25a9c1.png)

Space page, unchanged:

![compare-space-page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/1ffcac7343bc9887fb8a6e0540722f079bd3faa6/2026/09/edafc60d-68ca-4e2b-8ae0-4d914d3f7643.png)

Spaces list, unchanged:

![compare-spaces-list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/da1d344b75360029bfd3fe93217fdf691433ddc1/2026/09/bb058e2b-632f-481e-9536-31109e0661ef.png)

## How did you test this code?

The numbers above come from a temporary Storybook story that rendered each title bar with the real components, plus a Playwright script that measured the left edge of the first painted glyph in the bar and in the body. The story and the script are not part of this PR.

Ran `pnpm --filter @posthog/ui typecheck` and the Vitest files that cover the touched components (`ChannelBreadcrumb`, `SpaceHeaderRow`, `ShellLayout`, the inbox suite). No new test: the change is a spacing value, and a test that asserts a class string would not catch the drift it fixes.

Not checked: the running Electron app, and the surfaces outside the work layout that share these bars (canvas toolbar, inbox report detail). They take the same inset, so their titles move right by up to 20px.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

The `ChromeBar` rule in `products/desktop/AGENTS.md` now names the `title` inset and the two shared constants.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), Claude Opus 5

The work started as a root-cause question about the spacing before a pane title in the work layout, then moved to the fix and the measurements above.

Skills invoked: `/editing-agents-md`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: the CLI is not installed in this sandbox, so the PR opens without a local pass.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "pane title inset"` and a search for the chrome bar returned no PR on this.

Public artifact: nothing here comes from a customer conversation, a ticket, or a log. The screenshots render invented story data.

body:
Six files. The registry now declares the tree it already had, so Descent has real
edges to draw; the Gate config the project needs ships with it; and the README gains
the two sections. Nothing here depends on the objective tier or the release cut
lines.

## 1. The Gate column's successor

`cannon-template/workflow.json:85` now reads "Green advances to Align".

**Every "advances to" in the repository, both in that one file:**

    cannon-template/workflow.json:9   advances to Build
    cannon-template/workflow.json:85  advances to Align   (was Review)

Nothing else names the Gate column's successor, in `cannon-template/` or anywhere
else.

## 2. The registry is nested

    US-LEND-10
      FR-LEND-10
        AC-LEND-10, AC-LEND-20
    US-OUT-10
      FR-OUT-10
        AC-OUT-10, AC-OUT-20
    US-RET-10
      FR-RET-10
        AC-RET-10
    NFR-PRIV-10
      AC-PRIV-10, AC-PRIV-20
    NFR-DUR-10
      AC-DUR-10
    NFR-ENG-10
      AC-ENG-10
    US-UI-10
      FR-UI-10
        AC-UI-10, AC-UI-20, AC-UI-30
    US-UI-20
      AC-UI-40

**No ID and no statement changed.** Proved two ways: the sorted list of IDs before
and after is identical, and stripping leading whitespace from both versions of the
file gives byte-identical text. The diff is 24 lines changed, all of them
indentation.

**The choices, each with the line that decided it.** Only one parent was genuinely
ambiguous, the one you named:

- **AC-UI-40 → US-UI-20**, not US-UI-10. Decided by
  `specs/backlog/tasks.md:32`: "T905 Show what a borrower has had before, on the
  Lend screen, once they are named. **Carries**: US-UI-20, AC-UI-40". The
  reservation that carries the criterion names that story and no other. US-UI-20
  has no requirement between them, so the criterion sits directly under the story.

Two others looked ambiguous on the page and were not, once the spec was read:

- **AC-OUT-10 → FR-OUT-10.** Its statement is about an item *marked returned*, which
  reads like RET's. `specs/002-outstanding-list/spec.md:9` lists it in that card's
  own ids, and line 29 states it as a property of the outstanding list. It belongs to
  the list, not to returning.
- **AC-UI-10, AC-UI-20, AC-UI-30 → FR-UI-10.**
  `specs/004-browser-screens/spec.md:9` carries all four IDs on one card, and line 36
  makes FR-UI-10 the app that serves the screens the three criteria then describe.

Families with no story, PRIV, DUR and ENG, have their non-functional at the top and
their criteria under it.

## 3. The config the project needs, and where it lives

`.specify/` is not shipped, because BANG.md step 5 installs it. So the project's own
copy is **`cannon-template/specassay-check-config.yml`**, with `parent_derivation`
and `test_results` live rather than commented.

**The exact lines added to BANG.md step 6:**

    Then put this project's own settings in place of the
    installed defaults:

        cp cannon-template/specassay-check-config.yml \
           .specify/extensions/specassay-check/specassay-check-config.yml

    The installed file has two settings this project needs and ships
    commented out: `parent_derivation`, which is what makes the
    specification a tree rather than a flat list, and `test_results`,
    which is what makes a passing test count as proof rather than a test
    whose name merely matches. Receipt: the first two lines of
    `bash .specify/extensions/specassay-check/scripts/check-traceability.sh`,
    which name the config file it found, and
    `grep ^parent_derivation .specify/extensions/specassay-check/specassay-check-config.yml`
    printing `parent_derivation: heading-nesting`.

## 4. The Gate, with parents

Run in a throwaway copy of the rehearsal board with this PRD and this config, so

author: jongodi
body:
`npm run map:sync` stopped with `Villa: exaroton svaraði 404 fyrir <server>/files/info/bluemap/web`. The script assumed BlueMap's web app is in `bluemap/web`, and exaroton answers 404 when a path doesn't exist on the server. On this server, the plugin jar and the top-level `bluemap` folder are gone after a restart. The panel doesn't show a server's size, so a size tool was added to rule out exaroton's limit. It did: the server is 3.97 GB of a 10 GB limit.

## Changes
- **`scripts/sync-map.mjs` finds the folder itself.** It reads `webroot` from BlueMap's own `webapp.conf`: `plugins/BlueMap` on Paper/Spigot, `config/bluemap` on Fabric/Forge.
  - `BLUEMAP_WEBROOT` in `.env.local` overrides it; `bluemap/web` stays the fallback.
  - If the folder isn't there, the error says what to look for in exaroton's file manager.
  - If the folder isn't the default, it says to set `BLUEMAP_WEBROOT` in Vercel too.
- **`src/app/bluemap/[[...path]]/route.ts`** (live player positions) reads the same `BLUEMAP_WEBROOT`. When it's unset or empty it behaves exactly as before.
- **`npm run server:size`** (`scripts/server-size.mjs`) walks the server through the exaroton API, read-only.
  - It prints the total, then follows the large folders down to the dimension and region level.
  - It points out the usual things that can be trimmed: BlueMap, logs, crash reports, Paper's cache, and CoreProtect's database.
  - If the API won't list the top folder, it measures the usual top-level folders one by one.
- **Docs:** `.env.local.example` and the README list the new variable and command.

## Testing
- Lint, `tsc` and the 29 unit tests pass.
- The `webroot` parser was checked against BlueMap's stock `webapp.conf`: quoted and unquoted values, `./` prefixes and trailing slashes, and commented-out lines.
- `server:size` has been run against the real server (output: 3.97 GB, almost all of it in `world/dimensions/minecraft`).
- The new `webroot` detection in `map:sync` hasn't been run against exaroton yet.

body:
## Outcome

Core now carries opening capital from the immediately preceding governed business date. A Monday response therefore uses Friday's close, while a missing Friday observation fails closed instead of borrowing Thursday.

Fixes the remaining canonical acceptance defect tracked by #1143.

## Ownership and invariant

- Persistence selects the authoritative prior date from Core's `GLOBAL` business calendar.
- The application maps only those admitted prior observations into both position and portfolio source products.
- Transaction instants, trade dates, settlement dates, cashflow chronology, tenant authority, and financial fallback policy are unchanged.
- No runtime split, migration, API schema, IAM grant, docs, or wiki change.

## Evidence

- Red-first helper regression reproduced Friday being discarded for a Monday window.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/services/query_control_plane_service/application/analytics/test_analytics_timeseries_service.py tests/unit/services/query_control_plane_service/application/analytics/test_analytics_position_pages.py tests/unit/services/query_control_plane_service/infrastructure/test_analytics_timeseries_repository.py -q` — 88 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/integration/services/query_control_plane_service/test_analytics_cashflow_trade_date_postgresql.py -q` — 2 passed on real PostgreSQL in 62.91s.
- PostgreSQL proof covers UTC, Asia/Singapore, and America/Los_Angeles; Friday-to-Monday continuity; stale-Thursday rejection; position/portfolio opening equality; trade-date acquisition; settlement chronology; and independent 500 -> 514 -> 515 capital attribution.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/services/query_service/test_test_manifest.py -q` — 44 passed; the PostgreSQL file remains admitted to `critical-db-coverage`.
- `make lint` — passed.
- `make typecheck` — passed.
- `make check` — passed; 9,962 unit tests, 3 skipped, 16 deselected, zero warnings (the target executes the unit suite twice).

## Acceptance boundary

This PR supplies Core source correctness only. Demo acceptance still requires exact-main Core release checks, a source-built governed canonical rerun, Risk attribution `ready`, and browser-verified Workbench panels. It does not substitute for downstream consumer acceptance or production evidence.

Final candidate head: `4850dd89aa4096b1958d6a160b982b0dd148bfa0` (signed). The initial candidate touched the large analytics service only to remove an obsolete argument; the maintainability ratchet rejected that cosmetic edit, so the final candidate preserves the compatible call surface and confines the correction to the focused policy helper and PostgreSQL adapter. No baseline or threshold was changed.

author: santiagohb2830
body:
Código ejecutable de la PoC CFG-13. El informe va en Trama-AS/MANI-docs, PR aparte (ADR-0001, ADR-0007).

**Mergear después de #7.** Esta rama sale de `feature/SCRUM-929-poc-claims-tenant`, porque el caso 6 vive en `mani-aislamiento`, que solo existe ahí. Hasta que #7 entre, este diff incluye sus 11 commits; los propios de CFG-13 son los 6 últimos. Base `release` y no la rama de CFG-12 para que corra `ci.yml` (DoD punto 1).

## Qué responde

¿El bucket único con rutas `tenant_id/<usuario>/archivo` y la política RLS de ADR-0013 impiden que otro tenant acceda a los documentos KYC de un aliado, y en cuánto se carga un documento?

**Sí.** Cero accesos entre tenants por emisión de URL, descarga, listado o subida, y el control negativo confirma que lo produce la política.

## Resultados

Umbral publicado en SCRUM-930 antes de medir.

| Medición | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| Carga de 1 MB, p95 (30 corridas) | **1180 ms** (umbral 2000 ms) |
| `createSignedUrl`, peor p95 | **423 ms** (umbral 500 ms) — margen estrecho |
| `mani-aislamiento` completa, 6 casos de ADR-0015 | 95/95 |
| `mani-claims` (regresión CFG-12) | 40/40 |
| Control negativo — política que solo mira el bucket | 75/95, 20 fallidas |
| Suite sin bucket (línea base) | positivos en rojo, negativos en verde |

El control negativo no es "quitar la política": sin políticas Storage lo niega todo y los negativos seguirían verdes. Se reemplazó por una que deja pasar a cualquier autenticado. Todo lo que depende del predicado de tenant cae en rojo; N8–N10 siguen verdes porque los protege otra capa (`TO authenticated`, bucket privado, firma del token).

## Qué entra

| Ruta | Qué |
| --- | --- |
| `supabase/poc-cfg13/00_verificar_terreno.sql` | Terreno (solo lectura) |
| `supabase/poc-cfg13/10_bucket_kyc.sql` | Bucket `kyc-documentos` y `kyc_isolation` (SCRUM-977) |
| `supabase/poc-cfg13/20_seed_storage.sql` | Corrige `ruta_storage` de las filas de CFG-12 |
| `qa/storage/cargar_kyc.mjs` | Fixtures: cada aliado sube su cédula con su JWT (SCRUM-978) |
| `qa/storage/bench_carga.mjs` | Tiempo de carga (SCRUM-979) |
| `qa/newman/mani-aislamiento.*.json` | Caso 6 real, reemplaza la centinela de CFG-12 (SCRUM-980) |

Sin dependencias nuevas: `fetch` nativo de Node. Nunca `service_role`.

## Sobre lo aplicado en QA

En `hpsxdotaizzclkeufzct` quedan el bucket, `kyc_isolation` (restaurada tras el control negativo) y dos PDFs sintéticos. Los scripts traen bloque de reversión.

## Qué revisar con atención

- **Una URL firmada es un token al portador** (caso C1). La descarga por `/object/sign` no pasa por RLS: la política decide quién *emite* la URL, no quién la usa. Diseño de Supabase, no defecto. Las mitigaciones (TTL corto, no persistir la URL) son decisión del Backend Lead.
- **El segundo segmento de la ruta es `auth.uid()`, no `aliado.id`** como dice ADR-0013. N11 muestra que con `aliado.id` el dueño queda bloqueado. Es KI-05 del SAD con un caso concreto.
- **`kyc_isolation` es `FOR ALL`**: `admin_tenant` puede subir y borrar documentos de sus aliados, no solo leerlos.
- Cada caso de la suite declara qué criterio de aceptación cubre (DoR punto 7).

## Deuda que excede a este PR

- La suite de ADR-0015 sigue sin correr en CI (QS-17).
- La política de Storage no está en `database/migrations/` (misma deuda que SCRUM-1051).
- DEV y PROD sin evaluar (SCRUM-1053).

Ticket: SCRUM-930 · Subtareas: SCRUM-977, 978, 979, 980, 981 · Resuelve en QA: SCRUM-1053

body:
### Motivation

- Fournir une carte interactive des stations de ski en France réutilisable pour l'aperçu global et la fiche station en se basant sur l'API backend `GET /api/stations/map`.
- Utiliser les solutions Google Maps modernes (Maps JavaScript API, `AdvancedMarkerElement`, `@googlemaps/markerclusterer`) tout en chargeant la librairie côté client pour préserver le rendu SSR et la performance.
- Respecter l'architecture existante Next.js (Pages Router) et réutiliser les composants/styles/site structure sans casser le comportement actuel.

### Description

- Ajout d'une page publique SSR `pages/carte-stations-ski.tsx` qui récupère les stations via `fetchStationMapServer` et affiche la carte en mode `overview` avec clustering.
- Création d'un composant réutilisable client-only `src/components/maps/StationMap.tsx` (et son loader dynamique `StationMapDynamic.tsx`) supportant `mode="overview"` et `mode="station"`, utilisant `AdvancedMarkerElement`, une unique `InfoWindow`, `MarkerClusterer`, et le `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_MAP_ID` pour le rendu avancé des marqueurs.
- Ajout du fetcher serveur `src/lib/api/stationMap.ts` et du type public `src/types/stationMap.ts` qui normalisent la réponse backend (accepte `array`, `data`, `results`, `items`) et filtrent les éléments sans `id`, `slug`, `name` ou coordonnées valides.
- Intégration sur la fiche station `pages/stations/[slug].tsx` d'un bloc « Localisation de [station] » qui s'affiche uniquement si `latitude` et `longitude` publiées existent, et suppression du fallback Nominatim pour éviter de substituer des coordonnées non publiées.
- Mise à jour UI/SEO/navigation: ajout du lien de navigation (`ProHeader`, `Footer`), entrée sitemap (`src/lib/sitemap.ts`), styles responsive (`src/styles/globals.css`) et `.env.example` documentant `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` et `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_MAP_ID`.
- Déclaration de dépendance dans les manifests pour le clustering officiel : `@googlemaps/markerclusterer@^2.6.2` et ajout de tests contractuels `tests/station-map.test.js` vérifiant Advanced Markers, cluster, InfoWindow unique, Map ID, endpoint et absence de géocodage de substitution.
- Commande recommandée pour installer la dépendance (à exécuter dans un environnement réseau autorisé) : `npm install @googlemaps/markerclusterer`.

### Testing

- Exécution des tests unitaires avec `npm test` a réussi : `178` tests passés et `0` échec.
- Vérification TypeScript avec `npx tsc --noEmit` a réussi sans erreur de types.
- Build de production avec `npm run build` s'est déroulé avec succès et a généré la route `/carte-stations-ski` ainsi que les pages existantes sans erreurs de compilation.
- Vérification lint/installation réseau : `npx eslint ...` n'a pas pu être exécuté dans cet environnement à cause d'un problème d'export `eslint/config` lié à la plateforme, et l'installation réseau de `@googlemaps/*` a été bloquée par le proxy (HTTP 403), donc la dépendance est déclarée dans les manifests mais n'a pas été récupérée depuis le registre dans cet environnement.
