author: benemon
body:
## Why

The version screen needs four numbers per build and a cross-build headline, and derives them by downloading every package and finding: 25 pages and 24 to 35 thousand findings for a kernel image, on every visit. Recent console work (#215, #219) made that tolerable; this makes it unnecessary. The figures change only when a scan completes, so they are computed there, once, and stored.

## Change

**Schema, migration 000003.** `build_findings_summary` and `version_findings_summary`, tenant-scoped under the same RLS shape as the other scan tables, each row carrying an integrity MAC. No immutability trigger: rows are rewritten on each completion that advances the build's current findings run.

**Write path.** Inside `RecordScanRun`'s transaction, after the pointer advance and only when the run became current. The build row deduplicates findings by package identity and advisory (the same rule as the compat plane); the version row deduplicates across the version's builds under a version-level advisory lock, taking the worst band, which mirrors the console's `versionRollup`. Both are derived from rows the transaction has just written and verified, never from an SQL aggregate over unverified rows. Reads verify the MAC and fail closed. A build deleted while its scan was in flight makes the recompute a no-op.

**Backfill.** The scanner service writes missing summaries for builds with current findings when it starts. Cannot be a migration: the MAC needs the key.

**Endpoint, spec first.** `GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/projects/{project}/buckets/{bucket}/versions/{fingerprint}/findings-summary`, reader role, tenancy checked before role, audited as `findings_summary.read`. Returns `scanner_configured`, the version rollup (null when no build has a current run), and every build with its live distinct package count, an `inventory` flag, and a `summary` present only when a current run exists.

## Proof

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `make test-integration` | green (postgres, keyring, cmd) |
| `make test-rls-sabotage` | 17 tables incl. both new ones fail as required |
| `make test-contract` | green |
| unit, vet, lint, generate-check | clean |

Mutations, each observed failing its named test then restored:
- M1 count per build instead of deduping across builds → cross-build dedupe test
- M2 write the summary when the current run did not advance → stale-completion test
- M3 skip MAC verification on read → tamper test (`error = <nil>, want fail-closed`)
- M4 drop an RLS policy → sabotage lane
- M5 render `summary: {}` for an unscanned build → absent-not-empty test
- M6 authorise role before tenancy → foreign tenancy must stay 404

The console switch to this endpoint is the follow-on slice; the user guides change there.

author: ralphhtml
body:
## What changed

Ideas adopted from a Three.js storm-volume viewer, ported into the existing CPU ray marcher; the page stays WebGL-free by design.

**Raw pixels look** - a third option in the Look picker beside Lit cloud and Solid surface. It samples the nearest gate with no blending between gates or tilts, turns the light off entirely, and gives every gate above the Show above threshold one flat density, so the picture is the exact bytes the radar measured: crisp voxel edges, visible beam cones and all. Implemented as a `crisp` flag through the marcher (the coarse drag pass already sampled this way; crisp keeps it at full resolution) and a flat transfer function in the LUT.

**Glowing cores** - in Lit cloud mode, returns above about 72% of the product's scale now radiate brighter than their palette colour (up to ~1.6x at the top), so a hail core or debris ball glows out of the shading instead of sitting matte inside the cloud. Baked into the LUT, zero per-sample cost.

**Fullscreen** - a new button in the panel header pins the panel over the entire viewport (forced over the drag handle's inline position), Esc exits, and closing the panel always leaves fullscreen cleanly.

## Tests
- New section 7c in tools/test-radar-3d.mjs (7 checks): the crisp flag and its wiring, Raw pixels rendering the fixture block unshaded, the flat pixels transfer function vs the curved cloud one, the glow ratio, and the full fullscreen lifecycle (button on, Esc off, close always off)
- Full suite: 161 checks, all passing twice in a row

Note: tools/test-tutorial-truth.mjs has 3 pre-existing failures (account menu buttons, export coverage, bubble row internals) that reproduce on main before this change; not touched here.

author: ghigog
body: Closes out the three `migration_plan.md` §6.4 components, adds the CI job that was missing for half the shell, and writes up what Phase 6 actually amounts to. ## 1. CI covers the TypeScript front end The Rust job already covered `apps/desktop/src-tauri`. Nothing covered the other half: ~1,400 lines of `main.ts` reached `main` having never been type-checked. The new `desktop` job runs `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest` and `vite build`. It starts green, so it is a regression gate rather than a backlog item. `vite build` is there to catch what `tsc` cannot — an import that type-checks but does not resolve or bundle. The shell has to build offline-complete (§2.3), so a dependency that only works when fetched at runtime has to fail here. ## 2. The three §6.4 components | Item | Outcome | |---|---| | Markdown in chat ([#15](https://github.com/Ghigog/orison/issues/15)) | Bought — `marked` + `DOMPurify` | | Mind map ([#34](https://github.com/Ghigog/orison/issues/34)) | Bought — Cytoscape.js | | Chat virtualisation | **Declined, on measurement** | **Markdown** is nearly the one-line import §6.4 predicted, plus three constraints it did not. Model output is not trusted markup — a vault note, or an injection inside one, can put a link or an `` into a character's line — so links and images never become elements at all, and DOMPurify re-checks against an allow-list with no `a`, `img`, `script` or `iframe` and no attributes whatsoever. Streaming stays plain, because half-arrived markdown is broken markdown and a row parsed on every delta would flicker for the length of a 15-second turn. Quoted-speech bolding is a design decision rather than a markdown feature, so it is reapplied over the rendered tree. Markdown applies to narration and character speech only; SYSTEM, YOU and ERROR rows are engine output, the player's own typed words and a Rust error string. 21 tests, asserted against the rendered DOM rather than the parser's output string. **The graph** draws the decision `docs/design/README.md` records: the retrieval graph, not a world map. Nodes come from the edges as well as the entity lists, because the graph reaches lore notes, items and RAPTOR summaries that neither list returns. The canvas is `aria-hidden` with the node and edge lists beside it as the keyboard path, since a `` cannot be tabbed through. Cytoscape is ~440 kB for one screen, so `graph.ts` is dynamically imported and the main bundle stays at 105 kB rather than 541 kB. One bug worth recording, because no assertion would have caught it: Cytoscape parses colours with its own parser, which predates `oklch()` — and every design token is written in `oklch`. Handed one it falls back to black. The first render had black nodes and solid black blocks where the edge labels' backing plates should have been, while mounting cleanly, laying out, filtering and reporting correct node counts throughout. Tokens are now resolved to sRGB via a 1×1 canvas. `bench/graph-preview/` exists because looking is the only way that class of defect surfaces. **Virtualisation is the one §6.4 got wrong.** The cost that scales is streaming: every `StreamDelta` sets `scrollTop = scrollHeight`, forcing a synchronous layout of the whole container, hundreds of times per turn. Measured in Chromium against three arms, per delta, median of 3: | rows | plain DOM | windowed (ceiling) | `content-visibility` | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 40 | 0.52 ms | 0.26 ms | 0.008 ms | | 200 | 0.31 ms | 0.48 ms | 0.006 ms | | 1000 | 0.86 ms | 0.14 ms | 0.005 ms | | 5000 | 6.36 ms | 0.16 ms | 0.021 ms | The windowed column is an idealised list holding only visible rows — a ceiling no library reaches, chosen so that if the ceiling loses there is nothing left to buy. It loses at every size. Buying would also have meant replacing the append-only DOM that `StreamDelta` and the provisional-row pattern depend on, for a slower result. Checked rather than assumed: containment makes `scrollHeight` an estimate, and the transcript relies on it to land the newest row in view. Verified across 200 and 2000 rows with deliberately uneven heights — correct in every arm. Where the property is unsupported (WebKitGTK < 2.46, Safari < 18) it is ignored and behaviour is the plain-DOM column. `VirtualScrollContainer.gd` existed because Godot `Control` nodes are expensive to hold in quantity. Paragraphs are not. The port inherited the constraint along with the component. ## 3. Phase 6, closed honestly Two of three exit criteria are met. Feature parity is not, and the gaps are three different kinds the plan did not distinguish: no first-run path (real, small), no character creator (real — only the adventure-starter half of `OnboardingFlow.gd` was ported), and three image-generation screens blocked on D-7 being Open rather than on work. Toasts and floating emoji are not gaps; round 2 dropped both deliberately. **The finding that matters most is not on the checklist: nobody has run this application.** Every screen has been verified by `clippy`, `cargo test`, `tsc`, `vitest` and `vite build` in an environment with no display and no Ollama. [#30](https://github.com/Ghigog/orison/issues/30) existed to fix that and was closed without a playthrough, on the defensible reasoning that a playtest before parity would rediscover known gaps. The consequence is that no exit criterion has been confirmed by use — and "keyboard-navigable throughout" in particular is an argument from how the markup was written, not an observation of anyone navigating it. Also recorded: the design-token amendment ([#32](https://github.com/Ghigog/orison/issues/32) implemented round 2's tokens; `design_philosophy.md` still specifies round 1's), D-5 decided as "no framework, and that was a default rather than a conclusion", and the scene count corrected from 25 to 24. ## What this leaves open Not done here, and deliberately: the BBCode half of [#15](https://github.com/Ghigog/orison/issues/15) (`[wave]`, `[color=…]` are Godot `RichTextLabel` effects, and animated text argues against round 2's paper direction — a product decision, so the issue stays open), the first-run path, the character creator, D-7, and rewriting `design_philosophy.md`. The Phase 7 handoff has not been written; that was held back pending this. ## Verification `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest run` (21 passed), `vite build` all green. Benchmarks reproduced from a clean checkout per `apps/desktop/bench/README.md`. Both themes screenshotted and inspected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_016nSG69ojxQtqzkPnNkDq4S --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_016nSG69ojxQtqzkPnNkDq4S)_

author: mark-brannan
body:
## What

Closes #34. This repo defines six reusable workflows and ran none of them
on its own PRs — all `workflow_call` only, no caller, and the `main branch
protection` ruleset had no `required_status_checks` rule at all. #32 merged
with only the CodeRabbit app check on it.

Adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `on: pull_request`, fanning
`nonempty-diff` and `secret-scan` into a `ci-gate` job, the same pattern
`ci-gate.yml` documents and every vended repo (dotfiles, symphony,
colregs-engine) already uses.

## Local path vs `@main`

Every `uses:` here points at this repo's own
`./.github/workflows/{nonempty-diff,secret-scan,ci-gate}.yml`, not `@main`.

Every other caller of these workflows should keep using `@main` — a normal
repo has no reason to trust an unmerged version of someone else's shared
workflow. But this is the one repo whose PRs *are* changes to those
workflows. Self-referencing at `@main` would mean a PR that breaks
`nonempty-diff.yml` still gates on main's unbroken copy and merges anyway —
no different from having no gate. Local path tests what the PR actually
changes, at the cost of diverging from the pattern every vended repo
follows. That divergence is the point: this repo is the one place gating
main's copy of itself would be gating the wrong thing.

`secret-scan`'s two jobs (`gitleaks`, `trufflehog`) are folded into
`ci-gate` here rather than required directly the way dotfiles does it —
this repo has no other repo-specific gating jobs alongside them, so one
required context is simpler than three.

## Ruleset

Once this merges and a run exists to pick from, I'll add `ci-gate / gate`
to the `main branch protection` ruleset's `required_status_checks` (empty
today) — same shape as dotfiles' ruleset entry for the same context.

## Test plan

- [ ] This PR's own `ci-gate / gate` check runs and goes green
- [ ] Ruleset updated with `ci-gate / gate` as a required check after merge

author: lynnswap
body:
## Purpose

The release workflow currently creates a draft with generated notes and requires a separate manual publication step. Start from a draft containing approved notes instead, then let CI attach verified assets and publish the same release after all checks pass.

## Changes

- Require an existing draft, pin its target to the workflow commit, and preserve its title, notes, and prerelease setting.
- Keep package and process tests ahead of the release build. Download the build artifact by ID, verify its archive and uploaded asset digests, create any missing tag at the tested SHA, then publish the draft. Tag creation conflicts or failures leave the release unpublished.
- Leave failed releases as drafts, repair partial draft uploads on retry, and confirm an already-published release without modifying it.
- Add release orchestration tests to CI and update maintainer instructions for draft preparation and automatic publication.

## Testing

- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v` — 27 tests passed, covering target pinning, tag creation conflicts/failures, note preservation, failed verification/uploads, and retries. GitHub API calls and uploads are mocked; asset verification uses the existing shell scripts.
- `actionlint` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex review completed with no findings.
- An end-to-end GitHub Actions release has not been run with this workflow yet.

author: copilot
body:
The `update` Actions job failed while deriving `APP_ID` from the IPK filename because parsing depended on `VERSION` from the release tag. When tag-derived version and asset filename version diverged, extraction failed and the workflow exited.

- **Root cause**
  - `APP_ID` extraction assumed exact filename shape tied to `TAG`/`VERSION`:
    - `${IPK_NAME%_${VERSION}_arm.ipk}`
  - This is brittle when upstream release metadata and asset naming are not perfectly aligned.

- **Change**
  - Replaced version-coupled shell parameter expansion with suffix-pattern stripping based on the actual IPK filename format.
  - New logic removes the trailing `_<anything-without-underscore>_arm.ipk`, so app ID is derived directly from `IPK_NAME`.

- **Workflow impact**
  - Keeps existing asset selection behavior unchanged.
  - Removes false-negative failures in `Fetch latest stable Nuvio release` caused by metadata drift.

```bash
# before
APP_ID="${IPK_NAME%_${VERSION}_arm.ipk}"

# after
APP_ID="$(printf '%s' "$IPK_NAME" | sed -E 's/_[^_]+_arm\.ipk$//')"
```

author: jaumecornado
body:
## What

The connector rejected every real read through ALMA with `invalid_configuration` before any request reached Google.

## Why

The contract types configuration as `Record<string, string | null>`: the host hands the connector every declared key, with `null` for the fields the organisation left empty. The configuration schema only accepted `undefined` for `read_mode` and `report_date`, and the tests only ever passed strings or omitted the keys, so the null shape never ran against the schema.

## How

- `read_mode` and `report_date` accept nullish input; `read_mode` still defaults to `assignments`.
- A regression test reads a page with both optional fields set to `null`, and checks that `report_date: null` still raises `missing_report_date` in purchased mode.
- Version bumped to 0.1.2 in `package.json` and the manifest so the merge publishes the fix.

## Verification

`pnpm verify` passes: build, Biome, typecheck, 59 tests and the review-record check. The failing shape was reproduced first against ALMA's real runtime path, which is how the bug was found.

author: aajaces
body:
Thirteen commits off `wave`. The one that matters for a running box is the first.

## The day page had stopped advancing

`316ba30f`. The hourly tick has two jobs — drain the catch-up backlog, and write up yesterday at the maintenance hour — and it did them in the wrong order. The backlog went first and unconditionally, so `yesterday` was reached only once the queue emptied. The backlog reaches ninety days back and drains at one day per hour, so any import puts months of old days in front of last night and the day page simply stops moving. Silently: the applet reports `success` every hour while writing a day from two months ago.

Measured on a real box on 2026-09-22 — the nine most recent days had no article, no events and `narration_attempts = 0`, never even offered, while that day's runs wrote July 15th through 23rd.

The freshest day now goes first at the maintenance hour and is not preemptable. It costs the backlog one slot in twenty-four and bounds how stale the day page can be at one day rather than at the length of the queue.

Yesterday also gets a due-check for the first time. `DUE_PREDICATE` is now shared by `catchup_candidates` and a new `day_is_due`; before, the maintenance hour ran the chain regardless, so a day that had burned all eight attempts was retried nightly forever — the attempt ceiling governed the backlog and not the one day it ran most often. Two `sqlx::test`s, one asserting the queue and the single-day check agree so they cannot drift.

## The wiki panel

`d69ded4b`, `c9ad9fc9`, `727182fa`. Eleven flat rows was the rail's own memorisation-tax problem moved one level down. The panel now names the two questions the record answers — Time (Today, Days, Years, Chapters, Lifeline) and Subjects (You, People, Places, Organizations, Stories).

Overview left: its href was `/wiki`, which is the Wiki tile's own destination, so the tile and the first row of its panel were the same click. History left: it is neither a time nor a subject, and on a box where the editor has never run it opens on nothing. Both pages are untouched.

Today arrived — the day is the most-read page in the product and the panel had a row for the index but none for the day itself. `/day`, `/year`, `/person`, `/place` and `/org` moved from Home's `owns` to Wiki's, so reading a day lights the room whose panel is beside it. Settings' "You" became "Profile"; the wiki has the other "You".

Rows take Atlas glyphs rather than Remix — ten drawn on the set's grid, because a column of Remix glyphs under an Atlas rail tile is two icon languages in one sidebar. Group headings match the Home panel's labels to the pixel; they shipped briefly as uppercase serif, which `app.css`'s global `h1-h6` rule chose for them.

## X bookmarks, and two paces

`9323de8c`, `f2328297`, `83d64272`, `fbad8031` — the box replays X's GraphQL with session cookies, the backfill is paced, and both X and GitHub stars move to twice a day.

## Also

`5299c86e` the inline editor stops outranking the pinned model, and an empty stored pin cannot reach the gateway. `2d1427ef` copy baseline back to zero em dashes. Three plan docs on reminders and push encryption.

author: cd-rite
body:
# New client: two font families and a five-step type scale

Consolidates the clientV2 typography so every font size and family in the client comes from a token declared once in `style.css`, with a convention test that keeps it that way. Also fixes the column layout of the Collection dashboard metrics grids.

## Type scale

`style.css` declares the scale next to `--font-mono`:

| token | rem | at 12px root | for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--text-sm` | 0.85 | 10.2px | badges, pills, counts, author/timestamp lines, kicker labels |
| `--text-md` | 1 | 12px | everything read to act on: cells, inputs, labels, hints, validation messages, buttons, logs, table headers |
| `--text-lg` | 1.1 | 13.2px | Review checklist cell text, Rule titles, nav rail labels, in-page panel titles |
| `--text-xl` | 1.25 | 15px | section headings, modal titles, breadcrumb, large stat values |
| `--text-2xl` | 1.5 | 18px | page titles, wizard step titles, empty-state headlines, CORA score |
| `--text-display`, `-lg`, `-xl` | 2 / 3 / 5 | | 404 code, bootstrap art, large standalone icons |
| `--icon-xs` | 0.75 | 9px | standalone glyphs only (carets, clear and dismiss buttons, row pencils) |

`sm` is the only text size below the root. Sub-root text is for things that are scanned, not read; secondary text that is read stays at `md` and gets its hierarchy from `--color-text-dim`.

Before this change the client had 56 distinct font sizes, most of them within 0.6px of the root (`.flabel` alone appeared at five sizes). Every `font-size` in components, stylesheets and PrimeVue pt strings is now one of the tokens. Notable role decisions:

- Validation messages, form labels, hints, character counters and log/error detail moved up to `md`; they were the smallest text on screen.
- Modal titles are one size (`xl`): the custom `.modal-header-title` modals grew from 1.05rem and the PrimeVue Dialog titles set through `dialogPt.js` came down from 1.5rem.
- The Review popover History / Other Assets tabs keep their current sizes (they map to `sm` / `md` at the same values).
- The Rule ID heading in the Rule info panel stays at the display size.

`shared/lib/textScale.js` mirrors the rem values for code that needs numbers. `GRID_GEOMETRY` in `useGridDensity.js` reads it, so a density grid's row height derives from the same token as its cell text (`lg` for the three Review checklists, `md` for Findings and both STIG Library grids). `LabelsRow` measures its chips with the same constant, so the +N overflow estimate tracks the chip size.

`compactTablePt` no longer takes a `bodyFontSize` option; every compact table body is `md`.

## Font families

Ubuntu Mono is bundled behind `--font-mono` but nothing referenced the token; 18 files declared their own monospace stacks (`monospace`, SF Mono, JetBrains Mono, Menlo, ui-monospace) that rendered whatever the OS had. Every monospace declaration is now `var(--font-mono)`. Ubuntu Mono ships regular weight only, so the three places that paired it with a bold weight were adjusted: the Log Stream record panel keeps its header in Open Sans, the "+N more" revision pill and the diff section head drop their bold.

## Convention test

`shared/tests/typographyConventions.test.js` scans every `.vue`, `.css` and `.js` source file and fails on:

- a `font-size` that is not a `--text-*` / `--icon-xs` token, `--cell-font-size` or `inherit`
- a `fontSize:` string literal in a pt object
- a `font:` shorthand other than `inherit`
- a `font-family` other than `var(--font-mono)` or `inherit`
- `textScale.js` drifting from the `style.css` tokens

## Collection dashboard metrics grids

`MetricsSummaryGrid` (the STIGs, Assets, Labels and Checklists grids on the Collection dashboard) now gives every column a rem width and lays the table out fixed: Asset 14rem, Labels 18rem, Benchmark and Collection 20rem, with the count, duration, badge and completion-bar columns sized to their header text. Column resize uses expand mode, so dragging a column widens the table and scrolls it instead of squeezing the neighbouring column (which was clipping "Checks"). At 1920px wide all three grids fit their pane without horizontal scroll.

## Verification

- vitest: 1371 tests pass; vite build clean.
- Screenshots before and after across Asset Review, Collection Review, Findings, Manage Assets, Edit Label, STIG Library and the three dashboard tabs.

author: bee-san
body:
## Problem and change

Selecting text that had no dictionary hit opened the popup with "No definition found. Add your own with the pencil." — for **any** selection, including English words and URLs, because `resolveSelectedLookupCandidate()` and `resolveSelectionScanCandidate()` never consulted `onlyScanJapaneseText`, and `handleTermMiss()` always rendered the notice for an exact selection. There was no way to turn the notice off.

This PR finishes the work halted in the earlier draft of #308 (audited against `main`, kept where correct, completed where not):

- Both selection resolvers apply the same Japanese-text gate as pointer scanning (`options.onlyScanJapaneseText && !isJapaneseToken(query)` → no candidate). This alone stops the popup for English selections and URLs with the default settings. The gate also covers the keybind "Scan selected text" / "Scan text at selection" actions.
- New reader option `showNoResultNotice` (default `true`): `reader-options.js` default (booleans get strict validation and normalisation from the existing `typeof DEFAULT_OPTIONS[key] === "boolean"` paths), `OVERLAY_LOCAL_OPTION_KEYS` in `setup-state.js`, a Settings → Reading → *Personal dictionary* checkbox with a hint, and its keybind Toggle option label.
- `handleTermMiss()`: an exact-selection miss shows the notice only while the option is on; with it off and dictionaries loaded, the popup hides. The `dictionaryCount === 0` setup notice stays regardless, since it tells the reader nothing is installed.
- A hidden miss now keeps `activeSelectionCandidate` like a rendered notice does (the documented "a miss retains selection ownership" invariant). Without this, `hide()` cleared the selection ownership and the throttled hover scan re-dispatched `hd_lookup` for the same selection on every mouse move; Escape or a changed selection release it as before.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` no longer says selections "bypass the language gate"; `docs/overlay-mode.md` names the switch; `test/README.md` describes the new checks.

Closes #291.

## Benefit to the creator

Selecting text to copy or quote while reading (commit messages, English UI, URLs) no longer summons a Hachidori popup saying nothing was found. Before: select "Merge pull request" → popup with a "No definition found" notice. After: nothing happens for non-Japanese selections; Japanese selections behave exactly as before, and a reader who never uses the personal dictionary can switch the no-hit notice off entirely while still being told when no dictionaries are installed.

## Scope and trade-offs

One boolean option and one checkbox. Change (1) alone fixes the reported case with no new setting; the option additionally covers Japanese misses (proper nouns, typos) that some readers do not want a popup for. The pencil notice remains the only discoverable entry point for adding a personal-dictionary word from a page, so it stays on by default. The Japanese gate reuses the existing `isJapaneseToken()` rule and the option reuses the existing boolean normalisation, strict CAS validation, backup and options-broadcast paths; nothing new was added there.

Simplification pass: the option needed no bespoke normalise/validate code (boolean defaults are handled generically); the Settings group mirrors the existing *Lookup history* fieldset; the e2e check reuses `installMediaReplyProbe` lookups, `popupReader`, `editSettingsControls` and the `chrome.runtime.id` isolated-world discovery already used by `forceSourceFallback`. The selection-ownership fix is one assignment after `hide(level)`.

## Validation

All commands run from the repository root on the rebased head (`45ea73d`, on top of `c9cc64b`), Node 22.23.1, Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.75; real-browser suites in a private network namespace (`unshare --user --map-root-user --net`).

| Command | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `node test/make-fixture.mjs` | ok |
| `node test/run.mjs node` | 679 tests, 679 passed, 0 failed (the draft had failed `keybind-settings.test.mjs` "every toggleable option has its Settings label"; fixed by the label) |
| `node test/run.mjs smoke` | node-smoke 137/137, threaded-idbfs 137/137, fallback 132/132, threaded-bridge ok, extension-smoke **608 passed, 0 failed** |
| `node test/run.mjs chrome-e2e` | **246/246 checks passed** (rebased head; 245/245 on the previous base). author: nl404
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for rules that silently built a query for the wrong data. One commit per fix, both with regression tests; two follow-up commits from the review close the same bug in the Doctrine ORM target and test the nested case.

### Composite specifications broke parameters when renaming duplicates

`CompositeSpecification` renames a parameter name that an earlier specification already uses. It did that with `str_replace(':'.$name, ...)`, which had three problems:

- it also changed every parameter sharing the prefix: with `:price` renamed to `:price_1`, `:price_min` became `:price_1_min` and the query failed with an unknown parameter;
- a generated name could overwrite a parameter that already had it. `AndX(new SimpleSpecification('a > :price and b < :price_1', ['price' => 1, 'price_1' => 2]), new SimpleSpecification('c = :price', ['price' => 3]))` produced `price_1 => 3`, so `b < :price_1` silently used the wrong value;
- renaming inside one specification chained into `:price_1_1` and `:price_1_1_1`.

The most common shape hit all of them: composites of composites that reuse names. `AndX(OrX(a = :p, b = :p), OrX(c = :p, d = :p))` built `((a = :p OR b = :p_1) AND (c = :p_1_1 OR d = :p_1_1_1))` with the parameters `p => 1, p_1 => 3, p_1_1 => 4`: `b` got the value of `c`, and `:p_1_1_1` had no value at all.

Parameter names are now renamed as whole names in a single pass, and a generated name that is already taken is skipped. The naming scheme (`id`, `id_1`, `id_2`) is unchanged; the nested case gives `((a = :p OR b = :p_1) AND (c = :p_2 OR d = :p_1_1))`.

### Field names silently lost a part

`NameNode::getSplittedParts()` looped with `while ($part = array_shift($parts))`, so a falsy part ended the loop and the rest of the path was dropped:

- `items.0.price` became `items`, `a..b` became `a`, and a trailing backslash dropped the last part (`a.b\` became `a`);
- the lexer also accepted a leading dot, so `a = .5` built `(a = )` for ClickHouse and an invalid condition for the other targets;
- `DoctrineOrmVisitor::detectJoins()` walks over the path with the same loop. With only the name fixed, `category.0.key` would have become `category.key` — a valid query for a wrong field, where `master` at least builds invalid DQL.

`getSplittedParts()` and `detectJoins()` now walk over all parts, and the lexer accepts a property only as dot-separated non-empty parts of letters, digits, `_` and escaped dots (`\.`).

**Behaviour change:** a name with an empty part (`.5`, `a..b`, `a.`) or with a backslash that does not escape a dot (`a\`, `a\b`) now throws a `SyntaxException` instead of building a query for a wrong field. Such names never produced a valid query for the SQL targets. For the Doctrine ORM target, a `0` part of a path throws the `LogicException` of a part that is not an association, instead of a DQL syntax error when the query runs.

## Checks

`./bin/phpunit` (189 tests), `./bin/phpstan` and `./bin/phpcs` for `src/` and `tests/` are green. 22 tests were added; the 17 that cover the fixed behaviour fail on `master`.

## Note

This pull request, #10 and #11 all add an `Unreleased` section to the CHANGELOG, so the ones merged after the first will need a trivial rebase there.

body: **Do not merge as-is.** After #32 landed first, this PR fights live product config. ## Conflict review (main @ e2c8528 / #32) Fetched latest `origin/main`. Merging it into this branch produces **one textual conflict**: `app/data/studio-content.json` ``` #31: "numberedSets": [] #32: "numberedSets": ["set-5"], "numberedEvery": 30 ``` That is **not a simple conflict**. It is a conflicting intent: - **#31** closes numbered minting so the first idle copy is not `#1`. - **#32** (already on main) keeps set-5 open and stamps the 30th / 60th / 90th idle grant instead. `numberedEvery: 30` is additive and would be a simple keep-from-main. `numberedSets` is the product fork. I did not pick a side, and I aborted the merge so this branch is unchanged. Code that auto-merged (`app.js` overlay pin, cadence math, tests) still encodes both intents. The #31 test `studio ships with numbered minting closed` would fail against main’s `["set-5"]`. **Recommendation:** close this PR. #32 already replaced the “first pull is #1” problem. If you still want minting off, say so and we can empty `numberedSets` on top of the cadence (keep `numberedEvery: 30`, keep existing stamps). The overlay pin (file `numberedSets` wins over a stale `kalpi_studio_config`) can be cherry-picked later without closing the window. --- The first idle copy of a card should not become `#1`. `numberedSets` is empty. Existing stamps stay. A stale `kalpi_studio_config` overlay cannot keep set-5 minting on boot. **Grant vs open (why “1 numbered holder” was granted, not opened)** - Prepared queue: card chosen, not in inventory, no stamp. - Grant (idle due): inventory++, `kalpi_instances` row, `kalpi_numbered_issued` increments, `unseenPulls` gets the instance. Stamp happens here. - Open/walkout: only sets `seen_at` and drops the instance from `unseenPulls`. Holder chips count **granted** copies. There is no granted/opened split in the snapshot. Regular: `kalpi_inventory.copies > 0`. Numbered: `kalpi_instances.numbered_index > 0`. Unopened packs still count. Reopen later by putting set ids back in `numberedSets`.

author: mbret
body:
Three commits. The first is the one this PR was opened for; the third is a fire that merging master revealed.

## 1. `fix(build)` — the types declaration emit cannot infer

`vite-plugin-dts@5.1.1` is **inside** the declared `^5.0.1` range and fails the build:

```
react-reader: src/context/useReader.ts:10:14 - error TS7056: The inferred type of this
  node exceeds the maximum length the compiler will serialize.
react-reader: src/annotations/useReaderWithAnnotations.ts:3:14 - error TS7056
react-native: src/web/index.ts:20:14 - error TS7056
```

Only the lockfile pinning `5.0.3` kept CI green, so the build was one `npm update`, dependabot bump or regenerated lockfile away from red, with no source change to explain it.

Pinning hides the actual problem: a public symbol whose type is *inferred* through an enhanced `Reader` re-expands that entire structure into every `.d.ts` that mentions it. Each of the three now states its type, as a **reference** rather than a restatement:

| symbol | was | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useReader` | inferred | `ReaderContextType["reader"]` — cannot drift from what the provider holds |
| `useReaderWithAnnotations` | inferred | that, intersected with `AnnotationsEnhancerAPI` |
| `bridgeReader` | inferred | a named `ReaderBridgeController` |

`ReaderBridgeController` is a small win for consumers of `@prose-reader/react-native/web` too: the handle now has a name instead of needing a `ReturnType<>` incantation. That package also dropped its local `type Reader = ReturnType<typeof createReader>` in favour of core's export, which is defined identically. The rationale comments are `//`, not JSDoc, so they stay out of the shipped declarations.

Plugin moves to `^5.1.1`.

## 2. `docs(react-native)` — from review

`gitbook/react-native/prose-reader-react-native.md` was a heading and nothing else, while two pages send readers to it as *the* reference for the bridge. It now documents both entries the package ships — `createReaderBridge` / `bridgeReader` / `ReaderBridgeController`, and `useCreateReader`, `ReaderProvider`, `useReader`, `useReaderState`, `ReactNativeStreamer` — with examples taken from the demo. Archive creation is linked to the streamer's own React Native page rather than repeated.

## 3. `fix(release)` — master is red right now

Merging master in to update this branch surfaced it: **2.0.0 silently detached all three apps from the repository.**

`apps/*` are private, `lerna publish --no-private` leaves them out of versioning, and nothing maintained their sibling ranges — `apps/tests` had been asking for `@prose-reader/core@^1.120.0` for hundreds of releases. Every 1.x satisfied it. The moment the workspace became 2.0.0 the range stopped matching, and npm did the worst possible thing with that: it quietly installed the last published 1.x into `apps/*/node_modules`. Nothing failed at install time; `apps/tests` then typechecked against two copies of the reader at once:

```
Types of property 'viewport' are incompatible.
  Type '.../packages/core/dist/viewport/Viewport' is not assignable to type
  '.../apps/tests/node_modules/@prose-reader/core/dist/viewport/Viewport'.
```

A private app is never installed by anyone and the only copy it can mean is the one in this checkout, so it declares `*` and the question of keeping a range in step disappears. 25 duplicate registry installs leave the lockfile with it (−400 lines).

Published packages keep real ranges, since theirs are a promise to consumers. `scripts/sync-internal-peer-ranges.mjs` already corrected the peer ranges lerna does not reach at release time, so it takes this rule too and is renamed `sync-internal-ranges.mjs` for the wider job: `^<version>` for a published package's peers, `*` for anything internal in a private one. Verified by reintroducing both drifts and watching the hook rewrite each. AGENTS.md states the rule so it does not get "fixed" back into a range.

## Validation

- TS7056 reproduces on the parent commit with 5.1.1; a clean build (no `.tsbuildinfo`, no nx cache) is green with the fix
- all 18 projects build, `npm run tsc` green, unit tests green (16 projects), lint and format clean
- react-native demo typechecks against the newly emitted declarations
- `npm ci` from the rewritten lockfile relinks every app to the workspace, and no `apps/*/node_modules/@prose-reader` copy comes back
- e2e: 64 passing on the chromium projects; the rest fail here only for missing browser binaries / `-linux` baselines in the sandbox
- emitted `.d.ts` now reads `useReader: () => ReaderContextType["reader"]` and `bridgeReader: (...) => ReaderBridgeController`

Releases as **2.0.1**.

## Summary
Flagging and fixing a real, previously-unaddressed test-flakiness bug found while investigating today's CI failures: this repo's IT suite has a documented class of bug (BH-058) where a shared, table-wide "claim due work" query picks up leftover rows from earlier `*IT` classes in the same run. That fix covered `import_jobs` and `merchant_learning_events`. It never covered `notifications`, which has the identical query shape.

**Confirmed, not guessed:** `NotificationLogRepositoryIT` failed three different `claimDue`-based assertions in the same CI run. The clearest signal: `claimDue_ignoresTerminalNotifications` expects an empty list and got back exactly 10 — `claimDue`'s own `LIMIT` — meaning at least that many leftover `CREATED`/`QUEUED`/`RETRYING` notifications had piled up from earlier test classes (`NotificationDispatcherNudgeIT`, `AdminNotificationControllerIT`, and potentially others that create a notification without driving it to a terminal status).

**Fix:** extend `AbstractIntegrationTest.emptyTheSharedWorkQueues()` to also `DELETE FROM notifications` before every test, exactly the same treatment `import_jobs`/`merchant_learning_events` already get. Safe for the same reason: `notification_logs.notification_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE` (V126), and nothing else references `notifications`.

author: omarmohamedo-o
body:
## Summary
Takes a backup from the **containerized** database and verifies it — to be run before anything native is removed.

`/var/lib/mysql` has been the real safety net through this whole migration. Once it's gone, this dump replaces it, so it's checked rather than assumed:

- gzip integrity
- the dump contains the expected tables, **not an error message that happened to compress cleanly** (a 150MB file proves nothing by itself)
- row counts inside the dump against the live database

It **refuses** if the dump holds fewer than 50 tables, or is missing any of `users`, `offers`, `orders`, `transactions`, `migrations` — that's the failure mode where a backup exists, looks the right size, and restores nothing.

It also states plainly that the file sits on the same server as the database it protects. No script can download it for you, and **until it leaves this host, the backup and the thing it backs up share a single point of failure.**

## Test plan
- [ ] Run it; expect `VERIFIED: backups/prod-containerised-<stamp>.sql.gz`
- [ ] Download it off the server before deleting `/var/lib/mysql`

author: ziyabeey1-ai
fabriziosalmi
body:
> **Stacked on #861** (it uses the domain registrations that PR adds). Retargeted to `main` and rebased once the stack lands.

`certificate_expiring` is offered in Settings → Notifications, named in the README and in `docs/webhooks.md`, and listed as one of the five events a channel can filter on. **Nothing ever published it.** And nothing could have rendered it if it had: `_EVENT_TITLES` has no entry, so `build_notification_message` returns `None` and the notifier is never reached.

An operator who ticked that box got silence. The weekly digest was the only warning, so a certificate that failed to renew on a Monday was first mentioned the following Sunday.

## What now happens

A daily job at **07:00** — after the renewal sweep (02:00) and the registration check (06:00), so what it announces is still true this morning — publishes two events on the same bus every other alert uses.

| Event | Marks | Why those |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate_expiring` | 14, 7, 3, 1 days, and the day it lapses | Deliberately well inside the renewal window. With auto-renew on, a certificate still unrenewed at 14 days has failed roughly a dozen nightly attempts, so this cannot fire in ordinary operation. **With auto-renew off the first warning is at the renewal threshold**, because nothing else is going to act. |
| `domain_expiring` | 60, 30, 14, 7, 1 days, and the day it lapses | A registration is renewed by a registrar on its own schedule, so the notice starts far earlier. A registry that publishes no expiry (`.de`, `.eu`) is **not** a warning: an answer is not a date. |

**Each threshold speaks once per expiry date**, kept in a table in the inventory database (schema v3 → v4):

- a renewed certificate has a new expiry and starts again from the first mark;
- a repeated run says nothing;
- an operator who never fixes it is told at each mark, not every morning;
- the mark announced is the most recently crossed one, so an instance that was off for a week comes back and says something rather than nothing.

## Found on the way, same root, fixed here

`certificate_deploy_incomplete` is in the notifier's `_ALWAYS_NOTIFY_EVENTS` — the set that exists so an operator **cannot filter a failure away by accident** — and it had no title either. The event nobody could silence was silent.

Two gates now hold the class of defect:

- every always-notify event must be renderable;
- so must every event the settings UI offers as a filter chip.

## Verified by running it

- **End to end on a real instance:** a registration two days from expiry produces a `domain_expiring` delivery to a generic webhook, with the message and the details (`days_left`, `threshold_days`, `registrar`, `source`).
  The first attempt was **refused by CertMate's own SSRF guard** because the receiver was on loopback — the guard doing its job, and the thing that proved the chain reaches the webhook layer at all. Re-run with `CERTMATE_ALLOW_INTERNAL_WEBHOOKS=1`, the payload arrives.
- **Nine mutations, each caught:** the threshold arithmetic, the dedupe, the auto-renew distinction, the "not published" guard, the missing-certificate guard, both titles, and the `ON CONFLICT` clause that makes a notice claimable once.
  The missing-certificate guard **survived the first pass**, because the test covering it did not carry a day count; it does now, and the mutation dies.
- **Container suites and the real-certificate E2E on this branch: 67 passed**, in CI's order, against an image built from it.
- Coverage floor for `modules/core/expiry_watch.py` at 90% (measured 94.9%). Complexity and exception budgets unchanged.

## Summary

Hardens the development audit pipeline so audits are delivered reliably and recovery doesn't stall.

- **Audit correctness/delivery**: omit rejected optional notes instead of blocking audits; publish findings that validation wrongly rejected; audit with the lead agent and skip user-stopped runs.
- **Recovery**: new `scripts/recover-development-audits.sh` (with tests) and `scripts/repair-development-audit-issues.sh`; recovery no longer waits on finished runs; repair path hardened.

author: lxjoyner
body:
## Summary
Fixes the Transactions page so it includes older paid invoices, not only invoices that have rows in the newer `invoice_payments` ledger.

## Cause
The Transactions page was reading invoice income only from `invoice_payments`. Historical invoices imported before the payment ledger was introduced can be marked paid and have `amount_paid_cents`, but they do not have matching rows in `invoice_payments`. That is why only the newer 2026 payments were appearing.

## Fix
- Keeps normal transaction rows from `invoice_payments`.
- Adds a fallback transaction row for invoices where `amount_paid_cents > 0` and no payment-ledger row exists.
- Uses the invoice date for those historical fallback transactions.
- Avoids double-counting invoices that already have payment-ledger records.
- Keeps invoice rows linked to the existing admin invoice preview.

Build/tests were not run through the GitHub connector.

author: wagnerra23
body:
## Por quê

Primeiro dos 12 baselines de tolerância a sair, pela regra que a própria ADR 0409 escreve para o fim de vida:

> *"ao chegar a zero, o arquivo de tolerância é **apagado** e o gate passa a operar somente pelo critério absoluto."*

`governance/uc-id-baseline.json` estava com **`grandfathered: []`** — lista vazia. Com ela vazia, `--check --baseline` já era **idêntico** a `--check` cru: o arquivo não tolerava nada, só existia.

## Medido antes de apagar

```bash
node scripts/qa/uc-id-lint.mjs --check   # exit 0 · "0 fora do formato canônico"
```

Os 42 ids legados que motivaram o baseline em 2026-08-23 foram consertados desde então. O gate passa **sem tolerância nenhuma**.

## O que mudou

| arquivo | |
|---|---|
| `governance/uc-id-baseline.json` | **apagado** (`git rm`, reversível) |
| `governance-script-tests.yml` | step roda `--check` cru |
| `scripts/qa/uc-id-lint.mjs` | docblock registra a extinção e a data |
| `MAQUINAS-INVENTARIO.md` | regenerado — derivado; o `--check` acusou *"1 no índice que sumiu do disco"* e o hook exige em dia |

## LC-10 consertado de passagem

O comentário do workflow afirmava, **em presente**: *"Sem `--baseline` daria exit 1 hoje"*. Era verdade quando foi escrito e **apodreceu** — hoje o `--check` cru sai 0.

Virou fato **datado**: diz o que era verdade em 2026-08-23, o que é verdade em 2026-09-22, e por que o arquivo saiu. Afirmação em presente sobre medição é a classe que o ledger alarma em 11 ocorrências.

## Provas

```
--check cru ................. exit 0  (0 fora do formato)
uc-id-lint.test.mjs ......... exit 0
parser YAML estrito ......... parseia · 2 jobs · 224 steps · step alvo confere
maquinas-inventario --check . 608/608 · 0 faltando · 0 ghost
```

Duas delas merecem nota:

- **o bite-test não depende do baseline real** — `grep "uc-id-baseline"` no `.test.mjs` dá **0 hits**; ele usa fixture própria, então apagar o arquivo não o quebra. Conferi antes, não depois.
- **o YAML passou por parser, não por revisão** — LC-22: *doc que a máquina lê é código com cara de doc*, e mudança nele se valida rodando o consumidor, não relendo o texto.

## O que NÃO muda

A flag `--baseline` fica no código para quem precisar medir contra uma lista. Mas **recriar tolerância para este gate exige decisão de [W]** — ADR 0409: *"criar um novo exige nova decisão de [W]"*.

Refs: ADR 0409 · #7722 (o desenho irmão, no pageheader) · LC-10 · LC-22

author: melvinbot
body:
<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change

The wallet payment-method popup is no longer repositioned correctly when the viewport is resized (for example, when the Chrome DevTools pane is opened or closed while the popup is open).

The popup used to be owned by `WalletPage`, which had its own reposition-on-resize handler. [Partially setup account](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/67326) moved the popup into the shared `ThreeDotsMenu` component, and the page-level handler went away with it. `ThreeDotsMenu` has a generic replacement, but it is weaker than the handler it replaced in two ways:

1. **The re-measure is not debounced.** It runs on every intermediate dimension tick during a resize. The anchor lives inside a `FlashList`, whose absolutely-positioned cells re-lay-out *after* the resize, so `measureInWindow` can read the anchor's pre-resize coordinates and write them straight back — pinning the open menu to where the button used to be.
2. **The effect's dependencies are unstable.** `anchorAlignment` was an inline object literal at the call site and `calculatePopoverPosition` was re-created on every render, so the effect re-fired on every render rather than on dimension change, making its timing relative to the resize non-deterministic.

This PR fixes both in the shared components rather than adding a fourth Wallet-specific patch:

- `ThreeDotsMenu` now debounces the reposition measurement by `CONST.TIMING.RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_TIME`, so a resize collapses into a single measurement taken after the layout has settled. This matches the pattern already used by [`DatePicker`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7d3b2e3e58bd5dd92230d2f769487cfbf4404c37/src/components/DatePicker/index.tsx#L194-L202) and [`CopilotPage`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7d3b2e3e58bd5dd92230d2f769487cfbf4404c37/src/pages/settings/Copilot/CopilotPage.tsx#L171-L181).
- `usePopoverPosition` memoizes `calculatePopoverPosition`, and the two `anchorAlignment` object literals (the `ThreeDotsMenu` default and the one in `PaymentMethodListItem`) are hoisted to module scope, so the reposition effect now fires on dimension change instead of on every render.
- The dead `paymentMethodButtonRef` in `WalletPage/index.tsx` is removed. It was the anchor the deleted handler measured; it was still declared and assigned but never read. Removing it also drops two grandfathered `no-unsafe-type-assertion` entries from the ESLint seatbelt.

**Not changed, and why:** the proposal also suggested that `usePopoverPosition` returning `{horizontal: 0, vertical: 0}` when `isSmallScreenWidth` could anchor the popup at the origin when the width breakpoint is crossed. That value is never used for positioning in this case — when `isSmallScreenWidth` is true, [`Popover`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/7d3b2e3e58bd5dd92230d2f769487cfbf4404c37/src/components/Popover/index.tsx#L146-L149) renders a `BOTTOM_DOCKED` modal and explicitly passes `popoverAnchorPosition={undefined}`. Changing it would be a no-op here and would alter behavior for every other popover, so it is left alone.

author: aayanhetam
body:
The "Pick your handle" and "Your rating goals" cards lived on `/plan`, the daily-session page. They were there because the quiz is one-time and never asked either question, so an existing account had no other way to set them. The cost was a settings form standing between every user and their plan, on every visit.

Onboarding now asks both, and `/profile` is where they are changed.

## /onboarding

- New **perf-goals** step for the platform branch: bullet, blitz and rapid as current/goal pairs, currents prefilled from the lookup the username step already ran, with the projected date underneath. Only established controls prefill — a rapid box seeded from a control the player has never touched would be a number we invented and attributed to their account.
- The self-assessment branch keeps the single slider. It has one coarse derived rating behind it, so three boxes would be three guesses.
- New **handle** step, last, next to the signup it attaches to. Format-only validation: the availability endpoint is session-gated on purpose and the visitor has no session yet, so the atomic claim that runs straight after signup is what settles it.
- The result screen reads the targets back, so the answers visibly land.

## /profile

- `HandleCard` and the goal setter, under the performance panels — the same placement logic the page already applies to personalisation: they configure the product rather than report on it.
- `#goals` opens the form directly, so `/plan`'s "Change goal" stays one click.

## /plan

- Keeps `GoalProgressCard` ("am I on pace today") and the email prompt (an unrecoverable account is a worse problem than an unset goal).
- Links to `/profile#goals` instead of embedding the setter.

## Shared, so the two doors cannot disagree

- `lib/curriculum/perfGoalDrafts.ts` — draft parsing, per-control validation and the pace check. React-free and unit-tested: a form that accepts what `buildPerfGoalPatch` then refuses reads as a dead save button.
- `components/goals/PerfGoalFields.tsx` — the three cards, extracted from the setter.
- `lib/auth/handleClient.ts` — one claim/availability client, used by the card and by the post-signup flush.

## Two details worth a reviewer's eye

The flush carries the handle **alongside** the payload rather than inside it. Claiming is an atomic transaction on its own endpoint and the profile PATCH route refuses the field, so folding it in would silently drop it. A claim that loses the race is non-fatal: the card on `/profile` renders for any account without a handle and asks again.

Per-control goals are gated on the platform branch, like the username. Backing up and switching play style leaves the old branch's answers in the draft; without the gate, a player who typed chess.com goals and then said "over the board" would get targets written from a form they can no longer see, read on a scale they are no longer on.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 382 test files / 4922 tests pass, including 27 new ones (`perfGoalDrafts`, the new step rules, the per-control payload path, the handle envelope)
- Production build succeeds
- The new quiz steps walked in a browser end to end: prefill lands real ratings, a downward goal disables Continue with an inline reason, typed currents survive prefill, the projection chip appears, and a reserved handle like `admin` blocks the step. No console errors on `/plan` or `/profile`.

Not covered locally: `/profile` and `/plan` **signed in**. This container has no `.env.local`, so no session or Firebase Admin. Those paths rest on types, tests and the build rather than an eyeball.

author: benjamindemaille
body:
### What's wrong

The .pvar loader recognizes the header line with `tokequal_k(line, "#CHROM")` and skips other single-`#` lines, but `PvarInfoReloadHeader()`, which rereads the INFO column when a .pvar is written, uses `StrStartsWithUnsafe(line, "#CHROM")`. A comment line such as `#CHROMOSOME names below are GRCh38` above the real header matches; the INFO search then runs off that line and dereferences NULL. ASan: SEGV in `memequal` < `tokequal_k` < `PvarInfoReloadHeader` (plink2_data.cc:182).

### Reproducer

A .pvar containing `##INFO=<ID=AF,...>`, that comment line, then `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT INFO`: `plink2 --pfile x --make-just-pvar` segfaults.

### The fix

Use `tokequal_k`, as the loader and `--rm-dup`'s INFO reload (plink2_filter.cc:1087) already do.

### Testing

New block in `TEST_EXPORT_OPTIONS` checks that the INFO column round-trips; it segfaults on master and passes with the fix; full suite passes.

  - The logic is moved almost word for word: `setState` became `notifyListeners`, and `mounted` became `disposed`. The load-generation guards and subscription cancels are unchanged.
  - The screen passes it callbacks for snackbars, bringing chat to the front, opening a job, and closing the drawer.
- **`ChatScreen`** is down to about 575 lines. It keeps layout, the composer and attachments, share handling and navigation.
- **`ChatHeader`** is extracted to `chat/widgets/chat_header.dart`, along with a `ConnectionInfoButton` that takes an `onPressed`. It has Widgetbook use cases.
- **perf:** the thread view uses `context.select` on the display name instead of `context.watch<AuthController>()`, so a token refresh no longer rebuilds the whole thread.

Pure refactor with no behavior change: no existing chat test needed changing.

## Tests
The new `test/chat_controller_test.dart` covers send and stream (including binding to the server id), refusing a second prompt while a reply runs, switching threads mid-reply, and recording an approval answer. `widgetbook_test` passes. The full suite has 3249 passed, 87 skipped and 1 failed: a download test in `test/chat_media_test.dart`. It passes and fails on repeated runs, and did the same on the base commit without this change.

`chat_controller.dart` is 744 lines. Opening chats from outside and the profile logic could be split out further.

author: borjar20
body:
## Qué fallaba

Al pulsar «Nuevo pase» en una **película ya vista**, el panel encadenaba dos transiciones:

1. `in_progress + restart` → archiva y abre un pase «viendo».
2. `completed` → lo cierra.

Desde #824 cada transición publica su hito en `applyTransition`, así que la primera dejaba en el feed **«X ha empezado *peli*»** (con `autopost_started` activo), de algo que ya estaba visto y en un estado que las películas ni tienen. La UI lo disimulaba pintando «Vista» optimista.

## Arreglo

- `planTransition`: activo **cerrado** + `to = completed` + `resume = "restart"` ⇒ `archiveAndCreate` con el pase nuevo ya cerrado (`started_on = finished_on = hoy`). Sin `restart`, `completed → completed` sigue siendo no-op y `dropped → completed` sigue corrigiendo el mismo pase.
- `applyTransition`: el insert respeta el `finishedOn` que traiga el plan.
- `log-panel`: la rama de películas hace esa única llamada.

Resultado: una escritura, un solo hito (`finished`), ningún pase `in_progress` intermedio. **Libros y series no cambian** (siguen por `in_progress + restart`, donde «ha empezado» sí tiene sentido).

Decisión registrada al final de `docs/requirements/decisiones.md`.

## Verificación

- Unitarios nuevos en `transitions.test.ts` y `apply-transition.test.ts`; suite completa verde (3536), `tsc` limpio.
- E2e nuevo en `e2e/pase-hub.spec.ts` («revisionar una peli vista no publica «ha empezado» ni pasa por Viendo»): enciende `autopost_started` para devtest, revisiona y comprueba en BD 2 pases `completed` y 0 posts `started`. **Falla con el código anterior** (encuentra 1 post `started`) y pasa con el arreglo. Restaura las preferencias al acabar.
- E2e «nuevo pase» de libros sigue verde.

author: frank-7
body:
Fix 47 lint errors so main is green again

CI has been failing on main since #14 merged. The lint job reports 47 ruff
errors across eight files; the types job passes, so nothing here is a type
change.

Most were mechanical and taken with `ruff check --fix`: 25 UP037 quoted
annotations, 5 UP017 datetime.UTC aliases, 4 RUF046 redundant int() casts, plus
single C420, I001 and RUF005 cases.

Three were real and are fixed by hand rather than by the formatter:

- scripts/fetch_ot_associations.py and fetch_ot_associations_api.py each opened
  the disease-id file without closing it (SIM115). Both now use
  Path.read_text().splitlines().
- scripts/fetch_hecate_vocab.py swallowed every exception with try/except/pass
  (SIM105), now contextlib.suppress with a comment saying why a truncated final
  line is expected and skipped.

The seven N803/N806 naming errors are all `X`, `X_train`, `X_val_full` and
similar -- the standard design-matrix name in modelling code and in every
scikit-learn signature these scripts call. Renaming them would make the
experiments harder to read. exp05 already carried inline `# noqa: N806` for
exactly this, so exp01 and exp04 now do the same rather than the rule being
switched off in pyproject; that keeps the justification next to the code and
matches both the existing file and CLAUDE.md.

One subtlety worth noting for anyone repeating this: the formatter splits the
grouped_cv_ap signature across lines, which moves the parameter away from a
trailing noqa on the closing paren. The directive has to sit on the `X:` line
itself.

ruff check, ruff format --check and pyright all pass. Every file under
experiments/ and scripts/ still parses.

author: maleadt
body:
Bump BOLT to upstream `llvmorg-23.1.2` (85ac560262434c9ccfc0c183ec22d4138ed647fb) and backport llvm/llvm-project#215415 (c74738e6a5, "[BOLT] Avoid unnecessary AArch64 ADR relaxation"), which is on `main` but not in `release/23.x`.

Without the backport, BOLT cannot rewrite Julia's ThinLTO-built libLLVM on AArch64: `InstCombinePass::run` grows to about 1.5 MB, and both `--instrument` and a plain rewrite fail with `BOLT-ERROR: cannot relax ADR in non-simple function`. BOLT 22.1.8 and 23.1.1 both fail this way. BOLT 23.1.1 built from source with the patch instruments and rewrites that library on an aarch64 machine.

23.1.2 makes no changes under `bolt/`, and the patch applies to it cleanly. It only touches `bolt/lib/Passes/AArch64RelaxationPass.cpp` (plus a test that isn't built).

Add "Сконвертировать"/"Convert" action to SeamlyMe that converts an old-format individual measurements file (@-prefixed custom names, old rint() rounding syntax) into a new file in the current format:

- strips a leading "@" from measurement names ("@@" collapses to "@" instead of being removed entirely)
- updates every reference to a renamed measurement inside other measurements' formulas
- leaves a measurement's "@" untouched, with a warning, if removing it would collide with another name in the same file
- converts old rint(expr * 10^n) / 10^n rounding syntax to rint(expr; n)
- never overwrites the source file; always writes to a separate, user-chosen destination file
- records the conversion in an XML comment (not an element) so it never breaks the strict schema validation used when opening files
- shows a summary report after conversion (renamed count, rint conversions, collision warnings)

Also: when a file fails to open because it contains an unknown measurement, the error now names the specific measurement instead of showing a generic "file contains invalid measurement(s)" message.

author: jonbridgerapps
body:
## Block 82 — what can gap the walk inside the qubit (source-link direction, block 30; first after the rest-energy panel)

Hand-off PR against `main` (independent of the open stack; blocks 54, 77–81 restated or placed, not required). Nothing is adopted; no gravitational claim; no parked decision is touched.

**Question.** Block 81 (#8626) left rest energy without an in-framework source. A four-lens panel on the supervisor's dossier named the routes; the synthesis (supervisor's) was to settle first what a rest energy *can* be inside `M₂(ℂ)`: the complete map of backgrounds that separate the walk's two branches at its eight species points, and what the Record axiom's exclusion does to the one background the lane had in hand.

**Exact.**
- **T1 — no covariant translation-invariant term of any reach.** The rotations permute the eight corners in orbits `1, 1, 3, 3`; at each corner the stabiliser (order 24 or 8) acts irreducibly on the coin (commutant exactly the scalars). So every covariant translation-invariant generator, whatever its reach, is scalar at each species point: the branches touch there. Blocks 54 T1(d) and 77 are the reach-0 and reach-1 cases.
- **T2 — on sites: the chessboard scalar and the axis stripes, nothing else.** The backgrounds `m₀(x) + m(x)·σ` anticommuting with the walk form exactly a 4-dimensional space: `c₀ε` and `c_j(−1)^{x_j}σ_j` (a content read by the coin that leans along one axis and alternates along it). The three stripes anticommute pairwise: one rest energy `√(Σc_j²)` for all eight species; mixed with `ε` the gap is `||c₀| − |c||`. Block 81 T4's "content order gives no gap" was for the uniform and chessboard contents; the stripe is the content order that does gap — and the static law never weighs it heaviest (`qp²` per site against `p³`, `q³`).
- **T3 — on bonds: alternating lengths give every species one rest energy.** With `t_j(x) = 1 + δ(−1)^{x_j}`, `H² = β²Σ_j(sin²k_j + δ²cos²k_j)` exactly: `√3β|δ|` at all eight species, no zero anywhere. With the axioms' scalar hop through the same lengths the sixteen corner energies are `±√(4a²+3β²δ²)` (×4) and `±4a ± √(4a²+3β²δ²)` (×2). A staggered-phase scalar hop `iε·2aΣcos k` gaps too.
- **T3(c) — the scalar hop does not add to the rest energy.** `(A + H + mε)² = (A + H)² + m²` exactly: branches `±√(m² + (A ± |s|)²)`, least separation `2m` on the shell `A = ∓|s|`. Block 77's `√(m²+36a²)`, `√(m²+4a²)` are corner values; the rest energy is `m`, and quanta at rest sit on a momentum shell.
- **T4 — under exclusion a chessboard is a cage.** The walk restricted to the vacant sublattice is exactly zero; in general the projected walk has at least `2|n_e − n_o|` exact zero modes (equality on `4³` with one or two emptied layers: `48`, `32`). Block 79's `m = c/2` presupposes a record that can be entered at finite cost.

**Executed (control, floating point).** The alternating-length gap is not protected by the scalar hop: least `|E|` over the zone falls from `√3δ` at `a = 0` to ~0 once `a ≳ δ` (the chessboard's `2m` is exact at every `a`). The free sea lowers its energy under all three backgrounds, monotonically; second-order coefficients on `16³`: lengths `1.55`, chessboard `0.93`, stripes `2.73` (still drifting with size). Exclusion on `6³`: the chessboard's 216 states are all zero modes; random half fillings give `16, 12, 20` against bounds `16, 4, 12`.

**What it means.** Inside `M₂(ℂ)` a rest energy is a broken one-step translation, and the complete list of what breaks it usefully is short: a chessboard of something content-blind, a stripe of content read by the coin, or an alternation of the lengths. The record gas supplies none (block 81); the static law's content order supplies none; the only candidate built from a field the lane already carries is the alternating length — and nothing here fixes `δ`. Next: whether the lane's length dynamics alternate the lengths (the sea's response against the lengths' field energy of blocks 60/64), and the two-record exclusion problem on `4³`.

**Recorded.** A panel lens's claim that every corner is fixed by all 24 rotations was refuted by the runner's first check (a 90° rotation carries `(0,0,π)` to `(0,π,0)`) and the theorem was restated with corner stabilisers; a control metric that was zero by degeneracy was replaced by the least `|E|`; block 77's mass table and block 81 T4's scope were re-read against exact identities; every panel-suggested identity was re-derived in scratch before the build.

**Evidence.** Runner `scripts/admissibility_rule_what_can_gap_the_walk_no_invariant_term_any_reach_stripes_alternating_lengths_rest_energy_exclusion_cages_2026_09_22.py`: `TOTAL: PASS=18 FAIL=0`; 9 mutations, each failing in its own family only. Two pipeline passes (`rows=4880`, `graph_delta=acknowledged`); lints clean. Author checks only; no independent review has taken place.

body:
### What's wrong

`ScoreReport()` checks each `--q-score-range` name against `max_name_slen`, but the check only formats the error message; the `goto` is missing. Each range name is later appended to `outname` with `strcpya()`, so a name longer than about 4 KiB overflows the `kPglFnamesize` buffer on `main()`'s stack. ASan: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 5003 at plink2_matrix_calc.cc:10020; the release build aborts on the stack protector.

### Reproducer

A range file line of 5000 `r` characters followed by `\t0\t0.3`, then `plink2 --pfile d --score s.txt --q-score-range r.txt p.txt`: abort.

### The fix

Add the missing `goto ScoreReport_ret_MALFORMED_INPUT_WW;` (and wrap the test in `unlikely()`).

### Testing

New `TEST_Q_SCORE_RANGE` (ordinary names produce `.r1/.r2.sscore`; the 5000-character name is rejected with "Name too long") aborts on master and passes with the fix; full suite passes.

author: krishanraja
body:
## Summary

- Four migrations adding the permanent record underneath the disposable working surfaces: `trend_observations` plus side tables for story keys, entities and embeddings; `trend_entities`, the first company/lab/model/person registry this system has had; `snapshot_trend_weekly_metrics` and `trend_weekly_momentum`; and `claim_resolutions`, which finally reads `investigation_claims.falsifier_due_on`.
- Everything is append-only, enforced by trigger rather than by comment.
- The fourth migration fixes a hole the first three opened, found by reading the live database back.

## Why

An audit of what the OS collects about AI trends found exactly one store that compounds over time, the shifts register, and everything feeding it designed to be thrown away. The Monday purge hard-deletes whatever did not become a shift. CTRL keeps twenty cards from several hundred articles a day. Newsletter bodies go at read. Model prices overwrite every six hours.

Each of those is a defensible call about a **working surface**. `content_ideas` is a desk, and a feed that keeps its own noise makes every downstream reader responsible for filtering it. The mistake was letting the working surface be the only surface. Volume, share of voice, how long a theme took to reach a second outlet, which publisher leads and which follows, and any audit of our own filters all need what we discarded, and none of it was answerable.

`falsifier_due_on` is the sharpest case. The 2026-08-05 migration that added it says it "feeds the public corrections log, which turns an apology page into a scoreboard". It has been written on every claim since and never once read. A dated record of calls this system made and whether they came true is the one thing here that cannot be bought or caught up on later.

**Verdicts are deliberately not automated.** The machine records that a claim came due, permanently and one per claim, so a claim nobody looked at stays visibly unjudged. A system grading its own predictions produces a number nobody should trust, least of all published. `hit_rate_pct` excludes `unclear` and `not_checkable` from the denominator rather than counting them as wins.

## The security finding, which is the part worth reading

The first three migrations revoked everything on the six new tables from `anon` and `authenticated`. That was the whole access posture. **It did not hold.** Postgres creates a view `SECURITY DEFINER` by default, so it runs with the owner's permissions rather than the caller's, and Supabase separately grants public-schema objects to `anon`. So `anon` held SELECT on all six new views and could read straight through them into the tables it had just been revoked from. `claims_due` carries investigation claims and their falsifiers; `claim_scoreboard` carries the hit rate, which this repo's own `never_publish` list names.

Nothing in the migration files could have revealed that. The advisor and a live grant readback did, within minutes. Fixed with `security_invoker = true` **and** explicit revokes, either of which would have sufficed and neither of which is enough alone. The three new functions had mutable search paths and are pinned too.

Recorded and deliberately not fixed here: **fourteen older views carry the same SECURITY DEFINER property**, among them `decisions_waiting`, `pilot_daily`, `standards_efficacy` and `triage_queue`, several reading tables that hold named people and scorecard figures. That is a real pre-existing exposure that deserves its own review rather than being swept into this PR.

## Applied to production

Unusually for a PR, the migrations are **already applied** to the OS DB (`gojpffsrxybbpbdzzrvs`), following this repo's documented pattern in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:322-337`: out-of-band DDL is fine as long as the matching migration file is committed, which is what this PR is. The ledger records all four.

Production readback, quoted rather than asserted:
- 6 tables, 6 views, 3 functions, 22 seed entities.
- Append-only proven by inserting a row and confirming **both** an update and a delete raise.
- `snapshot_trend_weekly_metrics` ran and wrote its rows for the current week.
- `claims_due` and `claim_scoreboard` return against the real 10 claims with falsifier dates; 0 are currently due, so the sweep correctly notices nothing on its first run.
- 0 `anon`/`authenticated` grants remain on the six views; advisor reports none of the nine objects.

One honest consequence: the row inserted to prove the append-only guarantee **cannot be deleted**, by design. It is tagged `collector = 'readback_probe'` and is filterable. Proving the guarantee in production required a real row, and the alternative was not proving it.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `check-no-secrets` and `check-env-example` pass
- [x] Steward validation passes on NOW.md
- [x] All four migrations run, re-run idempotently, and were exercised with data against a local Postgres 16 before production
- [x] Append-only triggers proven to refuse both update and delete, locally and in production
- [x] Security advisor run after applying; my objects clear, pre-existing findings reported not filtered
- [x] `docs/DATABASE.md` updated, as CONTRIBUTING requires for a schema change
- [x] `NOW.md` updated
- [x] CI green: `verify` and `e2e`
- [ ] No tab changed, so no PRODUCT.md update needed
- [ ] No new "waiting on Krish" surface, so no `decisions_waiting` branch needed

## Ordering

author: mrhard9090
body:
`rm` filters out the special `.` and `..` entries that a leading-dot glob such as `.*` matches, but the check only compared against `/`:

```rust
if name.ends_with("/.") || name.ends_with("/..") {
```

On Windows, glob results use `\` (e.g. `C:\work\parent\child\..`), so the guard never matched. As a result, `rm -r parent/child/.*` deleted `child` (via `child\.`) and `parent` (via `child\..`), including unrelated files. Running `rm -r .*` inside a directory also tried to delete the current and parent directories and failed with "being used by another process" errors.

The check now looks at the final path component, splitting on every platform separator (`std::path::is_separator`), so it matches both `/` and `\` on Windows. `Path::components()` can't be used here because it normalizes away a trailing `.`.

Verified on Windows:
- Before: `rm -r parent/child/.*` removed all of `parent`.
- After: only the dotfiles in `child` are removed. `child`, `parent` and their other contents are kept.

## User-facing changes (Release notes)

Fixed `rm` with leading-dot globs such as `rm -r dir/.*` on Windows deleting `dir` and its parent directory. The `.` and `..` entries are now skipped on all platforms.

## Tests + Formatting

- Added `rm_leading_dot_glob_skips_current_and_parent_dirs`. It fails on Windows without this change and passes with it.
- `cargo test -p nu-command --test tests -- commands::rm::`: 35 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p nu-command --all-targets -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used`

## Additional notes

Fixes #13494

author: juho1337
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the first complete version of **Polar Activity Migrator**, an open-source tool for migrating historical Polar Flow training data to Strava.

The application processes a Polar user-data export locally, converts supported training sessions into validated FIT files, creates an auditable migration workspace, and safely uploads eligible activities to Strava.

The migration is designed to handle large training histories and can be paused and resumed without starting over.

## Highlights

- Import real Polar Flow `training-session` data
- Preserve available GPS, heart rate, distance, cadence, altitude, temperature, laps, and activity metadata
- Support sessions containing multiple exercises
- Generate and validate FIT files for Strava
- TCX export also available
- Audit the complete Polar export before uploading anything
- Detect activities requiring configuration or manual review
- Support explicit timezone overrides without guessing missing timezone information
- Generate portable migration manifests and reports
- Verify FIT files with SHA-256 before upload
- Authenticate with Strava using OAuth
- Perform dry runs before migration
- Upload individual activities, limited batches, or the complete migration
- Persist migration state in SQLite
- Safely resume interrupted migrations
- Resume polling of already-submitted Strava uploads without blindly re-uploading them
- Detect authoritative Strava duplicates
- Respect Strava overall and read-specific API rate limits
- Automatically pause at short-window API limits
- Safely stop and resume when daily API capacity is reached
- Display live migration progress and local migration status

## Migration workflow

```text
Polar user-data export
        ↓
Discover and import training sessions
        ↓
Normalize into the common activity model
        ↓
Validate and generate FIT files
        ↓
Create migration workspace and audit reports
        ↓
Review configuration and warnings
        ↓
Connect Strava
        ↓
Dry run
        ↓
Upload
        ↓
Resume safely when required
