author: overlookmotel
body:
Follow-on after #26919.

Fix a bug caught by AI code reviewer in https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/26940#discussion_r4073861589.

In `.tsx` files, the lexer peeks past a `<` to decide whether it opens a type parameter list or a JSX element. A `const` modifier (`<const T,>`) has to be on the same line as its parameter. But when `const` was followed by a line break, the check fell through and read `const` itself as the parameter name. So this JSX element (tag `const`, attributes `extends` and `U`) was lexed as a type parameter list:

```jsx
x = (
  <const extends U>
    hi
  </const>
);
```

Everyone seems to agree that this is indeed valid JSX:

- [Oxc parser](https://playground.oxc.rs/?t=ast&options=%7B%22run%22%3A%7B%22lint%22%3Afalse%2C%22formatter%22%3Afalse%2C%22transform%22%3Afalse%2C%22isolatedDeclarations%22%3Afalse%2C%22whitespace%22%3Afalse%2C%22mangle%22%3Afalse%2C%22mangleProps%22%3Afalse%2C%22compress%22%3Afalse%2C%22scope%22%3Atrue%2C%22symbol%22%3Atrue%2C%22cfg%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22parser%22%3A%7B%22extension%22%3A%22tsx%22%2C%22allowReturnOutsideFunction%22%3Atrue%2C%22preserveParens%22%3Atrue%2C%22allowV8Intrinsics%22%3Atrue%2C%22semanticErrors%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22linter%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22formatter%22%3A%7B%22useTabs%22%3Afalse%2C%22tabWidth%22%3A2%2C%22endOfLine%22%3A%22lf%22%2C%22printWidth%22%3A80%2C%22singleQuote%22%3Afalse%2C%22jsxSingleQuote%22%3Afalse%2C%22quoteProps%22%3A%22as-needed%22%2C%22trailingComma%22%3A%22all%22%2C%22semi%22%3Atrue%2C%22arrowParens%22%3A%22always%22%2C%22bracketSpacing%22%3Atrue%2C%22bracketSameLine%22%3Afalse%2C%22objectWrap%22%3A%22preserve%22%2C%22singleAttributePerLine%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22transformer%22%3A%7B%22target%22%3A%22es2015%22%2C%22useDefineForClassFields%22%3Atrue%2C%22experimentalDecorators%22%3Atrue%2C%22emitDecoratorMetadata%22%3Atrue%2C%22optimizeEnums%22%3Atrue%2C%22optimizeConstEnums%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22isolatedDeclarations%22%3A%7B%22stripInternal%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22codegen%22%3A%7B%22normal%22%3Atrue%2C%22jsdoc%22%3Atrue%2C%22annotation%22%3Atrue%2C%22legal%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22compress%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22mangle%22%3A%7B%22topLevel%22%3Atrue%2C%22keepNames%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22mangleProps%22%3A%7B%22include%22%3A%22_%24%22%2C%22reserved%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22quoted%22%3Afalse%2C%22debug%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22controlFlow%22%3A%7B%22verbose%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22inject%22%3A%7B%22inject%22%3A%7B%7D%7D%2C%22define%22%3A%7B%22define%22%3A%7B%7D%7D%7D&code=x+%3D+%3Cconst%0Aextends+U%3Ehi%3C%2Fconst%3E%3B)
- [Babel](https://ast-explorer.dev/#eNo9js0OgyAQhF9ls2eT3q310ldoT8UDIq0YBCJrY2N89y7+nRi+mczsjBZz7ORXRjWYQJhhYFDLWlvWivUENyiUd5GE0xNp10R4lq0pLissr5zznJuFAxAY/Tgo/fgFLTDnf++b0bLONjvY8WNcTN4rkcS6OO0+HDBh4o7tqtMFWFeORENr0VvaqA++bKJKT7WPWq8kGb72TO+GJJKqvfu+145XzqoFlz+ae1YT)
- [TS-ESLint](https://ast-explorer.dev/#eNpFy7EOwjAMBNBfiTwXsZfSkT+AKUsULJEqOFHsoqAq/45Tho737m6DCCMs7uPYl5AFBsgK8s34hxNyDNTdq1dzNZNPxGIJqyA92dznV5jOO84X3SXdbZaMsYD+7R5YOCSyMCpEJ6hfGI7+hk7WgtwH+60XC9eepazYqVlq0H40Tzho)

This PR makes a line break after `const` mean JSX straight away. The parser rejects every type-parameter reading of `<const` followed by a line break, so JSX is the only valid one.

body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `test_a_timed_out_migrate_deploy_takes_its_process_tree_with_it` fails whenever PID 1 is slow to reap or never does
- The SIGKILLed grandchild becomes a zombie, and a zombie still answers signal 0, so the test reads it as alive
- Its sibling in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db` already handled zombies, so the two tests disagreed on what "gone" means

How it solves it:

- One shared `process_is_gone` helper in `tests/_process_helpers.py`, used by both tests
- It reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` for state `Z` and reaps the pid when it is our own child
- Four unit tests cover live, reaped, unreaped, and someone-else's-zombie cases
- `test_interrupt_kills_background_jobs_and_removes_logs` in `tests/test_litellm/test_pre_commit_lint.py` polled its orphaned `make` stub with the same signal-0 check and flaked the same way, so it moves onto the helper too

## User Flow

Before: a contributor running the migration tests in a plain container (no `--init`) sees the timeout test fail even though the process tree was killed as designed

1. They run `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src -w /src python:3.12 uv run pytest tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_prisma_toolchain.py -k takes_its_process_tree`
2. The fake prisma CLI in the test times out after about a second and its whole process group gets SIGKILL
3. The killed grandchild reparents to PID 1, which never reaps it, so `ps` inside the container shows it as `<defunct>`
4. The test keeps polling that pid for 5 seconds and keeps counting it as alive
5. pytest prints `FAILED ... assert False` and the run exits 1

After: the same run passes, because a zombie counts as gone

1. They run the same `docker run ... uv run pytest ... -k takes_its_process_tree` command
2. The fake prisma CLI times out after about a second and its whole process group gets SIGKILL
3. The killed grandchild reparents to PID 1, which never reaps it, so `ps` inside the container shows it as `<defunct>`
4. The test sees the pid in state `Z` on the first poll and counts it as gone
5. pytest prints `1 passed` and the run exits 0

## Relevant issues

## Affected release

## Linear ticket

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more

- [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Every run below is the real test inside a Linux container built from `python:3.12-slim` with `uv sync --frozen --group dev --extra proxy` (image `mat455-rig:deps`), the repo mounted at `/src`. Three PID 1 shapes: `noreap` wraps pytest in a Python parent that waits only on its direct child, so orphans are never reaped; `pid1` runs `uv run pytest` as PID 1; `init` is `docker run --init`, the control where tini reaps. A sidecar `docker exec` scans `/proc/*/stat` every 0.5s and counts processes in state `Z`

```
RUN="docker run --rm -v /src-slice:/src -w /src -e PYTHONPATH=/src mat455-rig:deps"
T=tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_prisma_toolchain.py::test_a_timed_out_migrate_deploy_takes_its_process_tree_with_it
# noreap
$RUN python3 -c 'import subprocess,sys; sys.exit(subprocess.call(sys.argv[1:]))' uv run --no-sync pytest $T -vv --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
# pid1
$RUN uv run --no-sync pytest $T -vv --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
# init
docker run --rm --init ... uv run --no-sync pytest $T -vv --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
```

### Before (8603d6e259)

#### noreap

1. Run the `noreap` command above
2. `FAILED tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_prisma_toolchain.py::test_a_timed_out_migrate_deploy_takes_its_process_tree_with_it - assert False`, exit 1, and the sidecar logs the grandchild as `state=Z ppid=1` for the whole 5 second poll (20 sidecar sightings over the run)

#### pid1

1. Run the `pid1` command above
2. Same `FAILED ... assert False`, exit 1, grandchild `state=Z ppid=1` (22 sidecar sightings over the run)

#### init

1. Run the `init` command above
2. `1 passed`, exit 0, 0 zombie sightings: tini reaps the orphan, which is why ubuntu-latest CI has not hit this yet

### After (ab2bbe58ac)

author: toastygm
body:
A place states `data.population` and an affiliation states how many people it counts, and
nothing read the two against each other. The rules had been living as a script in one
setting repository's `nogit/`, carried between worktrees by hand to be run at all. They
belong here, beside `unheld land`, which is the same family of check: a question asked of
the whole corpus and reported on the note that answers it wrongly.

`engine/populations.mjs` is written as that module's sibling — same `data.parents` and
`data.domains` reading, same corpus cached per link index, same diagnostic contract.
`shortcodesOf` is now exported from `engine/holdings.mjs` and shared rather than copied,
because "which shortcode does this entry name" has one right answer.

Closes #626

## The four rules

Each is named by the phrase its message begins with, and `POPULATION_RULES` is the
module's own statement of the list.

| Rule | What it finds | Where it lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `over-held land` | The polities whose `domains` name a place count more people than the place states | the place's `data.population` |
| `over-full region` | The regions whose `parents` name a place count more than it states | the place's `data.population` |
| `oversized settlement` | A settlement states more than a place containing it does | the settlement's `data.population` |
| `disputed figure` | A `doc` note cites a figure the place's or affiliation's own note contradicts | the `~figure` the page wrote |

The reading rules the corpus forced, each with a test:

- A polity subordinate to another polity holding the same place is already inside that
  polity's figure and is not counted twice.
- A settlement is exempt from `over-held land`: a city-state's polity holds the city and
  counts the hinterland around it, so its figure is properly the larger.
- A region naming both its parent and its grandparent counts under the nearer.
- A settlement is held to every place above it, not only its own parent.
- Figures are authored to two significant digits, so a place rounded up to five per cent
  below what it contains is not a finding.
- A place or affiliation stating no figure is neither compared nor counted, so a
  half-written region is quiet rather than noisy.

## What it deliberately does not do

**No urban-share ceiling.** The script carried a fourth rule capping the share of a
region's people living in its named settlements. It is dropped, and its absence is
deliberate rather than an omission: the settlement layer names the notable places and is
complete nowhere, so the ratio reports how much of a region has been *written*, not how
much of it is urban. As a gate it only ever moved a figure to silence itself. This branch
carries a test asserting no rule mentions an urban share, so it cannot drift back in
unnoticed.

**Every finding is a warning, never an error.** A figure out of step with its neighbours is
something an author wants to see while the note is open, and the same gap is legitimately
temporary while a region is half written.

**A dependency's people are counted nowhere.** A fetched index carries `parents` and
`domains` but no `population`, so a dependency's places take part in the geography and
contribute no figure. Filed as a follow-on rather than widened here; the published index
record is a separate contract.

**A figure is read only where it carries `~`, and only whole.** That marker is what
separates a population from the other numbers a table puts beside a place — a distance, a
stage count, a tally of days. And a number carrying a magnitude letter, a decimal, a
percent sign or a dash into a second number is prose *about* a figure rather than the
figure: `~1M`, `~1.5M`, `~5%`, `~12–14M` are left alone.

## The guard

`tests/populations.test.ts` derives its cases from `POPULATION_RULES` at runtime, so a rule
cannot be added without evidence. Each rule gets a tree that must provoke it and a tree
that must not.

- **Before:** the suite failed to load at all — `Cannot find module '../engine/populations.mjs'`.
- **After:** 27 tests pass.
- **The guard property itself, proven:** adding a fifth rule with no case failed four tests
  — the set comparison, plus that rule's own three. Reverted, green again.

## Why `patch`

A package that did nothing behaves identically: all four are warnings, so no consuming
tree that was building starts failing. The only change a consumer meets is extra advisory
lines on a tree whose figures already disagreed — which is the "a removal is a patch until
it is enforced" test read forwards. Shipped as errors these would be a `minor`, and they
are not shipped as errors.

## Verification

`npm run format` (no churn beyond this change), `npm test` — 4,497 tests across 188 files,
`npm run build:types`, `npm run lint`: all green.

**Against a real consumer tree.** Installed over `thalorna`'s toolchain and run through
`content-build lint` on its 2,570 notes, 764 of which state a population: **zero findings
across all four rules**, with its 308 pre-existing `unheld land` advisories unchanged. That
the check is live rather than silent was proven by perturbing one settlement's figure,
which produced

```
assets/content/.../Kalm.md:15:15: warning: oversized settlement: Kalm holds 20,000, more than the 8,500 stated by The Vardain Valleys
```

and was reverted.

That run also caught a defect in this branch before it shipped: the citation pattern read
`~1M` as the figure `1` and reported Magnápolis as "carried at 1 here and 900,000 on its
own note". The pattern now refuses a figure it cannot read whole, with a case per rejected
form.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Embedding cache hit on a model that returns several rows per input returns one row
- Partial cache hit on a multi input request mixes up vectors and duplicates `index`

How it solves it:

- Skip the per input cache write when the row count differs from the input count
- Send only the uncached inputs to the provider (on a copy of the request kwargs) and merge results back by position
- Stamp `format_version` on every embedding cache entry and treat entries without it as misses, so rows truncated before this fix are refetched instead of served until their TTL expires
- Validate cache rows with a frozen pydantic model, string (base64) embeddings included
- Build the merged partial hit response instead of mutating the cached one
- Post call hooks get the same miss-only `input` the provider saw

## User Flow

Before: a developer reranking 7 documents through a Triton cross encoder gets 7 scores the first time and 2 the second time

1. Their app calls `client.embeddings.create(model="my-reranker", input=[json.dumps({"query": q, "documents": docs[0:5]})])` through the OpenAI SDK against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings, then again with `docs[5:7]`
2. The first pair of calls returns `data` with 5 rows then 2 rows, one score per document, 7 scores in total
3. They run the same two calls again a moment later
4. Both calls now return `data` with a single row, so the app ends up with 2 scores for 7 documents and its ranking silently breaks

After: the same repeat returns 5 and 2 rows again

1. Their app calls `client.embeddings.create(model="my-reranker", input=[json.dumps({"query": q, "documents": docs[0:5]})])` through the OpenAI SDK against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings, then again with `docs[5:7]`
2. The first pair of calls returns `data` with 5 rows then 2 rows, one score per document, 7 scores in total
3. They run the same two calls again a moment later
4. Both calls return the same 5 and 2 rows as the first time, 7 scores for 7 documents

Before: a developer embedding 7 strings, 3 of which were embedded earlier, gets vectors attached to the wrong strings

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"input": ["banana", "date", "fig"]` and get 3 rows with `index` 0, 1, 2
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"input": ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elder", "fig", "grape"]`
3. The response has 7 rows but `index` reads `[0,1,1,3,2,5,3]`, and the vector in the `cherry` slot is the one for `banana`

After: the second request comes back with one correct vector per string

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"input": ["banana", "date", "fig"]` and get 3 rows with `index` 0, 1, 2
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"input": ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elder", "fig", "grape"]`
3. The response has 7 rows with `index` `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]`, cached vectors in their original slots and fresh vectors for the 4 new strings

author: zoltesh
body:
## Problem

Loading the Strategies and Backtests pages took tens of seconds on a real library (398 strategies / 759 results):

- **Strategies (~43.5s per view):** `GET /api/v1/strategies` enriched every catalog identity before slicing a page — 1 draft query + 1 publication-index query + one verified `load()` per publication + one latest-backtest query per fingerprint + one deployment query per identity ≈ **1,192 sequential SQL round trips per page**, and `listStrategies()` followed all four 100-row pages → ~4,768 queries.
- **Backtests (~8.3s per page):** the unfiltered listing orders by `(published_at DESC, result_fingerprint ASC)` but no index leads that pair, so every page scan/sorted the whole `published_backtest_results` table (rows carry the large canonical result JSON). Differential proof: indexed filters ran 0.009–0.057s while unfiltered `limit=1` cost 8.5s.

## Fix

- `list_strategies` now **selects the page first** (cursor decode → newest-first by group activity → archive filter → slice) and enriches only the returned rows:
  - `PostgresBacktestResultStore.list_summaries_for_strategies` — one `DISTINCT ON` query for the newest summary per fingerprint (capability method with per-fingerprint fallback on old doubles; falls back to per-fingerprint reads if the batched call fails).
  - `list_by_strategy_ids` on the Postgres and in-memory execution stores — one `IN` query grouped per identity; delegating wrappers (leases/overlay) expose it with capability fallback.
  - `PostgresStrategyPublicationStore.list_published` fetches canonical documents in the same query and verifies each row via the same `_published_strategy_from_row` as `load()` (was 1 + N `load()` calls).
- New index `ix_published_backtest_results_published_result (published_at DESC, result_fingerprint)` + **Alembic 0047**.
- Ops contract **v38**, expected schema revision **0047** (all four pin locations).

Response JSON shapes and pagination semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

Red-first guards (fail on main, pass here):
- `tests/api/test_strategy_library_query_efficiency.py` — proved **40 enrichment queries and a 4.13s wait for one 2-row page** on main; now ≤2 + ≤1 queries and <1s with 50ms simulated store latency.
- `tests/backtest/test_backtest_listing_index.py` — metadata↔migration index parity.

Independent review confirmed the regression empirically (main's route fails the counting test) and verified pagination semantics byte-equivalent. Gates: full suite **1,267 passed / 15 skipped** (pre-existing PG-env skips), `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `ty check` clean.

## Verification note

The new DISTINCT ON / IN SQL paths and migration 0047 were verified by the metadata/migration-consistency tests plus code reading; PostgreSQL integration tests skip without `THYTRADER_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. Recommend verifying the listing latency against the running stack after merge.

body:
Mechanical adaptation of the proven ADR-0015 runner (`run_bounded_cycle_adr0015.py`) to the PR #93-rewritten `confabulated_recipe_detection` corpus content (commit `16b0108291f549d5e5f6b0e1f409a65c3d6fdd92`), per this project's standing ADR-0013/0014/0015 execution-gating convention: a data-admission ADR never grants training authority by itself, so this is the fresh, separately gated execution proposal.

Background: task `t_39041f28` diagnosed why `mtr-v2-heldout-0013` regressed in ADR-0015 despite 8 dedicated training examples -- they were long, third-person, retrospective meta-commentary rather than direct behavioral rehearsal of the item's own short first-person closed-question shape. PR #93 (`t_91c92f12`, Maya-approved, merged as `16b0108`) rewrote the family accordingly (8 -> 11 records; corpus totals 160 -> 163, train 112 -> 115), verified not to touch train/held-out split boundaries.

This PR:
- Adds `examples/pilot-metatrainer-v2/run_bounded_cycle_adr0016.py`, reusing ADR-0015's training configuration basis (`learning_rate=5e-6`, one-epoch-per-corpus-size invariant, evaluator, contamination machinery, 16384MB memory ceiling) unchanged. Only the dataset file hashes (recomputed against commit `16b0108`), `MAX_STEPS` (112->115) and `SAVE_STEPS` (56->58) to track the corpus's new 115-example train split, the run id (`adr0016-metatrainer-sft-20260922`), and the approval namespace (`codevolt-adr0016`) are new.
- Adds `examples/pilot-metatrainer-v2/approval_allowed_signers_adr0016`, a fresh copy of the same three-role trust root (`maya-security`, `maya-dataset-rights`, `rook-owner`) scoped to this cycle's namespace/run id/implementation SHA, per this project's standing convention that no prior round's signed approval carries over.
- Adds `docs/decisions/ADR-0016-execution-config.md` documenting the `MAX_STEPS`/`SAVE_STEPS` deltas and full rationale.
- CHANGELOG entry.

Validation-only mode exercised locally against the pinned reviewed venv (trl 0.24.0, transformers 4.56.1, datasets 3.0.0, accelerate 1.4.0, torch 2.8.0): `status=PASS`, `training_called=false`, `train_count=115`, `held_out_count=48`, all 8 dataset file hashes verified against the live repo at commit `16b0108291f549d5e5f6b0e1f409a65c3d6fdd92`. No training performed or authorized by this change -- the runner remains fail-closed pending fresh three-gate signed approval (`execution_blockers` lists all three: signer-key admission, Maya's live-execution approval, owner confirmation).

body:
## Summary

Establish a current, evidence-backed product/source direction without changing runtime behavior or expanding existing acceptance gates.

Related: #167. Existing implementation owners remain #114/#115, #136/#146, #161, #91 and #92/#99. **This PR closes none of them.**

Product focus: **evidence-backed reviews that converge, with your models, policy and control**. GitHub PR review is the first host integration; keep a provider-neutral engine and reusable CLI/library, not a second review engine or a hosted development-agent platform.

## Changes

- Add `docs/product-direction.md`: priorities, existing module responsibilities, planned DecisionProvider boundary, independent safety controls, finite ownership and explicit non-goals.
- Refresh `docs/architecture/index.md`: acknowledge the implemented publisher and providers, identify planned versus delivered capabilities, index ADRs 0053/0054, and distinguish the owner-approved merge-focused replacement from main's still-legacy default. Preserve existing ADR history and process links.
- Add a dated audit report with exact source/CI/artifact/channel identities, all 22 initially open issues plus #146, observed results and explicit limits.

author: dougzethug
body: This PR addresses two bugs in the arena battle system and adds corresponding test coverage. ## Summary Fixed incorrect handling of drawn matches in battle direction and corrected visual object caching logic that failed to account for object ownership. ## Key Changes - **Draw match handling**: Modified `BattleDirector.ts` to skip the victory cue when a match ends in a draw (`rec.winner === null`). Previously, draws would incorrectly trigger victory fanfare for actor 0. Added test coverage to verify draws emit no victory cue. - **Visual object caching**: Fixed `LiveArenaScene.ts` object caching to include both the object ID and owner's team in the cache key. This prevents incorrect object reuse when the same visual object ID (e.g., 'held') is used by different actors, which could cause presentation issues since factories bake team information into the visual representation. - **Error handling in playable**: Enhanced `review/playable.ts` to properly handle startup errors by: - Allowing `readyResolve` to accept an optional error parameter - Calling `readyResolve` with the error in the `onError` callback - Checking for errors after startup and allowing retry if initialization fails - **Test coverage**: Added explicit test cases in `tests/engine-tests.mjs` to verify that only decided matches produce victory cues and that draws specifically emit no victory cue. ## Implementation Details The visual object caching fix uses a composite key format `id:team` to ensure objects are cached separately per owner, preventing cross-contamination when the same logical object ID is reused across different actors. https://claude.ai/code/session_013CDxFphJSmMJDpKGj7k9Q3 --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes drawn matches incorrectly firing the victory fanfare and visual objects being cached without accounting for the owner's team, which made shared ids like 'held' render in the wrong player's colors. Also makes the export capture retryable after a failed start. - Draws no longer emit a victory cue; only decided matches play the fanfare. - Visual objects are cached per id and owner team so shared ids render with the correct team visuals. - The capture exporter resets after a failed start so it can be retried instead of hanging. Written for commit 1648c274be0c5c96c769893235f02114eeee0781. Summary will update on new commits.

author: benjamindemaille
body:
### What's wrong

Header storage modes 12 and 14 (low nibble of byte 12 of the .pgen) are single-sample encodings, but `PgfiInitPhase1()` accepts them for any sample count and `PgfiInitPhase2Ex()` only checks `assert(raw_sample_ct == 1)`. A corrupted header therefore aborts plink2, even under `--validate`; with NDEBUG, the vrtype/record-length tables describe 2 to 6 byte records while the decoder reads a dosage track for every sample.

### Reproducer

Take `--dummy 400 600` output, set `b[11] = (b[11] & 0xf0) | 12` (or 14), then:

    plink2 --pfile x --validate
    # Assertion failed: (raw_sample_ct == 1), function PgfiInitPhase2Ex, pgenlib_read.cc:1306

### The fix

Reject these modes in `PgfiInitPhase1()` when `raw_sample_ct != 1`, next to the existing rejection of the reserved modes 13 and 15.

### Testing

New block in `TEST_PGEN_MALFORMED` aborts on master and passes with the fix; full suite passes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- `Bun.Image` throws `ERR_IMAGE_DECODE_FAILED` for a JPEG that libjpeg-turbo decodes with only a warning, such as junk before a marker or truncation.
- TurboJPEG returns -1 for a fatal error and for a completed call that warned. `codec_jpeg.rs` failed on every -1.
- The same function ignored the return of `tj3SetCroppingRegion`, its bound on rows. A 2x64 lossless JPEG resized to 2x50 wrote 8 rows past the buffer.

### Fix
- `Handle::completed` accepts a -1 when TurboJPEG's warning flag is set. `patches/libjpeg-turbo/fatal-clears-warning.patch` clears that flag on every fatal exit, where upstream keeps it, and adds the accessor that reads it. A build without the patch fails to link.
- A refused region now decodes unscaled with pitch 0, so `TJPARAM_MAXPIXELS` bounds the bytes written.
- The EXIF orientation reader skips the junk that libjpeg skips, so an accepted file keeps its rotation.
- Verified: 39 new tests, 26 fail on 1.4.3-canary. Self-reviewed: 12 concerns raised, 10 addressed. Not done: an upstream libjpeg-turbo issue.

### Background
- libjpeg warns about corrupt data that it decodes around. A fatal error exits through `longjmp`.
- The output `Vec` is uninitialised capacity (#39417). Its length is set after a completed decode.

### Downsides
- A corrupt or truncated JPEG now resolves where it threw before. A header with no scan data decodes to grey. #40118 asks for strictness.
- The accept path depends on a libjpeg-turbo patch.
- A resized lossless JPEG, or one with unusual sampling factors, decodes at full size.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**Rule.** If libjpeg-turbo finishes the decode, `Bun.Image` returns the pixels. If libjpeg-turbo hits a fatal error, `Bun.Image` throws, also when a warning came first. This is the line `djpeg` draws between exit status 2 and exit status 1.

**Comparison with `djpeg`** (built from the same libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 source without SIMD, 96x64 q90 fixtures, baseline and progressive gave the same results). Accept and reject match djpeg's exit status at every cut of both files. The pixels match for the files below. Over every cut, 17 of 1214 baseline and 46 of 812 progressive decodes differ from that djpeg, only in the block where the data ends, and none differ when Bun runs with `JSIMD_FORCENONE=1`: libjpeg's SIMD and C IDCT disagree on the out-of-range coefficients of a half-decoded block.

| file | djpeg | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 junk bytes before EOI | exit 2, "13 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9" | decodes, pixels identical to djpeg |
| EOI removed | exit 2, "Premature end of JPEG file" | decodes, identical |
| truncated at 95% / 60% | exit 2, "Premature end of JPEG file" | decodes, identical |
| cut right after the first SOS header | exit 2 | decodes, identical |
| 16 junk bytes + SOF5 after the first scan | exit 1 | `ERR_IMAGE_DECODE_FAILED` |
| SOF5 after the first scan | exit 1, "Unsupported JPEG process: SOF type 0xc5" | `ERR_IMAGE_DECODE_FAILED` |

**sharp 0.34.5 on the same files.** The default `failOn: "warning"` accepts junk before EOI in a baseline file (libvips never reads to EOI there), rejects it in a progressive file, and rejects truncated and EOI-less files ("premature end of JPEG image"). `failOn: "none"` accepts all of them.

**The trap.** `my_emit_message()` in `turbojpeg.c` sets `jerr.warning` and nothing clears it. A progressive JPEG with junk bytes and then an SOF5 marker before the second scan warns, then fails inside `jpeg_start_decompress` before any row is output. `tj3Decompress8` returns -1 with `TJERR_WARNING`. With the Rust change alone (patch removed from `scripts/build/deps/libjpeg-turbo.ts`), "warning, then a fatal error after the first scan: rejects" fails with "Received promise that resolved" for both fixtures. Upstream has the same flag handling at 3.2.0 and at main (b33c60b4). There is no upstream issue.

**Why a patch and not a zero-fill or a sentinel.** The decode keeps the `with_capacity` fast path from #39417, with no memset per decode. A zero-filled buffer alone returns a black image for a warning-then-fatal file, which the request rules out. An alpha sentinel cannot cover the CMYK output format, which has no constant byte. The patch is two hunks at the `bailout:` labels of `tj3DecompressHeader` and `tj3Decompress8`: `retval` is non-zero there only after a `longjmp` or a `THROW`.

**The accessor.** `codec_jpeg.rs` reads the flag through `tj3BunCompletedWithWarning()`, which the patch adds, and no longer calls `tj3GetErrorCode()`. With the patch removed from the list the build stops at `ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: tj3BunCompletedWithWarning`, so a `--local-deps` checkout without the patch cannot produce a binary that reads a fatal call as a warning. With only the bailout hunks removed (checked at dc12c3a8f5, where the same flag was read through `tj3GetErrorCode()`), four tests fail: the two junk plus SOF5 cases, the progressive file cut inside the DHT or SOS after its first scan, and the 2-component header.

**EXIF.** `exif.rs` walks the segments on its own to find the orientation. It stopped at the first byte that was not 0xFF, so a file with junk between APP0 and APP1, which the decoder now accepts, came out unrotated. The walk now skips what `next_marker()` skips: bytes that are not 0xFF, and 0xFF00. Junk between SOI and the first marker never reaches the decoder, because the format sniffer wants `FF D8 FF`.

**Call order.** `tj3Set*`, `tj3SetCroppingRegion`, `tj3SetScalingFactor` and `tj3GetICCProfile` reset the warning flag (`GET_TJINSTANCE`). `tj3Get` does not. `Handle::completed` runs straight after each decompress call.

**Review comments not taken.** A scaled decode for a stream with unknown subsampling: with the region refused only `TJPARAM_MAXPIXELS` limits the second parse, and it checks the unscaled product, so at 1/8 an 8x8 header (1x1 buffer) lets a 1x64 second parse write 1x8. A strict default for truncated files: see the next paragraph.

**To reject truncated input instead.** A missing EOI and truncated scan data are the same warning (`JWRN_JPEG_EOF`), and TurboJPEG exposes only the text of the first warning, so a default that rejects missing data but accepts a missing EOI needs a larger patch that classifies warning codes and reads `coef_bits` for progressive files. The cheap variant: Turn the `JWRN_JPEG_EOF` warning in `fill_mem_input_buffer` (`jdatasrc-tj.c`) into a fatal error in the same patch. EOI-less files then reject too, as in sharp's default.

**The cropping region.** `tj3Decompress8` parses the header a second time and takes the row count from that parse, so the caller bounds the writes with the pixel count, the pitch and the region. The review of this diff found the refused-region hole. It is not new (released bun returns the wrong pixels for the same input, and a debug build aborts under ASAN), but the accept path reaches it more easily: a lossless JPEG with a header warning used to be rejected at `metadata()`. The same call also refuses a stream whose sampling factors are outside TurboJPEG's table, which the fix covers. A mid-decode mutation of the input buffer can still make the second parse disagree, which is #43792's subject; with pitch 0 the bytes stay inside the buffer.

**The fill.** libjpeg writes flat grey for a block with no data, in every kind of file: (128,128,128), or (64,64,64) after the CMYK conversion. A progressive file has data for every block once its first scan is complete, so a later cut costs detail and no area.

**Self-review.** Four reviewers (the C patch, the Rust side, the tests, the written claims) raised 12 concerns. Found and fixed: the refused cropping region (the overflow above), the same call's second refusal (unknown subsampling), two tests that passed without the patch (replaced by a progressive file cut inside the DHT or SOS after its first scan, and a 2-component header that fails the colorspace check after a warning), truncation tests whose cut could land inside

author: aron23
body:
## What this is

Folds in the five open Dependabot PRs this wave supersedes, on one branch, as
separate signed conventional commits. Per the operator ruling, no Dependabot PR
is merged — each is closed with a comment pointing at this PR.

- Branch: `facetheory/dependabot-fold-in`, cut from `origin/staging` at `a2da0d8`
- Commits: 5 signed SSH/ED25519 `chore(deps)` / `chore(deps-dev)` commits plus a
  `chore(gov-infra)` rubric-evidence commit, one logical change per commit

## Superseded Dependabot PRs

| PR | Group | Scope | Applied | Held back |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #475 | ts-runtime | `ts/` | 19 of 20 | `constructs` 10.8.0→10.8.1 |
| #471 | infra-sites | `infra/apptheory-ssg-isr-site/` | 6 of 7 | `constructs` 10.8.0→10.8.1 |
| #469 | infra-sites | `infra/apptheory-ssr-site/` | 4 of 5 | `constructs` 10.8.0→10.8.1 |
| #470 | github-actions | `.github/workflows/` | 22 of 25 pinned refs | the 3 gate-asserted steps |
| #468 | docs bundler | `docs/` | 3 of 3 | — |

Commits:

```
51a825f chore(deps): bump the docs bundler group in docs
bca027e chore(deps): bump the github-actions group across .github/workflows
275a769 chore(deps-dev): bump the infra-sites group in infra/apptheory-ssr-site
e01af5f chore(deps-dev): bump the infra-sites group in infra/apptheory-ssg-isr-site
123550f chore(deps-dev): bump the ts-runtime group in ts/
```

## Judgment calls

**1. `constructs` is held at 10.8.0 in all three npm projects (#475, #471, #469).**
The pinned `@theory-cloud/apptheory-cdk@4.2.3` release tarball declares an
*exact* `peerDependencies` `constructs 10.8.0`. Moving to 10.8.1 makes
`npm ci` fail outright in every one of those directories:

```
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer constructs@"10.8.0" from @theory-cloud/apptheory-cdk@4.2.3
npm error Conflicting peer dependency: constructs@10.8.0
npm error Fix the upstream dependency conflict, or retry this command with --force or --legacy-peer-deps
```

`npm ci` is a step in the CI `ts` job and in the rubric's QUA-1 leg
(`ensure_ts_deps_installed`), so applying that one bump would take both down.
The hold is not a preference: npm also warns that
`constructs@10.8.0` is deprecated because it "has a bug that breaks downstream
jsii consumers", which is what 10.8.1 fixes. **This reverse-dependency needs a
decision:** the bump lifts when the `apptheory-cdk` pin moves to a release whose
peer admits 10.8.1, or when the repo chooses to override the peer. I have not
added an override and have not used `--legacy-peer-deps`.

**2. Three github-actions refs are held at their current pins (#470), and
`scripts/verify-ci-rubric-enforced.sh` is left byte-identical.**
That gate asserts three specific steps verbatim:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:226` — `actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d… # v4`
- `.github/workflows/release-pr.yml:137` — `actions/checkout@de0fac2e… # v6.0.2`
- `.github/workflows/prerelease-pr.yml:81` — `actions/checkout@de0fac2e… # v6.0.2`

They are the three governance control-plane steps: the rubric evidence upload and
the two trusted-verifier checkouts the release-PR postcondition depends on
(pinned checkout + `persist-credentials: false` + the trusted
`workflow_dispatch ? protected-branch : github.sha` ref, positioned after
release-please and before the postcondition). Moving those pins means editing the
compliance surface, which is a deliberate change and not a dependency bump, so I
did not do it inside a fold-in. **Everything else moved**, so `.github/workflows/`
is now on two `checkout` and two `upload-artifact` versions — the visible cost of
not touching the gate. Flagging it as a follow-up: the pin should move in a
deliberate commit that updates the gate in the same change.

**3. prettier 3.8.3 → 3.9.8 reformats `ts/README.md` (#475).** One blank line is
inserted before the `x-release-please-end` marker. `make ts-format-check` is a
step in the CI `ts` job, so the reformat rides in the ts-runtime commit.

**4. The `facetheory create` test literal moves to `^19.3.0` (#475).** The
scaffold derives generated-project dependency versions from this manifest's
`devDependencies`, so a generated React starter now receives `react`/`react-dom`
`^19.3.0`; the two assertions in `ts/test/unit/create-cli.test.ts` that pin that
value moved with it. The assertion still tests the same property (the scaffold
mirrors the manifest); the template fallbacks are coarse (`^19`) and needed no
change. This matches how the prior wave aligned the scaffold TypeScript fallback
(`032f872`).

**5. `typescript` goes to `^7.0.2` in the two infra packages while `ts/` stays on
`^6.0.3` (#471, #469).** Dependabot grouped the directories separately and only
the infra group carries TypeScript. The infra packages run TypeScript through
`tsx`, not `tsc`, so the divergence is inert there and the snapshot test confirms
it changes no synthesized output. Not resolved silently — raising it in case the
repo wants one TypeScript major across the tree.

**6. Lockfiles are regenerated with `npm install`, not copied from the Dependabot
branches.** Measured against each superseded branch's resolution, for all three
npm projects: no package removed, no downgrade, no new direct dependency. The ts
tree resolves slightly newer in-range transitive patches (for example
`@aws-sdk/client-s3` 3.1138.0 against the snapshot's 3.1136.0, both inside
`^3.1136.0`) and adds four nested `@aws-sdk`/`@smithy` entries that already exist
elsewhere in the tree. `docs/Gemfile.lock` came out **byte-identical** to the
superseded branch.

## Determinism impact

Preserved, and this is the load-bearing check for the infra bumps.

`make infra-snapshot-test` passes for both reference stacks with **no snapshot
file changed**, so the esbuild 0.28.1→0.28.2, TypeScript 6.0.3→7.0.2, and
`@aws-sdk/*` bumps leave the synthesized stack — and therefore the bundled Lambda
asset content and its S3Key — byte-identical.

The docs site was rebuilt along the exact `pages.yml` path, since
`jekyll-relative-links` 0.8.0 changes how relative links inside Jekyll includes
are resolved. Build clean, all three post-build assertions pass.

## Validation at head `51a825f`

```
$ scripts/verify-version-alignment.sh
version-alignment: PASS (4.0.10)

$ scripts/verify-ci-rubric-enforced.sh
ci-rubric: PASS

$ scripts/verify-node-engines-floor.sh
  ts/package-lock.json project engines.node ">=22" (449 dependency engine ranges)
  infra/apptheory-ssr-site/package-lock.json project engines.node ">=24" (111 dependency engine ranges)
  infra/apptheory-ssg-isr-site/package-lock.json project engines.node ">=24" (213 dependency engine ranges)
node-engines-floor: PASS (self-test 82 matcher and scope cases + 13 synthetic lockfiles; floor Node 22.x; lockfiles 3; dependency engine ranges 773; distinct ranges 73)

$ scripts/verify-npm-audit.sh
npm-audit: PASS (ts)
npm-audit: PASS (infra/apptheory-ssr-site)
npm-audit: PASS (infra/apptheory-ssg-isr-site)
```

Full `ts` CI job step list, run locally at this head:

```
make ts-typecheck        EXIT=0
make ts-lint             EXIT=0  (verify-svelte-runes self-test + scan PASS)
make ts-format-check     EXIT=0  (All matched files use Prettier code style!
                                  verify-format-gate: PASS (127 docs/package/workflow files parsed))
make ts-examples-readmes EXIT=0  (Verified 26 example READMEs under ts/examples.)
make docs-export-map     EXIT=0  (verify-docs-export-map: PASS (36 package exports documented))
make ts-test             EXIT=0  (tests 708 / pass 707 / fail 0 / skipped 1)

author: alexander-bain
body:
Closes #8035.

## The defect

**Will Dallas Stars advance to the Second Round?** The Discover futures card printed

```
Not Dallas Stars    60%
Dallas Stars        41%      <- 101%
```

The quotes are `0.595 / 0.405`, an exact complement. Venues quote on a half-cent grid, so both sides of one question land on the `.5` rounding boundary at once and a surface that formats each outcome on its own rounds both up. #2060 clause (1).

**3 of the 39 futures cards on page one** of the phone's own query printed 101 on 2026-09-22 (`GET /api/feed?limit=50&offset=0&event_pct=0.15`). Across the database, 6,609 of 17,583 open two-outcome mutually-exclusive markets sit on that boundary today.

## The rule already existed and nothing called it

`renderedCardPercents` — `Utilities/RenderedPercent.swift`, native's arm of `contracts/rendered_percent.json` — was written for exactly this under #2060 and had **zero call sites in the app target**. Contract-tested, and unreachable from any screen.

So what ships is the **wiring**, and the wiring is what is guarded: the hero numeral, every outcome row and the share sentence now come from one decision per card.

## And the picture that leaves the app

`ShareCardRenderer.renderFuturesCard` rounded its own hero and rows too, so fixing only the card would have left the exported image printing `60% / 41%` under a card reading `60% / 40%` — the defect #7998 closed on the event card, still open on futures. Two causes, and **only the first is visible to a sum guard**:

1. **THE ROUNDING**, as above.
2. **THE LIST.** `renderedShareImage()` `compactMap`ped the unpriced outcomes away before handing the field over. The pair rule fires only on a two-outcome field, so a three-outcome market with one unpriced side reached the image *as a pair* and was normalised — on a field the card deliberately leaves alone. **Both surfaces then sum to 100 while printing different numbers.**

So `renderFuturesCard` has no `probability:` parameter and its `outcomes` list has no default — the two omissions #7998 made deliberately on the event card — and the list it takes is the whole served field, nils and all. `rowPercents` and `heroPercent` are internal rather than private because a `some View` is unreachable from XCTest: a mutant emptying either derivation survives every behavioural assertion otherwise.

## What does not change, deliberately

- A **three-way field still prints 101** (Brazil Presidential, in the fixture) — it is not a complement pair, and #2088's `card_sum_reason` sentence is what explains those. Asserted in both directions.
- A pair that was **already right** (Treasury yield, 93/7) does not move.
- The **leader keeps its own number**; the derived point lands on the side nobody is quoting. A sum-only guard is satisfied by moving the wrong side, so that is asserted separately.
- The **bar width still reads the raw probability** — a length is not a printed number.

## Evidence

Fixture `BainLuckTests/Fixtures/feed-futures-binary-101.20260922.json` is **production**: six cards lifted verbatim from one response. Nobody typed these probabilities.

```
gated tree   : /Users/bain/bainluck-dev/native
gated sha    : 989d1b3df7a96f1299d7ca516468cc1d7cd0020a
macOS build  : PASS   ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
recompile    : checked 4 changed Swift file(s)
Executed 3362 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 91.536 (92.230) seconds
```

### The mutation battery changed the shape of the fix

`tools/n298-2874-share-image-mutants.sh` — first run, 6 of 7 killed and **one survivor**:

```
caller-filters-the-field-again :: SURVIVED  <-- the guard does not see this
```

The list rule was stated inline in `renderedShareImage()` and guarded by a source scan for the exact old spelling of the filter, so the same filtering **in slightly different words** went unseen — a guard aimed at one *phrasing* of a defect rather than at its *behaviour*. The mapping is now `discoverFuturesShareRows`, a file-scope function a test can call, asserted by `test_theShareRowsKeepEveryOutcomeIncludingTheUnpriced`, and the battery gains a second arm for the call site. Re-run results posted as a comment.

(Sibling: `tools/n297-8035-mutants.sh`, the card's battery from native/297 — 3 of its 6 mutants originally survived, all view-layer, which is why the source scans exist at all.)

Both batteries now **resolve the simulator by UDID at runtime**: `-destination 'name=iPhone 17 Pro'` was refused on this machine with a simulator of that exact name installed, and the refusal **exits 70 — the gate never ran**, which a battery reads as "no kills" rather than as a broken rig (gotcha #124).

Tier A under notice 49(d): no production data, migrations, settlement, blending or ranking.

author: increasinglyhuman
body:
**Field, comm** (6.3 M triangles, 1,127 geometries): a `meshAdded` rebuild took **1,539 ms**. An unchanged rebuild takes 175 ms with every geometry cached, so the added mesh was falling off the cached path.

**Three causes, all fixed**
- **Repack.** Any change to the ordered geometry keys re-interleaved every vertex and re-based every index. Geometry is now interleaved once, when it's clustered. Indices stay local to their geometry, and each cluster record carries the geometry's vertex base (a spare slot, read by the caster vertex stage). A repack is one copy per geometry straight into the mapped GPU buffers.
- **Cache key.** It began with Babylon's `geometry.uniqueId`, so a prim World deletes and re-creates with the same shape missed and was re-clustered. The key is now content-addressed. As a bonus, identical shapes on different meshes share one geometry: the demo world goes from 98 to 33 geometries, with the same 2,896 instances.
- **Pruning.** The cache kept only what the last build used, so anything that dropped out of one rebuild (hidden while loading, say) was re-clustered when it came back. Unused entries now survive 4 builds.

**Measured** with `scripts/rebuild-probe.mjs` (new; 1,100 geometries, 2.4 M vertices, NVIDIA):

| Rebuild | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| +1 mesh | 262 ms (repack 177) | 105 ms (repack 44) |
| −1 mesh | 210 ms | 102 ms |
| 100 meshes back after one build out | re-clustered | all cached, 128 ms |
| same shape re-created | re-clustered | pure cache hit, 81 ms, nothing re-rendered |

**Correctness**
- The consumer test passes in all five configurations, including the add-a-box and remove-a-box shadow checks.
- Demo screenshots against main: the forest view is pixel-identical. The village view differs in 5 px, where shared geometry now draws in a different order at exactly equal depth. Main against itself differs in 0 px outside the stats panel.

**Not changed:** the unchanged-rebuild floor (~175 ms on comm) is content hashing. That's the next step if it matters.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem

Two separate paths silently discarded a note the user had just written.

### 1. Dismissing the sheet threw the note away

`closeNoteOverlay()` was bound to **both** the ✕ button and backdrop taps, and it unconditionally cleared state — no save, no confirmation:

```js
el('noteViewClose')?.addEventListener('click', closeNoteOverlay);
el('noteViewOverlay')?.addEventListener('click', event => {
    if (event.target === el('noteViewOverlay')) closeNoteOverlay();
});
```

The sheet is bottom-anchored (`.note-view-overlay { align-items: flex-end }`), so on a phone the dimmed backdrop covers the top of the screen and is easy to hit while typing or while dismissing the keyboard.

Reproduced before the fix:

```
typed:  title = "Chapter 4 summary", text = "Derivatives, limits, and the chain rule."
tap backdrop -> overlay closed, no confirm shown
localStorage dailykrd_guest_notes : null
notes in subject list             : 0
```

### 2. A failed write left a phantom note on screen

`saveOpenNote()` pushed an optimistic copy into `subjectNotes` and printed "Saved" **before** the write was attempted. When `persistNote()` threw, the `catch` only changed the status line — the optimistic copy stayed in the list, then vanished on the next reopen or reload:

```
before fix, write rejected:  rows right after save = 1  ->  after reopening subject = 0  ->  after reload = 0
```

## Fix

- ✕ and backdrop taps now call `dismissNoteOverlay()`, which saves first when there is content. **Cancel remains an explicit discard.**
- "Saved" prints only after the write is accepted.
- A rejected write rolls the optimistic copy back and restores the typed title/text into the editor, keeping the sheet open so the user can retry.
- `persistNote(note, subjectId)` now takes the subject explicitly. It previously re-read the global `selectedSubjectId` at call time, so navigating away mid-save made it `return false` and drop the note silently.

## Verification

The app's own `initSubjectsNotes` module was executed verbatim in jsdom against its own markup, with only the Firebase SDK stubbed:

- **15/15 behaviour assertions pass** — Cancel still discards; ✕ saves; backdrop saves; dismissing an *empty* note creates nothing; rejected write keeps the text and shows no phantom.
- **Lifecycle A–D** (guest, signed-in healthy, signed-in write-denied, guest→sign-in) all keep the note across a simulated reload.
- `node --check` on all three `<script>` blocks: OK.
- i18n untouched: en/ku/ar still 236 keys each, zero drift.

**Not verified:** no browser binary was reachable in the test sandbox, so this is jsdom — no real Firebase, no canvas photo compression, no touch events.

## Follow-up

There are no Firestore rules in this repo, so it could not be confirmed that production rules permit `users/{uid}/subjects/{id}/notes/{id}`. With this fix a denied write now shows a visible "couldn't save" instead of a silent disappearance — if notes are still lost while signed in, check those rules next.

author: benjamindemaille
body:
### What's wrong

`LoadPsam()` and `LoadPhenos()` decide from the first data line, by first character only, whether each phenotype column is categorical. `1e400` starts like a number, so the column is marked numeric; `ScanadvDouble()` then rejects the value as out of range, and the code takes the "categorical entry in a numeric column" error path. That path assumes an earlier line exists: it hits `assert(psam_info_reverse_ll->next)` (or `assert(pheno_info_reverse_ll)`), and without asserts it dereferences a null list pointer.

### Reproducer

    printf '#IID\tSEX\tP1\nper0\t1\t1e400\nper1\t2\t1\n' > x.psam   # plus a matching .pgen/.pvar
    plink2 --pfile x --freq
    # Assertion failed ... plink2_psam.cc:527, exit 134

A `--pheno` file whose first entry is `1e999` behaves the same way.

### The fix

On the first line, report `Error: Invalid numeric token '1e400' on line 2 of x.psam.`; later lines keep their existing message.

### Testing

Both new cases in `TEST_PHENO_UTILS` (including the CSV `--pheno` variant) abort on master and pass with the fix; full suite passes.

author: ukme13
body:
Stages 3 to 6 of [the studio guide plan](docs/roadmap/studio-guide.md), closing it. Stages 1 and 2 went in as #147 and #148.

The studio had no user-facing documentation: nine routes, anchors, undo, simulation, uploaded fonts, alpha and a handover command, with the knowledge in 45 journal entries written for people who already knew.

## What landed

**Stage 3 — the route factoring and `/studio`.** `packages/ui` keeps the rows a client receives; `@blueprint/ui/docs-routes` is its own entry point for the rest, following the precedent `primitive-usage` set. Then getting started: what the studio is, that it runs in this browser and nowhere else, the nine routes, undo, and how a system gets out. `/docs/button` also gained the nav — it was in the route list, so it appeared in every other page's sidebar and had none of its own.

**Stage 4 — six guides.** Anchors, semantic tokens and alpha, typography, the three scales, simulation and accessibility, export and handover.

**Stage 5 — the changelog**, badged with the date and the workspace file version current at the time.

**Stage 6 — the link**, on `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL` with a localhost fallback.

Along the way the documentation shell was rebuilt against a layout reference: fixed header, sticky sidebar, a contents column with a working scroll spy, and a footer.

## Two guards worth reviewing closely

**Route and page agreement, both ways.** The nav, the home page and the footer are all generated from the route list, so a typo is a dead link in three places and nothing else would say so. [routes.test.ts](apps/docs/lib/routes.test.ts) fails in both directions — a route with no page, and a page nothing links to.

**The changelog cannot drift.** The newest entry is asserted against `BLUEPRINT_WORKSPACE_FILE_VERSION`. Bumping the constant to 9 gives `the format is at v9 and the newest entry says v8`, so a format change without an entry fails on the day it happens.

## Facts checked, not remembered

Every number in the guides was verified against the code, because the roadmaps describe plans the app has moved past. Three would have been wrong: there are four vision deficiencies and `achromatopsia` is one, the severities are Machado's tabulated tenths rather than a free slider, and generated sizes round to even pixels with a floor of 11.

Writing the changelog caught one I had repeated four times, including in a merged PR: **version 8 is preview frames and layout uses**, not the button schemes, which arrived without a bump. The journal is corrected in place with a note saying what it used to say. It survived a plan, a PR, a merge and two rounds of review, and was caught by the first thing that had to *use* the fact rather than mention it.

## Checks

- `pnpm -r test`: 1172 in `packages/ui`, 51 in `apps/docs`.
- Lint at `--max-warnings 0`, types clean in all three workspaces, Prettier clean.
- `pnpm handover` and `verify-handover` clean, with no internal route in the archive — asserted by reading every byte, matching route paths by shape and label so it can tell a leak from this workspace's own prose about "the studio".
- Stages 4 to 6 ran on fast checks locally, by agreement, with the browser suite left to CI here. One known flake: `workspace-home.spec.ts` "clicking another card opens that name on the rail" failed once under parallel workers and passes in isolation. Unrelated to the change and left alone.

body:
## What

Masks `serial-getty@ttyS0.service` on every Utah flavor, so the agetty that
Hummingbird's server base spawns on a port desktop hardware does not have stops
respawning into the journal.

Fixes #103.

## Why this and not the karg

#103 names two halves. Both are real, and neither can be removed from *here*:

- `/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/00-base.toml` belongs to the Hummingbird base image.
  bootc's `kargs.d` is additive only; withdrawing an argument the base declared
  there is documented undefined behavior, so there is no supported way for a
  derived image to drop `console=ttyS0,115200n8`.
- `90-systemd.preset` belongs to the base too.

What Utah *can* control is the outcome: the unit the generator instantiates.
That is the second option in the issue's acceptance ("mask
`serial-getty@ttyS0`"), and unlike the karg it also reaches machines that
already carry the argument in their BLS entries, because a mask travels with an
image update.

The mask names the instance rather than `serial-getty@.service`: `ttyS0` is the
port the base names, so a genuinely attached serial device on any other port
keeps its login. Masking is also the only lever that works — the generator's
`getty.target.wants` symlink is created in `/run` at boot, so it cannot be
deleted at build time, and a preset entry alone would not stop it.

## Where it is wired

Same three places the update-timer policy already lives, so the shape is
familiar and each one is gated:

- `scripts/configure-services.sh` — `systemctl mask serial-getty@ttyS0.service`
  plus the `/usr/lib/systemd/system/...` → `/dev/null` symlink, the `/etc` +
  `/usr/lib` pair that keeps a cross-vendor `/etc` 3-way merge from
  resurrecting it.
- `85-utah-desktop.preset` — `disable serial-getty@ttyS0.service`. Presets are
  read in lexicographic order and the first match wins, so 85-* outranks the
  base's `90-systemd.preset`.
- `contracts/bluefin-desktop.toml` `[services].masked` — so
  `utah-verify-desktop-contract` fails the image build if the mask is dropped.

`just check` gains the matching greps, `tests/test_desktop_contract.py` gains a
parity test beside the bootc-fetch-apply-updates one, and
`docs/skills/desktop-contract.md` documents the whole thing (same PR, per
AGENTS.md).

## Testing

- `python3 tests/run_suite.py` — 369 tests, OK.
- `just check`'s static gates, run individually and all green:
  `check-script-syntax.py`, `verify-desktop-contract.py --check`,
  `verify-gnome-extensions.py --source`, `check-skill-frontmatter.sh`,
  `check-skill-index.sh`, `generate_skill_index.py --check`,
  `check-download-integrity.py`, `generate-site-data.py --check`,
  `check-doc-counts.py`, `check_workflow_outputs.py`, `flavors.py`,
  `install-packages.py --check`, `verify-rpm-contract.py --check`.
- **`just check` as a whole could not complete on this machine**: the host
  filesystem is at 100% (486G/488G used, 1.9M free), so its
  `git submodule update --init --recursive` step fails with `No space left on
  device` while cloning the GNOME extension submodules. That is an environment
  limit, not a result — no gate that does not need the submodules failed.
- No image build was run, so the mask is verified by source gates and the
  contract, not by a boot. `just check-desktop-contract` against a built image
  is the confirmation that would close that gap.

## Not in this PR

Utah still boots with `console=ttyS0` on the kernel cmdline, so printk is
mirrored to a port that usually is not there. Masking the getty removes the
log spam and the wakeups the issue reports; silencing the console itself needs
either the base to drop the karg or `--karg-delete` on the install path, which
is a separate change.

body:
The `build-dataset -t` smoke died three different ways on the wenceslaus cluster; this fixes all three and un-flakes the streaming smoke test.

## What

- **Direct buffer OOM** (`FinalizeWrite`): beam's per-slot grpc fn servers need direct memory outside flink's pools, and the JVM otherwise caps it near the 128m framework off-heap. Both compose templates now pass `taskmanager.memory.task.off-heap.size=2g`.
- **`ImportError: gliner2`** in the sdk harness: mining imports `gliner2` at runtime but it sat in the dev group, so the worker wheel shipped without it. Moved to `[project] dependencies` (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`).
- **Fullmap `I/O error: No such file or directory`** (`resolve mined batches`): the wheel baked the host Desktop path. `RELMEDNER_FULLMAP_DIR` env override in `src/relmedner/constants.py` lets the sdkworker point at its own `/opt/fullmap` mount; locked in `tests/test_constants.py`.
- **`src/relmedner/pipeline.py`:** new `output_path()` decides local-vs-`/opt/outputs` output by the declared runner, not options presence, so local prism runs carrying worker options keep the caller's path.
- **`tests/test_outputs.py`:** smoke runs with `--direct_num_workers=1` and `--job_server_timeout=1800`. Twelve ingests streamed concurrently trip unauthenticated HF rate limiting past prism's 300s result-stream default (measured: reddit shards 2-34s sequential, 207-237s concurrent).

## Verification

- `make test`: 625 passed on the laptop and on wenceslaus (`PYTEST_EXIT:0`, `RUFF_EXIT:0`); `make lint` clean.
- Deferred: US-006's end-to-end `SMOKE_EXIT:0` gate is still blocked on cluster ownership (the `better-flink-cluster` session owns the wenceslaus flink stack); this PR carries every code-side blocker.

author: samihanninen
body:
> Pinottu PR #22:n päälle, koska molemmat muokkaavat `KilpailijatView`ia. Kohde on `rosteriin-listalta`, ei `kehitys` — kun #22 menee `kehitys`-haaraan, tämän kohde vaihtuu automaattisesti siihen.

Rosteri oli taitettu osio kilpailijalistan yläpuolella. Avattuna samat ihmiset näkyivät sivulla kahdesti — rosterissa ja kisan kilpailijalistassa — eikä kumpaa listaa milloinkin muokkasi erottunut.

## Muutos

- **Oma reitti `/#/rosteri`** (`src/views/RosteriView.vue`). Tarkoituksella poissa päävalikosta: rosteri ei ole kisadataa vaan tämän laitteen oma nimilista.
- **Kilpailijasivulle jää kortti**, joka kertoo tilan (*2 henkilöä laitteella* / *tyhjä*) ja vie rosteriin. Tyhjässä kisassa linkki nousee ensisijaiseksi ja lukee *Täppää väki rosterista* — sama syy, jolla osio oli ennen valmiiksi auki juuri silloin.
- **Paluu kahdesti:** ylälaidan `← Kilpailijat` ja listan alta iso *Valmis — kisassa N kilpailijaa*. Alempi on se olennainen: puhelimella ollaan täppäämisen jälkeen listan pohjalla.
- `RosteriValinta` menetti `<details>`-kuorensa ja on nyt sivun sisältö.

## `replace`, ei `push` eikä `back()`

Paluu on sivupolun päättäminen, ei uusi askel. `push` jättäisi historiaan Kilpailijat → Rosteri → Kilpailijat, jolloin laitteen paluupainike toisi takaisin rosteriin. `router.back()` taas hajoaisi, kun sivulle on tultu suoralla linkillä tai uudelleenlatauksen jälkeen — paluu veisi ulos sovelluksesta. Molemmille on testi.

## Testit

- `src/views/__tests__/rosteri.spec.ts` — 3 uutta: paluu, historia (`go(-1)` ei palaa rosteriin), napin lukumäärä
- `src/views/__tests__/kilpailijat.spec.ts` — 3 uutta korttitestiä
- `e2e/kilpailijat.spec.ts` — 1 uusi selaintesti paluulle ja `goBack()`ille; vanhat rosteritestit kulkevat nyt rosterisivun kautta
- `README.md` ja `KILPAILUOHJE.md` päivitetty

Kaikki vihreänä: 429 yksikkötestiä, 57 selaintestiä (Chromium).

### Motivation

- Aclarar el mapeo de columnas sensibles: `RESUL. VENTAS` = cantidad de equipos y `FAC. VENTA DRONES` = `monto_equipos` (COP), que es la base para refacciones.

### Description

- Implementé la vista y la lógica cliente en `assets/scripts/modules/actualizacion-temporal.js`, incluyendo renderizado tabular por aliado, formateo numérico/moneda y la acción `applyPartner` que llama al endpoint `bulkImportTemporal` del Apps Script para escribir las metas y evaluaciones en una sola operación.
- Unifiqué la normalización de nombres para la importación (eliminando espacios y signos) para tratar variantes como `DRONE DEPOT` / `DRONEDEPOT` como el mismo aliado, añadiendo `normalizePartnerName_` en `appscript/Code.gs` y el análogo en el cliente.

- Validé la extracción del Excel con `python /tmp/validate_evaluations.py`, que confirmó `88` filas fuente extraídas de las 4 pestañas y que la vista retiene `68` evaluaciones únicas (canonical partners: 68 evaluaciones, 20 aliados, 4 periodos). (éxito)

author: irobinson010
body:
Closes #1221 (the activated-ability half; the statics half of the same issue is the next PR).

CR 113.6 is one rule and the engine had answered a quarter of it. `ActivatedAbilityShape.Zones` has existed since #660 and nothing but the hand ever used it — because the shape was never the missing part. **The consumers were.** The enumerator walked the battlefield and the seat's own hand and stopped; the view stamped `hand_abilities` on a hand card and nothing anywhere else; and `AbilityCost` had no component for the clause three of the four graveyard keywords print. The seam row said the same thing from the other side: four cards "one `Spec` edit away", and had been for months, because nothing would have offered the edit to anybody.

## Shapes

| shape | where | what |
|---|---|---|
| `AbilityCost.ExileSelf bool` | `server/internal/game/activated.go:282` | scavenge's and embalm's "Exile this card from your graveyard" — `DiscardSelf`'s sibling one zone over |
| `(*Game).validateExileSelfCostLocked` | `server/internal/game/exile_cost.go:50` | the graveyard check, with the rest of the cost, before anything is paid |
| `(*Game).payAbilityExileSelfLocked` | `server/internal/game/exile_cost.go:71` | paid last, through `routeCardToZoneLocked` with `MustSettleNow` |
| `(*enumerator).abilityZones()` | `server/internal/legal/abilities.go:137` | the activation sibling of #1014's five-zone cast walk — hand, graveyard, command, exile |
| `stampZoneAbilities` / `stampZoneAbilitiesInPile` | `server/internal/protocol/view.go:3772`, `:3805` | the same four piles on the wire |
| `castStamps.ZoneAbilities` + `(*CardView).stampZoneAbilitiesFor` | `server/internal/protocol/view.go:2821`, `:3092` | the per-seat carrier, merged rather than replaced |
| `CardView.ZoneAbilities` (`zone_abilities`) | `server/internal/protocol/view.go` | was `hand_abilities`; renamed, not duplicated |
| `ActivatedAbilityView.ExileSelf` (`exile_self`) | `server/internal/protocol/view.go:2003` | `discard_self`'s advisory sibling |
| `effects.ExileThis()` | `server/internal/cards/effects/activated.go:162` | the cost constructor |
| `effects.Unearth / Scavenge / Embalm / Eternalize` | `unearth.go:42`, `scavenge.go:32`, `embalm.go:41`, `:58` | the four keywords, in the `Cycling`/`Typecycling` mould |
| `effects.ExileInsteadOfLeavingBattlefield` | `server/internal/cards/effects/exile_instead_of_leaving.go:49` | factored out of Whip of Erebos, shared with unearth |
| `ZoneBrowserModal.onActivateAbility` | `client/src/lib/components/board/ZoneBrowserModal.svelte:311` | the prop the browser never had |

## The three decisions worth arguing about

**`ExileSelf` is a second bool, not a zone on one "the source pays itself" component.** Discarding is a CR 701.8 keyword action with its own event (`EventDiscardCard`), its own cause (`DiscardCauseCost`) and, for cycling, `EventCycle` on top. Exiling as a cost is a plain CR 406 zone change with none of that. A card file that wanted "discard this from your graveyard" would be writing a card that does not exist. What they genuinely share — the payment IS the source, so nothing is announced, picked, or sent — they get for free by both being a bool.

**The effects read their own source back out of exile; no LKI snapshot on the stack item.** Scavenge wants "this card's power" and embalm wants the whole card, and by then their own COST has moved it. `LookupCardForEffect` finds a card in whatever zone holds it, and a card outside the battlefield has no layers applied to it (CR 613 runs on permanents) — so the printed power read out of exile at resolution is the number the graveyard held. A snapshot field would be a second LKI store beside the damage event's, which `targets.go:96-105` already declines to build for the same reason. The cost is declared: a card moved out of exile between announce and resolution does nothing (CR 608.2a, the weaker direction, #259).

**`zone_abilities` is scoped, not merely hidden — and that is the change most likely to have been got wrong.** Through #660 the rows were written to the exported `CardView` field and took their privacy from the HAND: `FilterViewFor` blanks another seat's hand wholesale. A graveyard is PUBLIC. The same code would have shipped one seat's `legal_targets` and `clauses` to the whole table, which is exactly the surface #1055 / #1167 took off the cast stamps, arriving again one field over — hexproof, shroud and "target opponent" all narrow a target set *by who is asking*. So the rows ride `castOffers`, the per-seat carrier that already exists for that question, and `publicIn` drops them. The hand's rows moved there with the graveyard's rather than leaving two lifecycles for one field.

One wrinkle, because it breaks silently: `stampLegalTargets` and `stampGrantedPermissions` file a seat's entry with `stampsFor`, which REPLACES. The ability stamp therefore MERGES and runs after both — a plain `stampsFor` here would blank a flashback card's announce surface the moment that card also printed a graveyard ability.

**The library is not walked, in either consumer.** CR 401.2 makes it hidden, no printed ability functions from one, and an enumerator that read it would touch cards the seat may not see to answer a question whose answer is always "nothing". The one line it would take is named in the comment (`legal/abilities.go:137`'s doc) so the day a card prints such an ability it is a line, not a rediscovery. Exile, the one shared pile, gets the CR 108.4 treatment in both walks: the "you" comes off `Card.Owner`, not off the loop.

## Files

**Engine**
- `server/internal/game/activated.go` — `AbilityCost.ExileSelf`; the validate and pay call sites, beside the discard component's
- `server/internal/game/exile_cost.go` (new) — the component, modelled line for line on `discard_cost.go`
- `server/internal/legal/abilities.go` — `abilityZones()`, the four-pile walk, the CR 108.4 owner filter
- `server/internal/cards/effects/registry.go:372` — the boot-time refusal of `ExileSelf` off the graveyard

**Wire**
- `server/internal/protocol/view.go` — the rename, `castStamps.ZoneAbilities`, `publicIn`'s clear, `applyTo`'s promotion, `stampZoneAbilities` over four piles, `exile_self`
- `docs/protocol.md` — `zone_abilities` replaces the `hand_abilities` bullet; the `activate_ability` row gains the exile-this paragraph

**Catalog**
- `unearth.go`, `scavenge.go`, `embalm.go`, `exile_instead_of_leaving.go` (all new); `activated.go` (`ExileThis`, `Plus`); `whip_of_erebos.go` (refactored onto the shared helper)
- `dregscape_zombie.go`, `deadbridge_goliath.go`, `sacred_cat.go` (new)

**Client**
- `protocol.ts`, `faces.ts`, `contextMenu.logic.ts`, `Card.svelte`, `Hand.svelte`, `Board.svelte` — the rename
- `ZoneBrowserModal.svelte`, `Board.svelte` — the browser's ability rows and the CR 307.1 window

**Docs**
- `docs/decisions/0020-activated-abilities.md` — a dated addendum, decisions 24–28
- `docs/decisions/0071-designations-that-switch-abilities-on.md` — a dated addendum: the zone stays out of `Designation` and out of the accessors' return value, because `Active(c Card)` reads no zone and because a zone-filtered slice would renumber the announced ability index
- `docs/engine-seams.md` — the row rewritten, a Closed-seams entry, the two follow-ups linked
- `docs/decklists/card-coverage-roadmap.md` — regenerated with `go test ./internal/cards/coverage/ -update`, never by hand

## Tests

**Engine** (`server/internal/game/other_zone_ability_test.go`): activation from a graveyard and from exile; the CR 113.6 refusal in both directions (a graveyard ability on the battlefield, with the mana untouched); the CR 108.4 non-owner refusal; `ExileSelf` exiling the source at announce with the ability still on the stack and the card still readable by instance ID with its printed power; `ExileSelf` refused outside a graveyard with nothing moved and nothing spent.

**Per keyword** (`server/internal/cards/effects/graveyard_keywords_test.go`): every keyword declares

author: arnaudprioul
body:
## Le défaut, vérifié sur `develop`

```
lint-staged (le hook) : eslint --fix
lint        (la CI)   : eslint . --ext … --max-warnings 0
```

**Le hook n'a pas `--max-warnings 0`. La CI l'a.** Un avertissement ESLint passe donc le pre-commit et fait rougir l'intégration — vert en local, rouge en CI, sans que rien n'explique l'écart au développeur.

## D'où ça vient

C'est un trou laissé par **#564**, qui a mis `lint-staged` en place pour que le hook ne linte plus que les fichiers indexés — correction juste — **sans aligner le seuil de sévérité**.

Trouvé par un agent dont la PR est tombée sur `vue/one-component-per-file` **après un pre-commit vert**.

## La famille de défauts

C'est la même que le `pnpm -F <pkg> run <script-inexistant>` qui rend `exit 0`, ou que le `cmd | tail` qui renvoie le code de `tail` : **les deux commandes ne sont pas la même commande**, et l'une des deux ment par omission.

Un garde local qui n'applique pas le critère de la CI n'est pas un garde — c'est un délai avant la mauvaise nouvelle.

## Le changement

Une ligne.

```diff
-    "*.{vue,…,mts}": "eslint --fix",
+    "*.{vue,…,mts}": "eslint --fix --max-warnings 0",
```

⚠️ **Conséquence assumée** : un commit portant un avertissement ESLint sera désormais **refusé localement**. C'est l'intention — c'est exactement ce que la CI fera de toute façon, deux minutes plus tard.

author: the-ult
body:
Adds two Faker generator options, so the client, schemas, MSW and Faker groups can each be published as a separate package without generated files importing across package boundaries through relative paths.

- `importPath`: MSW files import (and re-export) the `get<Op>ResponseMock` factories from this package specifier instead of `'../../faker/<tag>/<tag>.faker'`. Applies in `split` and `tags-split`, the modes that write MSW and Faker to separate files.
- `schemasPath`: writes the `schemas: true` factory file (`index.faker.ts`) to this directory instead of the schemas directory, so the schemas package no longer imports `@faker-js/faker`. The relocated file imports schema types from `schemas.importPath`, or through a relative path back into the schemas directory. Operation mocks import it relatively, or through `schemasImportPath`, which now also works with `schemasPath` in place of `schemas.importPath`.
  When `schemasPath` sits inside the Faker `path` and `indexMockFiles` is on, `index.faker.ts` re-exports the factories with an explicit list. The list leaves out names an operation mock already exports: a `ListPetsResponse` schema and the `listPets` operation both produce `getListPetsResponseMock`, and exporting both would fail with TS2308.

```ts
{
  type: 'faker',
  path: './src/generated/faker',
  importPath: '@acme/mocks/faker',
  schemas: true,
  schemasPath: './src/generated/faker/schemas',
}
```

Both options are opt-in, and existing configs generate identical output: the `tests/` and sample snapshots are unchanged. Validation rejects a `schemasPath` without `schemas: true` or `output.schemas`, and one that equals the Faker `path` while `indexMockFiles` is on, because the barrel is also called `index.faker.ts`.

To find the schema factories at their new location, `generateImportsForBuilder` gets a trailing `filePath` argument, which is why every mock writer mode shows up in the diff. The core of the change is in `write-specs.ts` (`writeFakerSchemaMocks`) and `generate-imports-for-builder.ts`.

Also included:

- A test that generates all four groups into separate directories and checks that each barrel only re-exports its own group.
- A `petstoreArtifactGroups` sample in `samples/angular-app` with a Node-only vitest spec (`vitest.node.ts`, now part of the sample's `test` script). It loads the MSW barrel and asserts that Angular is never imported.
- An "Artifact groups" section in `output.mdx` that ties the existing options and the two new ones into one model.

Fixes #3832

author: mfrachet
body:
Factory UI used to build its own frame on every page (a local AppShell, ChatLayout, FactoryPageShell, SettingsPageLayout) and kept the sidebar provider inside a route element, so the chrome remounted between route groups and the app looked and scrolled differently from Studio.

This moves factory-ui onto the same building blocks Studio uses. One persistent `FactoryAppFrame` wraps `/factories/:factoryId` with playground-ui's `AppShell` and a rounded StudioCard-style surface, and every page renders playground-ui's `PageLayout` with breadcrumbs, so the sidebar stays mounted across navigation and the page body owns scroll instead of the document. Custom empty states are replaced with the DS `EmptyState`, and `ChatHeader` (app chrome) is split from a new `SessionBar` (page-level bar) so mobile no longer shows duplicate controls.

`PageBreadcrumbs` is promoted from playground into `@mastra/playground-ui` so both apps share it; playground keeps a thin react-router shim.

```tsx
<FactoryPage>
  {factory => (
    <PageLayout breadcrumbs={<FactoryBreadcrumbs crumbs={[{ id: 'factory', label: factory.name, to: ... }, { id: 'overview', label: 'Overview' }]} />} headerActions={<RangePicker />}>
      <OverviewContent factoryId={factory.id} />
    </PageLayout>
  )}
</FactoryPage>
```

Test plan: factory-ui typecheck, unit (450) and MSW (1048) suites green; playground-ui tests and playground typecheck green; verified in the browser at desktop, tablet and mobile widths that the sidebar persists across Overview → Work → Thread → Settings, a single sidebar trigger renders on small screens, and content scrolls inside the card with no document scrollbar.
