body:
**sc-24113** — Qwen Image 2.1: complete generation/editing controls and optional prompt rewriting. > ⚠️ **HELD.** Do not merge until the epic's feature-branch inference pin bump. Everything below is > correct against the S1/S3/S4 contracts, but this branch pins an inference revision that predates > the 2.1 provider, so the engine-side halves (the `output_channels` field, the `ReferenceRgba` > carrier, the descriptor read) are staged behind a named one-line swap rather than wired. Each one > is called out in place. Targets `feature/sc-24107-qwen-image-2-1`. Chains on #2913 → #2912 → #2909, whose head (`a4b14fa2a`, the fix-pass commit) is the base — so the manifest entry, routing, licence gate and alpha egress come in from there and are not re-litigated here. --- ## 1. The control surface The manifest declared seven presets and a step floor. Everything else was inert or wrong, and every gap had the same shape: **a bound the UI could not see, so the user met it as a failed render instead of a form error.** | Control | Before | Now | |---|---|---| | Aspect presets | 7 declared, read | unchanged (+ the free-size envelope below) | | Free width/height | blanket 256–4096, **no stride** | declared **32–2752 on a 32-px grid**, enforced at enqueue | | Steps | `min="1"` hardcoded vs a declared floor of **2** | reads `limits.hardMinSteps` | | Seed | worked | unchanged, round-trip asserted | | Negative prompt + true-CFG | worked (absent `image` block ⇒ both true) | unchanged, round-trip asserted | | Count | `limits.count: [1,2,4]` | `[1,2,4,8]` — the engine's own max | | References | refused by routing | **1–10 ordered**, with visible order and reorder | | Transparency | — | toggle + the prompt convention it needs | **Free size** needed two new manifest keys. Deriving the range from the preset ladder (what the web did before) gives 1536–2752 — the smallest and largest *preset* sides — which is not the engine's envelope and refuses every legal small size. So `limits.minDimension` / `maxDimension` join `requiresDimensionsMultipleOf`, and the API's shape-check floor drops 256 → 32. **That did not loosen anything else:** the 256 moved down one layer as `HISTORICAL_MIN_IMAGE_DIMENSION`, the per-model fallback, so a sub-256 request to any model that declares no floor is refused exactly as before — now naming the model. **References are ORDERED, and the order is semantic.** The engine's template numbers the images (`` …) and block-causal attention makes each one visible only to what follows, so swapping two references is a *different request*. Three consequences: - the enqueue gate **rejects** an 11th rather than truncating (truncation renumbers everything after the cut, which is not a smaller render but a different one); - the editor's rail shows each reference's ordinal and gives it arrows, because the prompt conventions for this family name images directly ("use the second image as a mask") and a user who cannot see which one is second cannot write that prompt; - the editor's single `MAX_EDIT_REFERENCES = 4` becomes a per-model reading of `limits.maxReferenceAssets`, with that constant as the fallback — so nothing about FLUX.2 / SenseNova / Krea moves. **Still refused**, each for its own reason rather than as leftovers: `maskAssetId` (there is no mask tensor in this family — a mask is an ordinary extra reference the prompt names, and the refusal says so) and pose / ControlNet (no strict-control tier exists to reach). ## 2. Transparency — the control most likely to be misread **There is no transparency mode upstream.** The 2.1 VAE is *always* four-channel; `output_channels: Rgba` only asks for the fourth channel to survive the decode instead of being composited over white. Whether that channel holds a cut-out is decided by the **prompt**. A toggle alone therefore hands back a fully opaque RGBA PNG and reads as broken. So it ships paired with the model card's own wording, offered as **editable text on a button** — never appended silently (a prompt the user cannot see is one they cannot fix), and never offered twice (the suggestion disappears once the prompt already says it, so replaying a recipe cannot accrete it). Per the confirmed **S4 contract** (inference #1009), the names are `Capabilities::supports_alpha_output` and `GenerationRequest::output_channels: OutputChannels { Rgb | Rgba }` — an **enum**, not a channel count, whose default is byte-identical to every pre-S4 render. They are spelled in exactly one module per side: `crates/sceneworks-worker/src/qwen_alpha.rs` and `apps/web/src/qwenAlpha.js`, pinned together by tests on both. **Staged behind the pin:** the pinned `Capabilities` has no `supports_alpha_output` member, so `engine_advertises_alpha_output` answers from a one-entry id list. Its *body* is the swap; its callers, tests and refusal text are already written against the descriptor read. Likewise `Conditioning::ReferenceRgba` — 2.1 has no worker-side edit route until the bump, so the carrier choice is named and tested (`reference_conditioning_kind`) with nothing to call it yet. ## 3. Prompt rewriting Upstream ships this as **two separate checkpoints**, and which one applies is decided by the **request** — references present means the editing half — never by a user-facing picker. | | repo | frozen revision | |---|---|---| | T2I | `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I` | `f3ed7985c788ad75b3ab7223e0c4c51e2a43545b` | | I2I | `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I` | `72927bc08afc99b7888ceb7d7d51a12db3700bbd` | Both are fine-tuned **Qwen3.5/3.6 (`model_type: qwen3_5`) 9.41B VLMs** — the same architecture the optional `film_planner_qwen3_6_27b` entry already runs. So they load on the **existing** native `core_llm::TextLlm` lane (`Architecture::Qwen35` → `Qwen35Config`/`Qwen35Model` on `mlx-llama` / `candle-llama`, with `Qwen35VisionModel` + DeepStack for the I2I image turns) as a `prompt_refine` task. **No new route, no new job type, no second LLM runtime.** **Licence:** Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT — **non-commercial**, the same terms as the base 2.1 weights. Both entries carry `requiresLicenseAcknowledgment`, `licenseUrl`, a transcribed `licenseNotice` and `nonCommercial: true` (which is what the packaging NC-weights guard and the Simple licence badge read). **The templates are frozen BY REVISION, not vendored.** Each snapshot ships its own `system_prompt.txt` — that file *is* the published template — so the worker reads it from the installed snapshot and verifies its SHA-256. This is the stronger freeze and the only licence-clean one: the prompts are Qwen Materials under a non-commercial licence whose §3 puts redistribution duties on anyone who passes them on, and SceneWorks' whole posture for this family is that it never redistributes them. A digest check also catches an upstream re-push *loudly*, where a vendored copy would keep using stale text against newer weights. **The rewrite is a suggestion, not a replacement.** It lands in an **editable textarea** beside the untouched original (the generic refiner's read-only `

` would not do), the aspect-ratio suggestion is accepted or ignored **separately** and always as one of the model's own seven presets, and `ratio_follow` is translated into the user's own 1-based reference numbering. **With neither rewriter installed there is no affordance at all** — no download, no prompt to install, no degraded path — and generating never enqueues a rewrite as a side effect. Both are `autoDownload: false`, asserted. ## 4. Fixed in passing `load_reference_image` flattened an alpha-carrying reference with `to_rgb8()`, which **drops** the fourth byte. 2.1's alpha is straight — `A=0` does *not* zero RGB — so a transparent background arrived at the VAE as whatever the encoder left behind, commonly black, on **every** reference lane in the app. It now composites over white, matching the engine's own `to_rgb_over_white()`. author: metr-background-agents[bot]
body:
## Overview

When a submission points Hawk at a package artifact by URL and the server refuses to serve it, the runner currently treats that as Hawk's own fault: it logs at ERROR under a Sentry fingerprint, which pages on-call and opens a fresh Sentry issue (and Linear ticket) for every distinct package name. Classify it instead — a 4xx on a URL the submission chose is the submission's problem, and Hawk cannot repair it.

Fixes [SEN-289](https://linear.app/metrevals/issue/SEN-289/uv-failed-failed-to-download-env-cheating-smoke) / [HAWK-49T](https://metr-sh.sentry.io/issues/HAWK-49T).

## Approach

uv fetches a URL dependency with a plain unauthenticated GET, so the status the server returns describes the URL the submission supplied, not the runner's credentials or its egress: a signed link whose signature no longer verifies, an artifact deleted from its bucket, an object that was never public. Nothing on the Hawk side can fix any of those, and the installation still fails loudly with uv's full output in the pod log — only the log level changes, from ERROR to WARNING.

This follows the pattern already used for the last several of these (SEN-190, SEN-202, SEN-260, SEN-262): rather than a blanket rule, the suppression is generated from the requirements the caller actually submitted, so it can only ever excuse a failure attributable to them. Three things must all hold. The failing package has to be one the caller pointed at a URL — either a named URL requirement, or a bare wheel URL, where PEP 427 fixes the name in the filename, which is exactly where uv itself got the name it printed. It must not be a package Hawk injects, since a dead URL in Hawk's own pins is Hawk's bug. And the cause has to be one of the statuses meaning "this URL will not serve this artifact" (400, 401, 403, 404, 410). Everything else keeps paging: 5xx and 429 are transient and worth knowing about if they persist, 407 is a proxy asking for credentials and so points at Hawk's own egress, and a registry-sourced package failing to download is the index misbehaving rather than a URL anyone chose.

As with the existing patterns, the framing line and the cause must sit inside a single uv failure block, so a refused user URL can never suppress a second, Hawk-owned failure reported in the same run.

Alternatives ruled out: retrying (a 4xx is not retryable, and uv already retries what is), and validating artifact URLs at submission time (it cannot catch a URL that dies between submission and install, which is this case).

## Testing & validation

- [x] Verified the change works (commands / manual steps described above)
- [x] Added or updated tests where it makes sense

- Drove **real uv 0.8.17** against a loopback server returning chosen statuses for a wheel URL, and classified the resulting output through the production code path. All 6 scenarios behaved as designed: 400 and 403 on a named URL requirement and on a bare wheel URL are suppressed; 503, 429, and a 400 on a Hawk-injected package still page. The output shape matched the production capture exactly.
- `pytest tests/core/test_shell.py` — 129 passed. New coverage asserts the positive case and each negative one: 5xx, 429, 407, Hawk-injected names, registry-sourced packages, sdist URLs, malformed wheel filenames, excluded markers, unselected transitive packages, and a user failure followed by a separate Hawk failure.
- `pytest tests/core tests/runner` — 3,139 passed, 3 xfailed. One unrelated failure (`test_normalize.py::test_refused_sources`) and the DB-backed errors reproduce identically on `main` in this sandbox (no Docker available for testcontainers).

## Code quality

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (ruff, basedpyright/mypy, eslint/prettier/tsc, shellcheck — what CI's Lint job runs)

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `basedpyright` (0 errors, 0 warnings) all clean on the changed files.

## Before merging

- [x] PR title is a [Conventional Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with a lower-case subject — it becomes the squash-merge commit subject and drives the SemVer bump
- [x] All commits are **signed** and show as **Verified** on GitHub — see [Commit signing](https://hawk.metr.org/contributing/#commit-signing)

## Risks

- The classification is a judgement call about who owns a failure, so the risk is a real Hawk bug landing at WARNING. It is bounded to caller-selected URL packages and five client-error statuses, and the negative tests above are what hold that line — widening either set should be a deliberate decision.
- Worth watching: a 403 can also mean a bucket policy changed under a submission that used to work. That is still not something the runner can fix, but it will now be quieter — it surfaces as failing eval-sets and WARNING logs carrying uv's full output rather than as a page.
- No API, schema, or runtime-behaviour change; installation still fails and the runner still exits non-zero exactly as before.

Linear: https://linear.app/metrevals/issue/SEN-289/uv-failed-failed-to-download-env-cheating-smoke

body:
## Summary

`CLAUDE.md` had two passages left over from before v1.0.0 shipped (`f859f3f`, 2026-09-23).

- The release-versioning paragraph carried a pre-1.0 carve-out, that a breaking change also bumps minor below 1.0. It no longer applies now that 1.0 is out, and the preceding sentence already covers the post-1.0 case on its own.
- The section "v1.0 までの内部構造の固定" still described the freeze as in effect. It is now "内部構造の固定の終了後も効く制約": the freeze ended with the v1.0.0 release, and only the constraints that bind for a different reason remain.

## What still binds

Three constraints, each verified against its source:

- **Dependency direction**, normative in `docs/design.md` 7a.7, checked by `TestDependencyDirection`, `TestPureLayersStayPure` and `TestVpsdSubpackagesDoNotImportVpsd` in `internal/dataplane/deps_test.go`.
- **The import boundary of the Admission Policy compiler**, normative in `docs/design.md` 7a.9, checked by `TestPolicyNftablesDoesNotImportGoogleNftables` in the same file. A test enforces both, so neither depends on the freeze.
- **The external compatibility guarantee** in `docs/design.md` 7a.11, which began with the v1.0 release. The freeze ending and the guarantee starting are two separate things: the internal build can change now, while the promises on the public surfaces hold.

## Stale references the rename would have left behind

- `internal/dataplane/userspace/tunnel/bind_windows.go` and `internal/dataplane/userspace/utun/bind_windows.go` justified duplicating five lines partly by saying it would touch the package boundary frozen until v1.0, citing `CLAUDE.md`. That rule no longer exists there. The comments keep the reason that still holds -- a new package is not worth it for five lines -- and drop the appeal to the freeze. Nothing is shared as a result; the freeze ending is not a reason to share.
- The revision record in `docs/design.md` carries a 2026-09-21 entry that placed the freeze rules in `CLAUDE.md` under its old heading. This follows the shape `d495cc4` used for the same situation: the existing sentence stays as written, a new sentence after it points forward, and the expiry itself gets its own dated 2026-09-23 entry at the end.

## What is deliberately absent

No policy for how internal structure is governed after v1.0. The freeze was bounded by its own terms and has expired. The rules it carried -- the standard of demonstrable harm, and the habit of recording rather than making an improvement found mid-task -- were written as conditions on the freeze and lapse with it. Keeping the harm standard as a general principle would read as "no demonstrable harm, no refactor", which is the wrong default for v1.1 and v1.2, where internal structure is expected to move. What replaces it, if anything, is an owner decision; the new revision-record entry states that the question is left open.

## Checks

- Lab gate on `f26c6a8`: ALL PASS, 325 s, no leftover VM
- `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` all pass
- `bash scripts/check-ascii-punct.sh` passes

## Noted, not fixed here

- `internal/vpsd/conncheck/conncheck.go:95` cites "CLAUDE.md の 7a.7 節"; 7a.7 lives in `docs/design.md`. The error predates this change.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins the windows-test and macos-test targets to literal package paths. Now that packages may move, those jobs can silently narrow. A coupling rather than a rule, so it is not listed as a constraint.

author: pavonis-martian
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1195.

Treat `Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation.` as a host lifecycle interruption at the runtime completion boundary. The summarizer propagates the lifecycle error without trying fallback providers or generating a deterministic fallback summary.

Pending-summary preparation releases the interrupted node's claim without consuming its retry allowance or marking the batch stale. The maintenance pass stops with the lifecycle cause. Source messages, pending work, and prepared siblings remain available for a later host-approved invocation with fresh capabilities. Existing deferred-maintenance backoff remains in effect.

This does not bypass inventory retirement or change genuine provider-failure handling. It does not repair fallback summaries that were persisted before the fix. The host-side admission issue remains separate.

## Regression coverage

- Exercise the real plugin completion adapter through maintenance and SQLite persistence.
- Cover below-threshold preparation and deferred threshold publication, with and without partial progress.
- Repeat retirement beyond the pending-node retry limit and verify that nodes remain retryable.
- Verify source messages and context remain intact, no fallback summaries are persisted, and fresh capabilities complete the work.
- Verify lifecycle failures do not produce provider keys/quotas advice.

## Validation

- `npm test`: 126 files, 2,006 tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run build:plugin`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Includes a patch changeset. No new host API, configuration, schema, or compatibility requirement.

author: mark-vieira
body:
included-regions doesn't work the way I intuitively expected. It only matches when all files in a changeset are matched by at least one regex. Essentially it is meant to be the inverse of excluded-regions (as the documentation states had I actually read it).

There's another use which is slightly more relaxed which is "only run this job if code that matches these patterns has been changed", but doesn't require that the entire changeset match. An existing example is the example-plugins job. This really should run anytime someone changes an example plugin, but we were skipping it if the PR changed anything else.

This adds a new any-included-regions option with said behavior and updates the example-plugins job to use it.

author: amazingnessly
altogetheragile
body:
`docs/PLATFORM_MIGRATION.md` was last true on 28 June. Two things changed since then that it did not record, and a reader would have been misled about both.

## What Was Wrong

**It said the two-surface split was the destination.** It is not. Nothing had removed the App's claim on the nine URLs the Site already served, so those pages had two implementations, and a visitor saw whichever one their route of arrival happened to render. The home page and the About page were each maintained twice.

**It said the session was deliberately left in `localStorage`** because the Site never server-gates. That reasoning was circular: the Site never server-gated because it could not, and it could not because of where the session lived. The bill was three months of `exam_attempts` recording nothing.

## What This Changes

- **New Section 6a** records the revised plan: one frontend, a group at a time, with the App's route deleted on the way out. Five steps, with 1 and 3 done (#724, #725, #728 to #731) and 2, 4 and 5 open.
- **The old auth-seam decision is kept and marked superseded** rather than deleted. The reasoning is worth being able to re-read, and so is why it was wrong.
- **Phase 0 corrected** from "in progress" to complete but for dependency scanning and uptime monitoring, both of which need an account rather than code. Rate limiting turns out to have shipped as our own `ai_rate_limits` implementation, not Upstash as planned.
- **The stale "next step" block** pointed at work finished in June. Replaced with the September log.

## Two Things The Tick Marks Hide, Now Written Down

Step 3 landed the session, but **no Site page calls `getUser()` on the server.** `layout.tsx` still reads the cosmetic `aa-auth` cookie. So the gate on the second half of the migration is open and has never been driven, and the first page to server-gate will also be the first real test of it.

Step 2's SEO case is **nearly spent**: one sitemap URL out of forty is still served by the App (`/ai-tools`). What remains is a maintainability argument, competing directly with Vision to Value.

Documentation only. No code changes.

body:
## Le problème

Rien n'indique quelle version une page a chargée. Impossible, alors, de distinguer :

- « le correctif ne marche pas » ;
- « le navigateur sert encore l'ancien fichier ».

Plusieurs allers-retours perdus là-dessus aujourd'hui, à se renvoyer la même capture
d'écran (#92, #93) sans pouvoir trancher. Le code publié était bon à chaque fois.

## Le changement

`__BUILD_ID__` existe déjà — c'est l'heure du build, injectée par Vite et utilisée par
`UpdateBanner` pour proposer la mise à jour. Il suffisait de l'**écrire quelque part** :


author: assanedu032-netizen
body:
## Le défaut, vu sur un vrai téléphone

La table des matières et la page de copyright s'affichaient en **un pavé justifié illisible**, où « Copyright 4 Préface - Loïc 5 Avant-Propos 7 » se lisait d'un trait.

**Cause :** je recollais les lignes sur le **seul** critère de la taille de police. Ça marche pour de la prose — la préface était parfaite — mais une table des matières et une page de copyright ne sont pas de la prose.

## La géométrie du PDF disait tout, je ne l'écoutais pas

**1. L'écart vertical.** Sur la page de copyright il vaut `16-17` à l'intérieur d'un paragraphe et `35-39` entre deux. On coupe désormais au-delà de **1,35 × l'écart médian de la page**.

**2. La forme « titre … numéro ».** Un sommaire a des interlignes parfaitement réguliers — l'écart ne le trahit pas. Mais chacune de ses lignes finit par un **numéro de page**. Quand la page en aligne au moins quatre, chaque entrée devient son propre bloc, avec son numéro.

**163 → 344 blocs.** La prose est inchangée : la préface garde ses cinq paragraphes.

## Et ça ouvre quelque chose

Puisque chaque entrée du sommaire porte son numéro de page, on sait laquelle est **dans** l'extrait :

- **Copyright, Préface, Avant-Propos, Comment utiliser ce livre, L'Histoire, les 8 Lois** → en doré, **cliquables**, elles sautent à leur page ;
- **Cours 1 à 12, Chapitres, Programmes** → estompés, avec un **🔒**.

L'athlète voit exactement ce qu'il n'a pas encore. C'est plus honnête qu'un sommaire muet, et c'est un meilleur argument que n'importe quel slogan.

**Aucune entrée hors extrait n'est cliquable** — c'est testé, parce que promettre une page qui n'existe pas serait pire que ne rien promettre.

## Vérification

**12 assertions de plus** (39 → 51), qui verrouillent exactement le défaut constaté : le sommaire ne doit plus jamais être recollé, le copyright doit rester en plusieurs paragraphes, la préface doit garder les siens, et **aucun bloc ne doit dépasser 1 400 caractères**.

**5 de ces assertions échouent sur `main`.** Les **27 suites du projet sont vertes**.

body:
## Auftrag
Schriftliche Freigabe des Inhabers (Chat, 22.09.2026): **„Ja, 10.000/Tag"** — Anhebung des Autopilot-Tagesziels von 5.000 auf 10.000 veroeffentlichte Profile.

## Änderungen (alle in Richtung Tagesziel, QA-Gate unangetastet)
- **Deckel/Ziele 5000 → 10000:** pipeline-publish.yml (Default), pipeline-run.yml (Auto-Publish), pipeline-watchdog.yml (AUTOPILOT_DAILY_TARGET + Dispatch), pipeline-health.yml (Ziel/REMAINING/Titel), pipeline_stats.py (DEFAULT_DAILY_TARGET), pipeline_quota_check.py (DEFAULT_TARGET), Test-Default.
- **Nachschub:** Ingest-Limit je run-small-Lauf 1000 → 1500 (12 × 1500 = 18.000/Tag).
- **QA-Kapazitaet:** batch_size_per_shard 50 → 60; Lane-Matrizen 8+8 → 10+10 Shards; total_shards 24 → 20; Lane-B-Cron 4 → 6 Slots.
- **Blindfleck-Fix:** Seit 36628f4f (8+8 von 24 Shards) waren die QID-Partitionen 8–11 und 20–23 nie aktiv (~1/3 des Pools unerreichbar). 10+10 bei total 20 decken jede QID ab, 20 parallele Jobs bleiben im Runner-Limit, Ueberschuss queut (fail-fast:false).

## Rechnung
~15.000 QA-Durchlaeufe/Tag noetig (65–70 % Pass-Quote) — Kapazitaet ≈ 21.600+ QA-Versuche/Tag (20 Shards × 60 × 18+ Slots) plus Selbst-Takt/Watchdog-Eskalation. Ehrlicher Hinweis: 22.09. wurden bis 18:47 UTC nur 761/5000 erreicht (Runner-Knappheit, blinde Shards) — 10.000 ist das Ziel, das der Watchdog jetzt aktiv nachschiebt.

## Validiert
- 655 Backend-Tests gruen (uv, Python 3.12; die 5 scheinbaren Shard-Fails waren nur Python 3.9)
- 3 Pflicht-Guards gruen, `npm run build` gruen, YAML-Parse aller Pipeline-Workflows gruen

## Rollback
`git revert` des Merge-Commits (alles in einem PR, QID-Partition zustandslos).

author: heddayam
body:
## Summary

Regional builds repeatedly loaded the same OSM topology, retained large temporary compiler/audit structures, and checked for finished artifacts only after expensive preparation. This change reduces those allocations and lets unchanged builds validate and reuse their saved pack before extraction or elevation sampling.

- Prepare OSM once; key buildings and named areas by the boundary-aware preparation identity. Stream hashes and OPL, share unchanged topology records, and remove the unused parser/intermediate exports.
- Bound temporary compiler batches and elevation-sampler input. Iterate persisted audit rows and reuse equivalent forward/reverse coverage checks without weakening geometry validation.
- Make source caches portable between Docker and native paths. Fingerprint DEM tile content and order independently of retrieval metadata. Use verified pins by default, with explicit `--offline` and `--refresh` modes.

Production TypeScript is 11 lines smaller; regression tests grow 360 lines. No new dependencies or pack schema changes.

## Validation

- Two full `npm run verify` passes: 506 tests in 82 files, lint, types, and production build. Two browser passes: all 7 offline flows each.
- Full current-pin Central Cascades build passed in a 4 GiB Docker container with swap disabled: 3.842 GiB cgroup peak, no OOM kill, zero audit errors. Approximately 170 seconds after source acquisition; 553 seconds including the PBF download. This is one measured acceptance run, not a universal RAM guarantee.
- Offline warm reuse passed with networking disabled in 34 seconds. The same container-written cache/artifact worked natively in 32.34 seconds with 1.075 GiB process RSS; every artifact checksum stayed unchanged.
- On the same existing Cascades artifact, standalone audit peak RSS fell from 2.081 to 0.980 GiB and time from 34.303 to 20.480 seconds; complete audit JSON stayed byte-identical. Compiler fixture database bytes and all five regional compatibility fixtures are unchanged.

Detailed evidence and measurement limits are recorded in `docs/rebuild/pack-build-audit.md`. Installed packs were preserved; generated verification data remains ignored.

author: zingzy
body:
Ticket: https://github.com/Zingzy/wsp-map/issues/1080

Closes the harness folder of https://github.com/Zingzy/wsp-map/issues/1077: the default agent's binary lands in /usr/local/bin on the image and on a box alike.

What it does:
- The agent's install line writes `install -D -m 0755` into `/usr/local/bin`, and the row's `bins` names that folder, so a box job's check finds it under the job's own PATH and the row stops reading failed and installing again on every run.
- `LOCAL_BIN` moves to `roads.ts` beside `HOME_BIN`; `road-modules.ts` and `catalog.ts` import it from there.
- No workspace on a box can rewrite the file its siblings run, since `/usr/local/bin` is read-only inside each one.
- The box test drops its one exception: no line the job sends names `/root/.local/bin` but the profile file.
- Comments that said the harness lives under the home now say what the code does.

An image sealed before this holds its agent under `/root/.local/bin`, first on its PATH. The image's setup removes that file before it installs the new one in `/usr/local/bin`, and an update runs that setup, so an update moves the agent as a rebuild does. The agent's row carries the install alone, so no line a box's job sends names a folder under the home.

Status: gate green (build, tsc, the named test files), CI green on the head (run 35792405101), build report and fix round 1 posted on the ticket.

author: asav-mx
body: Inicio abre contestando (8.8), y **las rutas son parte de esa respuesta**. Estaban detrás de un buscador, que pedía escribir antes de poder mirar. | Sin ubicación | Con ubicación | |---|---| | | | Fíjate en el **encabezado**: cambia con lo que la app de verdad sabe. ## El orden, que es materia de la 8.7 y no de diseño **Con ubicación:** por la **parada más cercana de cada ruta**, medida en el teléfono, y cada renglón enseña **su distancia** — un orden que no se puede comprobar pide que le crean; éste se puede comprobar. **Sin ubicación: alfabético.** La app no sabe quién eres (8.7), así que el orden no puede salir de rastrear a nadie: nada de «las más buscadas» ni «las más abiertas», que exigirían guardar lo que hace cada pasajero. **Se evaluó ordenar por camiones en vivo y se descartó**, y queda escrito en `rutas-cerca.ts` para no volver a proponerlo: cuesta una consulta por ruta cada 15 s para toda la ciudad —justo el costo que la lista de rutas ya había decidido no pagar— y en el arranque, con pocas unidades prendidas, el orden brincaría cada sondeo delante de quien lo está mirando. ## Tres cosas que la pantalla NO dice, y por qué **1 · No titula «cerca de ti» sin ubicación.** Ahí dice **«Rutas de la ciudad»**. Tres rutas cualesquiera bajo el título «cerca de ti» serían el **dato correcto con la afirmación falsa** (§D): no miente la lista, miente el encabezado. La sección se enseña igual —con tres rutas, no vacía—; lo que no se hace es llamarlas cercanas. Y eso no queda a criterio de quien escriba la pantalla después: `ordenarRutas` devuelve `porDistancia`, y **el título sale de esa misma bandera que el orden**. No se pueden separar. **2 · No dice «hacia Centro».** Saber hacia dónde va un sentido necesita el trazado de esa ruta: una petición por ruta. Se dice al abrirla, que es cuando importa. **3 · No dice «en vivo».** De los camiones sólo sabemos los de **tus favoritas**. Ponerlo en unas y no en otras se leería como «las demás no traen camiones», y eso no lo sabemos. Lo que sí lleva cada renglón es **su promesa** (8.2) y, si está cerrada o no ha arrancado, eso. ## El toggle, y «Ir a» sin lista | Desplegado | Con parada guardada | |---|---| | | | `vista-rutas.tsx` —la pantalla aparte de «todas las rutas»— **se retira**: su contenido vive desplegado aquí y su pie se mudó con él. **«Ir a» queda sólo como buscador.** ## Detalles que salieron al construirlo - **Una sola petición de permiso por pantalla.** Sin paradas guardadas, el bloque de arriba ya pide la ubicación y concederla ordena las dos secciones; el botón «Ver rutas cerca de mí» **sólo aparece cuando ese bloque no está** (captura de la derecha). Dos botones pidiendo el mismo permiso son un error que sólo se ve en el navegador. - **Una sola bajada de las paradas de la ciudad.** La piden las paradas cercanas y el orden de las rutas; se lee una vez en `VistaInicio` en vez de dos hooks con la misma petición. - **Una ruta sin paradas publicadas** no se esconde —una ruta que existe y no aparece deja al pasajero buscándola— pero va al final y **sin número**: no se le inventa una distancia. - `EstadoDeRuta` sale a `lib/ontoy/estado-de-ruta.ts`: lo leen la portada y dos componentes, y vivía dentro de la pantalla que se retiró. ## El Marco (lo mergeas tú) **Segunda enmienda ✎ del día a la 8.8**, agregando sin borrar — y esto vale la pena decirlo: **no se borra ni el punto 2 de la enmienda de la mañana**, el que mandaba la lista a «Ir a». Se quedó, con la nueva encima diciendo cuál rige. Es el registro de por dónde pasó la decisión en un mismo día, y borrarlo dejaría la ley pareciendo que siempre dijo esto. La enmienda ancla además el orden de las rutas a la **8.7**, para que «ordénalas por lo más popular» tenga una respuesta escrita la próxima vez que se proponga. ## Verificación **221/221** en verde (9 nuevas sólo para el orden, incluidas las que prueban que sin ubicación la bandera prohíbe el título), `tsc --noEmit` limpio, `next build` limpio. **Visto en el navegador en las dos pieles y en los cuatro estados** —sin ubicación, desplegado, con ubicación y con parada guardada— contra la base desechable con **cinco rutas publicadas**. Producción no se tocó. ## Una cosa que vi y no cambié solo Con ubicación **y sin paradas guardadas**, las dos secciones se repiten: «Av. de las Torres a 20 m (Circuito de muestra)» arriba y «Circuito de muestra a 20 m» abajo. Es la misma información contestando dos preguntas distintas (*qué parada* / *qué ruta*), y en la captura se lee redundante. No lo toqué porque el diseño que aprobaste dice que las dos secciones conviven. Si quieres, la de paradas se puede recortar a una sola cuando hay rutas debajo, o quitarse. **Dime y lo hago en un PR aparte** — no quiero cambiar el diseño aprobado por mi cuenta. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: krzysztof-smartdataengines
body:
## #148 and #149 — two things the binary said that were not true

Both found while reading the client loop and its flags before making the loop parallel. Neither
changes a byte a client reads today; both would have, at the next version bump or the next knob.

### #148 — the welcome banner and the CLI carried the version as literals

`s->send_response("OK ob_tcp_server v0.1.0\n\n")` — the first bytes every client of every node
reads — and `ob_cli`'s `"orderbook-dbengine CLI v0.1.0\n"`, both since the server's first commit.
#90 took the version out of the startup line so it would come from `project(... VERSION)`, and
missed these two.

**The guard #90 added could not have caught #90.** It refused `"v?0\.1\.0"`: a literal made of the
version and nothing else. The literal #90 removed was
`"ob_tcp_server v0.1.0 listening on port %u, data-dir: %s\n"`. Restored verbatim against #90's own test, that line **passes** — measured, row 4 below.

Now both greetings take `ob::version()`. The rule finds the version anywhere inside one literal, as a
whole number (`v10.1.0` is not `0.1.0`), in every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/`, `tools/`, `include/`
and `benchmarks/`, listed from the tree; it runs its own six cases through the same function first,
and the four files copies were found in must be among those it read. Three comments that called the
startup line "the only place" the version appeared are corrected.

### #149 — `--workers` was parsed, printed, documented, and read by nothing

`--workers <N>` → `ServerConfig::worker_threads`, printed by `--print-config`, documented in
`--help` and `docs/cli.md` as "Number of worker threads (default: 4)", read by nothing since March.
#32 printed a note that it did nothing; the flag stayed. The multi-reactor stage is about to add the
real knob, and a flag that looks like it and does nothing next to it is a trap.

**BREAKING:** `--workers` is refused as an unknown argument, on a command line and in a config file.

The mechanism is the link #32's static tests did not check: those hold the parser against the
known-flag list and the list against the docs, and they all agreed on `--workers` the whole time.
`CliConfigStatic.EveryParsedValueIsReadByTheServer` requires every `ServerConfig` field to be read
(`.field` / `->field`) somewhere in `src/`, `tools/` or `include/` outside the parser and the
formatter, with one exemption pinned in both directions (`profile`, resolved by the parser into the
knobs it names). Against the tree before this change it names `worker_threads` and nothing else.
What it cannot see is stated beside it: a field read only by code the binary does not build (#147's
io_uring flags were that).

### Mutations

Committed before the first mutation; every source restored from bytes kept beside the run;
verdicts are the test binary's exit status. **23 rows, 20 killed, 3 surviving as they should.**

| | #148 | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the banner's literal back | killed |
| 2 | the CLI's literal back | killed |
| 3 | #90's removed startup line back, against this rule | killed |
| 4 | **the same line, against #90's rule** | **survived** — the demonstration |
| 5 | a literal in a header | killed |
| 6 | #90's pattern back, over the whole tree | killed by the rule's own cases |
| 7–8 | either word boundary dropped | killed by the cases `v1…` and `…1` |
| 9 | the prefilter inverted | killed by the cases |
| 10 | a comment quoting the version read as code | killed by the cases |
| 11–12 | the walk loses `tools/` or `include/` | killed by the files that must be read |
| 13 | control: the message reworded | survived |

| | #149 | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--workers` back, whole | killed, naming `worker_threads` and nothing else |
| 2 | the same, against the refusal test | killed |
| 3 | a live field made dead (the hub built with a literal instead of `--max-subscriber-queue-bytes`) | killed, naming it |
| 4–8 | the parser or formatter not cut, `.deadline` read as `.dead`, comments read as code, a member without an initializer missed | killed by the rule's own cases |
| 9 | `profile`'s exemption dropped | killed |
| 10 | control: the message reworded | survived |

### Verified locally

Debug build without warnings; `ctest -j1` **1171/1171 in 204 s** (master has 1169: the refusal
test and the new static rule). The four affected binaries run on their own too: `test_version` 3,
`test_cli_config` 25, `test_cli_args` 23, `test_tcp_server` 63.

### Also here

`.github/rulesets/master.json` gains four parameters the live ruleset reports and the file lacked —
among them `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes: true`. `PUT` replaces the ruleset
wholesale, so applying the file as its README says would have set them to whatever GitHub defaults
to. Found while narrowing the live ruleset for #147, which was done from the live body for that
reason; after this the file and the live ruleset agree in every parameter, read back.

author: abarth
body:
This PR introduces `babeldiff`, a specialized diff tool designed to review changes that port C++ code to Rust. The tool was built for the Zircon kernel's in-place conversion strategy, where C++ implementations are replaced with Rust implementations called through FFI.

## Summary

`babeldiff` parses both C++ and Rust source code, pairs removed C++ functions with their Rust replacements, aligns them line-by-line, and flags semantic differences such as:
- Lost, added, or reworded comments
- Differing error returns or handling
- Locks taken in different places
- Control flow differences (if/loops/switch/match/return/break)
- Calls or steps performed by only one side

## Key Changes

- **Core analysis pipeline**: Implemented language-agnostic function extraction and alignment (`extract.rs`, `align.rs`, `analyze.rs`)
- **C++ extraction**: Tree-sitter based parser for C++ functions with support for class hierarchies and declaration comments (`cpp.rs`)
- **Rust extraction**: Tree-sitter based parser for Rust functions with support for modules, traits, and impl blocks (`rust.rs`)
- **Semantic checking**: Comparison logic that detects behavioral differences in comments, error codes, locks, and control flow (`check.rs`)
- **Normalization**: Language-agnostic identifier and code normalization to handle naming convention differences (`normalize.rs`)
- **Git integration**: Support for reading changes from git repositories and patches (`git.rs`, `patch.rs`)
- **Output rendering**: Plain-text side-by-side and stacked diff layouts (`render.rs`)
- **CLI and library**: Command-line interface with subcommands for analyzing patches, git revisions, and files (`main.rs`, `lib.rs`)
- **Comprehensive tests**: End-to-end golden tests with fixtures for job_policy and fifo_dispatcher conversions

## Implementation Details

- Uses tree-sitter for robust parsing of both C++ and Rust
- Implements FFI shim detection to link C++ callers with Rust implementations
- Provides configurable output layouts (side-by-side or stacked) with context filtering
- Distinguishes between "issues" (behavioral differences) and "notes" (translation artifacts)
- Supports both library and CLI usage patterns

author: misterjohannesson
body:
**On Windows a dormant session vanished when the daemon restarted.** The index finds a dormant session by globbing the state directory, and on Windows that directory comes from `%LOCALAPPDATA%` written with backslashes. `Path.wildcard` reads a backslash as an escape, so `C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\troupe/sessions/*/*/events.jsonl` matched nothing and raised nothing. I checked it against the build that was installed before this one (0.3.3, without this change), with the default state root and no `TROUPE_STATE_HOME`: a session was created and answered one turn, then the daemon was restarted. After that `session.list` returned 0 sessions, and `session.get`, `subscribe` and `input.send` all answered `not_found` for it, while its `events.jsonl` was still on disk. A `[` or `{` in a runtime path breaks the same globs another way: a workspace at `app[1]` is searched as `app1`.

**One helper, `Troupe.Paths.glob_escape/1`, and every glob that starts from a runtime path goes through it.** It turns backslashes into forward slashes and escapes `*`, `?`, `[` and `{`, so the directory matches itself and nothing else, and only what is joined on after it is still a pattern. The call sites are the index's `scan_disk` and `from_disk`, `Log.locate` (which `read_session`, `troupe resume` and the `read_branch` tool rely on), the watcher's context scan, `Workflow.available`, and the `glob`, `grep` (built-in scanner) and `list_files` tools.

**Both parts are needed; they are not alternatives.** Forward slashes are what fixes the reported bug. Escaping alone cannot fix a Windows path, because the backslash is the escape character, and `filelib` cannot match a literal backslash at all: `\\` in a pattern comes out as `@e` through its escape handling. Escaping fixes the `[` / `{` case, which forward slashes leave broken, and it costs one line. A backslash is treated as a separator on every host, as `Troupe.Workspace` already does, and on Linux a glob could not have matched one inside a name anyway. I considered globbing relative to the directory instead (`:filelib.wildcard/3` with a cwd, so no escaping at all), but that needs an undocumented `filelib` arity and Elixir's private `Path.Wildcard` to keep `match_dot: false`.

**The sites the issue lists, and what could reach each one.** A backslashed path reached `sessions/index.ex` (`scan_disk`, `from_disk`) and `session/log.ex` (`locate`) straight from `Paths.state_dir/1`. That is the reported bug, and it also meant `Log.locate` returned `nil`, so `Log.read_session` read nothing. `session/watcher.ex` and the three tools glob from `Workspace.real_path/1` output, which is always forward-slashed, so for them only glob characters in the workspace path mattered. `workflow.ex` is called with `Path.expand/1` output, which is forward-slashed on Windows, and the same applies. All of them now take the helper. Nothing else changed.

**Verified:**
- Reproduction first. Five new tests fail when the call sites are at `origin/main`: `apps/troupe_core/test/troupe/session/state_dir_test.exs` (3 of 3: the index lists `[]` for a backslashed state root, `state[1]` and `state{a,b}`), the new `workflow_test.exs` case and the new `file_tools_test.exs` case. All of them pass with the fix. The backslashed-root test builds the Windows spelling of the root itself (`String.replace(root, "/", "\\")`), so it runs the same way under WSL as on Windows.
- `mixw test` in `apps/troupe_core` on the pushed commit: 386 passed (3 doctests, 1 property, 382 tests). One earlier full run had one failure, in `watch/watcher_test.exs`: a poll-backend debounce test got a second trigger while the suite was busy. That file then passed 3 times out of 3 on its own, and the full suite passed after that. The test counts triggers, which this change does not affect. The suite includes the new `paths_test.exs`, `state_dir_test.exs` (the index's `list` and `get`, `Log.locate` and `Log.read_session`), and the new workflow and tool cases. The tool case covers `list_files`, `glob` and `grep`, and there is no `rg` under WSL, so `grep` ran on the built-in scanner that changed.
- `mixw credo --strict` on all 12 touched files: no issues. `mixw compile --force --warnings-as-errors` in `apps/troupe_core`: clean.
- `.\scripts\install-local.ps1` (daemon and TUI) installed 0.3.3 from this branch. `.\scripts\verify-local.ps1`: all five checks passed.
- The issue's reproduction against the **installed** daemon: a PowerShell script drove `troupe-daemon.cmd run` over its loopback TCP transport, with the default state root `C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\troupe` (`TROUPE_STATE_HOME` unset) and the fake provider from a scratch workspace's config. It created a session, ran a turn, killed the daemon and started it again. Run against the previous build, it showed the bug as described above. With this build installed every check passed:
  - After the restart, `session.list` returned 29 of this machine's sessions instead of 0, and the test session was among them as `dormant`.
  - `session.get` answered it.
  - `subscribe` from 0 replayed it (`head_seq` 6).
  - `input.send` woke it, and the next turn ran.
  - Its log reads `1:agent_started 2:session_created … 7:agent_restarted 8:session_resumed 9:session_activated 10:input_accepted …`, with one `session_created`.

**Not verified:**
- The watcher's context scan has no test of its own for a workspace path with `[` or `{`. It uses the same helper as the tools, which are tested.
- Linux pods and macOS. The change there is escaping only, because their paths have no backslashes, and the Linux side is what the WSL test run covers.
- The GUI against the installed daemon. It lists sessions through the same `session.list`.

Fixes #87

author: raphaellith
body:
### Issue

Using the `--onefile` option in PyInstaller produces a backend binary that embeds its own ad-hoc-signed `Python.framework`, with no Team ID. In `tauri build`, the bundler copies the sidecar into `Résumé Compiler.app/Contents/MacOS/backend` and re-signs it.

The default hardenedRuntime enables Apple's library validation, where a process may only load code signed by the same Team ID. As the embedded `Python.framework` bears a different signature,  it cannot be loaded and the PyInstaller bootloader aborts on startup.

Since the sidecar never binds, so `GET /health` becomes unresponsive and `ensureBackendIsReady()` polls forever.

Note that this issue does not affect dev mode, as `tauri dev` runs the raw PyInstaller binary straight from `src-tauri/binaries/` with no resigning or library validation.


### Fix

- Updated `src-tauri/entitlements.plist` and `tauri.conf.json` to disable library validation while keeping options for ad-hoc signing (`adhoc`) and hardened runtime (`runtime`)                                                                                                                                  
- Updated CI in release.yml to use `pyinstaller==6.22.2` and added:
  - a pre-bundle smoke test of `dist/backend` for verifying that the artifact boots correctly and that `/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`, and
  - a post-bundle validation that the re-signed backend carries the entitlement and actually boots against `/health`.
- `src/client/apiClient.ts`: Adds a 45-second deadline to the readiness poll so a dead backend surfaces a clear error instead of hanging forever.

author: dkaulig
body:
## Problem

Browser reloads of the chat did not recover cleanly, and freshly arrived Claude messages sometimes did not show up until the next write or the 30 s recovery timer:

- The first ready index of every session was reported as a replaced binding, which reset the chat generation, deleted the saved snapshot and discarded all cursors. After every reload or server restart the view jumped back, "load older" returned 409 and images briefly failed.
- A refresh after a transcript append could join an in-flight read that opened the file before the append and publish stale content.
- A reloaded tab received the cached stream value without a refresh while another tab or device kept the stream alive.
- The 30 s recovery timer blanked the native queue state, and a dead tmux input watcher was not reattached.
- Generated user records (`<task-notification>`, local command output, sidechains) rendered as user messages depending on timing, so live and reloaded views differed.
- A transcript rewritten in place or an oversized tail left history permanently unavailable (409 / 413).
- Streamed assistant fragments without block ids could overwrite each other; provisional pages could cut between fragments.
- Older pages could be inserted out of order, expired cursors broke "load older" permanently, and the HTTP fallback was aborted on every reconnect.

## Behavior

- The first index ready is a `history-indexed` event; only a real index generation change resets the binding.
- One provider history read per session with at most one queued follow-up; only the newest source epoch writes the cache and saved snapshot.
- New stream subscribers receive the cached value and always trigger a refresh.
- The native input queue state survives the recovery timer; a dead input watcher reattaches with backoff.
- A shared `claudeVisibleRecord` predicate is used by the full, provisional and indexed readers. Typed slash commands show as `/name args`; local command output and an explicit denylist of generated origins are hidden; unknown origins stay visible.
- Rewritten transcripts fall back to the provisional page and re-index; an oversized tail keeps serving the saved snapshot while indexing.
- Id-less fragment blocks are keyed per source record; provisional pages never split a message.
- Older pages prepend only unseen rows, cursors are LRU and refreshed on use, and the client restarts paging once after a 409.
- A slow HTTP fallback snapshot can land during reconnects (bounded by a 30 s timeout); the socket gets a 30 s first-snapshot deadline.
- Tool groups keep their open state when older rows are prepended; the tool details fallback label is localized.

## Validation

- Regression tests for every item (new: `chat-stream-freshness`, `chat-store-single-flight`, `claude-history-visibility`, `claude-history-recovery`, `claude-history-fragments`; extended unit, integration and browser specs). Each new test fails without its fix.
- `npm run check`: 2645/2660 pass; the only failure is the known local Unicode login-shell test in `shell.test.js`, unrelated.
- Playwright `chat*.spec.js` on Chromium: 123 passed.
- Provisional and indexed paging compared against a full read on 10 real local Claude transcripts (also while the file grows): 0 duplicate, missing or differing rows (3 files differed before).
- An independent code review of the branch found two regressions (parallel reads, empty placeholder overwriting a saved snapshot) and three minor issues; all are fixed with tests.

author: viniclus
body:
## What

Reorganizes `apps/agent`'s Java backend from eight technical modules (`identityaccess`, `sourceconnector`, `pecadapter`, `extractionstore`, `indicatorengine`, `indicatorpacks`, `jobrunner`, `resultstore`) plus a global `api/` HTTP package, into five vertical capability slices — `access`, `sources`, `execution`, `indicators`, `results` — plus `platform`. Purely structural: no HTTP contract, OpenAPI, SQLite schema/migration, NDJSON protocol, extract format, or indicator-logic change.

Documented in `docs/adr/0012-capacidades-verticais.md`. ADR 0009 marked superseded (module list only — its layer semantics still hold).

## Why

One capability (e.g. "a run") used to span six package roots (`api/runs` + `jobrunner` + `sourceconnector` + `pecadapter` + `extractionstore` + `resultstore`). ADR 0009's per-module hexagonal layering made this worse over time, not better — "where does execution happen?" required knowing six roots at once.

## Before / after

**Before:** 8 technical modules (Tech Spec §1.5 vocabulary) each internally layered `domain`/`application`/`infrastructure`, plus a global `api/` HTTP package organized by resource.

**After:**
```
br/gov/observatorioaps/
├── access/      IdentityAccessConfig — domain, application, adapter/in/http{,/security}, adapter/out/sqlite
├── sources/     SourcesConfig — domain, adapter/{in/http, out/sqlite}
├── execution/   JobRunnerConfig, AcquisitionConfig — domain/{job,acquisition,extract}, application, adapter/in/http, adapter/out/{sqlite,pec,process,file}
├── indicators/  domain, packs/{,c1}, adapter/in/http
├── results/     ResultsConfig — domain, application, adapter/{in/http, out/sqlite}
├── platform/    sqlite, lock, web
└── ObservatorioApsApplication.java
```

## Scope

266 files changed in `apps/agent/src`: 260 via `git mv` (257 detected as renames at git's default similarity threshold; `MeResponse`, `ReauthRequest`, `SourceNotFoundException` are small enough to need `-M30%` to show as renames — **use `git diff -M30%` to review this PR**, not the default), 2 genuine new files (`ResultsConfig`, `SourcesConfig` — wiring split out of `JobRunnerConfig`), 4 edited in place (`ObservatorioApsApplication`, `ApplicationBootTest`, `ModuleBoundaryTest`, `Eng19ReproducibilityWithoutPecLiveTest`).

## How to review

- **Commit by commit.** Commit 1 (`4d505ec`) is the mechanical `git mv` + import/package rewrite — diff it with `-M30%`, expect no logic change. Commits 2–3 split wiring and fix one seam (`ReproducibilityCheck` now takes `ExtractStore` instead of a raw path — same underlying `ExtractReader`). Commit 4 rewrites `ModuleBoundaryTest` (19 ArchUnit rules, replacing the old per-module set — **all 19 individually mutation-tested by hand**, one forbidden dependency injected per rule, confirmed red in isolation, reverted). Commit 5 is docs.
- Commits 1–3 are **red on `ModuleBoundaryTest`** until commit 4 lands — by design, not a regression; the old rules assert on package names this PR removes.
- `docs/adr/0012-capacidades-verticais.md` documents every deliberate deviation from a mechanical move (e.g. `CanonicalEncounter`/`SourceRef` → `indicators.domain` so indicators never depends on execution; `PecSourceAcquisition` → `execution.adapter.out.pec`, a misclassified adapter reclassified) and the remaining architectural debt (13 named classes, down from 14, with per-class reason — not hidden).
- The capability-cycle ArchUnit rule does **not** prove the whole capability graph is acyclic — `execution`↔`results` legitimately depend on each other at whole-capability granularity (ENG-23's single SQLite transaction spanning publication and job-row state transition). Documented in the ADR, not hidden.

## Testing

`mvn verify -Dsurefire.reuseForks=false`: 356 tests, 0 failures, 6 skipped (live-PEC, skipped without a reachable PEC per ADR 0002/0003) — BUILD SUCCESS. `@Test` count outside `architecture/` is identical to `main` (341 = 341) — no test lost in the move. `git diff --stat main -- apps/execplane apps/web contracts apps/agent/src/main/resources` is empty — no contract/schema/resource touched.

**No CI is configured in this repo** (no `.github/workflows`) — local `mvn verify` is the merge gate.

## Regression risk

Low. Pure structural move plus one seam signature change, verified behavior-equivalent by existing tests. No HTTP/OpenAPI/SQL/NDJSON/extract-format change.

author: bobhay75
body:
## Purpose
Replace the remaining Plan a Visit, Serve, and Find Your People mailto-only handoffs with reliable first-party KCMC intake while keeping submitted contact details private.

## Public flow
- existing `visit`, `serve`, and `groups` forms submit JSON directly to KCMC
- category-specific server validation uses only the fields already presented by the public UI
- visit validates first/last name, email, optional phone, and one of the three published Sunday services
- serve/group requests validate name, email, existing interest choices, and optional note
- unknown form categories and unknown public fields are rejected/discarded
- accessible inline success/error messages replace dependency on a configured email app
- event RSVP remains on its dedicated RSVP path
- email handoff remains as fallback for any future unrecognized form

## Private storage and abuse controls
- submissions live only under protected private data storage
- separate private rate state stores a one-way client-address hash, never the raw address
- 15 attempts per 10-minute client window
- request body capped at 8 KB
- explicit cross-site browser submissions rejected
- duplicate same-category/email requests within 30 minutes are idempotent
- retained store capped at 5,000 rows
- intake is separate from public content backups and PWA caches

## Administrator inbox
- Pastor/Recovery administrator role gate
- private/no-store page
- newest 300 requests
- category summary counts
- name, email, optional phone, selected service/interest, note, received time
- linked from the event RSVP administrator page

## Audit and client delivery
- separate friendly audit actions for visit, serve, and group submissions
- audit stores count only, not contact details or notes
- service-worker script refresh forces the proven cache-reload install path so installed KCMC clients receive the updated app.js

## Verification
Dedicated deterministic contract tests cover every form category, allowlisted options, rejection paths, unknown-field removal, rate limiting, duplicate handling, private storage, administrator authorization, audit privacy, client routing, RSVP regression, email fallback, and service-worker client refresh. Dedicated CI also checks PHP and JavaScript syntax.

Closes #51 after review and merge.
